You therefore wrongly charge Anastasius the Librarian and Nicetas the Paphlagonian with slander, since they relate Photius's tyranny against Ignatius and his impious crimes as they happened. That these things were done as they say, the other writers, in one voice and with one mind, make clear, so that it is not safe for you to deny it. For you, who are born for everything, would certainly deny outright that Photius, committing similar acts against the most holy men, was a doctor of the Styx, a servant of the Evil One, a crooked dragon, a magician and necromancer, who by the Sanctabarenian tricks bewitched the Emperor Basil. The Papists say little that is worth anything about him. I myself have seen nothing more seditious than Photius in Church History, no more monstrous monster, no more wicked eunuch, since in him there was no faith, but great audacity, and the other vices of a brazen forehead flourished. That these things were foretold by the most holy men is not a matter of Jesuit roses and narcissi, but a fact itself, if the writers who report it are to be believed. Hold, then, a similar prediction confirmed for you too, not from Jesuit flowerets, but from the Greeks themselves, who after the Schism carried it back to the ancient records. Simon of Byzantium, in his Letter to John Nomophylax: for Saint Michael, Bishop of the Synadi, when he foresaw with great acuteness the things to come, looking upon the mother of this Photius, who lived the monastic life in a monastery with other virgins and was pregnant with Photius, stretched out his staff to strike her, and pronounced: "Would that someone were present who might kill her and the embryo within her. For I see another, a serpent-pregnant Eve, and the male offspring, and by the permission of God I see the future Patriarch, to abolish the most venerable and precious Cross. He himself will also fall into impiety, and will lead almost all from the straight way into twisted paths, and will make them stray from the pure faith of Christ, and will compel them to the spurious worship of the Cross, and will make contemptuous of the sacred canons, and by his deceitful machinations will deprive countless people of the kingdom of heaven." But what is the use of talking to a blind man with a mirror? Robert Creighton, although he is the King's domestic chaplain or ordinary, Doctor of Sacred Theology and Dean of Bury, a man glorious in the esteem and titles of the common people, has not yet learned to distinguish white from black, day from night, light from darkness, virtue from vice, holiness from malice, integrity from wickedness. Nor is it surprising: for him all things, whether good or bad, are one. To this one thing the religion of such men has turned, so that they are more savage, more heedless and more bold than barbarians and Turks, and than those who, not yet washed in the saving bath of Christ, have given their names to Christ. They rashly and shamelessly spout to the people not what has happened but what has pleased them, and the more monstrous the lies they have invented, the more madly they clamour for them. Therefore, in this place, Creighton, in whom only his tongue survives through a defect of mind, is to be given up as harmless. For who would not firmly assert that he has sailed to Anticyra, when he hears: that he gave greater faith and reverence to the rarer monuments of Photius than to all the miracles of Saint Ignatius or the prescriptions of Saint Nicholas. Certainly this man did not look into the weight of these matters with his own eyes; or if he did look, surrounded by thick darkness, he pronounced a poor judgment. So it is no wonder that those who look more carefully and discern them hold his blinded sayings in derision and laugh at them as a jest. Thus he must abandon the hope of unanimous agreement among others.

units.la: Ludit quoque sane nos Actione 3. Elias Presbyter, cum Photij depositionem Α'θέμιτον[?], ἐ ἀδίσμον[?], ἀνοίαν[?], nefariam, scelestem, nefandam, impiam, asum[?] & amentiam appellat. Γινώσκει ἡ ἀγαθὴ τῆς Θεοῦ, ὃν οὐκ ἐν τῇ Παξιαρχῶ κύειν Φόνον ϑερεῖ-δον, ὃν, ὅπ ἔφεμα παρ᾽ αὐτῇ ἰδίξαμεν, ὅπ συμέ-τυχον αὐτῷ ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὴ[?] Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ ἀρξὰν αὐτὴν[?] καὶ τ ἀδίμωνῳ εἰς αὐτὴν[?] ξεδωμιῶν Ἰσόνοιαν[?], καὶ σὺν ἀλ ὀλπτεπτηρτατ[?] σὺν ἀδίους ἐκείνες διὰ ταῦ(α) παςαγήγορα.[?] Bene nouit bonitas Dei mihi antea Patriarcham Dominum Photium notum non fuisse, neque literas ab eodem accepisse, neque illis diebus sermonem cum eo habuisse, sed propter Ecclesiam, & virtutem illius, & nefariam in illum contumeliam peractam, & falsos illos, atque iniquos locum tenentes huc accessi. Quin etiam ipsa Synodus dum ait; Photium non vlla vi, sed omnium consensu, & ab Imperatore compulsum Episcopatum accepisse: quæ fusius ipse Photius persequens dicere non erubuit, se nunquam Episcopatum ambisse, nec vi, ac seculari potentia innixum, sed ab vniuersa Constantinopolitana Ecclesia coactum Patriarchale fastigium conscendisse, atque inde postea iniuste eiectum, æquo & libenti animo exilium passum, neque vnquam de reuocatione cum Imperatore egisse, sed illius pietate reuocatum, amicitiam sibi cum Ignatio fuisse, neque se vnquam eo viuo Episcopatum inuadere voluisse, quamuis eum multi ad id agendum impellerent. Verum eo mortuo se omnium consensu, atque adeo ab Imperatore ipso compulsum ex necess[?] cessitate Constantinopolitanam Sedem recepisse. His non dissona sunt, quæ idem Epistola ad Nicolaum satis ampullatis verbis ac sesquipedalibus proijcit.
units.tr: Elias the Presbyter also surely mocks us in the third Action, when he calls the deposition of Photius unlawful, unholy, foolish, nefarious, wicked, unspeakable, impious, mad and insane. The goodness of God knows well that I had not known the Patriarch Lord Photius before, that I had received no letter from him, and that I had not had any conversation with him in those days; but I came here on account of the Church, and his virtue, and the nefarious insult done to him, and those false and unjust officials. Indeed, the Synod itself says that Photius accepted the episcopate not by any force, but by the consent of all, and when compelled by the Emperor. Photius himself, setting this out more fully, did not blush to say that he had never sought the episcopate, nor had he relied on force or secular power, but had been compelled by the whole Church of Constantinople to ascend the patriarchal throne; and that afterwards he had been unjustly cast out from it, and had endured exile with an equal and willing mind; that he had never sought recall from the Emperor, but had been recalled by the Emperor's piety; that he had been a friend of Ignatius; and that he had never wished to seize the episcopate while Ignatius was alive, although many urged him to do so. But when Ignatius died, he received the see of Constantinople by the consent of all, and indeed, of necessity, when compelled by the Emperor himself. What is set out in the same Letter to Nicholas, in rather bombastic and long-winded words, agrees with these things.

units.la: CAPUT VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Ex scopo ac fine unico Concilij, quæ fuit resti- tutio Photij a depositis, & excommunicatis pro- secta, antequam accessisset assensus Ponti- ficis Romani, hoc idem ostenditur,
units.tr: From the sole aim of the Council, which was the restoration of Photius, deposed and excommunicated, before the assent of the Roman Pontiff had been given, the same is shown.

units.la: Quæ porro de causa Synodus ista cogitur? Non alia prorsus, nisi ut Photius, vel saltem illius restitutio Synodali decreto comprobetur. Sed ante coactam Synodum Photius iam thronum occupauerat, & Imperatoris violentissima tempestate, ac Ioannis Pontificis indulgentia, ut paucis aliquid dicam, novum in modum invaserat. Temere ergo Synodus celebratur, neque enim in possessionem auctoritate Romani Pontificis, & Imperatoris restitutus, calculo Synodali ad gradum, unde ceciderat, reponendus videbatur. Audiatur Basilius Martyropolitanus, & Locumtenens Antiocheni, Actione 5. Οἱ ἐξ ἡμῶν Θεὸν μέγιστον ἀρχιερέως ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἀδιάσπαστον τῷ Θεῷ τοῦ ἀνωθέν Παντοκράτορι Φώτιον ἡνωμένον ἔχονἐρπῆς, ἀφ' ἧς ἡμεῖς τὸν ἀρχιερατικὸν ἀνήνεχθη βα-θρόνον, ὅθι τοῦτο ὑμᾶς ἀπέστειλαν, δόντος ἐξουσίαν, καὶ αὐθεντίαν Φωτίῳ τῷ ἁγιωτάτῳ πατριάρχῃ. Καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Sediii[?] qua apud nos sunt maximi Præsules[?] summopere Photio sanctissimo Patriarchæ mente & animo, ac inseparabiliter addicti, ex quo ad Archiepiscopalem sedem euectus est, nos miserunt, facultatem, auctoritatemque Photio sanctissimo Patriarchæ tribuentes. &c. Et Actione secunda in Epistola Synodica Michaelis Patriarchæ Alexandrini, & aliorum, restitutio Photij tota auctoritati Imperatoris ascribitur: de Pontifice Romano restituente nullum verbum. Sed de his infra fusius. Quod tenetur, frustra ab aliis emendicatur, & quod certe possidetur, consultationibus aliorum inconsiderate concreditum, in dubium vertitur.
units.tr: For what purpose, then, was this Synod convened? For no other purpose at all, except that Photius, or at least his restoration, might be confirmed by a synodal decree. But before the Synod was assembled, Photius had already occupied the throne, and had seized it in a novel manner, through the most violent storm raised by the Emperor and the indulgence of Pope John, to put it briefly. The Synod was therefore convened rashly, for Photius had been restored to possession by the authority of the Roman Pontiff and the Emperor, and it did not seem right that he should be put back into the rank from which he had fallen by the vote of a Synod. Let Basil, Metropolitan of Martyropolis and deputy of Antioch, be heard in the fifth Action: [Οἱ ἐξ ἡμῶν ... Φώτιον ἡνωμένον ἔχον] "Those among us, the greatest of the chief priests, who have been closely and inseparably united to Photius, the most holy Patriarch, sent us, granting the power and authority to the most holy Patriarch Photius, from the time when he was raised to the archiepiscopal see." And so on. And in the second Action, in the Synodal Letter of Michael, Patriarch of Alexandria, and of others, the restoration of Photius is wholly ascribed to the authority of the Emperor; there is not a word about the Roman Pontiff restoring him. But of these things more fully below. What is held is vainly begged from others, and what is certainly possessed is rashly handed over to the deliberations of others and is cast into doubt.

units.la: Adde his Zachariæ Chalcedonensis de Basilio Imperatore sermonem, Actione 1. Ποιεῖ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἄπαιν [?] Θεὸς τῆς ἀγνωσίας [?] ἡμῖν ἰδιάζοντα [?] λεγόμενα πλάσματα, καὶ ὡς ἐδὲν ὑμεῖς [?] ἰδίν ὑμεῖς λῶ ἐκάδιν. συγάζεται ὁ καὶ καλῶς τῆς τῷ ἁγιωτάτῳ Πάπᾳ Ἰωάννῃ γνώμης, ὡς ἰδιαμῶς ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐπ' ὀλίθεφ, ἐ καθαλύοι [?] ἀφαιρεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν. ἀφορᾷ ὁ ἀεὶ τούτῳ ἐ ἀφεῖς αὐτὸν τὸν ἡ κατὰ, ἐ τῷ τε ὁ [?] Θεῷ ἀρθεῖσι ὡς τὸ πάλαι... τὸ πᾶν νομοθέτει ἀπαν ἰχωὶ ἐχῆ, ἐ ςὐγεύρ [?] ἐ... τῶν ταῦτα [?] δὲ ἡμῖς σαφῶς εὐθέως, ἢ ἡ φύσις, ἐ ἰωλον ἀιαφαίνεται ἐ [?] Ἀποκαθίσταται μὲν τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τὸ ἴδιον, ἐκ τῶν ὑμφίων αὐτῆς τοίχων [?] ἐπιλαμβάνει. Παίντα δὲ τὰ κατ᾽ αὐτὴν σημονόμενα λῆρος μὲν, ἐφωνάζειν νομίζῃ.
units.tr: Add to these the speech of Zacharias of Chalcedon concerning the Emperor Basil, in the first Action. [Greek largely illegible on the scan; the sense is that the speaker says God makes the things said by us to be fabrications, and that the mind of the most holy Pope John is rightly to be followed, since he does not permit anything to be taken away from the Church by those who act against it; the Church, once restored by God, recovers what is its own from the walls of its enemies, and all that is said against it is taken for mere nonsense.]

units.la: Namque his omnibus manifestum facit, quæ ab Oriente allata sunt, pura puta esse mendacia, & res fictitias, & nihil sanum inde accedere: & haud dubijs argumentis coniectat sanctissimi Papæ Ioannis mentem, nullo scilicet eum modo infisteres ijs, quæ in interitum ac dissolutionem Ecclesiæ acta sunt, sed ante omnia in ipsum Canonem inspicere, & probitatis naturam, cui si consonum fuerit quidquid fit, robur habet, & ab omnibus recipitur: quod si ab ea disfunctum fuerit, obsoletum, & irritum reputatur: & proprium quod fuerit Ecclesiæ restituitur, & sponsum illa suum recuperat. Omnia vero quæ contra ipsum actitata sunt nugamenta ingentia, & loquacitas existimantur. Quis hoc nisi Photianus asseveret, Pontificem Pontificum acta condemnare, & ludos facere, & auctoritatem propriam eodem momento opprimere? Hæc Zacharias. Quid vero Synodus? Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἐξεβόησεν. Ἡμεῖς τε ἀμωμήτῳ ἡμῶν Διαδότῃ, καὶ οἰκουμενικῷ Παῤῥιάρχῃ, οἳ μὲν ἀρχῆς ὄντες λωμωνίως οὐδ᾽ ἀπο ἐπὶ ἀμισί[illegible, ~6 letters] ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἄμεσα ἡμῶν ἀφεύρωμεν [illegible, ~8 letters] τῆς βουλομένοις ταῦτα ζῆν ἐν ἐνίμῳ ἕκαστα μὲν. Οὕτως ὁ καὶ εἶπε τινὰ προσὼς αὐτὴν [?] ἀποδεξάμενα πολλὰ ἐξεχώρησε τῆς ἀρετῆς ἡμῖν χαμῆς καὶ διάθε-σι[?] σεως νῦν ὁλοφύχῳ καρδίᾳ, καὶ ἀκλινεῖ τῇ φρονή-μάτῃ, ἐ ἀρχηείᾳ ἐς διαστόμν[?], ἐ πωὶ ὡμὰ ὑπορχωφόμιδα[?], ἐ ὅσον ὅτι τύπος διαςίζοντας ἐχθρὸς ἐ Ἐκκλησίας, ἐ ἀποβλὴν τῆς ἠνούμδα[?]. Sancta Synodus clamauit. Nos sanctissimo nostro Domino, & Oecumenico Patriarchae, qui ab ipso initio uniti fuimus, nunquam segregati sumus, sed & sanguinem nostrum lubenti animo pro eo effundere volentibus haec inquirere parati fuimus. quotquot autem cum ipso aliquo modo inimicitias exercuere nostram primam aduersus eundem sententiam & propositum condemnantes, nunc toto corde, & mente firma, & summum Sacerdotem, & Dominum, & Pastorem agnoscimus, & super his dubitantes, tanquam hostes Ecclesiae, & reiectos ab ea existimamus. Et clariora poscimus? Nondum lectis Ioannis literis, nec ab excommunicatione solutì, nec in communionem recepti, nec suis Ecclesijs restituti sententiam pronuntiant, & Photium restitutum agnoscunt, quibus uniti cum Ecclesia Romana assensum non praebent, neque factum laudant. Ad Zachariam denuo provoco. Ἀ᾽ξίως ἂς ἀπ᾽ ἀν[?] οἵπερ λοιπὸν ὑπελείφθησαν τῆς χειμαῤῥου πλάνης, μὴ ὁ[?] τῶν ἄλλων αὐτὰ μάτων ἐν ἐκείνοις ἡμωνῳν[?] καθίσαντ[?], καὶ τὸ πιστὸν ὁ[?] ἐν ἑνὶ αὐτῷ χιτακίξω[?], εἰ οὐ δύ τὸ τοῦτο; ἀν-τῶν τὴν Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίαν τῶν ἐκ πολλῶν χρό-
units.tr: For from all these things he makes it plain that what has been brought from the East is pure lies and fictitious matter, and that nothing sound comes from it. And by quite certain arguments he conjectures the mind of the most holy Pope John: that he would in no way rest upon those things which were done to the ruin and dissolution of the Church, but would above all look to the canon itself and to the nature of right conduct; whatever agrees with that has strength and is received by all, but whatever departs from it is regarded as obsolete and void; and what belongs to the Church is restored, and she recovers what is her own. But all the things that have been brought forward against this canon are considered huge trifles and empty talk. Who but a follower of Photius would maintain that the Pontiff of Pontiffs condemns the acts of the Pontiffs, makes a mockery of them, and at the same moment suppresses his own authority? So Zacharias. But what does the Synod say? [Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἐξεβόησεν.] The holy Synod cried out. We, to our most holy Lord and Ecumenical Patriarch, who have been united with him from the very beginning and have never been separated from him, and who were ready to shed our blood gladly for him, have been ready to ask these things; but as many as in any way have carried on enmity against him, condemning our first sentence and purpose against the same man, we now with the whole heart and a firm mind acknowledge as the High Priest, Lord and Pastor, and those who doubt these things we consider, as enemies of the Church, cast out from it. And do they ask for anything clearer? Not yet having read the letters of John, neither released from excommunication, nor received into communion, nor restored to their churches, they pronounce a sentence and acknowledge Photius restored; they, who are united with the Roman Church, do not give their assent to it, nor do they praise what was done. I call upon Zacharias again. [The Greek of this passage is largely illegible; the sense is that the speaker asks whether those who have remained behind from the violent error should not be seated among the others, and whether the faith is to be confined to one, and whether this is not so; and that the Roman Church, from many times...]

units.la: [The Greek in this paragraph is only partly legible on the scan; words marked [?] are uncertain.] ὧν ἀλλ' ἀθείας παμμυλῶν, ἀξίωμα ἢ κρᾶτος βιβλιοθηκῶν[?], ὑπὸ θεατῶν[?] ἐκ τῆς ἀρχιερατικῆς καταδύσεως[?]. Πῶς καὶ τίνα τρόπον[?]; τὰ τῆ Πάπα Νικολάου φασὶ δέχεσθαι, καὶ τὰ τῆ Ἀδριανῷ ὁμοίως ἀρέσκει[?]. τὰ δὲ τῶν ἀγωνιστῶν, ὁ μακαριωτάτου Πάπα Ἰωάννου οὐ δέχεσθαι[?]. τίνων χάριν; ὅτι ἐκεῖνοι μὲν τῇ ἡμετέρᾳ καταπολουθῶν θελήματι[?], οὗτος δὲ ἐχ' ἃ βουλόμεθα[?] ἔστιν, ἀλλ' ἄπερ ἐκεῖνος βούλεται, τούτοις καὶ ἡμᾶς καταπολουθῶν δύναμαι[?].
units.tr: [The Greek in this paragraph is only partly legible on the scan; the sense is that the Roman Church, with its dignity and authority, is said to be bound by the acts of certain men, and that the acts of Nicholas are said to be accepted, and those of Adrian are likewise pleasing, but the acts of the most blessed Pope John are not accepted. For what reason? Because those men followed our will, whereas he does not do what we wish, but follows what he wishes, and compels us to follow him in those things.]

units.la: Τὸ δὲ ἦν ὅτι ἄλλο, ἢ ὡς αὐτοὶ μὲν οὐχὶ τοῖς ἀρχιερατικοῖς τῆς Ῥωμαίων διλήμασιν ἔπονται, ἀλλὰ σὺν μεγάλοις ἐκείνοις, καὶ θαυμασίοις ἀρχιερεῖς τοῖς ἰδίοις διλήμασιν ἀξιακολουθῶν αἰσχύνουσι[?];
units.tr: [The Greek of this paragraph is largely illegible on the scan; the sense is that they themselves do not follow the sacerdotal decrees of the Romans, but with those great and wondrous high priests they follow their own decrees, and so bring shame upon them.]

units.la: Iure ergo reiiciuntur, qui schismatis errore complicantur.
units.tr: Therefore those rightly are rejected who are entangled in the error of schism.

units.la: Nam cum aliis causis, quarum ipsi auctores sunt, hoc quoque contra opinionem omnium afferunt, quod dum mente concipio, indignor. Quod vero illud est? In ipsam Romanam Ecclesiam, quae multis ab hinc annis libertatis honore fruitur, & dignitatis auctoritatisque fama praclarissimam audent in servitutem adigere, & ad mancipiorum conditionem deicere. Quomodo, & qua ratione? Nicolai Papae, inquiunt, acta recipimus, & Adriani quoque facta complacent, sanctissimi vero, & beatissimi Papae Ioannis nullo modo recipimus. Quam ob causam? quod illi quidem nostrae voluntati morem gerebant, hi vero non quae nobis prolubentia sunt approbant, sed quae sibi complacita sunt, illa sequenda a nobis esse decernit. Hoc quid aliud est, quam hos ipsos Praesulum Romanorum voluntatem minime sequi, sed magnos illos & admirandos Praesules suis voluntatibus obedire cogere? Vides hic fraudes[?] Romanus Pontifex non a Christo, nec ab ipsis Ecclesiae incunabulis, sed abhinc multis annis, auctoritate summa potitur. Nicolaus, & Adrianus venales Ignatij facti, sententiam contra Photium tulerunt. Quis similia excogitauit? Quis unquam ex fautoribus Ignatij Romanum Pontificem audire recusauit? Quis illius sententiam respuere ausus est? Condemnationi Photij plaudunt, restitutionem detestantur, non ob causam, quam hic e cerebro confictam Zacharias adducit. Sed quia iustum iniusto praeponunt, iuste enim depositus, iniuste restituitur; nisi ex praescripto Romani Pontificis in Synodo restituatur. Nicolai itaque, & Adriani acta, quia iustissima fuerunt, ex animo adamant, Ioannis eo modo quo erant concenturiata a Photianis, quia fictitia reputant, quaerantur[?], non vero quia illa voluntati suae morem gerebant, haec vero prolubentia non erant. Ideoque respuunt corrupta a Photio, & Ioannis nomine publice divulgata. Caeci ipsi Photianorum verborum ambages agnoscerent . Hinc concluditur Synodum hanc Photianorum commentum fuisse.
units.tr: For together with other arguments, whose authors they themselves are, they also bring forward this, against the opinion of all, which indignation stirs in me as I conceive it in my mind. And what is it? They dare to reduce to servitude the Roman Church itself, which for many years has enjoyed the honour of liberty, and to cast her down to the condition of slaves, though she is most distinguished by the fame of dignity and authority. In what way, and by what reasoning? "We accept the acts of Pope Nicholas," they say, "and the deeds of Adrian also please us, but the acts of the most holy and blessed Pope John we in no way accept." For what reason? Because those men indeed obeyed our will, whereas he does not approve what is pleasing to us, but decrees that what is pleasing to himself must be followed by us. What else is this than that they do not at all follow the will of the Roman Prelates, but compel those great and admirable Prelates to obey their own wills? Here you see the frauds: the Roman Pontiff holds supreme authority not from Christ, nor from the very cradle of the Church, but for many years past. Nicholas and Adrian, made venal by the partisans of Ignatius, pronounced sentence against Photius. Who has devised similar things? Who ever among the supporters of Ignatius refused to hear the Roman Pontiff? Who has dared to reject his sentence? They applaud the condemnation of Photius and detest his restoration, not for the reason which Zacharias brings forward here, invented in his own head, but because they prefer the unjust to the just: for he was justly deposed, and is unjustly restored, unless he is restored in a Synod by the prescription of the Roman Pontiff. So the acts of Nicholas and Adrian, since they were most just, they embrace with all their heart; the acts of John, in the form in which they were put together by the Photians, they regard as fabricated and seek to have them examined, not because they did not obey their will, and these were not pleasing. And so they reject what was corrupted by Photius and published abroad under the name of John. Blind as they are, the Photians would recognise the windings of their own words. From this it is concluded that this Synod was an invention of the Photians.

units.la: Clariora producantur. Non in ista Actione tantum, sed etiam in alijs, & potissimum quarta similia ad nauseam vsque inculcantur. Basilius Metropolita Martyropolitanus. Ὁ ἀγιώτατος μὲ Πατριάρχης Θεοδόσιος οὐδ᾽ ἵπποτε, μὴ γλυκύς, ἐπὶ δ᾽ αὐτῷ, ἐπὶ δ᾽ ἐπέρου εἰς τὸ ἀνέκαθεν ὑπὲρ τὸ ἀγιωτάτου [?], καὶ Οἰκουμενικῆς Πατριάρχου Φωτίου, κατ᾽ ἰδίαν τέχνην ἱκοινώνησεν, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀρχῆς, καὶ αὐτῷ ὁ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν εἰς τὴν ἀρχιερωσύνης δέσις αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, καὶ ἐν τῇ τῆς κλήσεως καταλελυμένῳ ζῆξί, ὕστερον τῆς τῆς Ἀντιοχείας Θεῶν διάκων ἐπὶ ἀληθινῶς ἀρχιερέως Θεοῦ, καὶ συλλαβοῦσαν καὶ ἐκ καὶ ὀνομάζει, καὶ ἕως μὴ ἅπως ἐχόντως ἐποτρέπει. Et infra: ἡ ὁ ἀγιώτατος ἢ Ἠλίας, ὁ αὐτὸς τῆς Ἱεροσολύμων ἀρχιερεύς καθῶς καὶ πάντα ἐπὶ ὠδῶν Θεοδοσίῳ τῷ περιφήμῳ Καμψῶ τῷ αὐτῷ Θεῷ ἱνῷ, ἐδίδοτε ὡς τὰς καὶ τὸ ἀγιωτάτου Πατριάρχου πυρινίας ἐλαμῶς ἐκοινώνησεν. ἀλλὰ ἐ ὅτι γνώρισε Ἀ πολεισιαρίους τῆς Σαρακηνῶν, καὶ πλαοσαυδῶς ὑπὲ τὸ φέσωπον χαυδὼν τοῦ αὐτῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβύτερος. Sanctissimus meus Patriarcha Theodosius nunquam, abfit hoc, neque per se ipsum, neque per alium huic impie actioni aduersus sanctissimum, & Oecumenicum Patriarcham Photium patrata assensum dedit, sed a principio, & ab antiquo tempore, ex quo ad praesulatus terminos peruenit,
units.tr: Let clearer passages be brought forward. Not only in this Action, but also in the others, and especially the fourth, such things are dinned into us to the point of nausea. Basil, Metropolitan of Martyropolis: "The most holy Patriarch Theodosius did not in any way, not sweetly, for himself or for another, from the beginning, communicate with the most holy and Oecumenical Patriarch Photius in his own art [Ὁ ἀγιώτατος μὲ Πατριάρχης Θεοδόσιος οὐδ᾽ ἵπποτε, μὴ γλυκύς, ἐπὶ δ᾽ αὐτῷ, ἐπὶ δ᾽ ἐπέρου εἰς τὸ ἀνέκαθεν ὑπὲρ τὸ ἀγιωτάτου [?], καὶ Οἰκουμενικῆς Πατριάρχου Φωτίου, κατ᾽ ἰδίαν τέχνην ἱκοινώνησεν]." And further on: "And the most holy Elias, who is now the high priest of Jerusalem, following in all the footsteps of his predecessor Theodosius, has never communicated with the most holy Patriarch in his insolence [ἡ ὁ ἀγιώτατος ἢ Ἠλίας, ὁ αὐτὸς τῆς Ἱεροσολύμων ἀρχιερεύς καθῶς καὶ πάντα ἐπὶ ὠδῶν Θεοδοσίῳ τῷ περιφήμῳ Καμψῶ τῷ αὐτῷ Θεῷ ἱνῷ]." The Latin reads: "My most holy Patriarch Theodosius never, God forbid, neither in person nor through another, gave his assent to this impious action carried out against the most holy and Oecumenical Patriarch Photius, but from the beginning and from ancient times, from when he came to the bounds of his office,

units.la: [?] Greek passage above is only partly legible in the scan; words marked [?] are uncertain. etiam cum in clericorum ordine erat, & postea cum Antiochia diuina gubernacula suscepit, Dei Pontificem, & comministrum habet, & nuncupat, & ijs, qui non ita tenent, aduersatur. Et infra: Et sanctissimus quoque Elias, qui nunc Hierosolymorum praesul constitutus est, in omnibus Theodosij praecessoris sui vestigijs insistens, nunquam aduersus sanctissimum Patriarcham petulantijs communicauit, sed eos etiam, qui Saracenorum Apocrisiarij, & illius personam mentiti fuerant, anathemate ferijt. Et Actione quinta: Οἱ τοποτηρηταὶ τῆς ἀποστολικῆς [?] θρόνων εἶπον. τῷ δὲ ἡ ἁγία [?] τῆς Ἱεροσολύμων Ἐκκλησία, ἥπερ τῆς [?] Ἀντιοχέων, καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων [?] ἀδιάπτωτον ἀπέβαλεν, [?] μὴ [?] ἴχνη αὐτῶν [?] τέκνον. [?] τὸν ἁγιώτατον Φώτιον [?] ἐνομολογούμενον, καὶ [?] Πατριάρχην Κωνσταντινουπόλεως [?]. Locumtenentes Orientalium Sedium dixerunt: Nanque sancta Hierosolymitana Ecclesia, nec non Antiochena, & Alexandrina nunquam reiecit, aut infitiata est sese reputare sanctissimum Photium quammaxime legitimum, & secundum Canonum statuta electum Patriarcham Constantinopolitanum, ex quo in sanctam hanc sedem proiectus est: sed eos quoque, qui sibi mendaciter Apocrisiariorum nomen vsurpauerant, & aduersus hunc sanctum virum iniqua peregere, eos ha sanctissimae sedes reiectos anathemate tradiderunt. Similia continet Epistola Theodosij Patriarchae lecta Act. 4. Et ne dicas, effata ista esse singularia, & paucorum Episcoporum assumenta, qui separati ab vnione Romanae Ecclesiae talia obloquuntur, sed Synodum vniuersam Ioanni Pontifici vnitam alia sensisse, suam ipsa Synodus sententiam profert at. Actione 4. [?]Ἡ μὲν ἡμᾶς καὶ σὲ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ταύτης[?] Patriarchae nempe Hierosolymitani, [?]ἀ μόνου δὲ ταύτης, ἀλλὰ καὶ σὲ τῆς ἐλθούσης δι᾽ Ἀνδρέου[?], ἧς ἐμαρτύρησεν[?] πᾶσαν ἐχομένην πληροφορίαν[?], ὅτι ἐδίκαιον διέσπα[?] οἱ ἀποστολικοὶ[?] ἐγνώσθη[?] Παζιαρχου[?], ἀλλ᾽ ἀεὶ καὶ συναρχικὰ[?], καὶ συλλήπτορον ἄχθος[?], καὶ ἀνικήτου[?]. Nos etiam non ante hanc Epistolam solum, sed ante eam quoq; quae per Andream missa est, & paulo ante lecta, satis certi sumus, nunquam Orientales Sedes a sanctissimo nostro Patriarcha sese separasse, sed continuo & coepiscopum, & comministrum habuisse, & praedicasse. Concludamus ergo hanc Synodum etiamsi vere coacta fuisset, nullam vim in Ecclesia obtinere, sed modis omnibus ex aliorum numero reijciendam, expungendamque fuisse.
units.tr: even when he was in the order of the clergy, and afterwards when he took up the divine government of Antioch, he has held and called him the Pontiff and fellow-minister of God, and he opposes those who do not hold him thus. And further on: And the most holy Elias also, who has now been set over Jerusalem, following in all the footsteps of his predecessor Theodosius, has never communicated in the wantonness of his acts against the most holy Patriarch, but has even struck with anathema those who falsely claimed to be the envoys of the Saracens and to speak in his person. And in the fifth Action: The locum tenentes of the apostolic thrones said: "The holy Church of Jerusalem, and likewise Antioch and Alexandria, never cast off or denied, [Ἡ μὲν ἡμᾶς καὶ σὲ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ταύτης] ... [ἀλλὰ ἀεὶ καὶ συναρχικὰ, καὶ συλλήπτορον ἄχθος, καὶ ἀνικήτου]." The Locum tenentes of the Eastern Sees said: For the holy Church of Jerusalem, as well as that of Antioch and Alexandria, has never rejected or denied that the most holy Photius is to be regarded as the most lawful Patriarch of Constantinople, elected according to the canons, since he was raised to this holy see; but they have also handed over to anathema, by this holy see, those who falsely usurped the name of envoys and worked iniquities against this holy man. A similar statement is found in the Epistle of Patriarch Theodosius, read in the fourth Action. And lest you say that these sayings are singular, and the assertions of a few bishops who, separated from the union of the Roman Church, speak thus, the Synod itself puts forward its own judgment in the fourth Action: [Greek, illegible in the scan]. We are certain, not only from this Epistle but also from the one sent through Andrew and read a little before, that the Eastern Sees never separated themselves from our most holy Patriarch, but always had him as fellow-bishop and fellow-minister, and proclaimed him so. Let us conclude, then, that this Synod, even if it had truly been convened, has no force in the Church, but must in every way be struck from the number of the others and expunged.

units.la: Argumentum efficacissimum fuerit. Synodus e Patriarchis, & Episcopis Schismaticis, improbis, rebellibus, percontumacibus, ideoque condemnatis & excommunicatis a Concilio legitimo, & vniuersali coacta, & celebrata Synodus legitima non est, sed Cociliabulum, & nequissimorum hominum congregatio, nec vllum in Ecclesia pondus, vel momentum habet, nec robur. Sed Synodus illa Photiana, Octava dicta, coacta fuit, & celebrata a Schismaticis, rebellibus, condemnatis, & excommunicatis a pluribus Synodis, & quod peius est in schismate, & excommunicatione persistentibus. Ergo Synodus illa neque valida est, neque legitima, sed nequissimorum hominum adumbratum commentum. Maior etiam Græcorum Schismaticorum est. Qua enim ratione, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, & ab eadem reiecti, & veluti membra noxia excommunicatione etiam signati de rebus Ecclesiasticis decernent? Quæ extra nos sunt, nihil ad nos. Minor dictis eiusdemmet Synodi probatur, ex qua satis aperte elicitur, non Patriarchas solum, sed Episcopos omnes in ea congregatos, etiam post condemnationem Photij, & excommunicationem a pluribus Synodis latam, Photij continuo vnionem, quidquid Rom. Pontifices aliiq; Episcopos, Epi-scoscopi Ecclesiæ proclamarent, amplexatos fuisse, illique adhæsisse etiam ante literas Pontificias Ioannis, quibus illius pœnitentia admittebatur, & qua peracta vnio cum Ecclesia, & ante vllũ aliud Synodale decretum. Sed qui ita se gerunt schismatici sunt, excommunicati sunt, extra Ecclesiam sunt. Ergo Synodus ista a Schismaticis, & excommunicatis celebrata nulla est.
units.tr: The following argument will be most effective. A synod gathered and celebrated by patriarchs and bishops who are schismatics, wicked, rebellious, obstinate, and therefore condemned and excommunicated by a lawful and universal council, is not a lawful synod but a conventicle and a gathering of most wicked men; it has no weight, no moment and no strength in the Church. But that Photian synod, called the Eighth, was gathered and celebrated by schismatics, rebels, men condemned and excommunicated by several synods, and, what is worse, men who persisted in schism and excommunication. Therefore that synod is neither valid nor lawful, but the shadowy invention of the most wicked men. The premise also holds for the Greek schismatics. For by what reasoning can those who are outside the Church, and cast out by it, and marked by excommunication like harmful members, decide ecclesiastical matters? What is outside us is nothing to us. The minor premise is proved from the words of the same synod, from which it is clear enough that not only the patriarchs but all the bishops gathered in it, even after Photius's condemnation and the excommunication pronounced by several synods, continually embraced union with Photius, whatever the Roman Pontiffs and other bishops, the bishops of the Church, might proclaim, and clung to him even before the letters of Pope John by which his repentance was admitted, and by which union with the Church was effected, and before any other synodal decree. But those who conduct themselves in this way are schismatics, are excommunicated, are outside the Church. Therefore this synod, celebrated by schismatics and excommunicated men, is null.

units.la: Probentur singula. Qui schismati cum Photio adhæserunt, a summis Pontificibus Nicolao, & Adriano in Synodis Romanis, & Octaua Generali vna cum ipso Photio condemnantur, & excommunicantur. Sed qui Synodo huic interfuere, partes Photij semper tutati sunt, & illi affixi, & vt ita dicam adcorporati ad extremum perdurarunt, nec ab vllo Pontifice absoluti Ecclesiæ vnquam reconciliati sunt, sed αὐτόνομοι Iudices facti, nulla eminentioris potestatis facultate sibi facta sententiam pronunciarunt: imo sese Romano Pontifici præponunt, tanquam qui viciniores, & a rebus actis minus absentes, ipso Pontifice vsu, & experientia promptiores cognitiones habuerunt. Procopius Archiepiscopus Cæsariensis Act. 2. Ἡ μὲν πολλάκις ἀπομνήμονας ... τῆς ἡμετέρας ... ὡς ... ἡμῶν ... Ἰωάννου ... τὸν Οἰκου-[?] [illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: Let each point be proved. Those who adhered to schism with Photius were condemned and excommunicated, together with Photius himself, by the supreme Pontiffs Nicholas and Hadrian in Roman synods and by the Eighth General Council. But those who took part in this synod have always upheld Photius's side, have clung to him and, as I may say, have grown into him, and have persisted to the end; none of them was absolved by any Pontiff, none was ever reconciled to the Church, but they made themselves autonomous judges and pronounced sentence without any authority of a higher power. Indeed they set themselves above the Roman Pontiff, as men who were nearer and less absent from the events, and who had more ready knowledge from the Pontiff's own use and experience. Procopius, Archbishop of Caesarea, Act. 2: [the Greek text is illegible in the scan here; the sense is that Photius has been acknowledged as Patriarch and as our high priest and shepherd, and that he has been embraced as a loving shepherd and master].

units.la: μυικὸν Παξιάρχῳ τὸν κύειν Φώτιον κεκτήμεθα [?] καὶ τὸ ὀφείλομεν [?] θελαβεῖν [?]. Οἱ δὲ εἰρίζοντες τῆς σεαυτῆς [?] τὰς πορβωτίας μᾶλλον αὐτῶν τῷ ἀκρι-βείας [?] ὅτισαν [?].
units.tr: [Greek text, largely illegible in the scan.] We possess Photius as Oecumenical Patriarch and owe him... but those who wish to be more accurate than the others in their knowledge... [illegible].

units.la: Καὶ ἐν αἱ χεῖρες ἐψηλάφησαν, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἑωράκασι τὴν ἐξ ἀκοῆς τὸ γνῶσιν ἀπολαμβανόντων, ἐξ ἧς τῆς ἀληθείας καθάπερ ἀπομάχῳ ὡς εἰρίζοντες ἀκριβέστεροι μᾶλλον καὶ κελευταί, καὶ ἐξίσασαι, καὶ ἐγκρατεῖ. Δὸ ἡμῖν παῖδα εἰσελθόντας, καὶ ἀμαθέστερος κεκεῖκαμεν, ἐν ἑλὶ ἄλλῳ τῷ σωτηρίαν ἡμῶν εἶναι, καὶ τὸ Χάρισον τῆς Θεοῦ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ ἐνωθέντων Φωτίῳ τῆς ἀνωτάτῳ Παξιαρχῇ. [illegible, ~6 letters]
units.tr: [Greek text, largely illegible in the scan.] Our hands have touched and our eyes have seen, and we who receive knowledge by hearing, from which the truth is more accurately judged as by a wiser and more experienced judge... We came to these things and have been more ignorant. Our salvation is in no other, nor is the grace of God, but in the union with Photius, the most holy Patriarch.

units.la: Nos saepius de nostro proposito locuti sumus, nos absque ulla haesitatione sanctissimum nostrum Dominum, Dominum Photium Oecumenicum Patriarcham reputasse. Nanqi rem praeripere debebamus. Qui enim rebus propinquiores sunt, illis qui longius absunt, melius rerum exquisitam notitiam tenent: & quorum manus contrectarunt, & oculi viderunt, illis qui auditu cognitionem acceperunt, integrius sunt iudices, & examinatores, & inquisitores. Quapropter nos omnibus sedulo conquisitis, & cognitis iudicavimus in nullo alio nostram salutem consistere, & Deo placere, quam in unione Photij sanctissimi Patriarchae. Nisi oculatus percurrerem, non crederem. Suum Pontificio iudicio praeferunt, quod integrius esse volunt, quasi Romani Pontifices turbulento, & nullo praevio examine sententiam dixissent. Ante Romanum ergà[?] excommunicatum a Synodo, & ipsis Romanis Pontificibus sententiam proferunt absolutionis: excommunicatum eiectumque a Synodo plena nulla in re hæsitantes, in osculum amplectuntur; & salutem suam, & Dei placitum in depositi excommunicatique communione ponunt. Et atrociora investigamus? Et ridiculum plane est, profiteri fautores Photij, se ipsos uti viciniores, & rebus præsentes, melius res tenuisse. Romani nanque Pontifices Nicolaus, & Adrianus non inconsulto, ac temere, sed re antea diligentius pervestigata, testium, qui rebus interfuerunt, accurato examine, tum præmissis ad Photium monitionibus, ut iniuste occupata restitueret, & eo obnitente, & restitutionem differente sententiam dixerunt. Et licet de Synodis Romanis in Photium idquoq; concederetur, quid ipsi dicerent de Synodo Generali Constantinopoli adversus ipsum Photium coacta? Eam etiam incompertas habuisse iuxta cum Romanis fraudes, & conatus Photij? Vides quam leviter Photiani isti in rebus serijs nugantur? Planum itaque est ante Epistolam Ioannis eosdem unitos fuisse Photio: nanque post lectam Ioannis Papæ ad Imperatores Epistolam idem Procopius subnectit eadem Actio-
units.tr: We have often spoken of our purpose: we, without any hesitation, have regarded our most holy Lord, Lord Photius, as Oecumenical Patriarch. For we ought to have anticipated the matter. Those who are nearer to affairs hold a better and more exact knowledge of them than those who are further away; and those whose hands have handled and whose eyes have seen are more complete judges, examiners and inquirers than those who have received knowledge by hearing. Therefore, having diligently sought out and examined everything, we have judged that our salvation and God's pleasure consist in no other thing than in union with Photius, the most holy Patriarch. Unless I had gone through it with my own eyes, I would not believe it. They prefer their own judgment to the Pontifical one, because they wish it to be more complete, as if the Roman Pontiffs had pronounced sentence in a confused manner and without any prior examination. Before the Roman Pontiff, they pronounce sentence of absolution on a man excommunicated by a synod: they embrace with a kiss, without hesitation in any point, one who was deposed and excommunicated and cast out by a synod, and they place their salvation and God's pleasure in communion with the deposed and excommunicated. And do we investigate more atrocious things? It is plainly ridiculous for the supporters of Photius to profess that they themselves, being nearer and present to the matter, have grasped it better. For the Roman Pontiffs Nicholas and Hadrian did not speak rashly or carelessly, but after the matter had been investigated more carefully beforehand, after a precise examination of the witnesses who had been present at the events, and after admonitions had first been sent to Photius that he should restore what he had unjustly seized; and when he resisted and delayed restitution, they pronounced sentence. And even if it were granted about the Roman synods against Photius, what would they say about the General Synod gathered at Constantinople against Photius himself? Did they also not know the frauds and attempts of Photius, just as the Romans did? Do you see how lightly these Photians trifle in serious matters? It is therefore plain that before the letter of John these same men were united with Photius; for after the letter of Pope John to the Emperors was read, the same Procopius adds the same Action...

units.la: Ἡμᾶς ὡς πολλάκις ἀπέμψε, καὶ ὡς τῆς ἡμετέρας ἡμίας ἐλλύσεως, ὁ ὡς τῆς εἰρηνικῆς πρὸ ἡμῶν γεράμεν παραγνώσεως Φώτιον τὸν ἁγιώτα-τον Πατριάρχην ἀρχιερέα ἡμῶν, καὶ ποιμένα καὶ ἀποδεξάμενα, καὶ ὑποδηλώσας, καὶ ὡς οἰκείῳ ποιμένι, ὡς δεσπότῃ ἐνολλίνθ[?]μενον, καὶ ἀσπασάμενα. Nos vt sapenumero diximus, & ante venerandum vestrum aduentum, (loquitur cum Legatis Pontificijs) & in honorandis vestris literis contentam adhortationem sanctissimum Photium Patriarcham nostrum Praesulem, & Pastorem agnoscimus, & agnoscimus: & vti proprio Pastori, & Domino conglutinati, eum amplexati sumus. Et Actione prima post lectam eiusdem Ioannis Epistolam Synodus vniuersa exclamauit.
units.tr: Our (speaking with the Papal legates) "We, as we have often said, and before your venerable arrival, and in accepting your letters with the exhortation they contain, acknowledge and recognise the most holy Photius, our Patriarch, as our Prelate and Pastor; and, as to our own Pastor and Lord, joined to him, we have embraced him." And at the first Action, after the letter of John was read, the whole Synod cried out.

units.la: Ἡμᾶς ἐχ ἁπάξ, ὡς δὲ[?]ς, ἀλλὰ πολλάκις ἐφημῶν, ὡς καὶ ὡς τῆς ἡμω-τάτης ἐπιστολῆς ταύτης καὶ λυώσηθμῳ, καὶ ἀποδεξάμενα Φώτιον τὸν ἁγιώτατον ἡμῶν Πατριάρχην, ὁ ἀγώεισοι ἀπὸ διεπλοῦμεν πάσας ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς ἡμῶν. καὶ γὰρ μὴ ἀποδηλωμένως τῶν ἀρχιεραι-καῖ ἀπ' ἀξίας, καὶ κανονικῶ, καὶ ἐνδίσμον, ὡς ἄλλο εἶδος τῆς εὐσεβείας, καὶ τῆς κανονικῶν διατάξεων καὶ ἡγουμένων, καὶ λογιζόμενα, Nos non vna, aut altera vice, sed saepissime diximus, & ante maxime venerandam hanc Epistolam, vniti Photio accepimus Photium sanctissimum nostrum Patriarcham, & inseparabiles ab ipso viuebamus omnibus diebus vitae nostrae. & eos, qui qui Sacerdotium illius uti legitimum, & canonicum non accipiebant, tanquam a pietate, & a canonum constitutionibus alienos & reputamus, & existimamus. Est ne hoc secundum Canonum constitutiones excommunicatum, & reiectum a legitime coacta Synodo Generali, & a Romanis Pontificibus comprobatis Conciliis, antequam absoluatur ab æquali Synodo, & ab ipsis summis Pontificibus in communionem, tanquam neque reiectum, neque excommunicatum excipere, & eiusdem dignitatis, e qua deiectus[?] fuerat, uti legitimum possessorem recognoscere? Qui ita rem tractant suspecti sunt, Schismatici sunt, excommunicati sunt, reiiciendi sunt. factis dictisque illorum nulla fides adhibenda est. Et nos similem Synodum veluti canonicam admitteremus, & illius auctoritate res Ecclesiasticas firmabimus? Nolo ipse horum quoque adiuvare insaniam.
units.tr: "We have said this not once or twice but very often, and before this most venerable letter, we accepted Photius, our most holy Patriarch, as united with us, and we lived inseparable from him all the days of our life. Those who did not accept his priesthood as lawful and canonical, we regard and consider as estranged from piety and from the constitutions of the canons." Is it in accordance with the constitutions of the canons that a man excommunicated and rejected by a lawfully convened General Synod, and by councils approved by the Roman Pontiffs, should be received into communion, before he is absolved by an equal synod and by the supreme Pontiffs themselves, as though he were neither rejected nor excommunicated, and should be recognised as the lawful possessor of the same dignity from which he was deposed? Those who handle the matter in this way are suspect, they are schismatics, they are excommunicated, they must be rejected; no faith is to be given to their deeds and words. Would we admit a similar synod as though it were canonical, and confirm Church affairs by its authority? I do not wish to lend my aid to their madness either.

units.la: Hoc plane nec ipsis Pontificiis Legatis licet mente, & animo corruptis placuit, & cum alia multa Photianis concessissent, id nihilominus tolerare passi non sunt, quare eadem Actione cum Photiani gloriarentur de Photio a se restituto, non potuere se continere, quin dicerent; Ὁ ἁγιώτατος[?], ὁ Οἰκουμενικὸς Πάπας Ἰωάννης ἐγνῷ ὑμᾶς[?] · ὧν αἰνῆλἀΐηλθε ὁ νῦν Φώτιος ὁ ἀμώμητος[?], Πατριάρ- χης νυῦ εἰς τὸν Θρόνον ἀνῆλθε[?]. Λέγομεν δὲ ὃν ἂν ἐν ᾧ καλὸν ἐστι τῆς ἐλλείψεως[?] ἡμῖν ἀχθῆναι αὐτόν[?].
units.tr: This plainly did not please even the Papal legates, minds and hearts corrupted as they were. Although they had conceded many other points to the Photians, they could not bear this. So when the Photians gloried in the same Action about Photius restored by them, the legates could not restrain themselves from saying: "The most holy Ecumenical Pope John knows you: the now blameless Photius ascended to the throne in such a way that..." and "We say that he should be brought to us in the proper time for correction."

units.la: Sanctissimus, ut Oecumenicus Papa Ioannes interrogat vos, qua ratione Dominus Photius Patriarcha sanctissimus ascendit in sedem suam? Dicimus enim non rectum fuisse ante nostrum adventum enim ascendere. Et cum respondisset Hierosolymitani Vicarius; Τὰ ἑῖα τῆς αἰαυολὰς Παϊριαρχία ἀλλὰ Πατριάρχῳ αὐτὸν ἔχον[?]. Οἱ δὲ Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἀρχιερεῖς, ἐ ἱερεῖς μὲν πάντες Πατριάρχων αὐτὸν ἔχουσι[?]. καὶ τί ἐκώλυε τὴν αἵρεσιν αὐτὸν[?]. Tres Orientis Patriarchatus semper illum Patriarcham reputarunt. Constantinopolitani Praefules, & Sacerdotes fere omnes Patriarcham ipsum tenent. Et quid impedimento erat, ne ille ascenderet? Cum similis responsio non satisfecisset, iterum repetunt Pontifices; Εἶπατε ἡμῖν, τῶν ἀνῆλθε[?]; Dicite nobis, qua ratione ascendit? Et Synodus respondet; Συμφωνία τῆς ζῶν ἀρχιερατικῶν θεόν[?], καθάπερ ὁ ἀμώμητος[?] Ἠλίας ἔφη. ἐπεὶ δὲ πολλῆς[?] ἐν πολλοῖς[?], μᾶλλον ἢ τάλις εἰπεῖν[?], βίᾳ μεγάλῃ τῆς ὑπάλων[?], καὶ χρισιν- ωπάτων Βασιλέων ἡμῶν[?], καὶ ὡς ἐπὶ τῆς βίας συμφωνία[?], καὶ ἱκεσίας πάσης τῆς τῷ Θεῷ Κωνσταντινουπόλεως Ἐκκλησίας. Consensu trium Patriarchalium Sedium, uti sanctissimus Elias dixit. Postmodum adhortatione multa, & supplicatione, & ut verius dicamus, ut ingenti sublimium, & Christianissimorum nostrorum Imperatorum, & ante vim illatam, consensu precibusque universæ Dei Constantinopolitanæ Ecclesiæ. His acquiescunt Romani, sic turbante ac convoluente omnia Photio. Est tamen id contra Constitutiones, & canones Ecclesiasticos, quod alibi fusius probavimus. Ante siquidem omnia assensus Romani requirebatur, & pœnitentia prævia. Sed nolo cum aliis contendere. Calculum Photius det, non longe sed ab hac eadem Actione petitum. Peccavit in Potium Thomas Berytensis Photium respuens, postmodum pœnitentia ductus, si hoc quoque mendacium[?] Photij non est, delictum confitetur, & in communionem petit admitti. Sed esto, erraverit ille, & pœnitentiam egerit, ut hoc Photio concedam. Nanque in Epistola Michaëlis Alexandrini legitur; Ο᾿ ἀ[?]έπεμψω αὐτὸν Θωμᾶς ὁ Βηρυταῖος ἐπίγνω τὸ πλάσμα Ἰωάννου, ἐ αἰτίαν [illegible, ~12 letters] συγγνώμης. Alius vero ipsorum Thomas Berytensis agnovit errorem suum, & cum postulasset veniam, illam a nobis impetravit: Et Abramius Amedorum, & Samosatorum Metropolita Epistolam ad Photium de eodem Thoma, Περὶ μὲν οὖν Θωμᾶ τῆς Τύρου, καὶ Ἡλίας, καὶ Ἰωάννη τῷ ἀπεσταλμένῳ[?] τῷ αὐτὸν, ἐν ᾧ ἐκ λῷ βαδιζῷ[?]. Πάλιν ὁ Θεὸς αὐτ-ἀπέδωκε αὐτῷ καθὼς λῷ ἄξιῳ[?], & πρὸ συμμε-τέχῳ αὐτῷ Ἡλίᾳ. Ὁ δὲ τῆς Τύρου ἀφείδεω[?] ἐξη-γρέσθαι αὐτῷ τὸ πλῆσμα ἐνώπιον τῆς Πατριαρχῶν[?] Θεῖς τῆς αὐτοῦ ἀναβάσως τε καὶ ἀφέξεως[?]. Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς αὐτῷ ὅτι κείτης[?]. Αὐτὸς ἐκλιπαρεῖ, & αἰτῶν συγχώρησιν.
units.tr: "Most holy, as the Ecumenical Pope John asks you: by what means did the Lord Photius, the most holy Patriarch, ascend to his see? For we say that it was not right for him to ascend before our arrival." And when the Vicar of Jerusalem had replied: "The ascent to the Patriarchate was not by his own right, but he held it as a Patriarch. The bishops of Constantinople, and almost all the priests, hold him as Patriarch. And what hindered his ascent?" The three Patriarchal sees of the East have always reckoned him Patriarch. The prelates and priests of Constantinople almost all hold him as Patriarch. And what was there to prevent his ascent? When a similar reply did not satisfy them, the Pontiffs again asked: "Tell us, by what means did he ascend?" And the Synod replied: "By the agreement of the three Patriarchal sees, as the most holy Elias said. Afterwards, by much exhortation and supplication, or rather, as we should more truly say, by the great force of the most high and most Christian Emperors, and by the agreement and prayers of the whole Church of God at Constantinople, and before force was applied." To these things the Romans gave their assent, since Photius was throwing everything into confusion. Yet this was contrary to the constitutions and ecclesiastical canons, as we have proved more fully elsewhere. For before all else the assent of Rome was required, and prior repentance. But I do not wish to contend with others. Let Photius supply the reckoning, a reckoning taken not far from this same Action. Thomas of Berytus sinned against Photius by rejecting him; afterwards, moved by repentance, he confesses the offence, and asks to be admitted to communion, if this too is not a lie of Photius. But granted that he erred and did penance, so that I may concede this to Photius. For in the letter of Michael of Alexandria it is read: "Thomas of Berytus, having recognised the fabrication of John, ... of pardon." And again, Abramius, Metropolitan of Amida and Samosata, in his letter to Photius about the same Thomas: "Concerning Thomas of Tyre, and Elias, and John, who was sent..., God again restored to him as he deserved, and with his partner Elias. The Bishop of Tyre, having recognised his error before the Patriarchs, ... of his ascent and descent. God ... he entreats him and asks for pardon."

units.la: Continebant autem literæ de Thoma Tyrio, & Elia, & Iosepho, qui se denominabat ex gradu, ad quem nondum erat evectus. Attamen Deus pro dignitate sceleris ei retribuit, & socio illius in crimine Eliæ. Verum Tyri Antistes errorem suum prævaricationem, & actionem coram Patriarchis confessus est. Deus vero eorum iudex est. Ipse autem rogat, atque exorat, ut sibi condonetur. Quid diutius moror? Hac eadem Actione post Epistolam Michaëlis adnectitur Thomæ Tyrij libellus, in quo se accusans ob separationem a Photio, misericordiam petit, pœnitentiam non respuens. Post lectum libellum Vicarij Papæ pronunciant de Thomæ pœnitentia referendum esse ad Papam Ioannem; Ἐπειδὴ ἢ τὸ ἁμάρτημα χαλεπὸν καὶ ἀνοσιώτατον[?] ... θεὸν ὑβρεῖν[?] ... τῷ ἀγωνιστῇ[?] & Οἰκουμενικῷ Πάπα Ἰωάννῃ[?], & τὸ ἀφεσὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ ποιεῖτω[?]. Cum vero scelus illius atrox esse intelligamus, & iniuriam Deo illatam, reponimus hoc sanctissimo & Oecumenico Papæ Ioanni, & quod illi complacitum fuerit in oculis suis faciat. Et tamen Thomas reconciliatus ab Alexandrino, & in communionem receptus ipsi Photio pluribus commendatur, vt ira demissa delictum demittat. Alter vero ipsorum Thomas Berytaeus agnovit errorem suum, & cum postulasset veniam, illam a nobis impetravit. Quid vero tum Photius? Legatorum postulatis auditis, ne minor esse videretur auctoritate Ioanne Pontifice, subdole respondit; Cum delictum commissum se tantum respiceret, auctoritate propria absolvere; quod si absolutioni assensum praeberet Ioannes, esset equidem id melius. Ὅσον τὸ ἐφ' ἡμῶν ἀδελφοί, μάλιστα [?] ὅτι καὶ οἱ τῆς [illegible, ~18 letters], ἀπολελυμένον αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς εἰς ἡμᾶς ἁμαρτίας, καὶ πλημμελήματος ἔχομεν. Εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ ἁγιώτατος Πάπας Ῥώμης Ἰωάννης ὁ πνευματικὸς ἀδελφός, καὶ συλλειτουργὸς, καὶ πατὴρ ἡμῶν ψῆφον ἐπιφέρει, μᾶλλον. Quod nostra interest Fratres, & praecipue quod Orientales throni supplicationem pro eo fecerunt, absolutum eum a delicto in nos patrato, & scelere habemus. Quod si & sanctissimus Papa Romanus Ioannes spiritualis frater, & comminister, & Pater noster calculum addiderit, melius. Plura in dicto Photij consideranda veniunt; inter ea non minimum, sed vere atrox, auctoritatem sibi Pontificiam vsurpat, & etiamsi ille renuat, nihil sibi curæ esse. Sed id relinquamus. Dicit, Si Romanus absolutioni calculum addiderit, melius. Quid hoc melius sit, non equidem intelligo. Venia, quam Photius impartitur, integrane, vel mutila, vel dimidiata est, ita ut additò calculo Romani integrior euadat? Quod persectum est, nihil ultra postulat. Absolutio data a Photio si perfecta est, frustra calculum alterius exorat; si imperfecta, ergo a quo perfectio additur postulanda est, & temere datur quæ imperfectior est. Et mirare hominis ingenium, cum Romanorum postulatis, qui ad Romanum dictam veniam deferebant, non haberet, quod opponeret, ne videretur Romano minoris efse[?] conditionis, fatetur se absoluere, verum si Romanus absolutioni assensum exhibuerit, tum melius se habere omnia. Ergo dicto Photij absolutio similis Romani auctoritatem poscebat, Tum adde, Romani dicunt, solutionem criminis pertinere ad Ioannem Papam, Photius replicat, pertinere ad se, quia delictum ipsum respiciebat. Sequere, sed delictum commissum a Photio Pontifices Romanos respiciebat. ergo Photiani sceleris solutio ad Romanos pertinebat. Qua ergo auctoritate ab Orientalibus ante Romani solutionem in communionem ipse admittitur? Photium non fuisse restitutum a Ioanne, sed sola Imperatoris auctoritate ex Epistolis Michaëlis Alexandrini, & aliorum hic assufis planū est. Dixerat supra Synodus. Ε'πεῖπα δὲ παραινέσει πολλῇ [?] ὦ ἀρχαλ[?] ..., μᾶλλον ἢ τἀληθὲς εἰπεῖν, βίᾳ μεγάλῃ τῆς ὑψηλῶν, ὦ Χριστιανικωτάτων Βασιλέων ἡμῶν, ὦ σὺν τῇ βίᾳ συμφωνίᾳ ὦ ἐκκλησίᾳ τ' Κωνσταντινουπόλεως Ἐκκλησίας. Postmodum adhortatione multa & supplicatione, & vt verius dicam, vi ingenti sublimium, & Christianissimorum nostrorum Imperatorum, & ante vim illatam, consensu, precibusque Constantinopolitanæ Ecclesiæ. Sed audiatur Photius eadem Actione narrans modum, quo in thronum post mortem Ignatij restitutus est, Πάλιν πάντων συμφωνούντων, ἡ τῆς ζωῆς ἀρχιερατικῶν θεσμῶν τὰς συνοδικὰς αὐτῶν ἡμᾶς παρακαλεσάντων [?] ψῆφος, ἐπ' ᾧ καὶ τῆς ἐμπεδώσεως γραμμάτων, ὧν ὁ ἁγιώτατος Πάπας Ἰωάννης [?] ἀγαπᾷ μὲν ὦ εἰς τὸν φιλόχρηστον, καὶ ὑψηλὸν Βασιλέα ἡμῶν τὴν πᾶσαν αἴτησιν αὐτοῦ καταδέξειν ὑπομνημάτων [?] αἰνέσεως εἰς τὸν Θεὸν τῶν [?]. Verum cum omnes concordassent, & tres Patriarchales Sedes Synodicis eorundem calculis nos provocarent: nec non antea iam positis literis a sanctissimo Papa Ioanne ad Dei amantem & sublimem Imperatorem nostrum datis, quibus se omnibus illius petitionibus annuere spondet, freti in hunc thronum ascendimus. Ergo IoIoannis literas ascensus ad sedem praeuerterat. Ergo prius euectus, quam absolutus, Vin plura? audi. Actione 4. prope finem: Βασιλεῶ ὁ Θεοφιλέστατος Μητροπολίτης Μαρτυρο-πόλεως, καὶ Ἐπισκοπῆς Ἀντιοχίας ἄπαν. Ὁ ἁγιώτατος Πάπας Μιχαὴλ Ἀλεξανδρείας ἅμα τίς σῶν ἀρχιερεῦσι Θεῷ πάλαι ἀπαν[?]τα τὰ τῆς τε ἀγιωτάτης Παξιαρχου Φωτίου πεφαρμακευμένα, καὶ ἀπεκήρυ-ξε, ἡ αὐτοῦ μάτην, καὶ οὓς ἀποξηρωμένους αὐτὰ πρὸς ὁμοίως αὐαδήμαται καὶ ὑπεβάλλειν. Ὁ μὲν ὡς καὶ ὁ ἐκ Παξιαρχης ἁγιώτατος Θεοδόσιος καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ οὗ ἀποξηρωμένους αὐτὰ, ἐξ οὗ ὀνομάζοντας αὐτῷ Σιώσθου τῷ αὐτοῦ κείμαι κατέκεινέ π, ἐ κατηδίκασε. Κοσμᾶς ὁ Θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος, ἐ Ἀποκρισιάρις Ἀλεξανδρείας ἄπε. Τὸ φαῦνημα αὐτὸ ὁ ἁγιώτατος Πάπας Ἀλεξανδρείας ἐν τοῖς π-μίοις αὐτοῦ ἡ ἐάμμαται ζαγῶς πᾶσιν αὐ ἐκηήρυξε, καὶ ὡς πάτῃ αρ' ἃ καὶ ὑπεβάλλε καὶ αὐτὰ, ἡ οὗν ἀποξηρωμένους αὐτά. Ἡ λίας ὁ Θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος, καὶ Ἐπισκοπῆς Ἰεροσολύμων ἔπε. Τοὺς μὴ ἀποξηρωμένους Φώπον Τὸν ἀγιώτατον Παξιάρχῃ ἐνομον, καὶ κεκανονισμένον ἀρχιερέα Θεῷ πρὸ αὐα-δήμαται καὶ ὑπεβάλλω, ὥσπερ πάλαι μὲν ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις Θεοδόσιος ὁ τῆς Ἱεροσολύμων ἀρχιερέως, νῦν ἢ ἐ ὁ αὐτὸ δ[?]ε[?]δ[?]οχος Ηλίας ἔπὶ σωκαταδηματίζει, καὶ ὑποβάλλε[?], ἐ πάντα τὰ κατ' αὐτὸ ἐμφαρδὸν πα-ραξιλύα, ἐν οἷς μάλιστα οἱ Σαρακηνῶν Ἀποκρισίαριοι κείται, ἐ νομοθέται ἀδύνομοι ἀφεγκαθέζοντο, Ἡ ἀγία Σιώσθ ἐξεβόησε. Παντὸς ἀπὸ δυξάζομεν, πάντες ἐπὶ κηρύπομεν, πάντες ἐν τούτοις ἀσμιζόμεθα. Ἐν τούτῳ τῷ καιρῷ τῷ ἀγιωτάτῳ Παπᾷ Γ'ωαίνε ἡμῖν ἄλλων ἀπάντων μᾶλλον ἐφαίνη. ἡμᾶς γὰρ ὡς πολλάκις ἐφιμεν, καὶ τὸ ὁμολογήσασθαι τὸν ἀγιώτατον Πάπαν Γ'ωαίνειν τῇ ἀθέσμων σκέναν ἀπαιρεῖν, πάντα τὰ ἀγιώτατα ἡμῶν Παπᾷ ἐφέντα λαλήσαντα, ἢ ἀνεδημιζόμεθα, ἢ ἀπὸ βαλόμεθα, ὡς ἑώντες ἀυτὰ ἢ κοινωνίζοντες, ἢ συλλήτους ἐνόμεθα. Καὶ νῦν ἢ πάλιν διαρμόσεσθαι τι, ἢ ἀπουδαιόμεθα ἅπαντα τὰ κατ' αὐτὰ ἢ ἀναθεματίζομεν, ἢ ὑπὸ βαλλόμεθα, ἢ οὖν ὑπὸ τὰ νῦν διεχθρύες ἀυ ἀ τῆς αὐτὰ ἐξ ἀπεμπόμεθα ἀναθεματ. [?]
units.tr: Those letters also concerned Thomas of Tyre, Elias, and Joseph, who called himself by a rank to which he had not yet been raised. Still, God repaid them according to the gravity of their wickedness, and Elias, Thomas's accomplice in the crime, received the same. The bishop of Tyre confessed his error, his transgression and his deed before the patriarchs. God, however, is their judge. He himself begs and entreats that pardon be granted to him. Why should I delay longer? After the letter of Michael, this same proceeding has appended the little book of Thomas of Berytus, in which he accuses himself of separation from Photius and asks for mercy, not rejecting repentance. After the little book was read, the vicars of the Pope pronounced that Thomas's repentance should be referred to Pope John: "Since the offence is grave and most impious ... to insult God ... to the champion and Ecumenical Pope John, and let him do what seems good in his eyes." Since we understand his crime to be atrocious and the injury done to God, we refer this matter to the most holy and Ecumenical Pope John, and let him do what pleases him. And yet Thomas, reconciled by the Alexandrian and received back into communion, was commended to Photius himself by many, so that, his anger laid aside, he might pardon the offence. The other of the two, Thomas of Berytus, acknowledged his error, and when he had asked for pardon, he obtained it from us. But what did Photius say then? When the requests of the legates had been heard, he replied craftily, so as not to seem inferior in authority to Pope John: since the offence committed concerned only himself, he would absolve him on his own authority; but if John gave his assent to the absolution, that would indeed be better. As far as we are concerned, brothers, especially since the men of ... we hold him absolved from the sin and offence committed against us. And if the most holy Pope of Rome, John, our spiritual brother, fellow minister and father, adds his vote, so much the better. Since it concerns us, brothers, and especially since the Eastern thrones have made supplication for him, we hold him absolved of the offence committed against us and of the crime. And if the most holy Roman Pope John, spiritual brother, fellow minister and our Father, adds his verdict, it is better. Many points in Photius's words deserve consideration; among them, not the least but truly atrocious, he claims for himself papal authority, and though he disowns it, says that it is of no concern to him. But let us leave that. He says: if the Roman adds his vote to the absolution, it is better. What this "better" means I do not really understand. Is the pardon which Photius grants whole, or maimed, or half-finished, so that with the Roman's vote added it becomes more complete? What is perfect requires nothing further. If the absolution given by Photius was perfect, it is pointless to seek another's vote; if it was imperfect, then the one by whom the perfection is added must be asked, and what is more imperfect has been rashly given. Marvel also at the man's cleverness: since he had no answer to the demands of the Romans, who referred that pardon to the Roman See, he does not want to seem of lesser standing than the Roman. He confesses that he absolves, but if the Roman gives his assent to the absolution, then everything is better. Therefore Photius's absolution claimed the same authority as the Roman's. Add to this that the Romans say the settlement of the crime pertains to Pope John, and Photius replies that it pertains to himself, because the offence concerned him. Follow the logic: but the crime committed against Photius concerned the Roman pontiffs; therefore the settlement of Photian wickedness pertained to the Romans. By what authority, then, was he admitted to communion by the Easterns before the Roman's settlement? That Photius was not restored by John, but by the sole authority of the Emperor, is plain from the letters of Michael of Alexandria and others cited here. The Synod had said above: "But after much exhortation and entreaty, and, to speak more truly, by the great force of the high and most Christian Emperors, and with the consent, and prayers of the Church of Constantinople, and before the force was used." Still, let Photius himself be heard, narrating in the same proceeding the manner in which he was restored to the throne after the death of Ignatius: "Again, with all agreeing, and with the synodal votes of the archpriestly ... requesting us ... and for the confirmation of letters, which the most holy Pope John has granted to our most pious and exalted Emperor, promising to assent to all his petitions, we ascended this throne, relying on them." Therefore the letters of John had preceded his ascent to the see. So he was raised before being absolved. Do you want more? Hear the fourth Action, near the end: "The most God-loving Metropolitan of Martyropolis and Locum tenens of Antioch said: The most holy Pope Michael of Alexandria, together with the archbishops of God, long ago anathematized and condemned all that was done against the most holy Patriarch Photius, and those who receive those things, and subjected them to the same ..." Theodosius, most holy Patriarch of Jerusalem, likewise ... condemned and rejected the same things ... Elias, most pious presbyter and locum tenens of Jerusalem, said: "Those who do not accept Photius, the most holy Patriarch, and the lawful and canonical archbishop of God, we anathematize and subject to condemnation, as Theodosius of holy memory, archbishop of Jerusalem, did long ago ..." And the holy Synod cried out: "We all glorify, we all proclaim, we all rejoice in these things. At this time the most holy Pope John appeared to us above all others, for, as we have often said, and as the most holy Pope John confessed, to remove the unlawful schism..."

units.la: Basilius Dei amantissimus Metropolita Martyropolitanus, & Locumtenens Antiocheni dixit. Sanctissimus Papa Michaël Alexandriæ simul cum suis Dei Præsulibus multo ab hinc tempore omnia, quæ contra sanctissimum Patriarcham Photium acta sunt, & reiecit, & anathemati subiecit, & eos, qui illa recipiunt simili anathemate feriit. Similiter, & meus Patriarcha sanctissimus Theodosius eadem ipsa, & ea recipientes, & ipsam Synodum eodem iudicio condemnauit, atque reiecit.
units.tr: Basil, most God-loving Metropolitan of Martyropolis and locum tenens of Antioch, said: The most holy Pope Michael of Alexandria, together with his fellow bishops of God, long ago rejected and anathematized all that was done against the most holy Patriarch Photius, and struck with the same anathema those who receive those acts. Likewise my most holy Patriarch Theodosius condemned and rejected the same acts, and those who receive them, and the Synod itself, by the same judgment.

units.la: Cosmas piissimus Presbyter, & Apocrisiarius Alexandrini dixit: Mentem suam sanctissimus Papa Alexandrinus in venerandis suis literis palam omnibus fecit; & omni maledictioni supposuit & ipsa, & illa recipientes. Elias piissimus Presbyter, & locum tenens Hierosolymorum dixit. Eos qui non recipiunt Photium Patriarcham, uti legitimum, & secundum Canones electum præsulem Dei, anathemati subijcio, æque atq; iam pridem sanctus Theodosius Hierosolymorum Antistes, nunc vero illius successor Elias similiter anathematizat, & reijcit, & omnia contra ipsum ante peracta, in quibus potissimum Saracenorum Apocrisiarij iudices, & legum latores iniqui præsidebant. Sancta Synodus clamauit. Omnes ita tenemus. Omnes ita prædicamus. Omnes hisce plaudimus. In hoc capite sanctissimi Papæ Ioannis inter alia præcipue gauisi sumus. Nos enim, ut sæpenumero diximus, ante quam sanctissimus Papa Ioannes iniquorum illorum demolitionem decreuisset, omnia aduersus sanctissimum Photium scripta, dictaque anathematizauimus, & reiecimus, cum illo uniti, & cum illo communicantes, etiam comministri facti: & nunc rursus ardentius, & serius omnia contra ipsum facta & anathematizamus, & reijcimus, & eos qui ea recipiunt, eidem anathemati subijcimus. Et Actione 5. Locum tenentes sedium Patriarchalium dicunt; Η ἁγία τῆς Ἱεροσολυμῶν Ἐκκλησία, ἡ τε τῆς Ἀντιοχέων, καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων, ἀλλ' ὅπως ἀπεβάλετο, ἢ ἀπηρνήσατο μὴ ἔχειν αὐτὸν τῶν τῆς ἁγιωτάτου Φώτιον ἐνομώτατον, καὶ κατα-νοησάμενος Πατριάρχου Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἐξόδου καὶ εἰς τὸν ἔσω τῶν [?] ἀπεβιβάσθη. Sancta Hierosolymitana, nec non Antiochena, & Alexxandrina Ecclesia, nunquam reiecit, aut negauit, hunc ipsum sanctissimum Photium esse secundum legum & Canonum praescripta Patriarcham Constantinopolitanum, ex quo in hanc sanctam sedem euectus est. Vides pertinaciam! Etiam post condemnatum a Synodis Photium, & excommunicatum in contumacia perseuerant, & nunc tandem obnitentibus legibus, & Canonibus contra Synodorum decreta, sine vllo causae examine sententiam ferunt. Et hi Synodum cogent, quae legitima in Ecclesia censeatur?
units.tr: Cosmas, the most pious presbyter and apocrisiary of Alexandria, said: The most holy Pope of Alexandria made his mind plain to all in his venerable letters, and he has placed under every curse both those things and those who accept them. Elias, the most pious presbyter and locum tenens of Jerusalem, said: I subject to anathema those who do not accept Photius as Patriarch, as a lawful prelate of God elected according to the canons, just as the late holy Theodosius, bishop of Jerusalem, and now his successor Elias likewise anathematize and reject him, and reject all the acts performed against him, in which the Saracen apocrisiaries, unjust judges and lawgivers, chiefly presided. The holy Synod cried out: We all hold thus. We all proclaim thus. We all applaud these things. In this chapter of the most holy Pope John we especially rejoiced in many things. For we, as we have often said, before the most holy Pope John had decreed the demolition of those wicked acts, anathematized and rejected all the writings and statements made against the most holy Photius, being united with him, communicating with him, and even made co-ministers with him; and now again, more ardently and more gravely, we anathematize and reject everything done against him, and we subject to the same anathema those who accept these things. And in the fifth Action the locum tenentes of the Patriarchal sees say: [Η ἁγία τῆς Ἱεροσολυμῶν Ἐκκλησία, ἡ τε τῆς Ἀντιοχέων, καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων, ἀλλ' ὅπως ἀπεβάλετο, ἢ ἀπηρνήσατο μὴ ἔχειν αὐτὸν τῶν τῆς ἁγιωτάτου Φώτιον ἐνομώτατον, καὶ κατα-νοησάμενος Πατριάρχου Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἐξόδου καὶ εἰς τὸν ἔσω τῶν [?] ἀπεβιβάσθη.] The holy Church of Jerusalem, as well as that of Antioch and that of Alexandria, never rejected or denied that this same most holy Photius is, according to the prescriptions of the laws and canons, Patriarch of Constantinople, since he was raised to this holy see. See their obstinacy! Even after Photius was condemned by the Synods and excommunicated, they persevere in contumacy, and now at last, resisting the laws and canons and the decrees of the Synods, they pronounce sentence without any examination of the case. And will these men compel a Synod, which is to be regarded as lawful in the Church?

units.la: CAPVT VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: Ex corruptis a Photio Ioannis Octaui literis Apostolicis, & condemnata Octaua Generali contra Photium, hoc idem probatur.
units.tr: From the letters of Pope John VIII, corrupted by Photius, and from the Eighth General Council's condemnation of Photius, the same point is proved.

units.la: Sed restitutionem Photij Literae Ioannis Pontificis confirmarunt. Hoc vero salsissimum est. Aliud Photius in corruptis a se Ioannis Epistolis, aliud Ioannes in suis edixerat. Actione septima Synodi Octauae contra Photium praecipitur ab Adriano, Τ᾽πολλιθῶας [?] ; καὶ λέγω, καὶ γραφὴν [?] ἐξαλγεῖλας [?] τὰ ἁμαρτήματα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναθεματίζας [?] τὰ παρανόμως γεγραμμένα, καὶ παραδίδως [?] ὑπ' αὐτοῦ δή; δὶς κ᾽ Ἰγνατίου τῆ Πατριάρχου αὐτὸ, Ὁμολογῆσαι ἡ μηδὲ μίαν μηχανὴν, ἢ συλλίνουσαν [?] ἐν πείθῃ. ἀλλὰ τὸν ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀρχιερέα αὐτὸ μὴ μεγάλης ἀξίως ἀποδέξασθαι· τῆς τε ἀποστολικῆς καθέδρας τὰς ἐκδί-οσεις τὰς ἀφ᾽ αὐτὸ, ἡ ὡς Ἰγνατίου τῆ Πατριάρχου ἐξιτιμήσας τιμίως ἀφαντυζασθ̀ [?]. Vti se submitteret, verboque, & scripto delicta sua faterétur, scriptaque impia, & acta bis contra sanctum Patriarcham Ignatium detestaretur, promitteretque se nihil in posterum contra illum moliturum moturumue, sed hunc pro germano Antistite magna cum veneratione recepturum: Apostolicae vero Sedis decreta aut de se, aut Ignatio prolata amplexurum. Ad impetrandam enim veniam requiritur prostratio, delictorum confessio, eorumque detestatio, promissio denique in posterum nunquam similia perpetrandi, & Apostolicae Sedis decreta summa cum veneratione recipiendi, & poenitentiam sibi impositam peragendi. Id quoque praecipit Ioannes suis genuinis literis ad Imperatores. Οὐκοῦν Φώτιον τὸν ἐπίσκοπον [?] πληγοφοείαν [?] δοῦναι, ἐλέειν [?] τῆς Σωσόδυ [?], ἐν ἀληθινῇ ἀγάπῃ ἀλλήλων, ἐν τῇ ἀρχιερατικῇ ἀξίᾳ συλλήπτορον, ἐν τῇ ποιμαντικῇ διδασκαλίᾳ συνεργὸν τε ὑπὸ τῆς εἰρήνης, καὶ ὠφελείας τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὸ Θεῖον διὰ τῆς Χριστοῦ βοηθείας ἐχέμεθά τε, καὶ ἐχομεν [?].
units.tr: But the letters of Pope John are said to have confirmed Photius's restoration. This is most absurd. Photius's version of John's letters, which he corrupted, says one thing, and what John himself had ordered says another. In the seventh action of the Eighth Synod against Photius, Adrian commands: "...and say, and set out in writing his sins, and anathematize what was written contrary to law, and be handed over twice to the Patriarch Ignatius, to confess, not by any device... but to receive him as a true high priest with great honour, and to honour the decrees of the Apostolic See, whether concerning himself or pronounced against Ignatius." [Τ᾽πολλιθῶας; καὶ λέγω, καὶ γραφὴν ἐξαλγεῖλας τὰ ἁμαρτήματα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναθεματίζας τὰ παρανόμως γεγραμμένα, καὶ παραδίδως ὑπ' αὐτοῦ δή; δὶς κ᾽ Ἰγνατίου τῆ Πατριάρχου] That he should submit, and by word and writing confess his offences, and detest the impious writings and acts twice committed against the holy Patriarch Ignatius, and promise that he would never in future attempt or set in motion anything against him, but would receive him as a true bishop with great veneration; and that he would embrace the decrees of the Apostolic See, whether issued concerning himself or concerning Ignatius. For to obtain pardon, prostration is required, confession of the offences, their detestation, and finally a promise never to commit such things again, to receive the decrees of the Apostolic See with the greatest reverence, and to perform the penance imposed. John orders this also in his genuine letters to the emperors. [Οὐκοῦν Φώτιον τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ... ἐν τῇ ἀρχιερατικῇ ἀξίᾳ συλλήπτορον, ἐν τῇ ποιμαντικῇ διδασκαλίᾳ συνεργὸν]

units.la: ᾽Itaque eundem Photium satisfaciendo, miseri-corcordiam coram Synodo secundum consuetudinem postulantem, in vera dilectione fratrem, in Pontificali officio comministrum, in pastorali magisterio consacerdotem pro Ecclesia Dei pace & utilitate amodo Christo fauente recipimus, & habemus. Licet ista inuerterit Photius in corruptis a se Ioannis Epistolis, & in hanc Synodum productis, non est tamen verosimile mutasse consuetudinem Ecclesiae, qua delinquentes recipiuntur. Quamuis enim multa Imperatori morem gerens indulserit, at non ita peragi rem voluit, vt etiam consuetudinum Ecclesiasticarum memoriam exitio daret. Quando iam Imperatori hoc gratum est, & petit Photium Patriarcham damnatum a Synodis atque excommunicatum conciliatum redigere in antiquam Ecclesiae concordiam, ex benignitate nostra atque indulgentia habeat suum Photium, seruatis tamen Canonibus, & consuetudinibus Ecclesiasticis, procumbat ante Synodum, fateatur delicta, promittat nunquam ausurum se similia, & causa discussa atque examinata poenitentiam accipiat, & ea peracta satisfaciat, tum Patriarcha agnoscatur, & obseruetur. Is enim tum erat vsus Romanorum Pontificum, & Ecclesiae vniuersae in iudicijs, cum delinquentes poenitentes communioni Ecclesiae restituebantur.
units.tr: Therefore we receive and hold this same Photius, now satisfying and asking mercy before the Synod according to custom, as a brother in true love, a fellow-minister in the pontifical office, and a fellow-priest in pastoral teaching, for the peace and benefit of the Church of God, with Christ's favour from now on. Although Photius altered these things in the letters of John that he corrupted and produced before this Synod, it is not likely that he changed the custom of the Church by which offenders are received back. For although, to humour the emperor, he yielded in many things, he did not want the matter so conducted as to destroy the memory of ecclesiastical custom as well. Since the emperor now finds this pleasing, and asks that Photius, condemned and excommunicated by the Synods, be reconciled and restored to the ancient concord of the Church, let him have his Photius, by our kindness and indulgence, provided the canons and ecclesiastical customs are observed: let him fall prostrate before the Synod, confess his offences, promise he will never dare such things again, and, once the case has been discussed and examined, accept penance, and, when that is done, make satisfaction; then let him be acknowledged and kept as Patriarch. For this was the practice of the Roman Pontiffs and of the whole Church in judgments, when offenders who repented were restored to communion with the Church.

units.la: Ὅ′τι ἐθέλως αὐτὸν ἐν πληρῷ ὑπολαβέσθαι[?], ὡς αὖ ἀκεί-βῶς τῶν ἡμετέρων Ἀποκρισιαρίων[?] κατ' αὐτὸν ἐξετασθῇ, καὶ ἡμῖν δηλωθῇ[?] ἐδύνης[?]. Eum a nobis nullo modo inter clerum admitti, quoad accurate per nostros Apocrisiarios tota illius causa excutiatur, nobisque significetur. Idem ipse Pontifex in Actis Synodi Romanae contra Photium; Καὶ ὅπως δὲ ἡμᾶς ὡς ἀδηδόπες[?] ὑπογκεί-νοντες ταῦτας[?] ἐπεάφαμεν[?]. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ Πέτρου θέ-σις ὑπ' ἄλλων κρίνεται, ἢ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, τὰς κλεῖς τῆς βασιλείας, ἀλλ' ἵνα ἡμᾶς κρίνῃ τὸ ἀρχαῖον διαφυλάττειν[?] μὴ κείνων[?], ἢ συναγῶν αὐτῶν τῆς ἡμῶν ἐμβαλὼν[?] ἀντιδόσεως[?]. Itemque nos nihil veritos ne male iudicauerimus haec scripsisse. Nam Sedes Petri a nemine iudicatur, nisi ab eo, qui illi claues regni dedit: Sed vos, vt antiquum morem seruetis, neque iudicetis, neque approbetis quidquam sine nostra auctoritate. Vides hic antiquum morem esse non iudicare, neque approbare quicquam sine Romani auctoritate? Et Photius mores, & Canones Ecclesiæ pessundans, & poenitentiam detrectans, nimis in suis laudibus iactabundus, & petulans, etiam renitentibus Romanis sese propria auctoritate in thronum restituit.
units.tr: Ὅ′τι ἐθέλως αὐτὸν ἐν πληρῷ ὑπολαβέσθαι, ὡς αὖ ἀκεί-βῶς τῶν ἡμετέρων Ἀποκρισιαρίων κατ' αὐτὸν ἐξετασθῇ, καὶ ἡμῖν δηλωθῇ. That he is by no means to be admitted by us among the clergy, until his whole case has been carefully examined through our apocrisiarii and reported to us. The same Pontiff, in the Acts of the Roman Synod against Photius, says: "And since we have no fear that we might have judged wrongly in writing these things. For the See of Peter is judged by no one else, nor by his brother, but by him who gave him the keys of the kingdom. But you, that you may keep the ancient custom, neither judge nor approve anything without our authority." Do you see here that the ancient custom is not to judge or approve anything without the authority of the Roman? And Photius, subverting the customs and canons of the Church and refusing penance, boastful and insolent in his own praises, even though the Romans resisted, restored himself to the throne by his own authority.

units.la: Sed accuratius res examinetur, & ex ipsis corruptis a Photio Epistolis corruptæ Synodi fabula eliciatur. Scribit Ioannes ab ImImperatoribus ante assensum Pontificis Romani, licet invitum Photium in sedem restitutum fuisse, tum ab ipsis petitam a Pontifice restitutionem. Id non approbat, licet non videatur improbare. εἰ καὶ ἡ [?] [illegible, ~60 letters] Licet nostra pietas, vim Photio inferens substituerit illum ante nos, hoc est prius quam missi a nobis Legati istuc venirent. Malo tamen se, ne status Ecclesiae integer dissipetur, remedium dicit afferre ex indulgentia, qua severitas legum Ecclesiasticarum moderatur.
units.tr: But let the matter be examined more carefully, and let the fable of the corrupted Synod be drawn out of the very letters that Photius corrupted. John writes that, before the assent of the Roman Pontiff, Photius, though unwilling, had been restored to the see by the emperors, and that the restoration was then sought from the Pontiff by them. He does not approve this, though he does not seem to disapprove it outright. [Εἰ καὶ ἡ ...] Although our piety, using force against Photius, placed him before us, that is, before our legates came there from us. Yet he says he prefers to bring a remedy by indulgence, by which the severity of ecclesiastical laws is tempered, rather than let the state of the Church be wholly broken up.

units.la: Non ergo probat restitutionem Photii, sed ausum illum Imperatorum, & vim illatam tolerat. Ubi enim necessitas fuerit, & vis, ibi ad utilitatem Ecclesiarum Dei, qui potestatem habet, dispensat. Si ante literas has Pontificis Photius receptus fuerat, & restitutus in sedem, frustra Pontifex tot inculcatis adhortationibus Photii reconciliationem Imperatoribus, aliisque Praesulibus suadet. Frustra enim quod actum est, fieri suadetur. Et qui a tot Synodis iustas ob causas, & ob ingentia scelera condemnatus, expulsus, inferisque per anathema devotus fuerat, & Christianorum nomine indignus declaratus, & ab Oecumenico Concilio exauctoratus, per multos annos veluti invasor, muneribus Sacerdotalibus, & Pontificalibus spoliatus, priuatam vitam agens, postmodum per vim ab Imperatoribus sedi redditus, absque praevio examine, nulla causae disquisitione a summo Pontifice statim approbabitur? Credant Photiani; Pontificum Romanorum illius temporis alii mores, aliae constitutiones Ecclesiae, alia Canonum observatio. Et eos non ita facile mutare sua scribit Iosephus Methonensis, Responsione in Libellum Marci Ephesii contra Synodum Florentinam. Δόγμα δὲ ἡ ἴδιος τὶ τῆς οἰκείων ᾧ ἀ[?] πρὸς σε, ἡ τῆς μὴ σε ἡ χρεία λῷ. Ἔνθα γὰρ ἡ ἀκραντήλυτος σοφία διδάσκει, καὶ τελείως ἐργάζεται ἐωυτοῦ ἐχιστὲ[?], ἐ Δημιτον ἀ[?] δόγμα πιστόν. Sed neque opus erat, ipsos a te vel a tuis edoctos dogma mutare vel institutū[?]; ubi enim germana docetur sapientia, & perfectos illa efficit sui studiosos, non est fas, instituti aut dogma Fidei commntari. Quod experientia edoctus ipse Ephesius confirmat ibidem; Ἐυ δὲ ἡμῖν ἀποχωρᾶν τὸ πέλας σωθῆναι, καὶ τις ἡμῖν ἀπέκτεινεν ἰδῶν εἰς πλησίον ἄλλων. χρὴ γὰρ αὖ αἱ ἀνδρες ἔξω τ' οἰκείων ἐσθ' ν' [illegible, ~12 letters] Confestim quidem nobis desperatio finis obuenit, & prope quis stantem sic est affarier orsus: haud fane homines isti mores suos, & dogmata vlla ex parte patientur immutari, qui tantum nobis supercilium offenderunt. Et ne longe a materia difcedamus, Stephanus Papa Epistola ad eundem Basilium, cum ille postremo suæ vitæ tempore seductus a Photio contra Papam Marinum crimina intendens scripsisset, rerum temporalium curam & principatum Imperatoribus, spiritualium summis Pontificibus traditam esse palam prædicat; & Ioannes solo nutu Imperatoris Photium restitutum, & tantam Romanæ Ecclesiæ iniuriam illatam tolerasset?
