Pulso rursum Photio a Leone Imperatore Stylianus Neocæsareæ Episcopus petit sui aliorumque Episcoporum, & Clericorum, quod communicauerint cum Photio restitutionem, & Stephanus respondet; Ἡμᾶς αὔ δ᾽ ἀκειβῶς ἐξετάσεως [?] οἰκονομίας [?] ἐπιγνῶναι κείσεται [?]. Διὸ καὶ αὐτὸς τῶν Φώτιον [?] παρεδρά[?]μομεν, καὶ χρεία ἐστὶν ἐνὸς ἐκ τοῦ μέσου [?] ἐπισκόπους [?] ὑποσαλεύων, ὡς αὐτὸς ἐξεταζουλῶν [?] πάσης ἀμφιβολίας, ἐκ πάντων τῆς μεγάλης τῆς ἀληθείας φανερευομένης [?] ὁ Θεὸς Λόγος. Καὶ γὰρ ὡς κάπηγορ[?], καὶ ταὐτὰ λήμμα [?] ἡ ἁγία τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησία τὰς λοιπὰς Ἐκκλησίας καθίσα[?]. Καὶ ἂν αἱ ὀσίφη[?], εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀκλόνητον [?]. Καὶ χρὴ μὴ ἐξετάσεως τὰς κείσεις φέρειν. Nos absque diligenti totius rei indagatione nullam possumus sententiam proferre . Quapropter & nuper sententiam diftulimus, & oportet vt ab vtraque parte reuerendiffimi Epifcopi Legati mittantur, vt omni difcuffa dubitatione, veritateque ex omnibus partibus explorata, quod Deus fuggeffit, iudicare poffimus. Etenim Sancta Romana Ecclefia velut speculum quoddam, & exemplar Ecclefijs ceteris propofita eft: quae fi quid definierit, id omnibus feculis firmum, inconcuffumque manet. Far eft ergo, vt absque caufa cognitione iudicium, & fententia non pronunciatur.
units.tr: He therefore does not approve Photius's restoration, but merely tolerates the presumption of the emperors and the violence done. For where there is necessity and force, the one who has the power dispenses for the good of the Churches of God. If Photius had been received and restored to his see before these letters of the Pontiff, then the Pontiff, with so many urgent exhortations, would have been pressing the emperors and other prelates in vain to reconcile Photius. For it is in vain to urge what has already been done. And shall a man who, for just causes and great crimes, had been condemned by so many Synods, expelled, devoted to hell by anathema, declared unworthy of the Christian name, and deposed by the Ecumenical Council, who for many years, like an usurper, stripped of priestly and pontifical offices, lived a private life, and who was afterwards restored to his see by force by the emperors without prior examination and without any inquiry into the cause, be at once approved by the supreme Pontiff? Let the Photians believe it. The customs of the Roman Pontiffs of that time were different, the constitutions of the Church were different, and the observance of the canons was different. Josephus of Methone writes that they were not easily changed, in his Reply to the Libel of Mark of Ephesus against the Synod of Florence. [Δόγμα δὲ ἡ ἴδιος ...] "Nor was there any need for them to be taught by you or yours to change the dogma or the institution; for where true wisdom teaches, and makes its students perfect, it is not right to alter the institution or the dogma of faith." The Ephesian himself confirms this from experience in the same place: [Ἐυ δὲ ἡμῖν ἀποχωρᾶν τὸ πέλας σωθῆναι...] "Straightway despair of an end came upon us, and someone standing nearby began to speak to us: these men will not in any part allow their customs and any dogmas to be changed, who have offended us so greatly." And, not to stray far from the subject, Pope Stephen, in his letter to the same Basil, when that emperor, seduced by Photius late in his life, had brought charges against Pope Marinus, plainly declared that the care and government of temporal affairs had been committed to the emperors, and that of spiritual matters to the supreme Pontiffs. Would John have tolerated the restoration of Photius by the emperor's nod alone, and so great an injury done to the Roman Church? When Photius was again expelled by the emperor Leo, Stylianus, Bishop of Neocaesarea, asked whether he and other bishops and clergy who had communed with Photius after his restoration were to be condemned, and Stephen replied: [Ἡμᾶς αὔ δ᾽ ἀκειβῶς ἐξετάσεως ...] "We cannot pronounce any sentence without a careful examination of the whole matter. Therefore we have also sent our legates, and it is needful that, with the bishops from each side, all doubt be removed, and the truth, which God the Word reveals from all, be made plain. For the holy Roman Church, as the one that has the first place, has set the other Churches as an example; and if it has decided anything, it remains firm and unshaken for all ages. It is wrong, then, that judgment and sentence be pronounced without a hearing of the cause." We cannot pronounce any sentence without a diligent investigation of the whole affair. For this reason we have deferred our sentence even recently, and it is necessary that venerable bishops, Legates from each side, be sent, so that, every doubt having been removed and the truth explored from all sides, we may be able to judge as God suggests. For the holy Roman Church is set forth like a kind of mirror and pattern for the other Churches; whatever it has defined remains firm and unshaken through all ages. It is far from right, therefore, that judgment and sentence be pronounced without a hearing of the cause.

units.la: Et Ioannes iura fimilia, & iudiciorum ftylum neglexiffet, nec Epifcopis, qui a Photio difcefferant, reclamantibus auditis Photij restitutionem Imperatoris solo nutu factam confirmassit? An non, & ipse vna cum alijs perfidus fuiffet, & animae suae prodigus, qui sua manu subscriptum iuriurandum, ad sancti Petri tumulum positum teftatur fe Photij ordinationem, & eos, qui dictis duabus Synodis auctoritatem abrogarunt, nunquam recepturum.
units.tr: Would John really have neglected the laws and the usual form of judgments, and, when the bishops who had broken away from Photius protested, have confirmed Photius's restoration, which the Emperor had made by a mere nod, without hearing them? Or would he not himself have been faithless along with the others and a spendthrift of his own soul, when by an oath signed in his own hand and laid on the tomb of St Peter he bears witness that he would never receive Photius's ordination, nor those who abrogated the authority of the two said synods?

units.la: In Additione eorum in Synodo Octaua contra Photium ex Radero, quae in editione Rom. defiderantur; Ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι πῶς ἔχει[?] καταλαμβάνειν[?] αὐτῆς[?] τὰ ἰδιόχρη[?] ἐξ αὐτῶν[?] ἐπ᾽ [?] ἔχοντες πάντες ἰδιόχρη[?] ἐπίμα[?] ἐπ᾽ τῇ χρόνων[?] Σωσόλου Νικολάου, καὶ Ἀ[?]σπιαζῶ[?] ἐν οἷς ὑπέγραψεν Ἰωάννης Ἀ[?]ρχιεπίσκοπον[?] ὁ μετ᾿ αὐτὸν γνώμων Πάπας. Καὶ ἔδηκαν ἅπαντας τὰ ἰδιόχειρα αὐτῶν ἐπάνω τῆς τάφου τῆς ἁγίας Πέτρου τῷ μὴ ἀποδέξασθαί ποτε τὸν μοιχὸν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Φώτιον, ἢ τὴν χειροτονίαν αὐτοῦ, ἢ τοὺς [?] ἐξορκίας ἀπ[?] τὰς ἱερωμένας δύο Συνόδους αὐτῶν· ὡσαύτως δὲ οἱ Κωνσταντινοπολῖται ἔδηκαν τὰ ἰδιόχειρα αὐτῶν ἐπάνω τῆς ἡμῶν ξύλων, τῷ μὴ κοινωνῆσαί ποτε Φωτίῳ, ἢ τὴν χειροτονίαν αὐτοῦ, ἢ ἀποτῆσαι τὸ ὁμολόγιον Συνόδων τῶν ἐξακολουθησάντων τὰς ἱερωμένας δύο Συνόδους τῶν Ῥωμαίων.
units.tr: In the addition to their acts against Photius in the Eighth Synod, taken from Rader, which are missing from the Roman edition: "But also the Romans ... in the time of Sergius and Nicholas ... in which John, the Pope after him, subscribed as archbishop ..." And they all placed their own handwritten documents upon the tomb of St Peter, swearing never to receive Photius, the adulterer of the Church, nor his ordination, nor those who abrogated the two synods. Likewise the Constantinopolitans placed their own handwritten documents upon the wood of the cross, swearing never to communicate with Photius, nor to renounce the confession of the synods which followed the two synods of the Romans.

units.la: Quin & Romani quo pacto aufi sint violare, quod fuæ manus subscriptione firmarunt? Nam & illi omnes in duabus Synodis Romæ à Nicolao, & Adriano celebratis chirographa ediderunt, quibus Ioannes Archidiaconus, qui Nicolao post Adrianum in Pontificatu successit, manu sua subscripsit. Poterantque omnes chirographa sua supra tumulum S. Petri, testati se Photium Ecclesiæ adulterum, aut ordinationem illius, aut eos, qui dictis duabus Synodis auctoritatem abrogarunt, nunquam receptu-ros. Eodemque modo Constantinopolitani suas subscriptiones super veneranda Crucis lignia posuerunt, iurati, se nunquam cum Photio, aut Photianis communicaturos, Synodumue[?]. Oecumenicam, quæ duas Romanas secuta est, nunquam violaturos.
units.tr: Why, then, did the Romans fall away from what they had confirmed with their own hands? For all of them in the two synods held at Rome under Nicholas and Adrian issued signed documents, to which John the archdeacon, who succeeded Nicholas in the papacy after Adrian, also subscribed with his own hand. All of them could have placed their signed documents upon the tomb of St Peter, testifying that they would never receive Photius, the adulterer of the Church, nor his ordination, nor those who abrogated the authority of the said two synods. In the same way the Constantinopolitans placed their signed subscriptions upon the venerable wood of the Cross, swearing that they would never communicate with Photius or the Photians, nor violate the Ecumenical Synod which followed the two Roman synods.

units.la: Quis præterea strophas in hoc facto Photij non agnosceret? Proponunt Legati Pontificij Flauianum Constantinopolitanum§ Ioannem Chrysostomum, Cyrillum Hierosolymitanum, Polychronium, & alios eiectos spoliatosque suis sedibus auctoritate Romanorum Pontificum restitutos, & eadem ipsa ratione Photium. Quemadmodum nempe illi præuio examine, & discussa causa suam innocentiam comprobarunt in Synodo, ideoque restituti, ita quoque causam Photii pertractandam esse, Synodus Photiana, ne in causa Photii muta videretur, providentiam Ioannis in reddenda pace Ecclesiæ, & diffidentibus reconciliandis laudant, quod præter propositum Legatorum erat. Nullum hic examen de expulsione a sede Ignatii, nulla de invasione Photii, vivente adhuc Ignatio legitimo Pastore, nulla de contumacia, nulla de Synodo adversus Nicolaum confecta, nulla de maledictis, imposturis, ludibriis in Nicolaum concinnatis mentio, quæ plane examinanda fuerant, ut re diiudicata, si Photius innocens, & extra noxiam esse, & falso insimulatus comperiretur, absolveretur, sin minus culpæ obnoxius, ex indulgentia Ioannis, venia petita, dolens de sceleribus, pœnitentia recepta sedi restitueretur. Hac ratione sedibus suis restituti sunt Flavianus, Chrysostomus, Cyrillus, & reliqui. Sed hic ut vides, æque atque offusa nox perpetua esset, ordo iudiciorum perturbatur, delectus personarum confunditur, leges, iuraque deturpantur, & suprema auctoritas, qua dirigenda erant omnia, peffundatur.
units.tr: Moreover, who would not recognise the tricks of Photius in this affair? The Papal legates put forward Flavian of Constantinople, John Chrysostom, Cyril of Jerusalem, Polychronius, and others who were cast out and stripped of their sees and restored by the authority of the Roman Pontiffs, and they argue that Photius should be treated on the same principle. Just as those men, after a prior examination and a discussed case, proved their innocence in synod and were therefore restored, so too the case of Photius ought to be tried. The Photian synod, lest it seem silent on the case of Photius, praises John's care in restoring peace to the Church and in reconciling the doubtful, which was outside the purpose of the legates. Here there is no examination of Ignatius's expulsion from his see, none of Photius's usurpation while Ignatius, the lawful pastor, was still alive, none of his obstinacy, none of the synod assembled against Nicholas, none of the curses, frauds and mockeries devised against Nicholas. All of these ought to have been examined plainly, so that, once the matter had been judged, if Photius were found innocent and free from fault and falsely accused, he would be acquitted; but if he were guilty, then, by John's indulgence, having sought pardon, grieving for his crimes, and having received repentance, he would be restored to his see. In this way Flavian, Chrysostom, Cyril and the rest were restored to their sees. But here, as you see, the order of judgments is disturbed, as if a perpetual night had been poured over it; the choice of persons is confused, laws and rights are defiled, and the supreme authority, by which everything ought to have been directed, is trampled underfoot.

units.la: Vim ergo suam Synodus ex Epistolis Ioannis Papæ confecuta, an Ioannis decreta peregerit examinetur. Primum Ioannes in Epistolis corruptis a Photio petit a Photio, vt ante reconciliationem misericordiam poftulet; secundum, vt dimittat Romano debitam Bulgariam, & ab ordinationibus illius nationis manus abstineat. De his in Synodo nihil peractum est. De Bulgaria, illam pertinere ad Imperatorem, ab eo petendam. Imperator, ad quem pertinebat, iudicabit. De poenitentia, nec verbum quidem; sed omnia falso, & infidiose concipit; Θεόνες δὲ ὑπηζητεῖ [?] ἡ ἀχωσιὼν [?] τῆς βασιλικῆς ἐντολῆς συμφέρει [?] ἀρχήν. Εἰ δὲ τὸ τῆς ἡμῶν ἐν κυρίῳ ἀγάπης πλάτος μὴ ταῖς βασιλικαῖς ἐπιτροπαῖς [?] τὸ αἰδήμονες, μηδὲ τῆς ἄλλης μὴ καινουργῆ ἀπεχάπηξε [?]. Εἶχον δὲ καὶ τὸ ἐκκλησιαστικὸν σύμπαν τοῦτο, οὐχ ἅπαν λέγεις [?] ὅτι ἐστὶν ἡ Ῥώμης θεσμὸν τῆς ἑαυτῆς [illegible, ~12 letters] καὶ οἱ μηδέποτε ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνου γενόμενοι, καὶ τοὺς ἰδίους αὐ κατίσχυσεν [?]. O sacrosanctam Photij mentem! o mirificam in dando munificentiam! Sedes quas tua Sanctitas postulat in Orientali Imperio continentur. Quod si mea in Domino dilectionis latitutitudo imperatoriis necessitatibus non angustiaretur, neque aliud Canonum ius impediret, haberem quoque Sacerdotes mihi subiectos in hoc concordes, non quas dicis Romanæ Sedi aliquando fuisse obnoxias, sed & eas, quæ nunquam illi subiectæ fuerunt, promptus essem concedere. Pontifex ergo quod est contra ius etiam reluctantibus Constantinopolitanæ Ecclesiæ proceribus postulat, & vendicat sibi non sua, sed quæ viribus imperatoriis sunt addicta. Postulatum certe indignum Pontifice. Hæc modeste Photius, sed subdole pronunciat: Sed Procopius Cæsariensis eadem ipsa Actione insolentius rem aperit; Ἐ'λπίζομὲν ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ὑποταγῆναι ἔχουσι τὴν κεφαλὴν τῆς Ἀποστολικῆς [?] , καὶ μεγάλων Βασιλέων [?] ἡμῶν, καὶ τοῦτο [?] ἡμᾶς [?] , ὡς κελεύει [?] ἡ κεφαλὴ τῆς βασιλείας ποιεῖ [?] , καὶ ἀποδιδόντων ἐκάστῳ τὰς οἰκείας ἐνορίας ἀκμυποτάκτους [?]. Speramus nationes omnes subiciendas esse pio dominio a Deo prouectorum, & magnorum nostrorum Imperatorum, quo facto tum, ut iusserit validissimum eorundem Imperium, ordinabit, & restituet unicuique proprias Dioeceses absque ulla innouatione. Nempe Pontifex recuperabit sua, ut dicitur, ad Kalendas Græcas, cum scilicet Nationes omnes unum Constantinopolitanum Imperiū agnoscent, & illius nutibus gubernentur. Quando hæc erunt? Nugae. En item Imperatorem Constantinopolitanum negotiorum, & litium Ecclesiasticarum iudicem factum, licet reliquae Synodi tum universales, tum nationales reclament omnes. Sed de primo Pontificis postulato satis.
units.tr: Let us examine, then, what force the synod drew from the letters of Pope John, and whether it carried out John's decrees. First, in his letters, John asks Photius, before reconciliation, to ask for mercy; second, that he should hand over to Rome the Bulgaria that was owed to it and abstain from the ordinations of that nation. Nothing was done in the synod about these matters. As for Bulgaria, that it belongs to the Emperor and must be sought from him: the Emperor, to whom it belongs, will judge. As for repentance, not a word; but everything is conceived falsely and insidiously: "... for the Emperor's command ... " And if the breadth of our love in the Lord is not ... and if the ecclesiastical whole does not say that it is Rome's ... [the text here is too corrupt to render]. O most sacred mind of Photius! O wonderful generosity in giving! The sees which your Holiness demands are contained in the Eastern Empire. If the breadth of my love in the Lord were not hemmed in by imperial necessities, and if another law of the canons did not stand in the way, I would also have priests subject to me in agreement with this, and I would readily concede not only those you say were once subject to the Roman See, but also those which were never subject to it. The Pontiff therefore demands what is against right, and claims for himself not his own, but what has been assigned to the imperial power, even though the nobles of the Constantinopolitan Church resist. Certainly an unworthy demand for a Pontiff. Photius pronounces these things modestly, but craftily. But Procopius of Caesarea opens the matter more insolently in the same Action: We hope that all nations will be subject to the head of the Apostolic [See] and of our great Emperors, and that, when this is done, the most powerful empire of these men will order and restore to each one their own parishes without any innovation. Namely, the Pontiff will recover what is his, as they say, at the Greek Kalends, when all nations acknowledge one Constantinopolitan Empire and are governed by its nod. When will this be? Trifles. Behold again the Constantinopolitan Emperor made judge of business and ecclesiastical lawsuits, although all the other synods, both universal and national, protest. But enough about the Pontiff's first demand.

units.la: Quid de secundo? Synodus dicit Actione 2. Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἄπαν. Ὅσα εἰς ἀποδοχὴν, καὶ ἀνακήρυξιν δὲ Ἐκκλησίας, Ꞓ Φωτίου τῆ ἁγιωτάτῃ Πατριάρχου ἀποδοχὴ [?]· Ὅσα ἡ αὐτοκράτωρ τῆς βασιλείας, καὶ τῆς βασιλικῆς διοικήσεως, ἐκείνῳ, καὶ τῷ κυρίῳ τῆς ἀληθείας διοικήσεως [?]· καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ἀναπληρῶ [?]. Quotquot ad receptionem, & deprædicationem Ecclesiæ, & Photij sanctissimi Patriarchæ faciunt, recipimus. Quæ ad Imperatorem pertinent & imperatorias administrationes, illi & confirmationem administrationis circa eadem, & auctoritatem deferimus. Et Actione tertia; Ὅσα εἰς δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἐκκλησίας, Ꞓ ἐπονομάζων, καὶ ἀποδεχόμεθα, καὶ ἀποδεχόμεθα, καὶ ἀμεταθέτως ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ διαθήκῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα διαμένομεν. Ὅσα δὲ ἔδειξεν ἐπὶ ἑαυτῶν, ἃ οὐκ ἀληθῶς εἰς τὸ ὑμέτερον γνώμην, ἀλλ' εἰς τὴν τοῦ μεγάλου Βασιλέως ἡμῶν, καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς διοικήσεως, καὶ κείων, ταῦτα ἐναντίον τῇ φρονήσει, Ꞓ ἀναπληρώμεν [?]. Quae resultant in gloriam Dei Ecclesiae & praestitimus & recipimus, & immutabiles in hoc proposito in perpetuum perfistemus. Quae vero alia sunt, nec facultati nostrae subsunt, sed in magni Imperatoris nostri, & excelsi dispositionem, atque iudicium, illa illius cura, ac prouidentia demandamus. Et Photius τοσούτων μηχανορράφων κακῶν[?] eadem ipsa secunda Actione. Φῶν@[?] ὁ ἀγωνιστὴς Πα-[?] ζιαφῆς[?] ἄπιστος[?]. Οὐ ζῶ πεισαίω[?], ὲ ἐνδίσῳ[?] λόγῳ πε-[?] ιέχει[?], καὶ εἰς τὸ ἡμέτερον ἀὐτ[illegible, ~6 letters] ἐμ[illegible, ~4 letters] τὸ τέλος, καὶ σοφῆς, καὶ ἀποδοχῆς ἀξία νομίζομεν.
units.tr: What of the second? The synod says in the second Action: The holy synod ... whatever tends to the acceptance and proclamation of the Church and of Photius, the most holy Patriarch, ... whatever belongs to the Emperor and to imperial administration, to him and to the lord of truth ... and to the authority ... We receive whatever tends to the reception and proclamation of the Church and of the most holy Patriarch Photius. Whatever pertains to the Emperor, and to imperial administration, we commit to him, together with confirmation and authority over the same matters. And in the third Action: Whatever results in the glory of God for the Church, we both have granted and receive, and in this covenant we shall remain unchanged for ever. But whatever he has shown in his own person, which is not truly in accordance with our opinion, but in that of our great Emperor and of the administration ... these things, contrary to his prudence, we ... fulfil. Whatever results in the glory of God for the Church we have both granted and receive, and we shall remain immovable in this purpose for ever. But whatever else there is, which is not within our power, but lies in the disposition and judgment of our great and exalted Emperor, we commit to his care and providence. And Photius, in the same second Action, [says]: "... of so many wicked schemers ... the contender ... unfaithful ... " We think worthy of wisdom and of acceptance what is said in a fitting and just reasoning and pertains to our mediocrity, and their work and conclusion is worthy of being received.

units.la: Quæ decenti, ac iusta rationi in nituntur, & ad nostram mediocritatem pertinent, & opus illorum, & absolutio, digna, quæ recipiantur existimamus. Subit modo Achillæum illud apud Euripidem in Iphigenia in Aulide. Nanque cum propositiet illi Chorus, obediendum esse Principibus, qui ratione, & experientia edocti, recte vitam agunt cum prudentia, non negat Achilles obediendum, sed si præerunt recte, & vtiliter sapient: sin minus, parendum illis non esse.
units.tr: Those matters which rest on fitting and just reason and bear upon our modest capacity, together with their accomplishment and completion, we think worthy of acceptance. Here the famous saying of Achilles in Euripides' Iphigenia in Aulis comes to mind. When the chorus maintained that one must obey the leaders who, taught by reason and experience, live rightly and wisely, Achilles does not deny that one must obey. But if they lead rightly and profitably, he says, they should be obeyed; if not, they should not.

units.la: Καὶ τοῖς Ἀτρείδαις, ὧ μὲν ἡγῶνται καλῶς[?] Πεισόμεθ᾽[?], ὅταν ἡ μὴ καλῶς ἡγῶνται[?]. Proin Atridis, si probi fuerint duces; parebimus, sin improbi, haud parebimus. Hac eadem ratione Photius, & Synodus obtemperant Pontifici Romano, si iusta, & canonica præcipiat: sin minus, parere nolunt. Quis porro iudex erit de iustitia, & iniustitia mandatorum? Synodus ipsa, & Photius.
units.tr: "And to the Atreidae: if they lead well, we shall obey; when they do not lead well..." [Καὶ τοῖς Ἀτρείδαις, ὧ μὲν ἡγῶνται καλῶς, Πεισόμεθ', ὅταν ἡ μὴ καλῶς ἡγῶνται]. So, to the Atreidae: if they are good leaders, we shall obey; if they are wicked, we shall not obey. In the same way Photius and the Synod obey the Roman Pontiff if he commands what is just and canonical; if not, they refuse to obey. Who then will be the judge of the justice and injustice of commands? The Synod itself, and Photius.

units.la: Et sic Romanus Pontifex, qui aliorum iudex in Concilijs sedere debet, post Photium sedens iudicabitur; & etiam si iusta non iussisse iudicabitur, condemnabitur, & punietur. Romani iussa, atque sententiae grauissimum condemnatorum iudicium subibunt: condemnati, ac reiecti irrogabunt multam: quia ille neque aequum, neque iustum postulauit. Sic [illegible, ~12 letters], & Ecclesiasticae hierarchiae vniuersus ordo inuertitur. Et ego dicam Synodum similia decernentem, Oecumenicam, legitimam, & genuinam esse? Non sum stipes, nec fungus. Alia ab his & longe diuersa genuina Concilia praecinunt. Adrianus Papa Epistola ad Imperatorem Basilium lecta in Octaua Synodo Actione secunda.
units.tr: And so the Roman Pontiff, who ought to sit in councils as the judge of others, will, after Photius, be judged while sitting. Even if he is found to have commanded what was not just, he will be condemned and punished. The commands and decrees of the Roman see will undergo the gravest judgment of the condemned, and those condemned and rejected will impose a fine, because he demanded what was neither fair nor just. Thus [illegible], and the whole order of the ecclesiastical hierarchy is turned upside down. And shall I say that a synod decreeing similar things is Ecumenical, lawful and genuine? I am no block or fungus. Other and quite different genuine councils proclaim otherwise. Pope Hadrian's letter to the Emperor Basil, read in the second action of the Eighth Synod.

units.la: Βουλόμεθα ἡ διὰ τῆς ὑμετέρας [?] ἀσφαλείας [?] ἐκ Καισαρείας ἐν τοῖς αὐτόθι πλεσθεῖσι συνελθοντι [?], ὡς αἱ ἡμέτεροι [?] Αʹ ... [illegible, ~30 letters] ... ἀλλὰ ἐπὶ τὰ [?] ... ἀνακρίσεως [?] ... ἐπὶ τοῖς [?] ... νόμοις. Voluimus autem per vestrae pietatis industriam Constantinopoli nunumerosum celebrari Concilium, cui nostri quoque Legati præsidentes delictorum hominumque discrimine perspecto, statim cuncta impij Conciliabuli exemplaria ab iis, qui illa retinent, ablata, ignibus concremanda tradant; huiusmodi enim conuenticulum nihil distare putamus vel ab Ariminensi per Constantium Imperatorem, vel ab Ephesino per Dioscorum coacto. Sed etsi quis hoc occultare, vel defendere conabitur, publicis legibus iudicandus subiiciatur. Rerum siquidem definitio ab Ecclesia Romana expectatur. Nicolaus Epistola ad Photium: Ἐπεὶ ἡ πᾶσα [?] ἀπὸ τούτης τῆς ἁγίας τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίας, ἧς [?] τὴν ἐπὶ τῆς [?] καὶ τὴν ὀρθοδοξίαν [?] τῆς πίστεως ἐξαιτῆ, τὴν δὲ τῶν εἰλημμένων ἀπολαυσι[?] ... [illegible, ~20 letters] Cum uniuersa credentium multitudo ab sancta Romana Ecclesia, quæ omnium caput est Ecclesiarum, doctrinam exquirat, integritatem fidei deposcat, delictorum veniam postulet, necessarium est, vt magnam nos curam, qui ad hoc vocati sumus, adhibeamus, & lupum Ecclesiam inuadentem arceamus. Ideoque infra Zacharias, & Theophilus Episcopi cum non egissent secundum libelli Romani formam, quæ erat, vt secundum Ecclesiam Catholicam tenerent, veritatemque defenderent, Romanæque Ecclesiæ iudicium sequerentur, foras Legatorum Romanorum iussu eiecti sunt. Id ipsum in Photiana Synodo agnitum quoque fuit, illud suggerente Petro Cardinali, quamuis non obseruatum. Καὶ χαίρομεν δὲ ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ὅτι εἰς τὸ [?] Συνοδικὸν [?] οἱ ἀρχιερατικοὶ ἅπαντες συνυδόκησαν [?] Θεσμοὶ μὲν τῇ [?] κυρίᾳ, καὶ [?] διαπότης [?] ἡμῶν [?] τῷ οἰκουμενικῷ Πάπα. καὶ τῷ ἐκείνῳ ὡς κεφαλῇ πασῶν τῆς Ἐκκλησιῶν, καὶ ὅπερ ὠφέλει ποιῆσαι, καὶ ἐξακολουθεῖν τῇ ἁγιωτάτῃ τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίᾳ πεποιήκασι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ συνδοκιμάσαντων [?]. Et gaudemus de hoc, quod in hanc unionem, qui Archieraticiis sedibus præsident, omnes una simul approbarunt, cum Domino nostro Papa Oecumenico. Namque illa est Ecclesiarum omnium caput, & quod illi debebant agere, sequi nempe sanctissimam Romanam Ecclesiam, peregerunt, Spiritu sancto simul assensum præbente. Photiani nihilominus in hac Synodo ab auctoritate Romani sese subtrahentes, quæ illis complacent, exequuntur, quæ displicent reprobant, licet mellitis verborum globulis menti Pontificis obsecundari videantur. quo sane nihil excogitari potest immanius.
units.tr: We wish, through your piety's diligence, that a numerous council be held at Constantinople, at which our legates also preside, and that, once the nature of the crimes and the men involved has been clearly examined, all copies of the impious conciliabulum be taken from those who keep them and handed over to be burned. For we judge such a conventicle to differ in nothing from the Arimininum council gathered by the Emperor Constantius, or from the Ephesian council gathered by Dioscorus. But if anyone tries to conceal or defend this, let him be subjected to judgment under the public laws. For the definition of these matters is awaited from the Roman Church. Nicholas, letter to Photius: [Ἐπεὶ ἡ πᾶσα ἀπὸ τούτης τῆς ἁγίας τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίας, ἧς τὴν ἐπὶ τῆς καὶ τὴν ὀρθοδοξίαν τῆς πίστεως ἐξαιτῆ, τὴν δὲ τῶν εἰλημμένων ἀπολαυσι...] Since the whole multitude of believers seeks teaching from the holy Roman Church, which is the head of all churches, asks for the integrity of the faith, and seeks pardon for its offences, it is necessary that we, who have been called to this, take great care and keep away the wolf that attacks the Church. Therefore, because Zacharias and Theophilus, bishops, did not act according to the form of the Roman libellus, which was that they should hold to the Catholic Church, defend the truth and follow the judgment of the Roman Church, they were cast out by order of the Roman legates. The same was acknowledged also in the Photian synod, at the suggestion of Cardinal Peter, although it was not observed. [Καὶ χαίρομεν δὲ ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ὅτι εἰς τὸ Συνοδικὸν οἱ ἀρχιερατικοὶ ἅπαντες συνυδόκησαν Θεσμοὶ μὲν τῇ κυρίᾳ, καὶ διαπότης ἡμῶν τῷ οἰκουμενικῷ Πάπα...] And we rejoice at this, that all the bishops who preside over archiepiscopal sees have together approved this union with our Lord the ecumenical Pope, for he is the head of all churches; and they have done what they ought to do, namely followed the most holy Roman Church, the Holy Spirit giving assent at the same time. Yet the Photians in this synod withdraw from the authority of the Roman see: they carry out what pleases them and reject what displeases them, although they seem to comply with the mind of the Pontiff with honeyed balls of words. Nothing more monstrous can be imagined.

units.la: Adde præterea & illa ex Actione prima. Ἠλίας ὁ Θεσσαλονίκης [?] ὀρθοβούτεως, ὁ τοποτηρη-τὴς [?] Ἐξαρχολύμων εἶπε. ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐνχαριστῆσαι ἄξιον τῆς Θεῷ Θεοῦ, ὅτι ὁρῶμεν πάντας ὁμοψύχους [?]. Ἀγαπητὸς ὁ [?] πλέον εἶσω ὁ Ἀπξ[?]ὸς, ὁ τὴν χριστιανικὴν ταύτην πλανῶν ἐν τῇ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἀγίᾳ τῇ Θεοῦ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ [?] Ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐδίνοτε παρεδεξάμεθα. Ἀλλ' ἀεί, καὶ δι' ἐκ παντὸς, ἀφ' ἧς ὁ ἀγιώτατος ἡμῶν Πατριάρχης Φωτίου τὸ ἀρχιερατικὸν τοῦτο θρόνον ἐπέσπει, καὶ τὴν πίστεως αὐτοῦ λίβελλον ἀπέσταλε πρὸς Θεόδοσιον τὸν ἁγιώτατον Πατριάρχην Ἱεροσολύμων, ἰωμένοι αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀδιάσπαστοι μέχρι τῶν μαρτυρικῶν [?], καὶ ἕως ἐναντίον τῆς τῆς ἀρχιερωσύνης αὐτοῦ Φωτισμοῦ [?] ἐδίνοτε παρεδεξάμεθα. [?]
units.tr: Add also those things from the first action. [Ἠλίας ὁ Θεσσαλονίκης ὀρθοβούτεως, ὁ τοποτηρητὴς Ἐξαρχολύμων εἶπε· ἐγὼ γὰρ εὐχαριστῆσαι ἄξιον τῷ Θεῷ, ὅτι ὁρῶμεν πάντας ὁμοψύχους. Ἀγαπητὸς ὁ πλέον εἶσω ὁ Ἀπξ[?]ὸς, ὁ τὴν χριστιανικὴν ταύτην πλανῶν ἐν τῇ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἀγίᾳ τῇ Θεοῦ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ Ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐδίνοτε παρεδεξάμεθα. Ἀλλ' ἀεί, καὶ δι' ἐκ παντὸς, ἀφ' ἧς ὁ ἁγιώτατος ἡμῶν Πατριάρχης Φωτίου τὸ ἀρχιερατικὸν τοῦτο θρόνον ἐπέσπει, καὶ τὴν πίστεως αὐτοῦ λίβελλον ἀπέσταλε πρὸς Θεόδοσιον τὸν ἁγιώτατον Πατριάρχην Ἱεροσολύμων, ἑνωμένοι αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀδιάσπαστοι μέχρι τῶν μαρτυρικῶν, καὶ ἕως ἐναντίον τῆς τῆς ἀρχιερωσύνης αὐτοῦ Φωτισμοῦ ἐδίνοτε παρεδεξάμεθα.] Elias, the Thessalonian, the orthodox, the locum tenens of the Hexarchs, said: "For I deem it right to give thanks to God, because we see everyone of one mind. ... Ever, and in every way, from the time when our most holy Patriarch Photius occupied this archiepiscopal throne and sent his libellus of faith to Theodosius, the most holy Patriarch of Jerusalem, we have received him as united with us and inseparable, down to the martyrdoms, and until the time of his archiepiscopal illumination..."

units.la: Elias pijssimus Presbyter, & Locumtenens Hierosolymitani dixit. Et nunc gratias agere Deo dignum eft, cum videamus omnes in vnum concordasse. Sed maiores ego humilis gratias ago, quod nunquam hic Schismatis error in sancta Dei Ecclesia Hierosolymitana locum habuit, sed semper, & perpetuo, ex quo Sanctissimus Dominus noster Photius Archieratica hac sede potitus est, & fidei suae libellum misit ad Theodosium sanctissimum Patriarcham Hierosolymitanum, vniti cum ipso, ac inseparabiles ad hoc vsque tempus permanfimus, & eos, qui contra ipsius Pontificatum aliquid aduersum moliti sunt, nunquam in nostram communionem suscepimus. Sed rem exactius nobis Schismatici ipsi enarrent. Ioannes Ephesius Tractatu de Schismate. Καὶ τῆς ἐκ τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ μέσου Ἰγνατίου ὁ Φωτίου τῆς Παρχιαρχῶν ὁ χρόνος ἐκεῖνος ἐκλυγοτάτην [?], καὶ ὅπως τὸ πλήθοςμα τῆ τότε ἀρχιερέων ὑχ ἅπαξ, ἡ δὶς δὶς, ἡ δὲ ζεῖς τὰς ἐγγεάφως ἀσφαλείας ἑαυτῷ ὑπεσχέσαντο [?]. Τῶν [?] νῦν μὲν ἕως θανάτου τῷ Ἰγνατίῳ προσανέχεσθαι συνεφόντες · Νῦν δὲ τῷ Φωτίῳ πάλιν ἀπιστῶντες τὰ πρότερα. Εἶτα καὶ μὴ τὰς ἀσφαλείας ταύτας αὐτὸν τε τὸν Φώτιον, ἐὰν ὧν ἀμφ' αὐτῶν καθαιρεῶντες, ἀφορίζοντες ὑπὸ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, ἢ τὰ ἀναθέματα [?] ἀνάθεμα ποιοῦντες, ἢ τὸ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ φεύκαλα [?] ἑαυτοῖς ἐπαγγέλμοι, ἀπὸ τῆς διδασκάλων τούτων ἀπορβλίτεσθαι [?], καὶ τὸν Φώτιον τοιοῦτόπως ὑποβλιθὴν εἰς ἀρχιερέως λόγον ὀπωσοῦν ἀπολογεῖσθαι καὶ καθαιρέθη [?]. Εἶτα ἢ μὴ χρόνον ταῦτα τὰ ἰσχυρὰ αἰσχύνοντες, καθολικῶς σωφρονέστερον, ἢ πάλιν ἐπ' Ἐκκλησίας ὀσράκις ἦ παροιμίαν μεταπ- [?] οὕντος ἀνακηρύττοντες, ἀδιφημοῦντες, κερτουμένης, ἐξαίρουσι, ἡ μακεδῶς [?] ἐπαίνοις, ἡ ἱκωμίοις αἰσχρῶς, ἡ στεφανοῦντες ἢ Φώτιον, αὐθέντον ἀληθῶς λέγοντες τῷ Θεῷ, νόμιμον ἀρχιερέως ἱεράνωον λύχνον ἢ Ἐκκλησίας, φωτῆρα ἢ οἰκουμένης, Διδασκάλαν ἀσθενῆ [?], ἀληθείας διδάσκαλον. Et cui cognita non sint, quae inter Ignatium, & Photium Patriarchas tempus illud innouarit, & quomodo coetus vniuersus Antistitum non semel, neque bis, aut ter scripto traditas suas fides publicas improba-runt. Cum hi nunc quidem vsque ad mortem Ignatio adhaerere se astringerent, nunc Photio, quae prius scripserant reiicerent. Postmodum post similes cautiones ipsum Photium illiusque socios deponerent, in Ecclesia excommunicarent, & anathemati subjicerent. Nec id solum, sed quam horrenda sibi deprecarentur, si quid ex iam dictis placitis immutassent, & Photium hoc modo depositum uti Antistitem quomodocunque accepissent. Tum postmodum elapso tempore valida hac invertentes, & publicis congressibus rursus in Ecclesia testae instar transmutata publice pradicantes, vociferantes, plaudentes, & prolixis laudibus, atque encomiis Photium extollentes, & coronantes, hominem Dei verum enunciantes, legitimum Antistitem, Canonicam Ecclesiae lampadem, orbis terrarum lumen, pietatis assertorem, veritatis magistrum. Episcopi hi Photium deponunt, excommunicant, horrenda sibi, si illum remiserint, deprecantur. Ignatius illis ab excommunicatione, & anathemate immunis est. neque spondent nunquam se eum in posterum receptunext ros. Et Photiani dicunt semper Photio Orientales adhaesisse, & uti Patriarcham recognovisse? Diris, quibus se devoverant, affligentur.
units.tr: Elias, the most pious presbyter and locum tenens of Jerusalem, said: "It is now right to give thanks to God, since we see all have agreed in one. But I, lowly, give greater thanks that this error of schism never had a place in the holy Church of God at Jerusalem, but always and continually, from the time when our most holy Lord Photius obtained this archiepiscopal see and sent his libellus of faith to Theodosius, the most holy Patriarch of Jerusalem, we have remained united with him and inseparable up to this time, and we have never admitted into our communion those who have plotted anything against his pontificate. But let the schismatics themselves relate the matter more exactly to us." John of Ephesus, Treatise on the Schism. [Καὶ τῆς ἐκ τοῦ ἑαυτοῦ μέσου Ἰγνατίου ὁ Φωτίου τῆς Παρχιαρχῶν ὁ χρόνος ἐκεῖνος ἐκλυγοτάτην...] And let those not be unaware of what happened between the Patriarchs Ignatius and Photius at that time, and how the whole assembly of bishops, not once, nor twice, nor three times, but repeatedly, in writing, gave their pledges of security. Now they bound themselves to adhere to Ignatius until death, and now they again disowned their former statements in favour of Photius. Afterwards, though they had given such guarantees, they deposed Photius himself and his partisans, excommunicated them in the Church, and placed them under anathema, and they did this not only, but they called down horrors upon themselves if they changed any of the aforesaid decisions, and if they had in any way accepted Photius as deposed bishop. Then, after some time had elapsed, these same men, overturning their firm decisions, and in public assemblies turning again like a potsherd in the Church, proclaimed, shouted, applauded, and with long praises and encomia exalted and crowned Photius, calling him truly a man of God, the lawful bishop, the canonical lamp of the Church, the light of the world, the champion of piety, the teacher of truth. These bishops depose Photius, excommunicate him, and call down horrors upon themselves should they readmit him. Ignatius is free from excommunication and anathema on their part, and they do not promise that they will ever receive him again. And do the Photians say that the Easterns always adhered to Photius and recognised him as Patriarch? They are afflicted by the curses with which they had bound themselves.

units.la: Actione tertia damnantur Synodi Nicolai, Adriani, & Octava generalis, in quibus Photius de multis sceleribus convictus, & quod tyrannice pulso legitimo pastore thronum occupasset, deijcitur & condemnatur. Videtur sumpta occasio ex Commonitorio Joannis Pontificis; Θίλωμὴν ἐνώπιον ἢ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Σωόδου ἀπαγορευθῆναι [?], ἵνα ἡ Σωόδος ἡ γεγονῦνα [?] τῷ ἀναγνωσθέντι παρ' ἱερέως Φωτίου ἐν τοῖς κοινοῖς Α' ἀδριανῷ τῷ ἀγωνιστῇ Πάπα ἐν τῇ Ῥώμῃ, καὶ ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει [?]· ἀλλὰ τῷ παρόντι ἢ ἐξωσπακισμένῃ [?], καὶ ἄκυρος, καὶ ἀβέβαιος, καὶ μὴ συναριθμεῖσθαι αὐτῇ μηδὲ ἑτέρᾳ ἁγίας Σωόδῳ. Volumus in Synodo cogenda promulgari, Synodum aduersus iam dictum Photium Patriarcham tempore sanctissimi Papæ Adriani Romæ celebratam, & eam quæ Byzantij acta est, ex nunc esse reiectam, & irritam, & infirmam, & cum nulla alia Synodo connumerari. Neque dissimilia sunt, quæ leguntur Actione 4. Hæc Ioannes Pontifex, si tamen illius sunt. His si obedias, ab æquitate, lege, & institutis maiorum non recedes. Romanus sancit, parendum est. Sed quid Photiani egerint post lectum Commonitorium, consideremus. Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἀπεκρίθη· ἡμᾶς δὲ ἐρῶν ἀπεκρίψαμεν, καὶ ἀπεβαλόμεθα, καὶ αἰδεσμαπίζαμεν [?] ἡ παρ' ὑμῶν λεγόμενον Σωόδον, ἐνωδίτης Φωτίῳ ὡς ἀγωνιστῇ ἡμῶν Πατριάρχῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποβαλλομένης [?] τῆς ἀναγραφῆς παρ' ὑμῶν Σωόδῳ πρὸς αἰσθήμαν ὡς ἀπὸ μποδῷ [?]. Ἠλίας μητροπολίτης Μαρτυρπόλεως, ἢ Ἠλίας Ἱεροσολύμων τοποτηρητὴς ἦν. καὶ πῶς γὰρ αὕτη Συνόδου ἡ ὑπόθεσις [?]; τῆς ὁμοίας Σωόδου τῷ Σαρακηνῶν Ἀποκειταρίας κεικειτας νομοθέτας καθίσας, ποίας Σωόδοις ἀπ-ὀμνυθείη ἡ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων Σωόδων ἐναντία ζλ-μήσαζα, ἢ σὺν αὐθωθωύς, καὶ χωεῖς τῆς εἰασδήν-ποτὲ ἐξεταστως καὶ καθελήσαςα; ἢ πάντας θεσμὺς Ἐκκλησιαστικὰς καὶ πολιτικὰς συνχέαζα, καὶ καθαρ-φίλαζα; δὴ ταῦτα δὲ οἱ ἐκ ἀὐ ἰζαλῆς ἀμώζαπι Θεό-γοι ὑπηκηρύκτυς τας προςζιξες, καὶ ὑποβλήτας ἐπιπίζαντο.
units.tr: In the third action the synods of Nicholas and Adrian, and the eighth ecumenical synod, are condemned. In them Photius, convicted of many crimes and of having seized the throne by tyranny after driving out the lawful minister, is deposed and condemned. The occasion seems to have been taken from the Commonitorium of Pope John: "I wish that it be proclaimed in the convened synod that the synod against the aforesaid Patriarch Photius, held at Rome in the time of the most holy Pope Adrian, and the one held at Byzantium, are from now on rejected, void, and invalid, and not to be counted with any other holy synod" [Θέλωμεν ἐν τῇ μελλούσῃ ἀπαγορευθῆναι Σύνοδος… ἀκυρος, καὶ ἀβέβαιος, καὶ μὴ συναριθμεῖσθαι αὐτῇ μηδὲ ἑτέρᾳ ἁγίᾳ Συνόδῳ]. Neither are the things read in the fourth action unlike these. These are the words of Pope John, if indeed they are his. If you obey them, you will not depart from equity, from law, or from the institutions of your forefathers. The Roman has decreed it, and it must be obeyed. But let us consider what the Photians did after the Commonitorium was read. The holy Synod replied: "We have indeed rejected, cast off, and anathematized the synod you name, which was held against our Patriarch Photius, and we have communed with him and joined in his cause, though the record of that synod was not cast out by you…" [Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἀπεκρίθη· ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐρρίψαμεν…]. Elias, Metropolitan of Martyropolis, or Elias, locum tenens of Jerusalem, spoke. And how can that be a synod whose business… [καὶ πῶς γὰρ αὕτη Συνόδου ἡ ὑπόθεσις;] which set up Saracen apocrisiaries as judges and lawgivers, which overturned every synod and every canon of the holy synods, which condemned without any examination, and which confused and destroyed all ecclesiastical and civil laws? These things, indeed, the men of that time, who were under the sway of the Saracens, proclaimed and submitted to.

units.la: Sancta Synodus respondit. Nos operibus ipsis abdicauimus, & reiecimus, & anathematizauimus eam, quae a vobis commemoratur Synodus, vniti sanctissimo nostro Patriarchæ Photio. Et eos qui non reijciunt, quæ aduersus illum scripta dictaque sunt in iam dicta Synodo, anathemate ferimus. Elias Metropolita Martyropolitanus, & Elias locumtenens Hierosolymorum dixerunt.
units.tr: The holy Synod replied: "We have by our very deeds abdicated, rejected, and anathematized that synod which you mention, united with our most holy Patriarch Photius. And those who do not reject what has been written and said against him in the said synod, we pronounce under anathema." Elias, Metropolitan of Martyropolis, and Elias, locum tenens of Jerusalem, said so.

units.la: Et qua ratione Synodus nuncupabitur, quæ innumeris plane dissidijs Ecclesiam repleuit? Quis Synodum appellabit, quæ Saracenorum Apocrisiarios sui iudices, ac legum latores constituit? Quibus connumerabitur Synodis, quæ reliquis aliis Synodis contraria decernere non vera est? quæ insontes & absque vllo examine condemnauit? Quæ Ecclesiastica iura omnia, & Ciuiles leges deturbauit, & euertit? Hanc enim ob causam Orientis sanctissimæ sedes illius actiones abdicarunt, & irritas declararunt, & anathemati subiecerunt. Itemq; Βασιλεὺς ὁ Θεοσ-βέστατος μητροπολίτης Μαρτυροπολέως, ἐ τυπ[?]ερτὴς Ἀντιοχίας εἶπεν· Ὁ ἀγιώτατος Πάπας Μιχαὴλ Ἀλεξανδρείας ἅμα τοῖς συνὼν αὐτῷ ἀρχιερεῦσι Θεοῦ πόλεως ἅπαντα τὰ ἀγιωτάτης πατριάρχου Φωτίου πεπραγμένα ἀπεκήρυξε, καὶ ἀνεθημάτισε καὶ σὺν ὑποδεχομένους αὐτῷ πάντα ὁμοίως ἀναθέματα καθυπέβαλε, ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος Πατριάρχης ὁ ἁγιώτατος Θεοδόσιος καὶ αὐτὸς, καὶ σὺν ὑποδεχομένους αὐτῷ, καὶ σὺν ὀνομάζοντας αὐτῷ Σωφόδον τὸ αὐτοῦ κείμενον καὶ κυρίως. Basilius pijssimus Metropolita Martyropolitanus, & Locumtenens Antiocheni dixit; sanctissimus Papa Michaël Alexandrinus una cum illis qui cum eo erant Dei Præsulibus iam olim omnia, quæ contra sanctissimum Patriarcham Photium acta sunt, & abdicauit, & anathematizauit, & eos, qui illa excipiunt, eodem anathemate subiecit. Similiter & meus Patriarcha sanctissimus Theodosius & ipsa, & ipsis assentientes, & vocantes eam Synodum eodem iudicio iudicauit, & condemnauit. Similia repetunt Cosmas Presbyter, & Alexandrini Apocrisiarius, Elias locumtenens Hierosolymitani, & deniq; tota Synodus clamauit.
units.tr: By what reasoning will that be called a synod which has filled the Church with countless dissensions? Who will call a synod that made Saracen apocrisiaries its judges and lawgivers? With what synods will that be numbered which decrees what is contrary to all the other synods and is not true? Which condemned the innocent without any examination? Which overthrew and subverted all ecclesiastical rights and civil laws? For this reason the most holy sees of the East rejected its acts, declared them void, and subjected them to anathema. Likewise, Basil, the most pious Metropolitan of Martyropolis and locum tenens of Antioch, said: "The most holy Pope Michael of Alexandria, together with the bishops who were with him, long ago cast off and anathematized all the acts done against the most holy Patriarch Photius, and subjected to the same anathema those who received them. Likewise our most holy Patriarch Theodosius, and he himself, and those who accept them, and those who call that synod valid, he has judged and condemned by the same sentence" [Βασίλειος ὁ εὐσεβέστατος μητροπολίτης Μαρτυροπόλεως, ἐπίτροπος Ἀντιοχείας εἶπεν· ὁ ἁγιώτατος Πάπας Μιχαὴλ Ἀλεξανδρείας…]. Cosmas the presbyter and the apocrisiary of Alexandria, Elias the locum tenens of Jerusalem, and finally the whole synod, repeated similar words and shouted.

units.la: Ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κεφαλαίῳ τὸ ἀγιώτατον Πάπα Ἰωάννου τὸ ἄλλων ἀπάντων μᾶλλον ἐφευρίσκομεν. ἡμεῖς δὲ ὡς πολλάκις ἐφημεν καὶ τὸ ἁγιώτατον Πάπαν Ἰωάννην ἐκ τῶν αὐτῶν ἐκείνων αἱρεσιν, πάντα ἐκ τῆς ἁγιωτάτης μὴ παρχιάρχε γραφέντα καὶ λαλησάντων. Καὶ αὐτὸ ἡμᾶς μὴ ἀποβάλλομεν, [?]ινωἰνωθέντες αὐτῷ. καὶ κοινωνήσαντες, ἐ συλλήτρεσθαι ψυόμενοι[?]. In hoc capite sanctissimi Papa Ioannis per quam maxime gauisi sumus. Nos enim, ut sæpissime diximus, antequam sanctissimus Papa Ioannes illarum impiarum euersionem decreuisset, omnia aduersus sanctissimum nostrum Patriarcham scripta siue dicta anathemati tradidimus, & reiecimus vniti cum ipso, & communicantes, & comministri effecti. Nondum de abroganda Synodo decretum Pontificis innotuerat, & ipsi propria authoritate Synodum & abdicarunt, & anathemati subiecerunt. Quis similia in Ecclesia, si tamen in Ecclesiæ vnione viuit, ausus est? Synodum summi Pontificis authoritate coactam, quatuor Patriarcharum consensu confirmatam, tot subscriptionibus Episcoporum munitam, absque authoritate Pontificis Romani, nullo Patriarcharum, vel eorum locumtenentium congressu, nulla Episcoporum congregatione coacta adeo temere condemnatam, & reiectam fuisse? Quis hic Schismaticorum astum? Quis excommunicatorum perfidiam, & conatus temerarios non videt? Quis hos eosdem Photij fautores, post sententiam a Nicolao, & Adriano Romæ, & Byzantij a Synodo generali latam ab excommunicatione absoluat, cum in perfidia perstiterint, & Ecclesiæ gremio restituat? Esto restituti sint a Ioanne, sed ipsi ante Ioannis prætensam restitutionem, & Synodos abdicauerant, & irritas declarauerant. Et Synodus, quæ similia adeo fidenter agit, legitima fuerit? Nouum item est, & nunquam alias, nec ante, nec post tempora Photij auditum, Ecclesiam Romanam semel ab ipso in Ecclesia Synodali calculo approbatum reprobasse. Sed hæc quoque vti & alia a Schismaticis, & Photianis immutata fuisse indicio est; quod similia de condemnatione dictorum, & factorum contra Photium in monumentis antiquis Græcorum non habeantur. Constantinus Leonis, frater, qui magistro suo multum debuit Photio, Anno Domini 920. Indictione 4. post restitutum Photium anno 43. & Acta huius Synodi accurate scire poterat, in Tomo Vnionis Synodicas acclamationes referens, inter alia hæc quoque complectitur. Γερμανῦ, Ταρασίου, Νικηφόρου, καὶ Μεθοδίου, τῶν ἀοιδίμων [?] καὶ μακαρίων Πατριαρχῶν αἰωνία ἡ μνήμη. Ἰγνατίου, Φωτίου, Στεφάνου, καὶ Αντωνίου. &c. Germani, Tarasij, Nicephori, & Methodij celebrium beatorumq; Patriarcharum eterna sit memoria. Ignatij, Photij, Stephani, & Antonij &c. Tum subdit; Ἀπάντων τῶν ἁγίων Πατριαρχῶν Γερμανοῦ, Ταρασίου, Νικηφόρου, Μεθοδίου γραφέντα [?], ἢ λαληθέντα ἀνάθεμα. Vniuersa qua
units.tr: In this chapter we find the words of the most holy Pope John more than all the others. As we have often said, before the most holy Pope John decreed the overthrow of those impious acts, we had anathematized and rejected everything written or said against our most holy Patriarch, united with him, communicating with him, and made fellow ministers. The papal decree on abrogating the synod had not yet become known, and yet they of their own authority abdicated the synod and subjected it to anathema. Who in the Church, if indeed he lives in the unity of the Church, has dared to do such things? That a synod convened by the authority of the supreme Pontiff, confirmed by the consent of four patriarchs, and fortified by so many episcopal signatures, could be so rashly condemned and rejected, without the authority of the Roman Pontiff, without any patriarch or their locum tenentes meeting, and without any assembly of bishops, is it not monstrous? Who does not see here the cunning of schismatics and the reckless attempts of the excommunicated? Who will absolve these same supporters of Photius from excommunication, after the sentence pronounced against them by Nicholas and Adrian at Rome and by the general synod at Byzantium, while they persisted in their perfidy, and restore them to the bosom of the Church? Granted they were restored by John, yet before John's alleged restoration they had themselves abdicated and declared void the synods. And is a synod that acts so confidently in such matters a lawful one? It is also new, and never heard of before or after the time of Photius, that the Roman Church, once approved by Photius in a synodal vote in the Church, should have rejected it. But that these things, like others, were altered by schismatics and Photians is shown by the fact that no similar condemnation of the things said and done against Photius is found in the ancient records of the Greeks. Constantine, brother of Leo, who owed much to his teacher Photius, in the year of the Lord 920, the fourth indiction, forty-three years after Photius was restored, and who could know the acts of this synod accurately, reports in the Tome of Union the synodal acclamations and includes among other things these: "Let there be eternal memory of Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus, and Methodius, the celebrated and blessed patriarchs. Of Ignatius, Photius, Stephen, and Antony, etc." [Γερμανοῦ, Ταρασίου, Νικηφόρου, καὶ Μεθοδίου, τῶν ἀοιδίμων καὶ μακαρίων Πατριαρχῶν αἰωνία ἡ μνήμη· Ἰγνατίου, Φωτίου, Στεφάνου, καὶ Ἀντωνίου, κ.τ.λ.]. Then he adds: "Anathema to whatever was written or spoken against all the holy patriarchs Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus, and Methodius" [Ἀπάντων τῶν ἁγίων Πατριαρχῶν Γερμανοῦ, Ταρασίου, Νικηφόρου, Μεθοδίου γραφὲν ἢ λαληθὲν ἀνάθεμα. Universa qua…].

units.la: qua contra sanctos Patriarchas Germanum, Tarasium, Nicephorum, & Methodium scripta, vel dicta sunt, anathema. Sic edita sunt in Iure Graeco-Romano apud Leunclauium. Sic leguntur fere in omnibus manuscriptis Codicibus. Quae de scriptis, dictisque aduersus Photium in Synodo referuntur, nullo modo, si ea fuissent, homo addictissimus Photio praeterijsset. Ea igitur, vel Synodo a recentioribus Schismaticis assuta sunt, vel Synodus illa prorsus coacta non fuerat, ex qua sua haurire potuerat Constantinus. Quis enim adeo inquam sententia tulisset? In Romanis, & Constantinopolitana Synodis examinatur causa Ignatij, & Photij, & re perspecta tanquam iniusfor[?] condemnatur Photius; Ignatius pastor legitimus sedem recuperat: ipsorum etiam Schismaticorum calculo Photius maximorum, & plurimorum, eorumque atrocissimorum criminum reus est: Ignatius insons, ac innocens, & per vim, ac iniuriam a sede deturbatus, & varie grauissimeque afflictus, ac pene consectus. Hinc Photius in Ecclesiasticis Graecorum officijs nullus vsquam apparet, Ignatius inter Sanctos relatus habet suapro dignitate Sanctorum praeconia, solemnesqi[?] laudationes. Non ergo potuit haec Synodus iuste acta contra Photium condemnare, iniufte patrata in Ignatium amplecti. ni dicant, illi Synodo vnum fuiffe omnia, & vim, & æquitatem fimul cum iniuftitia, & fcelere collocaffe; quod ftultum eft afferere. Sed hæc alibi fufius.
units.tr: Whatever was written or said against the holy Patriarchs Germanus, Tarasius, Nicephorus and Methodius is anathema. So these words are printed in the Graeco-Roman law of Leunclavius, and so they are read in nearly all the manuscript codices. As for what is reported in the Synod about writings and sayings against Photius, if such things had existed, a man so devoted to Photius would not have passed them over. Either, then, these items were stitched into the Synod by recent schismatics, or that Synod was never really assembled, and so Constantine could not have drawn his material from it. For who, I ask, would have pronounced such a sentence? In the Roman and Constantinopolitan synods the case of Ignatius and Photius is examined, and once the matter is thoroughly understood Photius is condemned as an unjust usurper, while Ignatius, the lawful minister, recovers his see. Even by the reckoning of the schismatics themselves, Photius is guilty of very many and very atrocious crimes, whereas Ignatius is blameless and innocent, thrown from his see by force and injustice, and variously and most grievously afflicted, nearly worn to death. Hence Photius appears nowhere in the ecclesiastical offices of the Greeks, while Ignatius is numbered among the saints and has the praises and solemn eulogies that befit saints. This Synod, then, could not have justly condemned Photius, nor could it have unjustly embraced what was done against Ignatius, unless they say that one and the same Synod contained everything at once: force and fairness together with injustice and crime. That is foolish to assert. But these matters I have treated more fully elsewhere.

units.la: At id præceperat Ioannes. Si verba Ioannis confiderentur in Epiftolis, longe hoc falfiffimum effe deprehenderetur. Nunquam Ioannes infontem, & a culpa immunem declarauit, imo uti nefarijs flagitijs contaminatiffimum, iuffit in plena Synodo, crimina confitendo misericordiam exorare, tum ob delicta poenitentia peracta in fedem collocari. Hi vero Synodi cognitores, & iudices terminos facultatis fibi conceffæ prætergredientes, nullum ab ipfo libellum confeffionis exigunt, nullam poenitentiam imponunt, & nullo præuio examine, tumultuofe iufte acta in Synodis condemnant, iniufte peracta in Ignatium deofculantnr. An non eft hoc insanire acerbiffime? Vbi leges? Vbi iudicia? & monftra, & prodigia aliun, de quæris? Zacharias Metropolita Chalcedonensis ibidem;
units.tr: Yet John had prescribed otherwise. If the words of John are considered in his Epistles, this claim will be seen to be utterly false. John never declared Ignatius innocent and free from fault; rather, as one defiled by most wicked crimes, he ordered him to beg for mercy in a full Synod by confessing his offences, and only then, after repentance had been performed for his sins, to be restored to his see. But these examiners and judges of the Synod, overstepping the limits of the authority granted to them, demand from him no written confession, impose no penance, and without any prior examination condemn in a tumultuous manner what was justly done in the Synods, and embrace with kisses what was unjustly done against Ignatius. Is this not madness of the bitterest kind? Where are the laws? Where are the trials? Why do you look elsewhere for monsters and portents? Zacharias, Metropolitan of Chalcedon, there says:

units.la: Οὐκ ἐν αὐτῷ [?] ὁ μόνῳ, οὐδὲ ἐν πᾶσι [?] χώρᾳ λαοῦ [?] ἡ [?] βασιλείᾳ [illegible, ~12 letters] ἀλλὰ μικρᾷ [?] παῖς ἐπήλθε τοῖς λόγοις τοῦ γλῶ [?] τῆς πλάνης [illegible, ~10 letters].
units.tr: Not in him alone, nor in every region of the people, nor in the kingdom [illegible] but a little child came upon the words of the tongue of error [illegible].

units.la: Καὶ μάρτυς ἡ Ἀφρικῶν [?] χώρα, ἡ ἐν Μεσοποταμίᾳ, καὶ ἔθνη ὁλόκληρα βαρβαρικά, καὶ ὠμὸν τὴν ζωὴν διαζῶντα βίον τὰς ὑπὲρ Διδασκαλίας τῆς παλαιᾶς ἀπαλλαμ-ῥύτες πλανῆς, καὶ [?]εἰς τὸ φῶς χειραγωγηθέντα δι' αὐτῆ τῆς εὐσεβείας κηρύγματος. Nec in isto tantummodo, neq; in populo sibi subiecto pietatem circumscripsit, sed universum fere terrarum orbem suis sermonibus peragrauit, homines ab errore conuertens. Testis hic aderit Armenorum regio, & Mesopotamia, & nationes integrae, quae prius barbaram, atque efferatam vitam ducentes, monitis illius ab erroribus liberatae, ad lumen pietatis praedicatione abductae sunt. Somnia. Et ne inferior reputaretur Ignatio, in fine Synodi additur. Οἱ ἁγιώτατοι τοποτηρηταὶ τῆς Πρεσβυτέρας Ῥώμης ἔπεν. Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς, ὅτι ἡ ἀγαθὴ φήμη τὰ ἀξιωπάτα [?]Φωτὸς τῷ Παῤῥισάρχου ὑμῶν μόνον εἰς τὸν καθ' ἡμᾶς χώραν, ἀλλὰ εἰς ἅπασαν τὸν κόσμον ἐξελήλυθεν, ἡ τοσοῦτον λόγος τὸ βέβαιον ἔχουσα, ὅσον ἔργοις τὰ πέρα[?]στα. οὐ μόνον ἐν Γαλλίᾳ, ἀλλὰ ἐν Ἰταλίᾳ ἡ [?]ἐν πάσῃ τῇ ὑφ' ἥλιον γῇ. ἡ τῶν μάρτυρες [?]οὐχ μόνον οἱ ἐλλάδες μεπόντες γλώσσας, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ βαρβαρικὸν, ἡ ὠφέλει[?]σθαι, ὅπερ ἐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ ὁμοίως ἐν σοφίᾳ, ἡ γνώσει, ὅτι ἐλεημοσύνῃ, σωφροσύνῃ, ἐν χρηστότητι, ἡ ζαπένωσις, ἡ ὅπ πάντοτε τὰ ἔργα πλείονα τῶν λόγων αὐτοῦ εἰσιν. Ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ὁ ὑποσολικὸς τὰς τῆς βασιλέως [?]καθαρὸς, ἡ ὑμετέρας δύναμιν ὅπως ἀμφοτέρας ἀπέστελεν ἡμᾶς ἐλαχίστους, ἵνα μὴ ὑμῖν τῷ Ἐκκλησίαν τῷ Θεῷ ὡς ἐν συναγαγῶ-μὴν.
units.tr: The land of the Africans bears witness, and so does the region in Mesopotamia, and whole barbarian nations, living a savage and brutish life, who were freed from the error of their former teaching and led by the hand into the light through the proclamation of piety. Nor did he confine his piety to that one nation or to the people subject to him, but he travelled through almost the whole circuit of the earth with his discourses, turning men from error. Armenia and Mesopotamia will bear witness here, and whole nations which, previously living a barbaric and savage life, were freed by his warnings from their errors and led into the light by the preaching of piety. Dreams. And lest he be thought inferior to Ignatius, it is added at the end of the Synod: The most holy locum tenentes of Elder Rome said: "Blessed is God [Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός], that the good reputation of your most worthy Patriarch Photius has gone out not only into our region but into the whole world, and that it holds its firmness not by rumour alone but has matched its deeds to its fame. It has reached not only Gaul and Italy but every land under the sun. Witnesses to this are not only those who know the Greek tongue, but the barbarous and most savage peoples themselves, that there is none like him, neither in wisdom, nor in learning, nor in giving alms, nor in compassion, nor in integrity, nor in self-contempt; and that his works always exceed his words and are more numerous."

units.la: [?] Greek passages are only partly legible at this scan quality; uncertain letters and words are marked. μὴν, ὁ δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ ματος τὸ ἀξίως γένηται, καὶ ἐν σῶμα, καὶ μία ποίμνη ἐφ᾽ ἑνὶ ποιμένι [?]. Sanctissimi Locumtenentes senioris Romæ dixerunt. Benedictus Deus, quod bona fama sanctissimi Photij Patriarchæ, non tantum in nostram regionem, sed in vniuersum mundum exiuit, non rumore solum firmitatem habens, sed operibus præstitis fines illius complexa; nec solum modo in Italiam & Galliam peruenit, sed in omnem terram, quæ sub sole est, & hoc testantur non tantum, qui linguam callent Græcam, sed barbaræ ipsæ, & efferatissimæ gentes, quod non est similis illi, neque in sapientia, neque in doctrina, neque in erogandis eleemosynis, neque in commiseratione, neque in integritate, & sui ipsius despicientia; & quod semper opera sermones illius excedunt, & numerosiora sint. Dominus noster Apostolicus Imperatoris precibus, & vestris supplicationibus flexus, misit nos minimos, vt una vobiscum Dei Ecclesiam in vnum congregemus, quod mediante Spiritu sancto peractum est, & vnum corpus, & vnus grex sub uno pastore coaluistis. Vin maiora? Πεγοκτὴν ὁ Θεοφιλέστατος Ἀγχιστικόπος Καισαρείας εἶπε. Ἑώσον ἐπαρτὴν ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας τὸν τῷ σύμπαντος κόσμου τὴν δύναμιν λαχόντα εἰς τύπον τῶν ἀγχοι-[?] μόνου Χρηστοῦ τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν. ὁ καὶ ἀναλαβὼν ὁ μακάριος ὑπεζωγράφησε Παῦλος εἰπών· ἔχοντες δὲ αἰτίαν ἀγαθὴν [?] Τολ-μήμήσα γὰρ μοι ὁ λόγος καὶ μέχρι τάτης [?] ἐπιβλέψαι, [?] ἐχθὲς ἂν ἦν ἡμερόφων Θεὸς [?] ἐκλαῖν οὖν [?] τὴν χαίρειν βι-[?]ωύζας. Οἱ ἀμφὶ [?] τὸ τοπότηρται [?] δ᾽ ἀφεβυτέρως [?] Ῥώμης εἶπεν. Ἀλλὰ δὴ ἡμᾶς [?] οἱ εἰς τὰ ἐχαλά [?] δ᾽ [?] γῆς καὶ οἰκουμένης ταῦτα ἀνέκομεν. Πεγκόπιος ὁ Καισαρείας ἔφη. Τοῦτο εἰδότες οἱ ὑψη-λοὶ καὶ μεγάλοι Βασιλεῖς ἡμῶν [?] δι᾽ ἀπνευον πίστιν, καὶ πόθον ἔχοντα εἰς τὸν ἀρχιερέα ἡμῶν. ὃ μόνον ἦ αὐτὸ, ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶς ἀρχιερεὺς, καὶ ἱερεὺς μοναχός τι, καὶ οἱ ἐν λαϊκῇ καὶ ζῶσά τῆ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἰσχύων, ἡ μαθητὴς, καὶ ἐκ τῆς πληρώματος αὐτοῦ πάντες ἐλάβομεν, ὥσπερ οἱ παρακλητοὶ δυσκόλοι ἐκ τῆς κυρίου ἡμῶν Γνοῦ Χεί-στοῦ. Procopius Dei amantissimus Cæsarea Cappadocia Archiepiscopus dixit; Talem addecebat vere esse eum, cui totius mundi gubernatio commissa est, Præsulum principem Christum Deum nostrum repræsentantem, quod & præripiens beatus Paulus præfiguravit dicens, Habentes ergo Pontificem magnum, qui penetravit Cœlos. Nanque oratio mea eo vsque progredi audebit, cum soleat Scriptura Deos appellare eos, qui in gratia vitam agunt. Sanctissimi locum tenentes senioris Romæ dixerunt. Verum est, quod dixisti, & nos extrema terræ incolentes similia audimus. Procopius Cæsarea dixit. Hoc scientes sublimes magnique nostri Imperatores, ardentem fidem, & desiderium in nostrum Pontificem possidentes, nec solum ipsi, sed & quilibet Præsul, & Sacerdos, necnon Monachi, & qui in statu viuunt, affecle illius fumus, & discipuli, & ex complemento illius accepimus, quemadmodum celeberrimi Apostoli ex Domino nostro Iesu Christo. Sileant nunc post unum Photium linguae difertissimae doctissimaque tot Patrum, tot Sanctorum pro propaganda Fide eaque stabilienda certamina pro derelictis habeantur. Gestaomnia[?], & basilica in genus humanum a pijs viris facinora, antequam Photius in Patriarchatum insereretur, & eo extincto, edita, silentio inuoluantur. Photiana tantum volent per ora virum, & ut cum Procopio insaniam, unus Photius terrarum orbis universi gubernationem obtineat. Unus Photius in Ecclesia Dei pro Deo, & Christo habeatur, quem praefigura verat Paulus. Unus Photius universos fideles, illos etiam, qui in dignitatibus Ecclesiasticis supereminent, complemento suo, & gratia aeque atq; Christus suos discipulos ditet. Eijciatur Deus de Solio, & Christus, & in eo reponatur Photius. Vides nugas? Vides blasphemias? Et Synodum, quae similia audet, & assensu comprobat, Synodum dices, & non potius fanaticorum hominum, & omnia audentium congregationem, vel potius figmentum? Quidquid tamen hi delirant, pius Graecorum animus aspernatus est, & vti abhominabilem pestem, & perniciosum venenum reiecit. Hinc Deo vires addente Photius cum suis tacitus negligitur, Ignatius relatus in Sanctos annuis præconijs celebratur, & eum tum Latina Ecclesia, tum Græca inuocat sibi propitium, & decretum de abolendis actis contra Photium Photiani sibi seruant, & in latebris fouent.
units.tr: Our lord, the Apostolic one, yielding to the prayers of the Emperor and your supplications, sent us, the least of men, so that together with you we might gather the Church of God into one, which has been accomplished through the Holy Spirit: you have become one body and one flock under one shepherd. Would you have greater things? The most God-beloved Bishop of Caesarea said: "Truly it is fitting that he who has received the power over the whole world be praised as a type of the Chief Shepherd, Christ our God; and the blessed Paul, having taken this up, portrayed him, saying: 'Having therefore a great high priest, who has passed into the heavens' [Hebr. 4.14]. For my speech will dare to go so far, since Scripture is accustomed to call those who live in grace gods." The most holy locum tenentes of the elder Rome said: "It is true what you have said, and we who dwell at the ends of the earth hear similar things." Procopius of Caesarea said: "Knowing this, our lofty and great Emperors, possessing a burning faith and desire toward our Pontiff, and not only they but every prelate and priest, and also monks and those who live in the religious state, we have been his followers and disciples, and from his fullness we have received, just as the most famous Apostles did from our Lord Jesus Christ." Let the eloquent and learned tongues of so many Fathers and so many Saints now be silent, and let their struggles for spreading and establishing the Faith be regarded as abandoned. Let all the deeds and the works of pious men toward the human race, done before Photius was put into the Patriarchate and buried in silence after his death, be wrapped in oblivion. They want only the Photian mouths to speak, and, with Procopius, in madness, one Photius to hold the government of the whole world. One Photius is to be held in the Church of God in place of God and Christ, whom Paul prefigured. One Photius is to enrich all the faithful, including those who stand out in ecclesiastical dignities, with his fullness and grace, just as Christ enriches his disciples. Let God be cast from the throne, and Photius be placed in it. Do you see the trifles? Do you see the blasphemies? And will you call a Synod, the one that dares such things and approves them with its assent, a Synod, and not rather a gathering of fanatical men who dare everything, or rather a fiction? Whatever these men rave about, the pious mind of the Greeks has rejected and cast off as a loathsome plague and a deadly poison. Hence, with God adding strength, Photius with his followers is silently ignored, Ignatius is recounted among the Saints and celebrated with yearly proclamations, and both the Latin Church and the Greek call on him as favourable to them; and the Photians keep the decree for abolishing the acts against Photius and foster it in hiding places.

units.la: CAPVT VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Ex approbatione, & annumeratione Synodi Nicæna Secunda contra Iconoclastas procu- rata a Photio, hoc idem confirmatur.
units.tr: That the same point is confirmed by the approval and listing of the Second Synod of Nicaea against the Iconoclasts, which Photius secured.

units.la: IN quinta Actione Photius in eo totus est, vt Synodus Septima, Nicæna nempe Secunda aduersus Iconomachos recepta inter alias sex Oecumenicas Synodos collocetur, ijsdemque atque illæ priuilegijs gaudeat, nec minoris dignitatis, ac firmitatis sit. Φώ-τιος ὁ Πατριάρχης ἐστιν[?]. Τὴν ἁγίαν[?], Ϛ οἰκουμενικὴν Σύνοδον, ἥτις ἐν τῇ ἐν Βιθυνίᾳ Νικαίᾳ τὸ ἕβδομον[?] σωσῆν[?] εἶπε Ἀδριανὸς τῷ μακαριωτάτῳ Πάπᾳ Ῥώμης, καὶ Ταρασίος τῷ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατριάρχῃ Κωνσταντινουπόλεως, ἥ μὴ καθ' ἡμᾶς Ἐκκλησία αὐτὴ μὲν ἑβδόμην ὀνομάζει[?] τι, καὶ ἀναχηρύττει[?], τὴν τῶν λοιπῶν ἁγίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐξ Συνόδοις τοῖς ἴσοις αὐτοῦ ἀρεσβείσης[?] γεγαῖς[?]. ἠδὴ τὴν Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησία, ὡς ἂν τις; ἢ ἐ οἱ τῆς ἀναζολῆς Θεῖνοι τὰ δόγματα ὑμῶν ἀπλανῶς ὑπολήψ[?], καὶ ἀσεβέ-σπινι[?]. Πεὶ ἢ τὰ συμαριθμὸν αὐτῷ τὰς λοιπὰς ἀξίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐξ Συνόδοις[?], καὶ ἱβδό-μῳ αὐτῷ αἰακημούῃ[?], ἵνα ὥσπαν ἓν ἀμ-φιβολία. Φήμη μὲν γὰρ πιαύτη ἀξιαληλλ[?]. Τὸ δὲ ἀληθὲς ὅπω καὶ νῦν ἐπισπάσθα[?]. Photius Patriarcha dixit. Sanctam, & Oecumenicam Synodum, quae Nicaeae in Bithynia secunda congregata est, sub Adriano beatissimo Romano Pontifice, & sancto Tarasio Patriarcha Constantinopolitano, nostra Ecclesia Septimam eam semper appellat, & praedicat, & inter alias sanctas, & Oecumenicas sex Synodos numerat, & paribus privilegiis exornat. Et Romana Ecclesia, similiter & Orientales sedes dogmata illius accipiunt, & fovent. Sed a nonnullis forte dubitatur, an inter alias sex sanctas, & Oecumenicas Synodos numeranda veniat; talis enim rumor ad nos praefertur. Veruntamen, an verus sit, ad hoc tempus ignoramus. Et alibi; Κατασκευάζοντα[?], καὶ κυρώζοντα[?], μὴ μόνον αὐτὴ ὡς ἀσεβῆ πάντα τὰ δόγματα, καὶ θεσμισμάτα[?], ἀλλὰ. καὶ τὸ συμαριθμεῖν αὐτῷ τὰς ἀξίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐξ Συνόδοις ἐβδόμην μετ' ἐκείνας ἀποδέχομεν[?], καὶ λεγόμενον[?], καὶ τὰ ἴσα ταύταις ὑποφέρεσθαι[?]. Firmetur, ac stabiliatur non solum haec, quemadmodum illius dogmata, & decreta, sed inter alias sex sanctas, & Oecumeni-ninicas Synodos collocetur, & Septima locum post illas teneat, & Septima nuncupetur, & aqualia cum illis priuilegia possideat. Et respondet Synodus; Καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔτω φρονῶν [?], νῦν ὀνομάζων τῷ ἁγίῳ [?], καὶ οἰκουμενικῇ ἐν Νικαίᾳ τὴν δευτέραν ἁγίαν Σύνοδον, ἔστω ἀνάθεμα [?]. Et qui non ita tenet, & nuncupat sanctam, & Oecumenicam Synodum Nicaenam secundam sanctam Synodum, anathema fit. Et alibi; Οὕτως τῷ ἁγίῳ [?], καὶ οἰκουμενικῷ Σύνοδον τῷ ἐν Νικαίᾳ οὐσίᾳ [?] ἐκ [?] Σινόδοις [?]. ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν ἐκείναις οἱ ἀρχιερατικοὶ πάντες συνεδρᾶσαν [?] θεγροι [?], οἱ μὲν δι᾽ ἰωσῆφ [?], οἱ δὲ διὰ τοποτηρητῆς [?], τὸ πνσον [?], ἐ βέβαιον τῆς ἀληθείας προεστῶσαν [?], ἔτως ἐ αὐτή [?]. καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγιωτάτῃ Πάπα Ῥώμης ἔπεσσαν τηρεῖν ἡξιο [?], ὁμοίως ἡ ἐ ἐκ τῆς καὶ᾽ ἡμᾶς ἀπαλαίας θεσσεως [?]. Τὰ δόγματα αὐτῆς συνῄρηκαν [?], ἐ αἰκεῖα [?], καὶ ὁμοιόδηκαν [?] τῆς οἰκουμενικῶν ἐξ Σινόδου ὑπῆρχεν [?]. ὁ αὐτὸ τούτο μὲν ἀθεμάτου [?] ἐκ [?] μηδὲ ὀνομάζων οἰκουμενικὴν [?], ἐ ἰβ [?] Σινόδον, ταῖς ἄλλας [?], κἂν ἀ πλαμφ [?] λέγῃ [?], ἀναχαφεῖ [?]. Διὸ ἄγις ταύτῃ οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται [?] ὡς ἐκείνας τὰς ἁγίας [?], ἐ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐξ Σινόδου [?], ἀ ἀνάθεμα. Quisquis sanctam, & universalem Synodum Nicaea secundo celebratam non amplectitur, hic nec reliquas sex Synodos amplectitur. Nanque sicuti in illis omnes Archieratici throni convenerunt, hi [?] quidem per seipsos, alii vero per suos Oratores stabilitatem, & soliditatem dogmatum proposuerunt, pari ratione & ipsasanctissimi Papæ Romani locum tenentes habuit: sic quoque ex nostris Orientalibus sedibus. Et dogmata ipsius conformia, & propria, eiusdemque tenoris cum placitis sex Oecumenicarum Synodorum fuere. Qui itaque hanc non recipit, neque nuncupat universalem, vel SeptimamSynodum, alias, licet id non audeat dicere, non amplectitur. Quapropter, qui hanc non recipit sicuti alias sanctas, & universales sex Synodos, anathema. Et alibi; Διὸ [?]ἅπας ταύτῳ ἐκ τοῦ [?]ἄνης [?]ὡς ἐκείνας τὰς ἁγίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς [?]ἑξ Συνόδους, ἀνάθεμα. ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἐστιν, ἀνάθεμα. Quapropter quisquis illas non accipit ut alias sex Sanctas, & Oecumenicas Synodos, anathema sit. Sancta Synodus dixit. Anathema sit. Conatus Photij laudabiles sunt, decreta Synodi sancta. Anathema sit illi, qui prædictam Nicænam Synodum secundam, æque atque sex alias Oecumenicas Synodos non veneratur, & colit, & quod magis est, sancita illius non observat. Romana Ecclesia semper eam, sanctam, & legitimam agnovit, voce, & sententia sua comprobavit, & Septimã nominavit, & nunc quoq; colit, & comprobat, & ab aspersis ignominijs vendicat. Sed in hoc quoq; vafrum Photij ingenium, & Photianas, ut semel dicam, artes conspice. Non videbatur sibi percommode ca-dedere, hanc frequentissimam Synodum pro sola sui restitutione convocatam fuisse: nam vel solo nutu Pontificio, si Photius sibi iam imposita non complesset, infirmari poterat: ideoque addendum erat aliquid divinius, septimae nempe generalis Synodi cultus, & veneratio debita, locusque inter alias generales Synodos assignandus. Et ne id absque ratione fieri videretur, sedem Romanam, & reliquos Orientales thronos, uti similis erroris reos infamat. Quia vero putidum hoc mendacium de facili improbari, & reiici poterat, quasi de eo incertus sit, perplexe pronunciat; Similiter dogmata illius recipiunt, & fovent, sed illam aliis sanctis, & Oecumenicis Synodis sex non annumerarant, & eam Septimam appellare forte apud nonnullos in dubio est, ut nobis nunciatur, cum ad haec usque tempora veritatem ipsam non sumus assecuti. Et ineptius Nicolaus Hydruntinus ideo, ait, Romanos non acceptasse hanc Synodum Septimam, quod ante Photium post Sextam, Septimamque Synodum inter Orientales, ac Pontificios amicitia extincta erat, studiaque in partes diducta; quod plane refutavimus illius verbis ascriptis in Hottingero falso fallenteque. Sed quidquid sit de Romanis, & Orientalibus, illud modo examinandum est, an Synodi adeo dilectæ Photio, & ad quam promouendam operam suam locauerat, decreta, & statuta Photius seruauerit.
units.tr: In the fifth Action Photius takes the line that the Seventh Synod, namely the Second Synod of Nicaea against the Iconoclasts, should be counted among the other six ecumenical Synods, enjoy the same privileges as they do, and be no less authoritative or binding. [Greek text in the source is too garbled to reproduce reliably.] Photius the Patriarch said: the holy and ecumenical Synod that was gathered at Nicaea in Bithynia, the second, under Adrian, the most blessed Pope of Rome, and the holy Tarasius, Patriarch of Constantinople, our Church always calls and proclaims the Seventh, and numbers it among the other holy and ecumenical six Synods, and adorns it with equal privileges. And the Church of Rome, and likewise the Eastern sees, receive and cherish its dogmas. But some doubt perhaps whether it is to be numbered among the other six holy and ecumenical Synods; for such a rumour has been brought to us. Yet whether it is true, we do not know up to this time. And elsewhere: Let it be confirmed and established, not only this Synod, as well as its dogmas and decrees, but let it be placed among the other six holy Synods, let the Seventh hold the place after them, let it be called the Seventh, and let it possess privileges equal to theirs. And the Synod replies: "Whoever does not think thus, and does not call the Second Synod of Nicaea a holy and ecumenical Synod, let him be anathema." [ἀνάθεμα] And elsewhere: "Thus the holy and ecumenical Synod at Nicaea, ..." For just as in those Synods all the archiepiscopal thrones met, some in person, others through their envoys, and set forth the firmness and soundness of the truth, so likewise in this one the most holy Pope of Rome held the place of honour, and likewise our Eastern sees. Its dogmas agree with, and are the same as, those of the six ecumenical Synods. Therefore whoever does not accept this one, nor calls it ecumenical or the Seventh Synod, though he may not dare to say so openly, does not embrace the others either. Wherefore, whoever does not accept it as he accepts those holy six ecumenical Synods, let him be anathema. Therefore everyone who does not accept this as those holy and ecumenical six Synods, let him be anathema. The holy Synod is anathema. Quapropter quisquis illas non accipit ut alias sex Sanctas, & Oecumenicas Synodos, anathema sit. The holy Synod said: Anathema be to him. The efforts of Photius are praiseworthy; the decrees of the Synod are holy. Anathema be to him who does not venerate and honour the aforesaid Second Synod of Nicaea, equally with the six other ecumenical Synods, and, what is more, does not observe its decrees. The Roman Church has always acknowledged it as holy and lawful, has confirmed it by its voice and judgment, has named it the Seventh, and now also honours and confirms it, and defends it from the stains of disgrace. But in this too, look at the crafty cleverness of Photius, and, to say it once for all, his Photian arts. It did not seem to him quite fitting that this most crowded Synod had been called only for his own restoration; for by a mere nod of the Pope it could have been weakened, if Photius had not fulfilled the commands already laid upon him. Therefore something more divine had to be added: the due cult and veneration of a Seventh general Synod, and a place to be assigned to it among the other general Synods. And lest this should seem to be done without reason, he brands the Roman see and the other Eastern thrones as guilty of the same error. But because this stinking lie could easily be disproved and rejected, as if he were uncertain about it, he pronounces it ambiguously: They likewise receive and cherish its dogmas, but they have not numbered it among the other six holy and ecumenical Synods, and it is perhaps doubtful among some whether it is called the Seventh, as is reported to us, since up to this time we have not attained the truth itself. And Nicolaus of Otranto is more foolish when he says that the Romans did not accept this Seventh Synod because, before Photius, after the Sixth and Seventh Synods, friendship between the Easterns and the Papists had been extinguished and their zeal divided into parties; this I have plainly refuted from his own words, written in Hottinger falsely and deceptively. But whatever be the case with Romans and Easterns, the question now to be examined is whether Photius himself kept the decrees and statutes of that Synod, so dear to him, and for whose promotion he had hired his own efforts.

units.la: In Synodo Nicæna secunda ad illum diem antiquam Ecclesiæ consuetudinem retinentes Legati Pontificij præsident; in hac ab ea recedens, & ordinem rerum præuertens primum locum Photius occupat, secundum Pontificij concedit, & in omnibus Actionibus [illegible, ~7 letters] Photius: in ea semper Romani nomen præponitur, in hac Photij: in illa, vt mos erat, primi Legati Pontificij subscribunt, subsequitur Tarasius Patriarcha, in hac nulla subscriptio Photij est. Pudebat scilicet illum in similibus nævis, & patentibus Hagitijs sui nominis subscriptionem videri, homo pudentissimus, quod non veritus est Imperator, & illius filij. Septimæ Synodi Patres in literis Pontificijs contenta, absque vllo examine exosculantur; Photianæ illis impudentissime reluctantur, & apertissime aduersantur, clamantque, indebite illa sibi a Pontifice imponi: nunc ea se recipere, si suo vsui sutura sunt, dictitant: nunc sibi proposita a Pontifice despicientes silentio prætereunt. Non animaduertit Photius supremam Romanorum Pontificum auctoritatem, in Nicæna Synodo cognitam, qua etiam in illa declaratur, eos Orthodoxos non esse, qui ab ea dissentiunt. Et ne multa hic conferam, in Nicaena rei criminis in conspectu Synodi admissum crimen etiam libello exhibito fatentur, quod vocant Legem Ecclesiasticam canonice traditam desursum ab initio, tam a sanctis Apostolis, quam a successoribus eorum sanctis Patribus nostris, atque magistris, sed & sanctis, & universalibus sex Synodis, seu localibus Conciliis, quae orthodoxè collecta sunt, & ab haeresi quacunque ad Orthodoxam confessionem, & traditionem Catholicae Ecclesiae conversi in scriptis suam abnegant haeresim, & Fidem confiteantur Orthodoxam. Veniam de crimine petunt a Patribus, a quibus etiam sibi indulgentiam a Deo peti exorant: tum denique profitentur, se velle in posterum sequi Catholicae, & Apostolicae Ecclesiae dogmata. Et ne Photius contendat sermonem esse tantum de haeresi, non de aliis criminibus, discat ex ipsis ipsis Canonibus Patrum, exemploque Procli admittentis in communionem Aemilianum Hegumenum, quem Ecclesiae leges Palestinae Praepositum non noverant, aeque atque Photium Byzantij. An non legit Tarasij verba Act. 3. Tempore persecutionis quidam Episcoporum intolerabiles persecutiones pijs viris intulerunt. Novit tota sancta Synodus haec, quia Canon sanctorum Apostolorum, Episcopum, Presbyterum, vel Diaconum percutientem fideles delinquentes, aut infideles inique agentes, & per huiuscemodi timeri volentes deponi praecipit. Tum interrogat Synodum. Si intulit Episcopus quascunque plagas, & tormenta viris timentibus Dominum, qui tunc persecutionem patiebantur, est ne dignus Episcopatu? Sancta Synodus respondit. Non est dignus. Et in 4. Synodus exclamavit: Dioscorum foras mitte, eo quod manus iniecit super viros insontes. Et Gregorius Neocaesariensis, quia nullum persecutus fuerat, neque manus iniecerat, post praevaricationem, cum poenituisset eum, receptus est. Documenta haec de recipiendis delinquentibus clarissima sunt, quae probavit ipse Photius, & Synodus Photiana eodem Photio postulante confirmavit. In reconciliatione tamen Photij neglecta sunt.
units.tr: In the Second Nicene Synod, keeping the ancient custom of the Church up to that day, the papal legates presided. In this one, departing from that practice and reversing the order of proceedings, Photius occupies the first place and concedes the second to the papal legates, and in all the Actions [illegible] Photius. In the former the name of the Roman always comes first, in this one that of Photius. In the former, as was customary, the first papal legates subscribe, followed by Patriarch Tarasius; in this one there is no subscription by Photius. Surely he was ashamed to appear in such notorious and open disgraces with his name subscribed, a most shameless man, which the Emperor and his sons did not hesitate to do. The Fathers of the Seventh Synod embrace without any examination what is contained in the papal letters; the Photian party most impudently resist them and openly oppose them, and they cry out that these things were unduly imposed on them by the Pontiff. Now they say they will accept them if they are to be of use to their own purposes; now, scorning what has been put before them by the Pontiff, they pass it over in silence. Photius does not heed the supreme authority of the Roman Pontiffs, recognised at the Nicene Synod, by which it is also declared that those who dissent from it are not Orthodox. And not to multiply examples here: at Nicaea, those who had committed the crime in the sight of the Synod confessed it also in a written petition, which they called the "Ecclesiastical Law canonically handed down from above from the beginning, both by the holy Apostles and by their successors, our holy Fathers and teachers, and also by the holy and universal six Synods, or local Councils, which were gathered orthodoxly, and by which those who have turned from any heresy to the Orthodox confession and tradition of the Catholic Church renounce their heresy in writing and confess the Orthodox Faith."
