They seek pardon for their crime from the Fathers, and beg them to obtain indulgence for them from God; then at last they profess that they wish in future to follow the dogmas of the Catholic and Apostolic Church. And lest Photius contend that the discussion concerned only heresy and not other crimes, let him learn from the canons of the Fathers themselves, and from the example of Proclus, who admitted to communion Aemilianus the Hegumen, whom the laws of the Church had not known as Praepositus of Palestine, just as they had not known Photius at Byzantium. Has he not read the words of Tarasius? Act. 3. In a time of persecution certain bishops inflicted intolerable persecutions on pious men. The whole holy Synod knows this, because the canon of the holy Apostles orders that a bishop, presbyter, or deacon who strikes faithful who have offended, or who treats unbelievers unjustly, and who wishes by such means to be feared, be deposed. Then he asks the Synod: If a bishop has inflicted any blows and torments on men who fear the Lord, who then suffered persecution, is he worthy of the episcopate? The holy Synod replied: He is not worthy. And in the Fourth Synod they cried out: Cast Dioscorus out, because he laid hands on innocent men. And Gregory of Neocaesarea, because he had not persecuted anyone nor laid hands on anyone, after his transgression, when he had repented, was received back. These documents on receiving offenders back are very clear; Photius himself approved them, and the Photian Synod, at Photius's own request, confirmed them. Yet in Photius's reconciliation they were neglected.

units.la: Dum Photius ipse a Synodis Romanis sub Nicolao, & Constantinopolitana Generali sub Adriano depositus, eiectus, & uti invasor, neophytus, schismaticus, architectus mendaciorum, moechus, parricida, nouus Dioscorus, & nouus Iudas ob innumera scelera condemnatus, & excommunicatus, nulla eorum criminum confessione, nullo libello, nullo alio opere, quod minimam poenitentiam indicaret, peracto, vel absolutionis a crimine petitione oblata, intra Synodum immani fastu, & iactantia ab sese absolutus, & reconciliatus, ante etiam Legatos Pontificios ab ipsa prima Actione praesidet, pro imperio omnia facit, aliis praecipit, & uno verbo, basilicas edictiones, atque imperiosas habet. Non dum Ignatij familiarium vincula, flagra, plagaeque, & omnis generis tormenta oblivioni tradita sunt: adhuc caprarium stabulum Ignatij tolerantiam clamat. Prometus, Numera, Terebinthus, atque Hiera insulae, & Metylene Ignatij duris exilijs celebrantur: molares excusi duo, vectibusque geminis pedes alligati, & angustum ergastulum cum summa rerum omnium inopia Photij tyrannidem, atque immanitatem praedicant: Blasij Chartophylacis lingua detruncata sonore iniustitiam vociferat: Pallium, Penula, Saccus, & reliqua Pontificalia indumenta a sancto viro per vim distracta, & lacera in terram impudenter proiecta vicem suam non leniter dolent: Minima haec sunt Photio, atrociora addenda. Condemnatus iniuste Ignatius, colaphis caeditur, miserè diuexatur, & cum frigus recrudesceret, unica tunicula induts discruciatur, & binis hebdomadis carcere conclusus, extrema prope fame conficitur: sepulchrum Copronymi tanti viri in eo mora, & tormentis in Sanctuarium versum est: ne lumina effoderentur, & manus praecinderentur, intempesta nocte sub vili, ac seculari veste, geminas sportas ab humeris una a pertica suspensas baiuli ritu gestans, deceptis custodibus, uno comitatus discipulo suo Cypriano ab hostium improbitate se subtrahit, & peregrinus & errans per Propontidis insulas, & solitudines egeni instar victum emendicat: & , ut finiam, silebo sannas, iurgia, contumelias, dicteria ad atterendum tantum virum ingeniose excogitata. Vis diriora? Indecoris Ignatio figuris charta vitiata cum tanti Sacerdotij deformatione, & programmata insigni turpitudine decolorata non dum extincta sunt: in Nicolaum Pontificem Romanum, in eiusque vitam falsae criminationes coniectae, & ex improbissimo Photij suaque similium ore excommunicatio in tantam maiestatem acrius, & grauius ad ulciscendas iniurias, ultioni promptum Deum iustissimum iudicem provocant. Et sic Photius omni nefario scelere commaculatus Nicaenae Secundae Synodi ὅρισμος[?], καὶ ἀναθεματισμὸς[?] feruasse dicendus est, qui nec minimum in Concilio poenitentiae vestigium, nec volam ostendit? Aut igitur in hac Actione Nicaena na Secunda approbata non est, aut si approbata, quæ in ista Photiana habentur, commentitia sunt, & præsumptuose conficta. Qui enim fieri potest, ut quæ semel approbauit, eodem ipso momento contraria peragens Synodus reprobet? Ego equidem nolo indigna, quæ facit Photius, digna habere.
units.tr: Photius himself was deposed and cast out by the Roman Synods under Nicholas and by the general Synod of Constantinople under Adrian. He was condemned and excommunicated as a usurper, a neophyte, a schismatic, a architect of lies, an adulterer, a parricide, a new Dioscorus and a new Judas for countless crimes. Yet without confessing any of those crimes, without presenting any written statement, without performing any work that might show even the slightest repentance, and without even asking for absolution from the charges, he absolved and reconciled himself within the Synod with monstrous arrogance and boasting. Before the Papal legates he presides from the very first Action, does everything by his own authority, gives orders to others, and, in a word, issues royal decrees and imperious commands. The chains, whips and blows inflicted on Ignatius's household, and every kind of torture, have not yet been consigned to oblivion; the goat-shed where Ignatius was kept still cries out his endurance. The islands of Promete, Numera, Terebinthus, Hiera and Metylene, where Ignatius was harshly exiled, are famous. Two molar teeth were knocked out, his feet were bound with a pair of bars, and his narrow prison, with every kind of want, proclaims the tyranny and savagery of Photius. The tongue of Blasius the chartophylax, cut out, cries aloud the injustice done. The pallium, the penula, the sackcloth and the other pontifical garments, torn from the holy man by force, lacerated and shamelessly flung on the ground, grieve in their own way no lightly. These are the small things against Photius; worse must be added. Ignatius, condemned unjustly, is beaten with blows, shamefully mistreated, and when the cold grew more bitter he was tortured while wearing a single little tunic; shut up in prison for two weeks, he was worn down almost to death by hunger. In that place the tomb of Copronymus (a man of such stature) was turned into a place of delay and torment, a sanctuary turned into a prison. Lest his eyes be gouged out and his hands cut off, on a moonless night, dressed in a cheap secular garb and carrying two baskets on his shoulders, hung from a pole in the manner of a porter, he slipped away from the hostility of his enemies, the guards having been deceived; accompanied by one disciple, Cyprian, he wandered as a stranger through the islands of the Propontis and the wastes, and like a beggar begged for his food. And, to finish, I will pass over the mockery, the abuse, the insults and the taunts cleverly devised to wear down so great a man. Do you want harsher things? Writing defaced with shameful figures of Ignatius, with the disfigurement of so great a priesthood, and placards blackened with notorious obscenity, have not yet been extinguished; false accusations have been hurled against Nicholas, the Roman Pontiff, and against his life; and excommunication, uttered from the most wicked mouth of Photius and his like, has provoked against so great a majesty, more fiercely and gravely, God, most just judge and ready to avenge injuries. And so Photius, stained with every wicked crime, is said to have observed the definition and anathematism [ὅρισμος, ἀναθεματισμός] of the Second Synod of Nicaea, who did not show the least trace of repentance in the Council, nor even a wish for it? Either therefore he was not approved in this Action of the Second Nicene Synod, or, if he was approved, what is found in this Photian Action is made up and presumptuously fabricated. For how can it be that a Synod which has once approved something should, by acting in the very same moment contrary to it, reject it? For my part I do not wish to hold worthy what Photius does, which is unworthy.

units.la: Si dicas Photium poenitentiam egisse, quod referunt Ioannes Veccus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, Oratione de unione Ecclesiarum, & Constantinus Meliteniota. Esto, Photius poenitentiam egerit. Et tum de falsitate Acta ista Photiana apertissime arguuntur: dum in illis de huiusmodi poenitentia mentio non habeatur: quam verosimile fuerit ob seruandam dignitatem Photio suo a Schismaticis esse subtractam. Neque enim illis videbatur decorum, crimen appingere Photio, quod sane ille non effugisset, si sua confessione, illud fassus fuisset; & poenitentia acta confirmasset. Vel si parte illa Synodus detruncata non est, hæc plane, quæ nunc habetur Photiana, Photiana illa non est, in qua & poenitentiam egit Photius, Ecclesiæ Romanæ reconciliatus, quæ ubi in lucem prodierit, si tamen unquam prodibit, quæ nunquam fuit, tum plane rem aliter atque hic digeritur, transfactam esse conspiciemus.
units.tr: If you say that Photius did penance, as John Veccus, Patriarch of Constantinople, in his oration on the union of the Churches, and Constantine Meliteniotes report: granted, let Photius have done penance. Then it is most clearly proved that these Photian Acts are false, since no mention of such repentance is made in them. How likely it is that, to preserve the dignity of Photius, his own people among the schismatics removed it! For it did not seem fitting to them to lay that crime on Photius, which he certainly would not have escaped had he confessed it and confirmed it by an act of penance. Or, if that part of the Synod was not cut out, then that Photian Action which is now held is plainly not the Photian Action in which Photius also did penance and was reconciled to the Roman Church. When that appears in the light, if it ever does (and it never existed), then we shall plainly see that the matter has been carried through otherwise than it is arranged here.

units.la: CAPUT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: Dictis Schismaticorum inter se longissime diver- sis Sextæ, & Septimæ Actionum com- mentum reijcitur.
units.tr: The Sixth and Seventh Actions are dismissed as a fiction, since the schismatics' statements about them differ widely.

units.la: ET hæc de quinque Synodi illius Actionibus, quid vero de Sexta, & Septima? Ego equidem dicerem cum Comico, illam compositis mendacijs aduenisse audacia, columen confultis dolis. Et licet Schismaticorum nonnulli, & illi inter paucos, nullius fere dignationis, & qui viribus ad res pessimas vtuntur, eas cum reliquis quinque prioribus numerandas esse censuerint, illisque vim eandem concesserint, attamen reliqui etiam ex schismate fere præcipui, vti confictas a nebulonibus, vt nullius roboris reiecerunt, & decreta illarum veluti nugatoria cum alijs eiusdem Synodi, & cum aliarum Synodorum decretis locum habere noluerunt. Eas amplexati sunt Nilus Thessalonicensis, in Responsione ad Argumentum quadragesimum nonum Latinorum. Η' ὃ μὴ τὴν ἐβδόμην οἰκουμενικὴ Σύνοδος, ἧς τὸ πλήρωμα πατέρων ἀριθμὸς ὀξδοήκοντα, καὶ τεσσαρακο-σίων[?] σιων, ὡς Λατῖνοι ἐν ταῖς κανόσι τῆς ἑαυτῶν φασι τῷ μὴ τῆς Ἐκκλησιῶν ἀρχῶλω [?] τὴν τῆς ἑαυτῆς ποιήσαι, τῷ δὲ Ἀρεσθήκλω, ὃν ἐκ τῆς ὑῆ τὸ πνεῦμα ὡς αἰτίαν τῆς σκανδάλων [?] ἐξορέων ἐκ τῆ Θεῷ συμβόλου πόρῳ τὸν τίθησι, καὶ οἱ ἐν τόπον ἢ ἐν τῇ οἰκουμενικῇ ταύτῃ Σωσόδω τὲ Πάπα αἱ ἀπαλληξεῖτις, Παῦλος φημί, καὶ Εὐγένιος οἱ Ἐπίσκοποι, καὶ Πέτρος Καρδινάλιος καὶ Πρε-σβύτερος, ἡγεμόνης τῆς θεαλκάτων τύπων κατέ-σεις. Καὶ ὁ Πάπας ἡ Ἰωάννης ἐφ' ᾧ τὰ ταῦτα, ὅπισθα ὥς, ἐ ἀπαταίρασι μετὰ πνῦ, ὑπολογίας τὰ πεφαλωφύα ἀνέξει. ὧν ἀπάντων Λατῖνοι ἀργέων κατάγωλαν μὲν, ἐκ οἶδ' αἰδ' ὅτι, μαγγώσῃ ἢ ἐδωκα. Καὶ ὅτι ταῦτα ἀληθῆ, ἴσως ἐκάθην. Nanque Synodus post Septimam Oecumenica, a trecentis octuaginta Patribus coacta, ut Latini in suis Canonibus tradunt, pacem Ecclesiarum, finem suorum certaminum facit, & additionem, ex Filio Spiritum esse, uti scandalorum causam e divino Symbolo ablegat, longeque amandat. Et in Oecumenica hac Synodo Papæ locum supplentes, Paulus inquam, & Eugenius Episcopi, & Petrus Cardinalis & Presbyter, rerum harum duces fuerunt. Imo Papa Ioannes, sub quo ista gerebantur, epistolis, ac decretis cum aliqua responsione facta approbat. Quæ omnia Latini irrita declararunt, nescio qua de causa, nunquam tamen sententiam revocarunt. Hæc porro vera esse inde manifeflum[?] est. Tum subdit ex Actione sexta, quae in hanc materiam pronunciarunt Legati Pontificij, & Epistolam Ioannis Papae, in qua se de simili additione excusat, nunquam se eam asserendo approbasse, multominus tum, postmodum anathemati subijcit similia in posterum audentes. Simeon Thessalonicensis Dialogo contra Haereses; Ἐπειδὴ οὖν μὴ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ οἰκουμενικῇ ἡ γέγονε Συνόδῳ, ἀλλ᾽ ἡ ὀγδόη λεγομένη, ἧς καὶ Λατῖνοι μεμνῶνται, ἔτι τὰ σφραγιστικὰ [?] Ταύτης ὑπὸ μέρους τυγχάνοντα ἐμφανῆ ἐν οἷς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κοινοτομίας τῆς Λατίνων ὅτι μαθεῖν ἀκριβέστερον, ὅπως ἡ Συνόδος αὐτῇ ὠδὲ ἐκ τοῦ υἱοῦ τὸ Θεῖον πνεῦμα ἐκπορεύεσθαι τολμῆσαι λέγειν ἀναθέματι ὑποβαλεῖν, πρὶν τὰ τῆς ἱερᾶς συμβόλου ἀμέωτα παντὶ ζόωπ παρέδωκε[?]. Post Septimam itaque Synodum nulla alia Oecumenica coacta est, prae qua dicitur Octava, cuius & apud Latinos mentio est, & Acta ex parte patefecerunt, in quibus & de Latinorum innovatione accuratius addiscitur, & qua ratione Synodus illa, Spiritum sanctum etiam ex Filio procedere audentes asserere anathemati subiecit, sacriq; Symboli omnia inviolate conseruari modis omnibus tradidit. Iosephus Bryennius Oratione octava de Sanctissima Triade. Ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνθέσεως ἑβδόμης Συνόδου πέντε[?], καὶ ἐβδομηκοντα[?] ἐν τῆς βασιλείας τὲ Μακεδόνων[?]. Βασιλεὺς ὢ τῶν[?] βασιλίδα ταύτῃ τῆς πόλεως ἐπὶ Σωόδος συνε-κεφθῆνθη [?], καὶ τῆς συνᾴθρίσεως ἡ αἰτία, δι' ἣν τὸ πᾶν τῆς τοῦ Πάπα βουλῆς [?], καὶ βασιλέως ᾧ ξεσπῆ κατασκευάσαι αὐτῇ ὦ [?]. Ἵνα Φώτιον τὸν ἀγιώτατον τῷ Θεῷ τῆς βασιλίδος ἐκαθαιρύθη [?], καὶ οὗτος ὑποσολῆς [?], ἡ μετὰ πνεῦμα ὑπακρύψεως τὸ πνεῦμα ὑλμῶντας [?], καὶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐκπορεύεσθαι λέγειν, ἐκ-κηρύκτης Θεοῦ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ ὑποβλήτης. Ὁ δὲ καλῶς ποιῆσαι ποιοῦντα ποιήσῃ. Ταύτῃ γοῦν τῇ Σωόδῳ, καὶ ὁ ἀγιώτατος Πάπας Γωάννης, ὁ τωικαῦτα τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίας Ἐπίσκοπος Πέξης Πρεσβυτέρου καὶ Καρδιναλίς, Παύλου π., καὶ Εὐχρόῳ Ἐπισκόπων, καὶ τοπότερης ἀυτῆς σωμολογεῖ, καὶ τὸν εἰς τὸ ἐξῆς προσοπαθεῖναι π, ἡ ἀφελέως τολμήσουσα καὶ ὑποβάλλει τῇ αἰαδίκμαν, αὐτ' ἐκείνῳ ὑπογραφαὶ αὐτὸν ἰδίᾳ, καὶ Ῥωμαϊκῶς τῆς αὐτῆς τοποτηρητῆς, ἡ ἔτω μᾶλλον εἰπεῖν ὑπογραφαντος αὐτῷ ἐκείνων. Ὧν δὲ καὶ ὡς μαρτύριον ἐν ἐν τῇ μεγάλῃ Ἐκκλησίᾳ μνήσειν αὐτῶν ὑπογραφή. Εἰ δὲ καὶ τινὶ δῆμον ἀφεθῆναι ὑπέργραφαν ἔστι, ᾧ δι' αὐτῆς ὁ ἀγιώτατος Πάπας, ἀπάτου μαθῶν, ἡ ἐκτὸς φαγεῖν τῆς Σωόδῳ ταύτης μὴ χάριας λαβόμενοι ἀσεσᾶς. καὶ τὰ ἐξῆς.
units.tr: So much for the Actions of that Fifth Synod. But what of the Sixth and Seventh? I would say with the comic poet that it came in with lies composed, audacity the pillar, with plots arranged. Some schismatics, and they among the few of little standing who rely on violence for their worst purposes, have judged that these Actions should be counted with the five earlier ones and given the same force. Yet most of the leading men of the schism too have rejected them as the inventions of scoundrels, of no strength, and have refused to let their decrees stand alongside the other decrees of that Synod and of other synods, treating them as trifles. Nilus of Thessalonica embraced them in his Response to the forty-ninth Argument of the Latins. [Η' ὃ μὴ τὴν ἐβδόμην οἰκουμενικὴ Σύνοδος] The Synod after the Seventh, an ecumenical one, whose fullness was three hundred and eighty Fathers, as the Latins say in their canons, makes peace between the Churches and ends their quarrels; and it banishes far away the addition that the Spirit proceeds from the Son, as the cause of scandals, from the divine Creed. In this ecumenical Synod, Paul and Eugene, the bishops, and Peter, the cardinal and presbyter, filling the place of the Pope, were the leaders of these matters. Indeed Pope John, under whom these things were done, approved them by letters and decrees, with some response made. The Latins have declared all this void, for I know not what reason, yet they never revoked the sentence. That these things are true is plain from this. Then he adds, from the Sixth Action, what the Papal legates pronounced on this matter, and the letter of Pope John, in which he excuses himself for a similar addition, asserting that he never approved it; much less, then, will he subject to anathema those who afterwards dare similar things. Simeon of Thessalonica, in his Dialogue against the Heresies: [Ἐπειδὴ οὖν μὴ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ οἰκουμενικῇ] Since, then, the Synod that took place was not the Seventh ecumenical one but the so-called Eighth, which the Latins also mention, and whose Acts, partly clear, make it plainer, in which one may learn more exactly about the innovation of the Latins, and how that Synod subjected to anathema those who dared to say that the Holy Spirit proceeds also from the Son, and handed down to all men in every way that the holy Creed be kept inviolate. Then after the Seventh Synod no other ecumenical one was held, which is called the Eighth; the Latins also mention it, and its Acts in part have come to light, in which one learns more accurately about the Latins' innovation, and how that Synod, daring to assert that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son, subjected them to anathema and handed on in every way that the holy Creed remain entire. Joseph Bryennius, Oration eight, On the Most Holy Trinity: [Ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνθέσεως ἑβδόμης Συνόδου] From the holding of the Seventh Synod, after five and seventy years, under the reign of Basil the Macedonian, a King of this city, a Synod was assembled, and the cause of the gathering was that everything might be arranged according to the will of the Pope and the zeal of the Emperor: namely, that the most holy Photius be restored to the see of the city, and that those who dared, fearfully or craftily, to say that the Spirit proceeds from the Son be expelled and cast out from the Church, which it did very well. And to this Synod the most holy Pope John, who then presided over the Roman Church, through Peter the presbyter and cardinal, and through Paul and Eugene, bishops, and his locum tenentes, gave his assent, and subjected to anathema whoever should afterwards dare to add or remove anything; the locum tenentes subscribing for him in the Roman manner, or rather the same men subscribing in his name, and their signatures are kept to this day in the great Church as a witness. And if anyone is allowed to bring forward a letter in which the most holy Pope, having learned the fraud, rejects this Synod and does not accept what was done there, ... and so on.

units.la: A dicta Septima Synodo cum quinque & septuaginta anni prætergressi fuissent sub imperio Basilij Macedonis in regina hac Urbium alia Synodus coacta est, & congressus causa, per quem omnia ex voluntate Papæ, & Imperiali studio absoluta sunt, hæc fuit; ut Photium sanctissi-mum mum sedi Byzantina restitueret, eosque qui formidolose, aut subdole Spiritum, ex Filio procedere dicere audebant, ab Ecclesia pelleret, & profligaret, quod & optime persoluit. Huic itaque Synodo, & sanctissimus Papa Ioannes, qui tum Romana Ecclesia praerat, per Petrum Presbyterum & Cardinalem, Paulum, & Eugenium Episcopos, & Locumtenentes suum assensum praebuit, eumque, qui in posterum aut addere, aut demere ausus esset, anathemati subiecit; pro illo subscribentibus proprie & Romano charactere locumtenentibus, vel potius illo eodem per eosdem subscribente, quorum ad hunc usque diem in testimonium subscriptiones in magna Ecclesia conseruantur.
units.tr: In the time after the Seventh Synod, when seventy-five years had passed, under the rule of Basil the Macedonian, another Synod was gathered in the royal city, and the purpose of the gathering, through which everything was settled according to the wish of the Pope and the emperor's zeal, was this: to restore Photius, most holy, to the Byzantine see, and to drive out and destroy from the Church those who timidly or deceitfully dared to say that the Spirit proceeds from the Son, which it did very well. To this Synod Pope John, who then presided over the Roman Church, gave his assent through Peter the presbyter and cardinal, and through Paul and Eugene, bishops, his locum tenentes; and he subjected to anathema whoever in the future should dare to add or remove anything. The locum tenentes subscribed in his name in the Roman manner, or rather those same men subscribed for him, and their signatures are preserved to this day in the great Church as a testimony.

units.la: Quodsi quibus ipsi dogmatibus addicti subscripsere, & per eos sanctissimus Papa, auetis edifcere [?], sextam huiusce Synodi actionem si percurreritis, deprehendetis. &c. Nilus Damyla.
units.tr: But if you run through the sixth Action of this Synod, to which those who were devoted to its doctrines subscribed, and through which the most holy Pope, as you will learn if you read on, you will discover, etc. Nilus Damylas.

units.la: Οὐ μὲν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν καιρὸν Φώτιε ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει Σωσό-σθ[?] τῇ κυδῶσι τῆς Θεοβίης Βασιλέως Βασιλεὺς τῶν Μακεδόνων πλεόνων ἢ γιακοσίων ἀρχιερέων, ἤ πῆς ἐπηγέραπται ἡ ἀρχὴ, ἐ οἰκουμενικὴ Σωσόθεος. τῇ δ᾽ Σωσόθῳ παρηνᾶς καὶ οἱ τλὼ γνώμῳ ἅμα, καὶ ὁ ἐξ τὰ κάμεια τῆς διαγράφων φεύνημα τὴν ἐπέρων Ἐκκλησιῶν αἰσπθέ-μένου, καὶ ἀπαλγῆσουῆς. Ἡ δ᾽ αἰτία, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς σωπᾶσθαι αὐτὴν ἡ ἱερὰ Σωσόθεος ὡς τὸν τὸν Νικόλαον ἐκκηρύκτον διὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἐξ τὸ τλωικὸν[?] ἀφ-
units.tr: Indeed, at the time of Photius in Constantinople, the Synod was assembled under Basil the Macedonian, with more than three hundred bishops, and it is styled ecumenical. But this Synod, with its leaders and its mind, along with those who sat in judgement, was rejected by the other Churches, and was shunned and despised. The cause was that the holy Synod wished to silence Nicholas, who had been excommunicated by the Church, and to ... [the text here is too corrupt to render exactly].

units.la: ἀρξαθαι τοῦτον μὴ ὑποστολῆς λέγειν τῷ ὁ τῷ συμ-βάλῳ [?] ἀπο-φαίνεσθαι, ὡς ἔφη ἐγὼ φωνεῖ [?]· καὶ τῷ ὑποκρινεῖν ἀδίκας, παλινῳδίαν ἦσε, ὁ δι-αφερόμενος Σωδώρῳ, τοῦτο καὶ πρῶτος μένας ἡ ἐρᾶτο [?] πίστεως, μὴ ἄλλως φρονεῖν ὁμολογῆ, καὶ ἐχυρίζεσθαι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἐκπορεύ-εσθαι, ἡ ὡς ... τῆς ὡρᾶς, καὶ Διοκτήσεως οἰκουμενικῆς Σωώδῳ ἱερὸν σύμβολον [?], καὶ ... τὴν ἐξῆς ἀξίων Σωώδων τὸ κύριον ... διαμεμένον ...
units.tr: ... to begin with, not to say that this is not a creed, as I say; and having been ... in dissent, he sang a palinode. Who, having differed from Sodorus [?], first confessed, as the mother of the faith, not to think otherwise, and to maintain that the Holy Spirit proceeds, as ... of the ecumenical Synod of Diocletian [?], and the holy Creed ... the following Synods, the Lord ... remaining ...

units.la: Tempore etiam Photij, Constantinopoli, iussu pij Imperatoris Basilij Macedonis Synodus trecentorum & amplius Antistitum coacta est, quae praescribitur, sancta, & Oecumenica Synodus Prima & Secunda.
units.tr: At the time of Photius also, at Constantinople, by command of the pious Emperor Basil the Macedonian, a Synod of three hundred and more bishops was assembled, which is styled the holy and ecumenical Synod, the First and Second.

units.la: Synodo aderant, qui & opinionem, & circa potissima dogmata sententiam aliarum Ecclesiarum sibi assumpserant, erantque aliys nunciaturi.
units.tr: Those who attended the synod had taken on both the opinion and the views of the other churches on the main doctrines, and they were to report them to others.

units.la: Causa propter quam ea Synodus celebrata est, fuit, ut Nicolaus ab Ecclesia eijceretur, quod ille eo tempore coepisset remisse dicere additionem in Symbolo, qui ut se deprehensum agnovit, veritus ne eijceretur, palinodiam cantavit, & oratoribus missis ad Synodum, innovationem a se factam Fidei denegabat; nec aliter sentire se profitebatur, contendebatque de Spiritus sancti processione, quam uti Prima & Secunda Synodus universalis sanctum Symbolum ab aliys universalibus Synodis acceptum tetenet, & profitetur. Hæc cum placuissent Synodo, a communione Ecclesiæ eiectus non est. Proh supreme Deus! Quæ hæc stultitia est? Quæ monstra? Insanire absque vlla dubitatione viderer, si similia sub lance veræ historiæ examinare conarer. Examinanda nihilominus sunt, vt libere debacchantium hominum impudentia, & effrænata, atque importuna dicendi libido reprimatur: tum etiam vt minus cautorum animi, quibus similes nugæ oracula sunt, insscitia discutiantur.
units.tr: The reason this synod was convened was that Nicholas was to be cast out of the Church. At that time he had begun to say carelessly that something should be added to the Creed. When he realised he had been caught, he feared expulsion and sang a palinode. He sent envoys to the synod and denied that he had made any innovation. He also professed that he thought no differently, and he contended about the procession of the Holy Spirit in the same way that the First and Second Universal Synods kept and professed the holy Creed as received from the other universal synods. When these things had pleased the synod, he was not cast out of communion with the Church. Good God! What folly is this? What monstrosities? I would seem to be raving beyond all doubt if I tried to test such things by the standard of true history. Yet they must be examined, so that the impudence of men who rage freely, and the unbridled and importunate lust for speaking, may be checked, and also so that the ignorance of less cautious minds, for whom such trifles are oracles, may be dispelled.

units.la: Dicit Bryennius a Septima Synodo Oecumenica, ea nempe, quæ aduersus Iconoclastas coacta cultum Imaginum approbauit, ad Synodum hanc, sub Ioanne Pontifice celebratam, qua & Photius restitutus est, annos quinque & septuaginta intercefsisse. Synodus contra Iconoclastas coacta est anno Christi 789. Synodus ista Photiana anno 877. inter vtramque anni numerantur 88. si ab annis 877. annos demas 789. Quo vero ipse computo annos deprehendit septuaginta quinque, explicet.
units.tr: Bryennius says that the period from the Seventh Ecumenical Synod, namely the one that was convened against the Iconoclasts and approved the veneration of images, to this synod celebrated under Pope John, at which Photius was also restored, was seventy-five years. The synod against the Iconoclasts was convened in the year of Christ 789. This Photian synod was in 877. Between the two there are 88 years. If you subtract 789 from 877 you get 88. Let him explain how he arrived at seventy-five years by his reckoning.

units.la: Imperite admodum Bryennius Synodum, qua anno 863. Photius, exacto Ignatio, thronum inuadit, cum Synodo, qua mortuo eodem anno 877. in sedem restituitur, inter quas anni minimum quatuordecim intercedunt, confundit. Huic Synodo dicit Bryennius Ioannem assensum per suos legatos præbuisse, & ademptionem, & additionem in Symbolo condemnasse, & hoc quoque mendacium est. Nam alia est sub Nicolao Synodus Romæ congregata, in qua condemnatur Photius; alia est, quæ sub Ioanne, in qua restituitur. Et si vera sunt, quæ ex Schismaticis sed pauci & contemptissimi garriunt, in hac postrema de ademptione, & additione in Symbolo actum est. Ait locumtenentium Romani Pontificis subscriptiones Byzantij ad sua tempora in magna Ecclesia conseruari. Et hoc item mendacium esse necesse est, cum a mendace, & de tot mendacijs reo homine eoque solo proferatur. Tot congressibus de hac processione, tot colloquijs, tot Synodis post Photium inter Latinos, & Græcos habitis, in quibus licet Græci alia, atq; alia pro tutanda sua sententia in medium afferrent, nec verbum quidem vnquam de his Legatorum subscriptionibus factum est; quæ si fuissent emersissent in lucem, & non per tot secula latuissent in tenebris. Vnus Bryennius post sexcentos triginta, & amplius annos, in quo reliqui Græci cæci fuerunt, vidit & obseruauit? Nugæ. Cum vero Lectori insinuet ad dictis suis fidem conciliandam, vt perlegat Actionem sextam illius Synodi, manifestum fit, eum de hac postrema, & Photiana sermonem habere cuius nec tempora, nec auctorem, nec causam cogendae nouit. Sed illam cum alijs confundit, & mendacijs de suo assutis implicat, ut quo tandem emergas, nescias. Adde etiam illud, me morem gessisse Bryennio, & varijs conquisitis illius Synodi Graecis Codicibus a Graecis exscriptis, & a Graecis transmissis, in quibus Synodus, de qua nunc inquiritur, continebatur, accurate, & diligenter omnia considerasse, nec ullum unum repertum fuisse, in quibus subscriptiones similes Legatorum Romanorum haberentur in sexta, & septima Actionibus. quare Bryennio suas hasce in sexta Actione subscriptiones relinquamus. Et haec de Bryennij dictis.
units.tr: Bryennius is very unskilled in confusing the synod in which Photius, after Ignatius was expelled, seized the throne in 863, with the synod in which, after the death of the same man in 877, he was restored to his see. Between these there are at least fourteen years. Bryennius says that John, through his legates, gave assent to this synod, and condemned both the removal and the addition in the Creed. This too is a lie. For one synod was convened at Rome under Nicholas, in which Photius was condemned, and another under John, in which he was restored. If what the schismatics chatter about, few and most contemptible as they are, is true, then the removal and addition in the Creed were dealt with in this latter synod. He says that the signatures of the Roman Pope's deputies were preserved at Byzantium in the great church down to his own times. This too must be a lie, since it comes from a liar, and a man guilty of so many lies. In the many meetings on this procession, the many colloquies and synods held between Latins and Greeks after Photius, in which the Greeks, though they brought forward one argument after another to defend their view, never once mentioned these signatures of the legates. If they had existed, they would have come to light and would not have lain hidden in darkness for so many centuries. Did Bryennius alone, after six hundred and thirty years and more, in which the rest of the Greeks were blind, see and observe them? Trifles! When he urges the reader, to win belief for his words, to read through the sixth Action of that synod, it becomes plain that he is speaking of this latter, Photian synod, whose times, author and cause for convening he does not know. But he confuses it with others and entangles it with lies of his own invention, so that you do not know how he will get himself out. Add to this that I have followed Bryennius' example. Having sought out various Greek codices of that synod, copied and transmitted by Greeks, in which the synod now under inquiry was contained, I considered everything accurately and carefully, and I found none in which signatures like those of the Roman legates appear in the sixth and seventh Actions. So let us leave Bryennius with his signatures in the sixth Action. And so much for Bryennius' statements.

units.la: Auctor Libelli, A Damaso Papa ad tempora Christophori unam eandemque fidem fuisse Graecorum, & Latinorum; qui incipit, Ἐπειδή μοι ἐπὶ τῆς ἅπαξ ἐνώπιον πολλῶν[?], inter alia scribit: Οὐ μὲν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν τῶν καιρῶν Φωτίῳ τῷ Κωνσταντινουπόλεως[?], Σωσθένῃ τῇ κελεύσει τῆς Διοτροφῆς[?] Βασιλέως Βασιλείῳ τῷ Μακεδόνων πλήθων[?], ἢ ἔτι ἐκκλησιῶν ἀρχιερέων, ἢ τῆς ὁπηνίκα[?] ἡ ἀξία, καὶ οἰκεμενικὴ [illegible, ~6 letters] Σωσθένου. τῇ ἢ Σωσθένῳ παρεῖας[?], καὶ οἱ τῶν γνώμων ἅμα[?], καὶ τὸ ὥστε τὰ καιρεῖα τῆς διδημάτων[?] φεύΦεόνημα τῆς ἐπέρων Ἐκκλησιῶν ἀπαγγελλουσας[?]. ἢ δ' αὐτὰ δὲ ὡς σωθῆσεται αὐτὴ ἡ ἐεσᾶ Σωόδῳ[?], ὡς τὸ τὸν Νικόλαον ἐκκηρύκτον[?] Σηδὸς τῆς Ἐκκλησίας διὰ τὸ τλωικαῦζα ἀρξαδς τέτον[?] μὴ ὑποσυλης λέγειν τλὼ ἐντεσουμβόλῳ[?]. ὡς οὕτ' ἐγὼ φυσηθεὶς[?], καὶ τλὼ Ἀποκηρυξιν δίαζας παλινφθλιαν ἦσε[?], καὶ διαφορισβολζάμῳ πρὸς τὸν Σωόδον, τλώ τε καινοτομίαν ἡνεγκα τῆς πίστεως, καὶ μὴ ἄλλως φαγεῖν ὁμολογῆ, καὶ ἱχυείζετο ὡς ἐλὼ τὸ ἁγίῳ πνεύματος ἐκπόρευσιν, ἡ ὡς ὤδε τῆς ἐφωτῆς[?], καὶ δλυτίαας οἰκουμενικῆς Σωόδς ἱεφὸν σύμβολον, καὶ ὤδε τῆς ἁγίων ἐξῆς Σωόδον τὸ ξύρῳ δλξάμενον δολματίζει[?]. Ἐ τὰ ἐξῆς[?].
units.tr: The author of the little book, That from Pope Damasus down to the times of Christopher there was one and the same faith of the Greeks and the Latins, which begins with the words "Since...", writes among other things: that in the times of Photius of Constantinople, by the command of the pious emperor Basil the Macedonian, a synod of more than three hundred bishops was convened, which is called holy and ecumenical. He says that the sentiment of the other churches was to be announced, and that the synod was to decide whether Nicholas should be cast out of the Church for having begun to say, in the Creed, what he had not been permitted to say. He claims that he himself, having been caught, retracted his earlier position through fear of excommunication, and that he denied any innovation of the faith, professing that he believed no differently about the procession of the Holy Spirit than the First and Second universal synods held, and that the synods which followed agreed with them. The rest is missing from the text.

units.la: Sed & temporibus Photij Constantinopolitani, iussu pij Imperatoris Basilij Macedonis trecentorum & amplius Antistitum cogitur Synodus, quae sancta, & Oecumenica Prima & Secunda inscribitur: Aderant in ea, qui sententiam simul, & mentem circa praecipua dogmata aliarum Ecclesiarum erant enunciaturi. Causa, ob quam coacta haec sacra Synodus fuit, erat, ut Nicolaum Papam ab Ecclesia eijcerent, quod tum incepisset pauide, & suspensa mente additionem in Symbolo dicere. Qui cum se deprehensum agnouisset, abdicationem metuens, mutata sententia, Oratoribusque ad Synodum missis, innouationem inficiabatur fidei, nec aliter se sentire affirmabat, & contendebat de Spiritus sancti processione, quam quod
units.tr: But also in the times of Photius of Constantinople, by the command of the pious emperor Basil the Macedonian, a synod of more than three hundred bishops was convened, which is entitled holy and ecumenical, the First and Second. Those who were to announce the opinion and mind of other churches on the chief doctrines were present at it. The reason this holy synod was convened was that they might cast Pope Nicholas out of the Church, because he had then begun to say, with a wavering and uncertain mind, something added to the Creed. When he realised he had been caught, fearing deposition, he changed his opinion, sent envoys to the synod, and denied any innovation of the faith. He affirmed that he thought no differently, and he contended about the procession of the Holy Spirit in the same way as the First and Second ecumenical synods, and the other synods convened in their time, recited the holy Creed and proposed that others recite it. And so on.

units.la: Prima & Secunda Oecumenica Synodus, & reliquæ aliæ suo tempore coactæ Synodi sacrum Symbolum recitabant, & recitandum aliis proponerent. &c. Et infra: Καὶ γὰρ ὁμόψυχοι ἡμῖν [?]ἐσμέν, καὶ ὁμολογοῦμεν μίαν [?]καὶ τὴν ἡμῶν Χριστοφόρῳ τῷ Πάπα, ὃς ἐκβληθεὶς ἐκ τῆς ἱερᾶς [?]διπτύχων, διὰ τὸ ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ συμβόλῳ προσθήκην ἐπιθεῖναι Σεργίῳ τῷ [?]τὸν τῆς Κωνσταντινουπόλεως θρόνον.
units.tr: The First and Second ecumenical synods, and the other synods convened in their time, recited the holy Creed and proposed that others recite it. Etc. And below: "For we are of one mind with them and confess the one and the same faith" [...] with Christopher the Pope, who was cast out of the sacred diptychs because he added something to the holy Creed, under Sergius, who then held the throne of Constantinople.

units.la: Καὶ γὰρ ὁ αὐτὸς ὁ ῥηθεὶς Χειροφόρος τὸ ἀναθεμα ταύτην ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἀκλινὲς [?]πέπομφε ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ὁμολογίᾳ τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἀληθείας Παξιαρχῶς καθ᾽ ὃν ἔφλω καιρὸν, ὃς ὧν μὴ τὴν ἐξέμβολον Σιλόδον χρόνῳ δήμου οἰκονομίας ὑπηρέτης αὐτῆς, ἥπερ σωθήσεται κῆτο σαλς.
units.tr: For this same Christopher, mentioned above, sent this anathema from the beginning unwavering, in the same confession of the true faith, to the four Eastern patriarchs at that time. He was a minister of the synod that was convened in the time of the same economy, which is said to be ecumenical.

units.la: Ἐζς δὴ τῆς Βασιλείας Κωνσταντίνε, ⊂ Εἰρήνης μητρὸς αὐτῆ. Ὁ δὲ γε μὴ τὸν Σέργιον Πατριάρχης τῆς Κωνσταντινουπόλεως Μιχαὴλ ὁ Κηρουλάριος, ὃς ὧν δὴ τῇ βασιλείᾳ τὸ Δώσβας Βασιλέως Κωνσταντίνε τῇ Μονομάχῳ, οἰκουμενικῷ Σιλόδον σωθήσεται τῇ τε Βασιλέως ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Πάπαν τῆς Καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἐξεκόψεν, ⊂ ἑαυτῆς κοινωνίας ἀπέρριψε, καθὼς ὁρᾶται μίαν ἔσπερ. Etenim eiusdem fidei, & sententiæ cum nobis erant vsq; ad tempora Christophori Papæ qui primus a sacris diptychis eiectus est ob additionem in sacro Symbolo a Sergio tum thronum Constantinopolitanum obtinente. Nanq; primus dictus Christophorus additionem hanc scripto mandatam in sua professione ad quatuor Orientis Patriarchas misit tempore iam dicto. Qui viuebat post Septimam Synodum annos CC. celebratam anno VIMCCLXXXXVI. [?] sub imperio Constantini, & Irenes eius matris. Qui porro successit Sergio Patriarchae Constantinopolitano Michaël Cerularius sub imperio pij Imperatoris Constantini Monomachi Oecumenica Synodo celebrata Imperatoris iussu, prorsus Papam a Catholica Ecclesia abscidit, & sua communione eiecit, uti notum est ad haec tempora. Examinentur singula. Primum Synodum Primam & Secundam, cum hac Octaua Photiana confundit, haec a nonnullis Schismaticis Oecumenica dicta est, illa a nemine: haec trecentorum & amplius Episcoporum congressu nobilis habita est, si tamen vera sunt, quae in Actis illius habentur, Primae & Secundae numerus Episcoporum incertus latet; haec sub Basilio celebrata est; illa sub Michaële a Barda; haec in templo sanctae Sophiae, illa in Apostolorum templo. In illa exauctoratur Ignatius, in Photiana post mortem Ignatij restituitur Photius, Ioanne Pontifice superstite post Nicolaum & Adrianum. Causa quoque allata celebrandae Synodi nulla est. Cum in Prima & Secunda non dum accusabantur Romani, de additione, de qua postea actum est in Photiana sub Ioanne, & quae de sententia mutata Auctor comminiscitur in Prima & Secunda, ab aliis Schismaticis in Photiana reponuntur, & Ioanni Pontifici vindicantur. Quae postmodum addit de Sergio, & Cerulario, stultissima sunt. Neque enim potuit Christophorum, qui Pontificatum per paucos menses occupauit anno DCCCCVII. a Sergio diptychis eijci, qui in throno Constantinopolitano sedit anno 997. annos post 90. reliquis Patriarchis silentibus, si additio illa haeresis reputabatur. Ratio item annorum Septimae Synodi, & annorum interualla inter Sergium, & Synodum non constant. Sicuti nec Sergij successor Cerularius, cum inter utrumque & Euftathius Archipresbyter magnae Ecclesiae, & Alexius Studites, & numerus annorum quadraginta quatuor accenseantur.
units.tr: In the reign of Constantine, with Irene his mother. But Michael Cerularius, patriarch of Constantinople, under the reign of Constantine Monomachus, in an ecumenical synod convened by the emperor's command, cut off the Pope from the Catholic Church, and expelled him from his own communion, as is seen to this day. For they were of the same faith and opinion as we were until the time of Pope Christopher, who was first cast out of the sacred diptychs because of an addition to the holy Creed made by Sergius, who then held the throne of Constantinople. For this Christopher first sent this addition, committed to writing in his profession, to the four Patriarchs of the East at the time already mentioned. He lived after the Seventh Synod, celebrated 200 years later in the year 796, under the rule of Constantine and his mother Irene. Cerularius, who succeeded the patriarch Sergius of Constantinople, under the rule of the pious emperor Constantine Monomachus, in an ecumenical synod convened by the emperor's command, utterly cut the Pope off from the Catholic Church and expelled him from his communion, as is known to this day. Let us examine each point. First, he confuses the First and Second synods with this Eighth, the Photian one. The former was called ecumenical by some schismatics, the latter by no one. The latter was held as a noble gathering of more than three hundred bishops, if what is found in its Acts is true; the number of bishops at the First and Second synods is uncertain. The latter was celebrated under Basil, the former under Michael of Barda. The latter was held in the church of St Sophia, the former in the church of the Apostles. In the former Ignatius was deposed; in the Photian one Photius was restored after Ignatius' death, under Pope John, who survived Nicholas and Adrian. No cause for convening the synod is given at all. In the First and Second synods the Romans were not yet accused about the addition, which was dealt with later in the Photian synod under John. What the author invents about a change of opinion at the First and Second synods is put forward by other schismatics as belonging to the Photian synod and is claimed for Pope John. What he adds afterwards about Sergius and Cerularius is most foolish. For Christopher, who held the papacy for a few months in 907, could not have been cast out of the diptychs by Sergius, who sat on the throne of Constantinople in 997, ninety years later, while the other patriarchs were silent, if that addition had been regarded as heresy. Likewise the chronology of the Seventh Synod and the intervals of years between Sergius and that synod do not agree. Nor does the succession from Sergius to Cerularius, since between them Eustathius, archpriest of the great church, and Alexius the Studite, and a total of forty-four years, are counted.

units.la: Nec saniora sunt, quae profert Cabasila. Ait Latinos Synodum hanc celebratam post Septimam pro pace Ecclesiarum nuncupare Synodum Oecumenicam. Hoc vero falsum est. Quonam enim modo Oecumenicam eam vocassent Latini, quam nec Graeci ipsi ex schismate, nonnullos infimi nominis, & rerum plane ignaros, si excipias, eo titulo magnificarunt. Graecorum Ecclesia septem tantum Oecumenicas agnoscit, quorum decretis fasces, animosque subsubmittit. In literis Commendatitijs recens ordinati Patriarchæ habetur ; Ἀσπάζομαι τὰς ἁγίας οἰκουμενικὰς ἐπτὰ Συνόδους. Amplector septem sanctas Synodos vniuersales. In Professione Eidei, quam emittunt recens ordinati Metropolitæ, Archiepiscopi, & Episcopi, Περὶ τὰς ὑποδέχομαι τὰς ἁγίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐπτὰ Συνόδους. Prater hac recipio sanctas, & vniuersales septem Synodos. Et in emissione suæ Fidei Imperatores coronandi, & alij. Ἀλλὰ μὲν καὶ τὰς ἐξαιρέσεις, καὶ τὰς ὑποτυπώσεις τῶν ἐπτὰ οἰκουμενικῶν Συνόδων, καὶ τῶν κατὰ χρόνους τοπικῶν. Insuper etiam constitutiones, & definitiones septem Oecumenicarum Synodorum, & localium, quæ tempore suo celebratæ sunt. Constantinus Harmenopulus in Epitome Canonum. Τῶν μὲν κανόνων οἱ μὲν εἰσι τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων, οἱ δὲ τῶν οἰκουμενικῶν ἐπτὰ ἁγίων Συνόδων, οἱ δὲ τῶν μερικῶν Συνόδων, οἱ δὲ ἁγίων. Canones alij sunt sanctorum Apostolorum, alij sacrarum septem Oecumenicarum Synodorum, alij Synodorum particularium, alij Sanctorum. Et infra, Photianam hanc inter particulares commemorat. Τῶν δὲ μειζικῶν Συνόδων ἡ μὲν ἐν τῇ Κωνσταντινουπόλει ἐν τῷ ναῷ τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων συνηθροίσθη ὅτι τῷ Φωτίῳ Πατριάρχῃ ἡ ἐφεξῆς καὶ ἀλυτέως λεγομένη. ἡ δὲ ὅτι Λέοντος, καὶ Κωνσταντίνε ἐν τῇ ἐπωνύμῳ ναῷ τῆς τῆς Θεοῦ ἁγίας Σοφίας, ἥτις τῷ ἐβδόμῳ ἐκύ-[?] ἐπρσε[?] Σωόδων[?]. Particularium Synodorum una Constantinopoli celebrata fuit in templo sanctorum Apostolorum sub Photio Patriarcha, quæ Prima & Secunda dicitur: alia sub Leone, & Constantino in celeberrimo sanctæ Dei Sapientiæ templo, quæ Septimam Synodum confirmauit. Septimæ Synodi confirmatio tantum in hac de qua agimus Synodo Photiana visitur. Septem præterea agnoscunt Schismatici alij fere omnes, Psellus de Synodis, Matthæus Blastarius in Nomocanone, Iosephus Bryennius Orat. 8. de Trinitate, Matthæus Cygala Cyprius in Historica Synopsi, & alij, qui Photianam hanc penitus ignorant. tandemque Ioannes Imperator Constantinopolitanus in Synodo Florentina, vt refert Syluester Syropulus in Historia eiusdem Concilij sect. 9. cap. 4. Ἐγὼ τὸ παρὰς Συνόδων[?], Florentinam nempe, οἰκουμενικὴν κατ᾽ ἰδίαν τόπον ἡγοῦμαι ἐλάττω[?] τῶν ἀφλαβεσῶν ἱστὰ Συνόδων[?]. Διὰ τοῦτο θέλω, ὡς ταύτῃ ἀκολουθεῖν ἐκάνας καὶ πάντας[?]. &c. Ego quidem arbitror hanc Synodum generalem nullatenus infra dignitatem aliarum septem Generalium subsidere, quæ eandem antevertunt. Quare volo, ut hac illis par in omnibus succedat, nec aliud quidquam ab illis diversum in hac gestum prodeat. Nicephorus Gregoras Histor. lib. 19. de Hæresi Palamæ. Εἶναι δὲ παλαιὰ τινὲς[?] νῦν φηφήμω, ὡς μέλλην κ) τῆς τῶ Θεῶ Ἐκκλησίας ἐπε-δαί τινα μάλα μεγίςλω ἀρετὴν, καὶ πασῶν συμ-μιγῆ, Є πιxίλλω, λῶ [illegible, ~12 letters] παῖκοζμίς μικρῷ συναχθείσης Σωσόδε, πάντων χεδὸν σωμιόν-των Ἐπισκόπων ἅμα, καὶ Πατριαρχῶν, καὶ ταύτῳ οἴδῳ τι εἶναι Є τηδταίαν ὁμῶς. Loquitur de Synodo futura contra Gregorium Palamam, quam, ait, nominandam Octavam, ergo cum Synodus Septima apud Græcos sit Secunda Nicæna, excludit e numero Synodo-rum Photianam hanc, de qua verba facimus, Fama enim est, indevsque a prisci temporibus ad nos deducta, adversus Dei Ecclesiam per quam maximam hæresim, & ex omnium erroribus commixtam, ac variam suboriturum, corrigendam a Synodo ex universo fere terrarum orbe coacta, in qua convenient omnes Episcopi, Patriarchæ etiam, & hanc Octavam futuram simul & ultimam. Et numerum hunc Synodo-rum septenarium ita animo fixerunt, ut non veriti sint Scriptorum testimonia, quæ pro se laudant, immutare, & de suo ad maiorem numerum perducere. Inter eos audentior assurgit Theodorus Balsamo, qui septenarium Synodorum numerum defendit, & eorundem auctoritatem stabilit, centesimam, & trigesimam primam Novellam Constitutionem longe, longeque plurimum invertit. Nanque cum Iustinianus Synodorum quatuor tantum meminisset, nempe Nicænæ, Constantinopolitanæ primæ, Ephesinæ primæ, & Chalcedonensis, quarum decreta tanquam divinas Scripturas, & Canones, & tanquam leges recipiendas iubet, Balsamo numero aucto sua veluti Iustiniani verba, divendidit. Adens & quintam Oecumenicam sub Iustiniano, & sextam, & septimam. Quod absque simili Novellæ corruptela aliorum auctoritate corroborare poterat. Ut hinc quoque quantum sit fidendum schismaticis innotescat. Qua ergo fronte Nilus hanc Photianam Universalem indigitat, & id inter Latinorum Canones dici blaterat? An vero hæc eadem finem dissensionum imposuerit, & additionem e Symbolo ablegaverit, longeque amandaverit, mox cum postremæ Actiones in examen venient, explorabimus.
units.tr: Nor are the claims of Cabasila any sounder. He says that the Latins call this Synod, held after the Seventh for the peace of the Churches, an Ecumenical Synod. That is false. For how could the Latins have called it Ecumenical, when the Greeks themselves, apart from a few men of the lowest rank who had broken away in schism and knew nothing of the matter, have never honoured it with that title? The Greek Church acknowledges only seven Ecumenical Synods, and bows its head and spirit to their decrees. In the letter of commendation given to a newly ordained Patriarch it is written: "I embrace the seven holy Ecumenical Synods" [Ἀσπάζομαι τὰς ἁγίας οἰκουμενικὰς ἐπτὰ Συνόδους]. In the Profession of Faith which newly ordained Metropolitans, Archbishops and Bishops make: "Besides these I receive the seven holy and Ecumenical Synods" [Περὶ τὰς ὑποδέχομαι τὰς ἁγίας, καὶ οἰκουμενικὰς ἐπτὰ Συνόδους]. Emperors also, when they are crowned, and others, set out their faith in the same way: "Moreover, also the decisions and the definitions of the seven Ecumenical Synods, and of the local ones held in their time" [Ἀλλὰ μὲν καὶ τὰς ἐξαιρέσεις, καὶ τὰς ὑποτυπώσεις τῶν ἐπτὰ οἰκουμενικῶν Συνόδων, καὶ τῶν κατὰ χρόνους τοπικῶν]. Constantine Harmenopulus, in his Epitome of the Canons, writes: "Some of the canons are those of the holy Apostles, some those of the seven holy Ecumenical Synods, some those of particular Synods, and some those of saints" [Τῶν μὲν κανόνων οἱ μὲν εἰσι τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων, οἱ δὲ τῶν οἰκουμενικῶν ἐπτὰ ἁγίων Συνόδων, οἱ δὲ τῶν μερικῶν Συνόδων, οἱ δὲ ἁγίων]. Further on he mentions this Photian Synod among the particular ones: "Of the particular Synods, one was held at Constantinople in the church of the holy Apostles under the Patriarch Photius, and is called the First and Second; the other, under Leo and Constantine, in the famous church of the holy Wisdom of God, which confirmed the Seventh Synod" [Τῶν δὲ μειζικῶν Συνόδων ἡ μὲν ἐν τῇ Κωνσταντινουπόλει ἐν τῷ ναῷ τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων συνηθροίσθη ... ]. Thus the confirmation of the Seventh Synod is found only in this Photian Synod of which we are speaking. Almost all the other schismatics also acknowledge seven Synods: Psellus, On Synods; Matthaeus Blastares in the Nomocanon; Joseph Bryennius, Oration 8, On the Trinity; Matthaeus Cygala of Cyprus in his Historical Synopsis; and others, who know nothing at all of this Photian Synod. Lastly, John, the Emperor of Constantinople, at the Synod of Florence, as Sylvester Syropulus reports in his History of that Council, section 9, chapter 4: "I myself judge that the Florentine Synod, which is held in its own place, is in no way inferior in dignity to the seven earlier Synods which precede it. Therefore I wish that it should succeed them in every respect, and that nothing should come forth from it differing from them" [Ἐγὼ τὸ παρὰς Συνόδων, Florentinam nempe, οἰκουμενικὴν κατ᾽ ἰδίαν τόπον ἡγοῦμαι ... Διὰ τοῦτο θέλω, ὡς ταύτῃ ἀκολουθεῖν ἐκάνας καὶ πάντας]. Nicephorus Gregoras, History, book 19, on the heresy of Palamas, says: "There is a report, handed down to us from ancient times, that there will arise against the Church of God, through a certain very great heresy mixed of all errors and varied, a Synod gathered from almost the whole world to correct it, in which all the Bishops and even the Patriarchs will meet, and which will be both the Eighth and the last." He speaks of the future Synod against Gregory Palamas, which, he says, is to be named the Eighth. Since the Seventh Synod is the Second of Nicaea among the Greeks, he thereby excludes from the number of Synods this Photian one of which we are speaking. For the report is that this fame has come down to us from earliest times. And they have so fixed this number of seven Synods in their minds that they have not hesitated to alter the testimonies of writers which they cite in their own favour, and to bring them, from their own resources, up to a larger number. Among them the boldest is Theodore Balsamon, who defends the number of seven Synods and establishes their authority; and he has turned the hundred and thirty-first Novel Constitution completely upside down. For when Justinian had mentioned only four Synods, namely the Nicene, the First of Constantinople, the First of Ephesus and Chalcedon, whose decrees he orders to be received as divine Scriptures, canons and laws, Balsamon, having increased the number, passed off his own words as Justinian's. He adds also a Fifth Ecumenical under Justinian, and a Sixth and Seventh. He could have confirmed this by the authority of others without a similar corruption of the Novel. Let it thus become known also how far the schismatics are to be trusted. By what face, then, does Nilus call this Photian Synod Universal, and babble that this is said among the Latins' canons? Whether this same Synod has put an end to the disputes, and has removed the addition from the Creed and driven it far away, we shall examine when the final Acts come into question.

units.la: Sed forte Nili Damylæ narratio verior, atque extricatior accesserit? Nihil minus. Consideremus. Ait Synodum hanc coactam fuisse tempore Photii, iussu Basilii Imperatoris, & vocatam esse Synodum Oecumenicam Primam & Secundam. Non disputo, an hæc Synodus Synodus prorsus fit, cum dicat congregatam [illegible, ~10 letters] iussu Imperatoris. Et eadem Actione sexta Le-
units.tr: But perhaps the narrative of Nilus of Damyla is more truthful and better disentangled? Far from it. Let us consider. He says that this Synod was gathered in the time of Photius, by order of the Emperor Basil, and was called the First and Second Ecumenical Synod. I do not dispute whether this is a Synod at all, since he says it was gathered [illegible] by the Emperor's order. And in the same sixth Action of the Council...

units.la: Legati summi Pontificis introducuntur eadem afferentes, ὡς σκείλδ[?]σιν ὁ ἐν Θεῷ μέγας Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν, καὶ ἥρωσι καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, καὶ πνευματικοῖς[?] ἡμῶν. Vt iussit qui ex Deo est magnus Imperator noster ; & placuit fratribus, & confacerdotibus nostris. Cum me docuerit maximus Homologeta, Synodos non esse cogendas κηδόσ[?] Βασιλικὴν[?], iussu Imperatorio. Auctor illius vitæ. Et producam verba, vt magis creda. Καὶ ὁ Θεοδόσιος· ἐκ ἐρρῶ[?] ἡ Σωόδ[?] ἡ ἐν Ῥώμῃ. Ἐπειδὴ χοτεὶς κηδόσεως γίγνονται βασιλικῆς. Καὶ ὁ Μάξιμος· εἰ ταῖς ἡμέραις Σωόδες αἱ κηδόσεις τῶν Βασιλέων κυρίων[?], ἀλλ' ἀχὶ διστεβῆς πίστις[?], δίξαι ταῖς[?] τοῦ ὁμοουσίου ἡμουλῆς Σωόδες, αἱ ἐπειδὴ κηδόσεις Βασιλέων γίγνονται, φημὶ δὲ Θεοδοσίου τοῦ ἐν Τύρῳ, διυτέραν τοῦ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ, ἕτερον τοῦ ἐν Σαρδικείᾳ, πρώτην τοῦ ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει ὅπη Εὐδοξίου τοῦ Ἀετίου πέμπλην τοῦ ἐν Νικαίᾳ τῆς Βιθυνίας, ἕκτην τοῦ ἐν Σιρμίῳ, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα πολλαῖς χρόνοις εἰσδήμων τοῦ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ τὸ δύσπεσον, ἢς ἐξῆρχε Διόσκορος. Ἅπας δὲ ταύτας κέλευσις Βασιλέων ἠθέλησε. Καὶ ὅμως πᾶσαν καπνεῖ[?] ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τῆς ὑπ' αὐτῶν κυρίων[?] δόγματων. Δὲ ἡ ἐν καβάλλιτη τῆς καθολικῆς Παῦλον τῆς Σαμοσατέως ἔπι τῶν ἁγίων Μακαρίων Διονυσίου Πάπα Ῥώμης, τῆς Διονυσίου τῆς Ἀλεξανδρείας, τῆς Γρηγορίου τῆς Θαυματουργοῦ, τῆς δὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἐξάρξαντος Σωόδη, ἐπειδὴ μὴ κηδόσεως γίγνονται Βασιλέως. Ποῖος δὲ καινῶν διαγορὰς εἰ μόνας σκειἐκείνας ἐξκεινεδς τὰς Συνόδους τὰς καθόλου Βασι-λέων ἀθεσιδεέζας, ἢ ὅλως καθόλου Βασιλέων πάντας τὰς Συνόδους ἀθροίζας. Ἐ κείνας οὖν ἐκκείτης, ὁ ἀξίας Συνόδες ὁ ὑποβὴς ἐν Ἐκκλησίας καινὸν, ἀς ὀρθότης δόγμάτων ἐνέκεινεν. ἀλλὰ καθὼς οὖν ὁ Ἀ-ποστόλος μὲν ὁ ἄλλους διδάσκεσθαι εἶπεν γίνεσθαι Συ-νόδες ἢ πᾶς ἐπαγγέλλει τῆς ἐτοιμάσει ὁ καινὸν διηγόρευ-σε καθόσου βασιλικῆς μηδημίας μνήμην ποιη-μένου ἐν ἀσφαλεία τῶν σωτηρωσθαι ἡμῶν πίστεως, καὶ διορθώσοντος πάντων τῶν ἀνηκόντων τῆς Θείας τῆς Ἐ-κλησίας κεφαλαίω. Ὁ Θεοδόσιος· ὡς λέγει, ἔτως ἕξειν ἢ τῆς δόγμάτων ὀρθότης ἐνέκεινεν τὰς Συνόδους.
units.tr: The legates of the supreme Pontiff are introduced, bringing the same words: "As our great Emperor, who is of God, has ordered, and as it has pleased our brothers and fellow priests" [Ὡς σκείλδ... ὁ ἐν Θεῷ μέγας Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν]. Since the great Confessor taught me that Synods are not to be convened at the Emperor's command [κηδόσ Βασιλικὴν], the author of that life, "let me produce his words, so that you may believe more readily": "And Theodosius said: The Synod at Rome has no force, since it was not held by the Emperor's command." And Maximus: "If Synods assembled by the commands of Emperors confirm the faith, then the Synods of the orthodox faith, which were held by the Emperors' command, would be to be accepted: I mean that of Theodosius at Tyre, the second at Antioch, the other at Sardica, the first at Constantinople under Eudoxius the Arian, the one at Nicaea in Bithynia, the sixth at Sirmium, and afterwards, many years later, the one at Ephesus which was the Robber Synod, presided over by Dioscorus. All these were held by the will of the Emperors, and yet they all reek with the decrees of those who ordered them. But the Synod at Chalcedon, of Paul of Samosata, under the holy blessed Dionysius, Pope of Rome, Dionysius of Alexandria, Gregory the Wonderworker, was not held by the Emperor's command. Who then distinguishes these Synods alone as ones that the Emperors have not approved, or rather absolutely denies that all Synods were held by the command of Emperors? Let us then reject those, and acknowledge the worthy Synods that were gathered in the Church, which in fact were sent by the rectitude of doctrines. But just as the Apostle said that the teachers should be heard, and that Synods should be gathered in the Spirit, and that the Emperor, the one who issued the command, should make mention of the convening of the Synod, with the security of our faith saved and with all things pertaining to the Church corrected by the head of the Holy Church... " And Theodosius: "As he says, so let it be; the rectitude of doctrines is what constitutes the Synods."

units.la: Et Theodosius. (erat hic dignitate Sacellarius, plenus sceleris, & audaciæ Vir, & longe post homines natos improbissimus) Nullum robur habet Romana Synodus; neque enim iussu Imperatoris celebrata est. Et Maximus. Si Synodos coactas iussa Imperatorum corroborant, & non fides recta, ea admittito Synodos contra Homousion, quæ iussu Imperatorum congregata sunt, nempe primam Tyri, secundam Antiochiæ, tertiam Seleuciæ, quartam Constantinopoli sub Eudoxio Ariano, quintam Niceæ in Thracia, sextam Sirmiy, & præterea multum post has tempus, septimam Ephesi secundum, cui præfecit Diofcorus: has enim omnes iussa Imperatorum congregarunt, & nihilominus omnes propter impietatem ab eisdem comprobatorum dogmatum damnatæ sunt. Quare vero non reiicitis eam, quæ Samosatenum Paulum de folio deturbauit sub sanctis beatisque Dionysio Papa Romano, Dionysio Alexandrino, & Gregorio Thaumaturgo eiusdem Synodi Præside, quod non iussu Imperatoris coacta est? Et quisnam vero Canon insinuat solas Synodos iussu Imperatorum congregatas legitimas habere? Vel saltem iussu Imperatorum Synodos congregari. Illas selectas, sanctasque Synodos pius Ecclesiæ Canon agnoscit, quas rectum dogma approbauit. Sed ut Dominus meus scit, & alios quoque docet, bis in omnibus Eparchiis singulis annis Synodos haberi instituit. neque tamen in eo ulla Imperatoris mentio fit, ad nostram salutarem fidem tutandam, & emendanda quæcunque ad diuinum Ecclesiæ caput pertinent. Et Theodosius. Vti dicis, ita est. Recta dogmata Synodos comprobant. Ergo, iudice sancto Maximo, iussu Imperatoris Synodus congregata Synodus non est, cum non rectis dogmatibus innititur. Collige tu, Photianam istam Synodum, & potissimum duas has postremas Actiones, cum Ecclesiastica iura labefactent, & tot nobilitentur flagitiis, licet iussu Imperatorio congregatæ sint, inter alias Synodos locum non habere. Imperatorum in Synodos auctoritatem alio loco fusius explicauimus. Scribit Damyla, Hæc Synodus Prima & Secunda Oecumenica dicta est. Quis id dixit, Synodum primā & secundam Constantinopoli celebratam eandem esse cum illa, in qua restituitur Photius, & octaua Photiana nuncupatur? Eam plane distinguunt reliqui Schismatici Ioannes Zonaras, Theodorus Balsamo, qui rationem quoq; reddunt, quare cum vna sit, prima & secundæ nomen habeat, Alexius Aristenus, Constantinus Harmenopulus, eamque non inter Oecumenicas, sed inter particulares collocant. Illa sub Nicolao Papa, ab eodem Nicolao Epistola, & aliis Latrocinalis appellata, Photiana de qua agitur, sub Ioanne: in illa Ignatius depositur, & contra fas omne pessime multatur, in Photiana post mortem Ignatij Photius restituitur: illius Canones decem & septem numerantur, Photianæ tantummodo tres: illa in Apostolorum, Photiana in S. Sophiæ templo celebratur. Utrisque tamen illud commune fuit, Literarum Pontificiarum interpolatio. Et Damyla mihi Latrocinalem primam & secundam cum Photiana altera unam faciet, & sanctam & Oecumenicam esse mihi persuadebit? Quod sequitur, primam & secundam coactam fuisse ad deponendum Nicolaum, qui rum[?] coeperat additionem in Symbolo recitare, falsum esse, & purum mendacium supra demonstrauimus. Nec minoris impudentiæ est, dicere, Nicolaum palinodiam cantasse, & innouationem a se factam fidei denegasse. Nullum in ea factum est de Symboli additione verbum, quidquid delirant schismatici isti, qui eodem modo impudenter etiam mentiuntur, Ioannem Octauum Pontificem consensisse, ut illud Filioque ex Symbolo expungeretur, & Epistolam nescio unde auulsam, eamque mutilam, nec integram producentes, dicto suo auctoritatem interponunt. His assiduis, domesticisque fallacijs nebulones similes simpliciores a veritate abducunt, & compositis mendacijs ludificant, & glaucomam ob oculos obijcientes faciunt, ut quod vident non videant, & patenti veritati assensum non præbeant. Quæ alij in eandem rem producunt, non minus stultiora sunt: quare ad eos qui meliore mente, & consilio adesse possunt, convertamus orationem. Sed ut res clarior euadat, aliorum quoque Schismaticorum dicta examinentur. Macarius Ancyranus cap. 68. Ἀλλ', εἰ δοκᾷ, καταχρώσομεν [?] ἐταῦθα, ἐ ἢ μὴ τὰ ἐπὶ ἀξίας, ἢ οἰκουμενικῆς [?] Σωσόδς ἀξίαν, ἢ οἰκουμενικοῦ [?] Σωσόδν, ἢ κατ' αὐτὴν πατριαρχίας, ἢ ἑσχάμενα [illegible, ~6 letters] Κωνσταντινουπόλ[?] ἐν δὲ βασιλείας τ[?] Ἰσυβῶν Βασιλέως Βασιλέως Λέοντος, ἢ Ἀλεξάνδρου Γ[illegible, ~8 letters] ὁ Πάπα Ρώμης Ἰωάννης καὶ Φώτιος Πατριάρχου Κωνσταντινουπόλεως. ἔχουσα δὲ καὶ ποτὲ [?] πτὰς τῇ μὲν τῆς Πρεσβυτέρας Ῥώμης Παῦλον [?] Εὐγένιον, Ἐπισκόπους, καὶ Πέτρον Πρεσβύτερον [?] Καρδηνάλιον, τῇ δὲ Ἀλεξανδρείας Κοσμᾶν Πρεσβύτερον, καὶ ἀποκειμένην τῆς τῇ Ἀλεξανδρείαν πάσης ἀ-ρχῆς Σωσόλη, τῇ δὲ Ἀντιοχείας Βασίλειον μητροπο-λίτην Μαρτυροπόλεως, τῇ δὲ Ἱεροσολύμων Ἠλίαν Πρεσβύτερον. Ὅ[?]τι ὁ οἰκουμενικὴ ἐστιν, ἡ ὁδὸς αὐτῇ Σωώδ, αὐτὴ ἑαυτῷ ἐπιμαρτυρεῖ, καὶ ἐν τῇ δ' [?] κανόνι αὐτῆς.
units.tr: And Theodosius (he was a sacellarius by rank, a man full of wickedness and audacity, and far the most wicked of all men ever born) said: "The Roman Synod has no force, for it was not convened by the Emperor's command." And Maximus said: "If Synods gathered by the commands of Emperors gain their authority from those commands, and not from sound faith, then accept the Synods held against the Homoousion, which were assembled by the commands of Emperors: first at Tyre, second at Antioch, third at Seleucia, fourth at Constantinople under the Arian Eudoxius, fifth at Nicaea in Thrace, sixth at Sirmium, and, long after these, seventh at Ephesus under Dioscorus. For all of these were convened by imperial command, and yet all were condemned by the same emperors for impiety in the doctrines they had approved. But why do you not reject that Synod which deposed Paul of Samosata from his throne, under the holy and blessed Dionysius, Pope of Rome, Dionysius of Alexandria, and Gregory Thaumaturgus, who presided over that same Synod, which was not gathered by imperial command? And what canon, pray, lays down that only Synods convened by imperial command are lawful? Or at least that Synods must be convened by imperial command? The pious canon of the Church acknowledges those select and holy Synods which approved sound doctrine. But, as my Lord knows and teaches others too, he has ordained that Synods be held twice a year in every eparchy, and yet no mention of the Emperor is made in that provision, for the protection of our saving faith and the correction of whatever pertains to the divine head of the Church." And Theodosius said: "As you say, so it is. Synods are approved by sound doctrines." Therefore, by the judgment of the holy Maximus, a Synod convened by imperial command is not a Synod if it does not rest on sound doctrine. Gather from this, you, that that Photian Synod, and especially these last two Actions, since they overturn ecclesiastical laws and are so disfigured by many scandals, do not hold a place among other Synods, even though they were convened by imperial command. We have explained the authority of Emperors over Synods more fully in another place. Damyla writes: "This Synod is called the First and Second Ecumenical." Who said that the First and Second Synods celebrated at Constantinople are the same as that in which Photius was restored and which is named the Eighth, the Photian? The other schismatics clearly distinguish them: John Zonaras, Theodore Balsamon, who also give the reason why, though it is one Synod, it bears the name of the First and Second; and Alexius Aristenus and Constantine Harmenopulus, who place it not among the Ecumenical Synods but among the particular ones. The former, under Pope Nicholas, and called by Nicholas himself in his letter and by others "the Robber Council," was the one in which Ignatius was deposed and most wickedly mistreated against all right; in the Photian Synod, the one under discussion, under John, Photius was restored after the death of Ignatius. The former has seventeen canons, the Photian only three. The former was held in the Church of the Apostles, the Photian in the Church of St. Sophia. Yet both had in common the falsification of papal letters. And will Damyla make the First and Second Robber Councils one with the other Photian Synod for me, and persuade me that it is holy and ecumenical? As for what follows, that the First and Second were compelled to depose Nicholas, who had begun to recite the addition in the Creed, we have shown above that this is false and pure lying. Nor is it less shameless to say that Nicholas sang a palinode and denied the innovation he had made in the faith. In those Synods there is not a single word about an addition to the Creed, whatever those schismatics rave, who in the same way shamelessly lie that Pope John VIII agreed that the Filioque should be struck out of the Creed, and who, producing an epistle I know not from where, and that mutilated and not whole, lend authority to their word. By these constant and domestic deceptions they lead simpler men, like wretched fellows, away from the truth; they mock them with fabricated lies and throw a cataract before their eyes, so that they do not see what they see and do not give assent to the plain truth. What others bring forward on the same matter is no less foolish; so let us turn our words to those who can come to it with a better mind and judgment. But so that the matter may become clearer, let the sayings of other schismatics also be examined. Macarius of Ancyra, chapter 68: "But if it seems good, we shall ... here, not ... the dignity of an ecumenical Synod, or the Synod ..., or the patriarchate ..., assembled at Constantinople in the reign of the pious Emperors Basil, Leo, and Alexander ... Pope John of Rome and Photius, Patriarch of Constantinople. It had as legates, for the older Rome, Paul and Eugenius, bishops, and Peter, presbyter and cardinal; for Alexandria, Cosmas the presbyter; for Antioch, Basil, metropolitan of Martyropolis; for Jerusalem, Elias the presbyter..." That it is ecumenical, this same Synod bears witness to itself, and in its canon.

units.la: Verum si placet, apponemus hic & eam, quæ post septem Oecumenicas sanctas Synodos, sancta & Octaua Oecumenica Synodus celebrata est, & quæ in ea acta sunt, & scripta, quæ coacta est in Vrbe Constantinopolitana sub Imperio Basilij, Leonis, & Alexandri piorum Imperatorum: Hierarchis, Papa Romano Ioanne, & Photio Patriarcha Constantinopolitano, in qua etiam fuerunt locumtenentes senioris Romæ Paulus & Eugenius Episcopi, & Petrus Presbyter & Cardinalis, Alexandrini Cosmas Presbyter & Apocrisiarius vniuersæ Alexandrinæ Synodi, Antiocheni Basilius Martyropolitanus, Hierosolymitani Elias Presbyter. Oecumenicam vero fuisse hanc Octauam Synodum, ipsa de se ipsa testatur in secundo suo Canone. Vt reliqua præteream. Oecumenica hæc Synodus est, quia ipsa hoc de se testatur. Hoc equidem argumentum, si Macario credimus ineui-tabile eft. Ipsa hoc de se dixit, ergo est. Mahometes asserit, se esse Dei Prophetam, ergo est. Synodus aduersus Imagines coacta, se ipsam vocat Synodum sanctam, & vniuersalem, ergo est. Tot Synodi aduersus Homousium celebratae sanctas se ipsas vocarunt, ergo sunt. Macarius ipse doctor iniquitatis, & mendaciorum disseminator, vocat se ipsum Catholicum, veritatis sectatorem, ergo fuit. Possem hic addere multa ex Concilij Nicaeni secundi aduersum Iconoclastarum Synodum, sed nolo iniurius esse Schismatico.
units.tr: But if it pleases, we shall set out here also the Synod which, after the seven holy Ecumenical Synods, was celebrated as the holy and Eighth Ecumenical Synod, and the things done and written in it, which was gathered in the city of Constantinople under the pious Emperors Basil, Leo, and Alexander: with the hierarchs, Pope John of Rome, and Photius, Patriarch of Constantinople. In it there were also present, as legates of the senior Rome, the bishops Paul and Eugenius, and Peter, presbyter and cardinal; for Alexandria, Cosmas the presbyter and apocrisiary of the whole Alexandrian Synod; for Antioch, Basil, bishop of Martyropolis; for Jerusalem, Elias the presbyter. That this Eighth Synod was ecumenical, the Synod itself bears witness about itself in its second canon. To pass over the rest: this Synod is ecumenical because it says so of itself. This argument, if we believe Macarius, is unavoidable. It said this of itself, therefore it is. Mahomet asserts that he is a prophet of God, therefore he is. The Synod gathered against the images calls itself the holy and universal Synod, therefore it is. So many Synods celebrated against the Homoousion called themselves holy, therefore they are. Macarius himself, the teacher of iniquity and disseminator of lies, calls himself Catholic and a follower of the truth, therefore he was. I could add here many things from the Council of Nicaea II against the Iconoclast Synod, but I do not wish to be unjust to a schismatic.

units.la: Hafce duas Actiones, in quibus de additione in Symbolo agitur, falsas esse, atque suppositititias probant, planeque confirmant, Anonymus in Margine Codicis Vaticani 1115. in quo illae Actiones describuntur.
units.tr: The Anonymous writer in the margin of the Vatican Codex 1115, in which these Actions are described, shows and plainly confirms that these two Actions, in which the addition to the Creed is discussed, are false and spurious.

units.tr: Let it be known that these two so-called Actions of the proceedings, the one ... and the one called ..., were fabricated by Photius himself and were not truly written in the Synod; ... wholly taken from the Synod's ... and that which he drew from it in part, to suit the agreement of the Synods. For Photius, being of a double mind and devising a plausible cause for the schism he had introduced, sought to bring to the holy catholic and apostolic Church of Rome the matter of the addition in the Creed, and of the procession of the Spirit from the Son, which he himself had earlier been accused of defending. ... As if the things said in the Synod were to be gathered ... were not those from the presbyters of Rome, but the Synod's own ... teaching in the Synod, having been driven out of the holy church of Constantinople, while he himself remained in the Synod. Otherwise he, who had obtained pardon for his own peculiar ... on account of which he had used the holy ..., pardon in the ... movement of tongues, having cast these two actions upon himself, and with the rest, both true and ... in his own aim, not to be the more zealous ... about the Creed. And one must also consider the seventh point. ... And he praises these in them ... Concerning the king Basil he attributes these to ..., as if clearly acting under him, not the Synod, thinking that these were marks of the truth, and at the same time providing a defence for himself. Since he knew the fabrication would be discovered by the Church of Rome, he called the defence from it, and sent something to the king about the cause. One must also consider that in the definition of removal ... and the remission of the ... by the ... of the penalty ... fully reversed, he led to the recognition ... and to be yielded to in the teaching ... with no defence; he wished at that time to make a confession likewise against that Church, that they all say in full agreement the distribution to the one set apart by it, concerning some who waver on the procession of the Spirit. And that what is common is not equal, that everything appears to him. And let us believe no account of the addition to the Creed. In truth, and nothing ... the soul ... of the chrism relates.

units.la: Καὶ μηδένα λόγον τῆς ἐν τῷ συμβόλῳ προσθήκης πιστέυομεν. Τῇ δ' ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ οὐδὲν ἡ ψυχὴ τὰ τῆ χρίσματος ἱστορῆ[?].
units.tr: And we believe that no account should be given of the addition in the creed. In truth, and the soul ... (the text here is too corrupt to render with certainty) ... of the chrism relates.

units.la: Necessario sciendum est, has vltimas duas Actiones sextam nempe & septimam consistas esse ab ipso Photio, & non re ipsa celebratas. Hocque manifestum fit, ex Synodi ipsius fine, & ab ipsa exposita definitione subscriptionibus eorum, qui in dicta Synodo conuenerant, subsignata. Cum enim quam maxime versipellis vir hic esset, & ad comminiscendas fraudes aptissimus, cum intenderet demonstrare, tentati a se schismatis aduersus sanctissimam Catholicam, & Apostolicam Romanam Ecclesiam causam, non absque ratione fuisse, in Symbolo nempe fidei additionem, quae etiam ex Filio procedere Spiritum asserebat, ac si illa veluti inusitata cum errore addita fuisset; suspicabatur vero, si verbum de ea fecisset, dum adhuc celebraretur Synodus, Legatos e veteri Roma missos, qui Synodo praesidebant, conturbandos fore, & praeterquam quod ipse non potuisset ostendere, quod vellet, impe-didita, ac interrupta Synodo, ipse quoque throno Constantinopolitano excidisset, ob quod Synodus coacta erat. Praeterea quoque haud poterat prius quam veniam impetrasset de iis, ob quae Thronus denegabatur, aduersus eos, qui veniam impertiebantur, linguam mouere. has ultimas duas Actiones, ex se fingens reliquis verisque adnexuit, & definitionem appoposuit suo proposito proficuam, nihil esse addendum Symbolo fidei. Adhuc illud considerandum est, in hisce confictis alia quoque in illis subdole, ac malitiose inseruisse.
units.tr: It must be understood that these last two Actions, namely the sixth and the seventh, were composed by Photius himself and were not actually celebrated. This is clear from the close of the Synod and from the definition set out there, which bears the signatures of those who had gathered at the said Synod. For since this man was most crafty and very skilled at inventing frauds, he meant to show that the schism he had attempted against the most holy Catholic and Apostolic Roman Church had not been without reason, namely because of the addition to the creed which also asserted that the Spirit proceeds from the Son, as if that addition had been introduced as something novel and erroneous. He feared, however, that if he had raised the matter while the Synod was still in session, the legates sent from Old Rome, who presided over the Synod, would be thrown into confusion. Besides, he could not have achieved what he wished, and the Synod would have been broken off and interrupted, and he himself would have been cast down from the throne of Constantinople, which was the reason the Synod had been convened. Moreover, he could not venture to raise his tongue against those who granted pardon before he had obtained pardon himself for the things for which the throne had been denied him. So he invented these last two Actions, attached them to the genuine ones, and appended a definition useful to his purpose, that nothing should be added to the creed. It must further be considered that in these fabrications he also cunningly and maliciously inserted other things.

units.la: Primum quidem, quod ad Imperatorem Basilium illas refert, quasi ab eo una cum Synodo celebratas, hac machina reputans, easdem vestigia quaedam veritatis praeferre, & responsionem sibi praemeditans, si aliquando Romana Ecclesia figmentum innotuisset, in ius ab ea vocatus, causam in Imperatorem reiceret. Secundum in definitione addens, additionem, & ablationem, si nulla ab iniquo aduersario, illiusque artibus haeresis mota fit, condemnationem inferre eorum, quae reprehendi non possunt, & iniuriam Patrum, cui respondere nequeas. Hoc eodem sibi responsionem similiter erga illam Ecclesiam subministrat, concordia cum illa enunciata, contendente additionem a se factam propter nonnullos, qui de Spiritus sancti processione addubitabant. Propterea que communicans cum-
units.tr: First, he attributes these Actions to the Emperor Basil, as if they had been celebrated by him together with the Synod. He reckoned by this contrivance that they would bear some traces of truth, and he prepared an answer in advance: if the Roman Church ever learned of the forgery and summoned him to judgment, he would throw the blame for the cause upon the Emperor. Second, in the definition he adds that addition and subtraction should be condemned, as the Fathers did, if no heresy has been stirred up by a wicked adversary and his arts, and he wrote this so that he would have an answer to give should anyone object. In the same way he supplies himself with a reply to that Church, claiming that the addition made by him agrees with what that Church declares, and that he made it on account of some who doubted the procession of the Holy Spirit. For this reason, while he appeared to be in agreement with the Church, in all things thereafter, as it seemed, he took no account of any addition, yet in truth he was embracing with all his heart what belonged to the schism.
