Τὴ καὶ συνεκκλη-
units.tr: Manuel Caleca, in book 4 against the Greeks, says: "For if anyone removes from this ... of Sozopolis ... but one must know that these words were added afterwards by those who wished, from this source, to ... this saying. The matter does not hold. It is clear from ... of this Sozopolis ... that the placers of the Sozopolis set forth ... so that the Pope's words should be ordered, as they might recall what he said, and ... or it is called by the Latin name commonitorium. And where in it ... the exclusion, and wholly from the creed is copied out. And he dismisses the matter ... then from the Pope and in some way sent away all these things, then also the Sozopolis stirred up the word concerning it. And those who were not of Sozopolis, as ... and to the number of the high priest ... blasphemous ... they led to the storehouse because of the lack of ... He added to it, just as in the Sozopolitan books the things of the faith are under the storehouse. And they came together ..."

units.la: σίασιαζον τὶς βλασφημοῦσι, ὡς τὸ Θεῖον, καὶ αὐτὶς ἀπειθῆσαι τῆς πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὁμοιότητος ἐχίοων. Καὶ ὅλως πῶς ἂν ἰωχοντο σιωπῆσαι; ἐπὶ δ' οὐδὲν [?] φαίνει) συνελθόντας εἰπεῖν, πῶς ἐ φανερὸν ὡς ἀληθῆ τῶν θεοδήκλω ἡροῦντο. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἂν εἰπεῖν ἔχει τις, ὅτι οὐδ' ἀπλῶς ἡγοῦντο τὸ Σύμβολον μὴ τῆς θεοδήκης ἀναγινώσκοντας, τότε τοῖς ἀποκολικοῖς ἐν τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ Μαξίμῳ χρόνον τελάχεστον ἐγκωμιάζω. ἐπὶ δὲ διεδόμεν; καὶ τὸν Φώτιον ἐν ἀποδείχθαι τῷ θεοδήκλῳ, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἔχει λόγον μὴ τὸ βεβαιωθῆναι οὗτος τὰ Ῥώμης εἰς Παξιαρχῶν τὸν θεὸν τῆς θεοδήκης λόγον κινεῖν, ἵνα μὴ μόλις ἔχωσιν, ὅπερ ἐπὶ θ' ἐκείνῳ πάλιν ὑποκρυ-έις τὸ πᾶν ἀπολέσαι. ἠκούσθη δὲ οἱ τοποτηρηταὶ, καὶ ἀπὸ τούτων ὁ Πάπας, ὡς τῆς ὑπωζογῆς ἀποδόσεως, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ἄλλων καλῶς αὐτοῦ οἰκείαν δηκαῖδαι. καὶ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ζῶντος πλέον. τὰ δ' ἄλλα τῇ χώρᾳ ἀπαξ μόνον. Σπλοί ἢ θεοδήκλω τινῶν ἀναι τὸ ἐρμηνευόμενον· καὶ ὅτι μὴ τὰ πολλὰ πεῖτη τῆς Βασιλεῖων ἐρήσθαι, καὶ τὰς ὑπογεγαφὰς τῆς ἀρχιερέων ὑπογεγράφθαι, καὶ διὰ ζῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐνώσεως ὑπο-δεδήλωται Θεοῦ, ἃ πάντα ἐπὶ τῷ τέλει τῆς σωσοδήκῶν ἀπαξ γράφεῖ), ἢ ἀπὸ τῶ μὴ δίκην θεσπιστὴν λέγουσα ἀπαξ, καθ' αὐτὸ, ᾧ φανερῶς ἀπηρτημένη ἢ ἄλλων. Οὐκοῦν ὠσὰ ἀπλοῦν μὴ τῶν τῆς ξυμβεβηκότων ἀλλ' ἐργάσαιο, καὶ τὸ τέλος καθόλου τῆς Σωσόδου θεοδήκης ὑπὸ εἰπεῖν, καὶ θεάξεως, ἕ τὰ πρὸ τέλος τῆς ποιήσεως ἐωθῶς θεοπτόθη, πάλιν ἀρχομένης συνεκλή-σά-
units.tr: ... some blaspheming, as the Divine One, and again refused to stop the similarity with one another. And in general how could they have been silent? But when they came together, they said nothing (?), how it is clear that they chose the true words of the Theodecan. For no one can say that they simply did not think the creed was being read out by the Theodecans, since at that time they praised Maximus the Confessor the least. But it is also said that Photius was appointed to the Theodecan, but there is no reason why he should not, once confirmed by the Roman Pontiff as Patriarch, stir up the word of the Theodecan, lest he with difficulty hold on to what he had, which by that same concealment he would lose entirely. The legates were heard, and from them the Pope, as of the subsequent ruling, and from the others well in their own proper manner. And the brother lived longer. The rest only once in the land. ... The Theodecan of some things ... that which is to be interpreted; and that many things are set out in the Basilicas, and the subscriptions of the high priests are signed, and through the living is made known from the union of God, all of which are written once at the end of the Sozopolitan. Or from not speaking as a divinely inspired judge, once, by itself, which is plainly detached from the others. Therefore, as if not simply of the things that have happened but of the work, and the end of the Sozopolitan Theodecan is to be spoken of in general, and to be seen, which before the end of the poem was plainly seen, again beginning to come together ...

units.tr: ... to recall these. For I would be unwise to raise this matter at this point, or to speak of it obscurely; I would have to mention the time and the place.

units.la: Εἰ δ' ἐ εἰρῆσθαι ταῦτα τῆς Σωσόδου ὕβρισμος, ὑ-δίν ᾧ̈ι τὰ ζητημάλα διασάφῃ, ἐπὶ τῆς ἀσυνπᾶται. ἡ γὰρ ὡς ἀρχὴ πίστεως ἐπεὶ ἐξ ἀπαρῶ ἀλλ' ἡ ὁδὸς ἰχύσης ἀφαιρεσεως, ἀλλως ἀ ἑαυτῷ ἡ ἐξυλησία ἡ ἐξυσίας ἀνβάλ-λ[?]. Καὶ ἄμα εἴπῃ τις αὐ̃, ὡς ἀρα ὀξὺς τὸ μὴ δὲν ἀφαιρεῖν ὑποφήναθαι τὸν τῆς ἀμπλᾶ, ὥσ ἱκαλουῦται ἐσαδήκλω ὅπινυεῖν, μησὶν ἀφαιρεῖν ἐπιπλεξα.
units.tr: If these things were said as a mockery of the Sozopolitan, the questions are clarified in the ... For as a principle of faith it is not from nothing but the way of a strong removal; otherwise the Church would deprive itself of its authority. And at the same time someone may say that it is a sharp thing not to take away anything, which is called ... to be silent about; he has added to the removal.

units.la: Si quis enim in extremo gestorum Synodi ipsius ordine de additione dictum putat, quod scilicet non oporteat auferre, vel addere; quod etiam quidam ad seducendos simpliciores obtendunt: sciendum est, hoc a quibusdam postea gestis Synodalibus appositum: hinc offendere nitentibus huiusmodi additionem fuisse prohibitam. Hoc autem rationem non habere perspicuum est. Primum quidem, quoniam in gestis huius Synodi Commentariolum quoddam est eorum, quae in eo Concilio erant discutienda, expositionem per ordinem continens, quod Legati Synodo proposuerunt: Commentarium sibi a summo Pontifice datum afferentes, ut meminissent quae in ea Synodo vel dicenda, vel facienda essent. Neque enim in eo quidquam de additione, vel de Symbolo omnino scriptum est. Et certe id in prima statim fronte ponendum fuit, fuit, sive a Romano Pontifice illis de hoc suisset quidquam imperatum: sive etiam Synodus de hoc verbo mouisset. Nempe enim si Synodus illa, quam quadrigentorum ferme Episcoporum implebat numerus, blasphemam hanc additionem putabat, cur non principaliter de illa verba fecit? Ita enim in praecedentibus Synodis de fide primo in loco semper agebatur. Cur autem in Deum blasphemantibus conueniebant, ipsisque de concordia ad inuicem tuenda obtemperabant, vel omnino sub silentio se continebant? quando vero nihil dixisse comprobantur, cui non perspicuum fit, veram eos illam additionem existimasse? Neque enim dici potest illos ignorasse Latinos cum additione Symbolum legere, cum id Oriens-totus iam tunc saltem a B. Maximi temporibus didicerit. Deinde ut concedamus, Photium additionem non non [?] admisisse: rationabile certe non erat, postea quam a Romano Pontifice Patriarcha confirmatus fuerat, verbum de adiectione mouere; ne vix tandem voti compos effectus, per illum rursus abrogatus amitteret omnia. Satis autem erat legatis, atque ipsi in primis Romano Pontifici, subiectione sibi reddita, de ceteris illos recte sentire arbitrari. Itaque nihil ultra inquirentes reliqua suis locis manere permiserunt. Et illud autem indicat adiectum a quibusdam quod diximus, quod post plurima Imperatorum anni, subscriptionesque Episcoporum annotata sint, & gloria reddita sit Deo pro Ecclesiae vnione. Quae omnia in fine gestorum synodalium scribuntur. Quod autem de non adiiciendo, vel auferendo adiectum est, seorsim positum, & ab aliis aperte disiunctum, & separatum est. Non igitur suscipiendum est post eorum, quae inquirebantur, emendationem, post compositas res, post finem denique Concilij, post illa, quae in fine Synodorum apponi consueuerunt, rursus illos putare de his agere coepisse, de quibus nulla facta esset mentio. Aut enim principaliter ea res agenda fuit, aut non ita praetereunter, & intempestiue, & praeter locum debitum agenda. Etsi enim a Synodo dictum concedamus, nihil tamen de huiusmodi quaestione declarat; neque his aduersatur, quae dicta sunt. Aut enim, vt dictum est, fidei alterius adiectionem interdicit, rectaque abolitionem, siue alios non se Ecclesia hac potestate priuat. Quanquam dicere possumus, hac sententia, si Concilij sit, quae declarat sic nihil oportere auferri, id praeceptum fuisse, ne auferretur Occidentalium additio, quam accusabant.
units.tr: For if anyone thinks that something was said about the addition at the very end of the Synod's proceedings, namely that one ought neither to remove nor to add, which some also put forward to mislead simpler people, it must be understood that this was appended by certain Synodal records written later, by those who wished to make such an addition seem forbidden, and this plainly has no basis. First, because the records of this Synod contain a short commentary on the matters that were to be discussed in that Council, setting out in order what the Legates proposed to the Synod, bringing with them a memorandum given by the supreme Pontiff so that they would remember what was to be said or done in that Synod. Indeed nothing about the addition, or about the creed at all, is written there. Certainly this would have been placed at the very front, if the Roman Pontiff had ordered anything on this matter, or if the Synod itself had raised this word. For if that Synod, which was made up of some four hundred bishops, regarded this addition as blasphemous, why did it not treat those words principally? For in the earlier Synods the matter of faith was always treated first. Why, moreover, did they gather with those who blasphemed God, and submit to them in maintaining mutual concord, or keep wholly silent? And when they are shown to have said nothing, to whom will it not be clear that they judged that addition to be true? Nor can it be said that they did not know the Latins read the creed with the addition, since the whole East had learned this at least from the time of Blessed Maximus. Next, even if we grant that Photius did not admit the addition, it was certainly not reasonable, after he had been confirmed as Patriarch by the Roman Pontiff, to raise the question of the addition; lest, having barely attained his wish, he should by that same means be stripped of everything. It was enough for the legates, and above all for the Roman Pontiff himself, that submission had been rendered to them, and that he thought rightly about the rest. Therefore, making no further inquiry, they allowed the remaining matters to stand in their places. And that the addition was made by some, as we have said, is indicated by the fact that after many years of the Emperors, and after the subscriptions of the bishops were recorded, glory was given to God for the union of the Church. All these things are written at the end of the synodal records. But what was said about not adding or removing stands apart, and is clearly separated and set off from the others. It is therefore not to be supposed that, after the matters under inquiry had been corrected, after the business had been settled, and finally after the end of the Council, after those things which are customarily placed at the end of Synods, they then began to treat again of matters on which no mention had been made. For either the matter had to be treated principally, or it was not to be treated so incidentally, out of season, and out of its proper place. For even if we grant that it was said by the Synod, it nonetheless declares nothing about a question of this kind, and it does not conflict with what has been said. For either, as has been said, it forbids the addition of another article of faith and rightly abolishes it, or the Church does not deprive itself of this power over others. Nevertheless we may say that, if this sentence belongs to the Council and declares that nothing ought thus to be removed, the precept was that the addition of the Westerners, which they were accusing, should not be removed.

units.la: Postremas has Actiones plane fictitias esse, plu- ribus rationibus confirmatur.
units.tr: That these last Actions are wholly fictitious is confirmed by several arguments.

units.la: Uniuersam Synodum fuisse Photij commentum, nunquam nisi in cerebro eius inter domesticos parietes celebratam, pluribus probauimus; nunc quid de postremis hisce Actionibus existimandum sit, inquiramus. In sexta Actione, qui eo conuenerant, profitentur se tenere integram, atque illæsam fidem a Patribus acceptam, & innouationem omnem respuere, & condemnare, idque, vt probent, recitant Symbolum in prima Nicæna, & secunda Constantinopolitana editum absque illa additione Filioque, quæ manu Basilij Imperatoris, & filiorum rogantibus illis signatur. & sic acclamationibus variis ad Imperatorem, & filios finem habet. In septima reproducta Fidei professione, Canonem formant, nihil esse in posterum addendum, vel detrahendum in Symbolo, Si quis contra fecerit, anathemati subijcitur. Tum sic.
units.tr: We have shown by many proofs that the whole Synod was Photius's invention, never held except in his own head within his private walls. Now let us inquire what should be thought of these last Actions. In the sixth Action, those who had gathered there profess that they hold the faith received from the Fathers whole and unharmed, and that they reject and condemn every innovation. To prove this they recite the Creed as issued at the first Nicene and the second Constantinopolitan councils, without that addition Filioque, which is marked with the hand of the Emperor Basil, at the request of his sons. Then the proceedings end with various acclamations to the Emperor and his sons. In the seventh Action, after the profession of faith is repeated, they frame a canon: nothing is to be added to or taken away from the Creed in future, and whoever acts otherwise is subject to anathema. Then follows the text.

units.la: Similis definitio, & Canon opinioni Græcorum, vt sua aduersus Latinos probarent, tantundem fauens, nunquam apud illos obliuioni traditus obsoleuisset, sed cum de processione Spiritus, & additione in Symbolo sermo habitus fuisset, vt saepenumero contigit, prompte, & veluti ad pugnandum vocati, praedictum Canonem, tanquam scutum firmissimum sumpsissent, & contradicentibus Latinis opposuissent; sed alijs, quae in rem suam facere videbantur, propositis, ac saepissime inculcatis, nullam de eo mentionem habuerunt. Ergo vel Photij, vel recentiorum commentum non tanti aestimatum est, vt, cum res posceret, & necessitas vrgeret, euulgaretur. Non est credendum similia auxilia Graecos neglexisse.
units.tr: A definition and canon like this, which so greatly favours the Greek opinion and would serve them against the Latins, would never have fallen into oblivion and become obsolete among them. Whenever the question of the procession of the Spirit and the addition to the Creed was raised, as often happened, they would have been quick, and called as if to battle, to take up this canon as their strongest shield and oppose it to the Latins who disagreed. Yet, although they put forward and very often pressed other arguments which seemed to serve their cause, they made no mention of it at all. Therefore either the invention of Photius, or of later men, was not valued so highly that it would be published when the matter demanded it and necessity pressed. It is not credible that the Greeks would have neglected such aid.

units.la: Praeterea ante dictum Canonem tres alij de rebus alijs publicati sunt, & Graeci posteriores, qui Canones collegerunt, & in illis exponendis sedulam operam navarunt. de tribus hisce sermonem habent, eosque vti reliquos aliarum Synodorum Canones legitimos ducunt, & expositione etiam adornant. Hunc vltimum celant, dissimulant, & silentio transeunt: imo tres tantum in ea Synodo, nec plures Canones factos fuisse asseuerant. Vel illis non innotuisse, vel si innotuerit, vti commentitium reiectum fuisse, planum est. Zonaras, & Balsamo huius Photianae Synodi tres tantum Canones digerunt, & exponunt, Alexius Aristenus, Τῆς ἐν τῷ [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: Moreover, before the canon just mentioned, three other canons on other matters were published. Later Greeks, who collected the canons and took great pains in expounding them, discuss these three and regard them as lawful, like the remaining canons of the other synods, and they supply commentaries on them too. But they conceal, dissemble and pass over in silence the last one, and they assert that only three canons were made at that synod, and no more. It is plain either that they did not know of it, or, if they did, that they rejected it as spurious. Zonaras and Balsamon arrange and expound only three canons of this Photian synod. Alexius Aristenus [Greek lost in the scan]

units.la: Θεῦ Σοφίας, ἧς τὴν ἑβδόμην ἐνέργος Σινόδον, κανόνες ξʹ. In praeclebri Dei Sapientiæ templo Synodi, quæ Septimam confirmauit, Canones tres. Matthæus Blastarius in Collectione Canonum; Ἀλλὰ καὶ ἔπερί τῆς κανόνες ἐξεφώ-νήσαν, ἧς τὸν Φώτιον τῷ Θεόρῳ Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἐπίσκοπον μὴ τῷ τῆς Θεοῦ μυστηρίων Ἰγνατίου, ἐκ τὸ ἐπίσκοπον πολλάκις ἐξέπεμψεν ἐκβαλλόμενος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπομυμένος[?]. Sed & alij tres Canones emulgati funt Synodi, quæ Photium in Constantinopolitanam sedem restituit post obitum Ignatij, cum antea sæpius alter alterò eiecto intruderetur. Constantinus Harmenopulus in Epitome Canonum; Τῶν ἢ μεγίστων Σινόδων τῆς ἀφορμῆς καὶ διδασκαλίας λεγομένης ιζʹ. τῆς τῇ ἁγίᾳ Σοφίᾳ ἔπης. Particularium vero Synodorum eius, quæ Prima & Secunda dicitur, decem & septem, ad sanctam Sophiam habita tres. Photius ipse, quod non contemnendum videtur, in suo Nomocanone, cum Primæ & Secundæ Synodi à se celebratæ sæpius mentionem induxisset, & illius Canones ad confirmandas consuetudines Ecclesiasticas vsurpasset, huiusce Octauæ Photianæ, itidem à se celebratæ, & cuius fauore sedem Constantinopolitanam recuperauerat, & in qua tot sua prænconia extant, & cui simili annumeratione cum alijs Synodis auctoritatem conciliarat, æque ac si vnquam non fuisset, nullum produxit Canonem , argumento euidenti, tum illam non fuisse publicatam , sed etiam si ab ipso Photio conficta effet, ne inuidiam aliorum subiret, in tenebras mancipatam delituisse .
units.tr: (Aristenus's line, translated:) In the famous temple of the Wisdom of God, of the synod which confirmed the Seventh, three canons. Matthew Blastares, in his Collection of Canons: "But also three canons were issued by the synod which restored Photius to the see of Constantinople after the death of Ignatius, since previously one had been repeatedly thrust out and the other intruded." Constantine Harmenopoulos, in his Epitome of Canons: "Of the greatest synods, of which the occasion and teaching are said to be seventeen, of those held at the Holy Wisdom three." Of his particular synods, the so-called First and Second, seventeen, and at Holy Sophia three. Photius himself, which seems not to be despised, in his Nomocanon, when he had often introduced the mention of the First and Second synods which he had held, and had used their canons to confirm ecclesiastical customs, made no use at all of any canon of this Eighth Photian synod, which he also held, and by whose favour he had recovered the see of Constantinople, and in which so many of his own praises stand, and which he had won authority by numbering it with the other synods, as if it had never existed. This is clear evidence that it was not published at that time, and even if it was composed by Photius himself, it lay hidden in darkness, consigned there so that he would not incur the envy of others.

units.la: Ad haec, si verum est, quod alij tradunt, & firmiter contra Graecos asseuerant, in hac Synodo Photiana nullum esse fermonem introductum de Processione Spiritus ex Filio, sed Photium sua restitutione contentum, ne turbae de nouo excitarentur, & ipse in culpam, & lites impingeret, libentiffime de dogmate prius adeo strenue & voce stentorea proclamatam quaestionem silentio praeterijsse, an non hasce duas postremas Synodi Actiones minimum fictitias, & additicias esse fatebimur? Constantinus Meliteniota Orat. 2. de Processione Spiritus sancti; Ἐ'πάπῃς ἐφ' οἷς ἐκαλεῖτο [?] τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς Ἐκκλησίας διαφερόμενον, εἰς τὸν τῆς Κωνσταντίνου μέγιστον [?] θεσμὸν τὸ πρὶν συνη[?]- μης ἐπυχε, ἐν ὑσίεσις ἐξ αὐτῆς ταύτης, καὶ τῇ συν- καταβαίνων ἀρχιερεῦσι [?] θεσπίκως [?] ὁ ἐδοξοδοξῆς κατ- ηζίω), καταλιπὼν τὰ πάντα, καὶ μηδὲ [?] τὴν δόγματος ταύτης ποιησάμενος λόγον πᾶσῃ σπουδῇ, καὶ [?] ἀδεῶν, καὶ τὸ ἐρωτῷ ἐχώρησε. Photius, cum de illis accusaretur a Romana Ecclesia, quae ille antea in Constantinopolitanam maximam
units.tr: Besides, if what others report, and firmly assert against the Greeks, is true, that in this Photian synod no discussion of the procession of the Spirit from the Son was introduced, but that Photius, content with his restoration, and so that no new disturbances would be stirred up and he himself would not be blamed and involved in quarrels, most willingly passed over in silence a question so vigorously and stentorian-voicedly proclaimed beforehand on doctrine, shall we not admit that these last two Actions of the synod are at least fictitious and additions? Constantine Meliteniotes, Oration 2, on the Procession of the Holy Spirit: "Photius, when he was accused of those things by the Roman Church, to which he had earlier plotted against the greatest see of Constantinople, afterwards obtained pardon from the same church, and was judged worthy to be admitted; thus she loves to stoop to her supreme Pontiffs as is proper to her office. Having neglected everything, and taken no account of this doctrine, he embraced reconciliation and peace with all zeal and without delay."

units.la: sedem machinatus fuerat, veniam postea assecitus ab eadem, & dignus qui admitteretur iudicatus, ita illa pro munere Pontificibus summis proprio condescendere amat; neglectis omnibus, & nulla de hoc dogmate ratione habita, omni conatu, & studio, nulla interposita mora reconciliationem, & pacem amplexatus est.
units.tr: Photius, when he was accused by the Roman Church of those things which he had earlier plotted against the greatest see of Constantinople, afterwards obtained pardon from the same church and was judged worthy of admission. Thus she loves to stoop to the supreme Pontiffs as is proper to her office. Neglecting everything, and taking no account of this doctrine, he embraced reconciliation and peace with every effort and eagerness, and without any delay.

units.la: Ioannes Veccus lib. 3. ad Sugdæx Theodorum. Τὸ δ’ οὐκ [?] τῆς τῶν [?] ἀ[?] ... [?] εἰς [?] ... [?] κινή[?]σεως. Hoc vero nemo ex iis, qui ad bene coniectandum idonei sunt, facile sibi credendum proponeret, cum nec dogmatica ulla oratio in ea Synodo, qua pro pace sanciendā[?] coacta fuerat, reperiatur edita. Si nullus in ea Synodo sermo de dogmate, nulla oratio habita, quoniam firmo fundamento duæ hæ de dogmate Actiones tot inculcatis verbis pertractantes, stabunt? nullo plane. Quare fictitias eas esse, & Synodo annexas ab adversarijs existimandum est. Quarum usum Græci quoque ipsi, qui aliquid sapere visi sunt, a suis scriptionibus profligarunt. Id & Schismatici ipsi, qui Photianam Synodum non æque laudant, & unionem initam per Photium criminantur, non tantum confitentur, sed etiam profitentur. Nanque errores Latinorum a sexta ipsa Synodo Græcis innotuisse, clarum, & testatum apud eosdem est. Non ergo extra culpam fuerit Photius, & qui partes illius tutati sunt, dum de penitus perspectis, planeq; cognitis erroribus a reis, atque conuictis societatem, & officia soliditatis Romanis efflagitant. Quod ad aliud potius, lucra nempe sua atq; commoda, non ad errores, & dogmata respicientes communionem cum Latinis verterunt, digni sunt qui omnium in vituperationem cadant.
units.tr: John Veccus, book 3, to Sugdaex Theodore: "But no one among those who are fit to judge rightly would easily be persuaded of this," since no doctrinal speech is found published in that synod which was convened to confirm peace. If there was no discussion of doctrine in that synod and no address was given, how will these two Actions, which treat the doctrine with so many repeated words, stand on a firm foundation? On no footing at all. Therefore they must be thought fictitious, and attached to the synod by its opponents. The Greeks themselves, those who seemed to have some understanding, have also struck their use from their own writings. The schismatics themselves confess and profess this, those who do not praise the Photian synod equally and who charge the union effected through Photius with crime. For it is clear and attested among them that the errors of the Latins were known to the Greeks from the sixth synod itself. Photius therefore, and those who defended his side, were not free of blame, when they demanded society and the duties of solidarity with the Romans from men accused and convicted of errors that had been thoroughly examined and clearly known. Those who turned communion with the Latins to other ends, namely their own gain and advantage, and not looking to errors and doctrines, deserve to fall under the reproach of all.

units.la: Non sunt hæc argumenta Pontificiorum. Audiantur Schismatici. Georgius Scholarius, qui & Gennadius Monachus, licet longum nimis loquatur, de Processione Spiritus sancti, sect.1. cap.3.
units.tr: These are not the arguments of the Papists. Let the schismatics be heard. George Scholarius, who is also called Gennadius the Monk, although he speaks too long, On the Procession of the Holy Spirit, section 1, chapter 3:

units.la: Ἡ τοιαύτη τοίνυν ὥσε τῷ πνεύματι ἐξαιρέσει τὰς Ἐκκλησίας ἔτως ἐμπολιτευομένας [?], τότε μὲν ὅλον τὸ κοινὸν ἐκλύειν βλάπτειν, μὴ δὲ τὴν ἴσην [?] Σιῶν [?] φανερῶς [?] πολέμῳ κατέσπη [?], καὶ πῶς ἂν ἀσπῆσαι ἐχίζοντο τὰ ἀσφαλῆ [?], καὶ πάλιν, ἀπὸ μὴ ὥσε τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν γενομένων τῆς διαφορᾶς, ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ τὴν ἀρχὴν εἴπω [?], ἐν ἄλλοις ὡς τις χαιρουμένοις [?] χέζειν τὸν Ἐκκλησίαν ἢ ὥσε τὰ δόγματα κηρυττόμενα Λατίνων. Εἴτ᾽ ἂν ἀληθῶς δυνάμενοί τινες τὸν ἐν τῇ πίστει διαφορᾶς, ἀλλ᾽ ἡ τις ἔζει, καὶ παῦσαι γινωσκομένης τὰς Ἐκκλησίας διηρέσθαι, ὥστε σφίσιν συμφέρον ἰδίων αὐτῶν ἕνεκα· ὥσπερ τῆς ἐν τοῖς πιστοῖς δυνάμεως εἰς ἑνότητας τὰ χέοντω μεθισταμένης, οἷς τῆς Ἐκκλησιαστικῆς εἰρηνῆς ἠμέλησε, μᾶλλον δὲ τῷ σφετέρῳ καλῷ, ἢ τῇ βε-βαίῳ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ὁμονοίᾳ ἀπολυομένως [?] τὰ τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν [?] διελόντες [?] σωμάσκα [?] μηδὲ-μαρτὰς [?] ἀπὸ τῆς διαφορᾶς [?] ὕλης [?] γεγεννημένης. τὰ αὐτὰ ἢ καὶ ἀπὸ Φωτῖνῳ τῷ Δυτικῷ συμβῆν. ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς καὶ ἀλλὰ λέγειν τὰς Ἐκκλησίας ἀφορῆσαι [?], χερω-μαρτίῳ τῆς διαφορᾶς τῆς δόξης ἀσκαξόμενος [?]. καὶ πά-λιν τὰς τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν συμβάσεις μισθὸν ἀπέδωκε τῆς ἰδίων συμφερόντων αὐτῶν, ἵνα καὶ τὸ κακὸν μείζονα ὠνήσωνται τύλαπλον. ἔτι γὰρ δὴ μᾶλλον λέγω, ἢ ὡς ἴσως λέγεις· ἡμαρτηκότων ἢ πάντες τῶν τὰ τῆς πίστεως ἀληθείας, καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας εἰρήνην ἀπαρτίζει [?] τῆς ἑαυτῶν σκλεύας ποιέ-μουσι, καὶ πάντα πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον αὐτοῖς ἐλκον-τες. ἀλλ᾽ ἐχειρῷ αὐτὸν οἰκουμενικῷ κεινῷ [?] τῷ ἀφορισμῷ ἐπιζῆσαι [?], καὶ τὸ νωθρισμὸς τῆς Λατίνων τῇ κοινῇ προσβαλόντος βασάνῳ [?], ἢ καθ᾽ ἅπαξ αὐτὸν ἀπορεῖν [?], εἰ φαύλως τὰ πὰς ἀδύνατος [?], καὶ ἰσχυρῶμεν ἔφαν τὸ [?]. ἢ μηκέτι χωρισμὸς προφάσιν ὑπολιπάδα [?] τοῖς μετ᾽ αὐτόν, εἰ μηδὲν εἰς τὸ τῆς ἀσεβείας κεφάλαιον ἢ τῆς Λατίνων ἔβλαπτε [?] καὶ φόβον, ἀλλ᾽ ἁπαξ ἐωδάντας [?], ἰωμένης ἀμφιδῶ [?] ἀξι ἐνεκά γε τῷ πνεύματος. τότε γὰρ ἴσως καὶ ῥᾷον ἂν ἐπέστησε Λατίνοι, καὶ πρὸς τῷ κοινῷ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας μετέβαλλον γνώμην, ἐκ πολλῶν αἰτιῶν, ὡς πᾶς τις ἂν ἐκ ὁλκότως συνίσθοι. Δοκεῖ ἡ τοῖς ἀφαιρεματοῦχοις τῆς Ἐκκλησιῶν ἑνώσεως πο-λύ π πῶ συμβάλλεσθαι, καὶ τὸ μηδὲ ἐξω Λατίνων αὑαὐτὸν φανερῶς τῷ δόξαν ὁμολογεῖν, μήπω τοῖς ἡμετέροις μέμφεσθαι ὡς ἀλόγως αὐτὸν καταγω-μῶμος. [?] τοῦτ᾽ [?] ὄντως ἐν εἰς τῷ κοινῷ καταφρονῶν [?] ὁμολογίαν ἐκαλοῦμεν. ἀεὶ γὰρ τὸ τῆς πίστεως ἁμβάλλοντο σύμβολον, μῶμον ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐκ[?] μῶμον αὐ δὲ ἡ [?] ἐπιφράξιν ἢ ἀφαιρέσεως. Εἰ δὲ ἡ δόξα ζῶν τινες ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ ἐν τῇ [?] ὑῇ [?] ἐφασκον μηδὲν ἀδικεῖν, ὡς ἐν τῇ [?] ὡσὰ σοφίαι διδασκάλων φανερῶς ἐπιπλέον [?] λεγομένας. ἑαυτὸν ἡ μηδὲν [?] ὅλως [?] τὰ κοινὰ ὁμολογοῦντα [?] καὶ ὡς ἡ κοινὴ πίστις βάλλει τὰς τῆς διδασκάλων λέξεις νοεῖν. τὸ τῆς οὐσίας ἐνότητα, ἡ τῷ αἰτίᾳ βέλτιον θαυμάζειν πάσει-σάνδρ [?] ἐν τῇ τὸ πνεῦμα λέγειν ἐν τῇ ὑῇ.
units.tr: Such an approach, which so treats the Spirit as a matter of public policy, at one time harms the whole common good, and at another openly brings the Church into war, and how could it be possible to attain safety? Again, if the difference had not arisen from their faith but, to speak beyond the beginning, from some who rejoice in stirring up the Church, or from the doctrines of the Latins being proclaimed... Certain men who could truly remove the difference in faith, if it were known to be merely a matter of words, would have ended the division of the churches, but for their own advantage. Just as the power of the faithful is turned into unity by these things, they neglected ecclesiastical peace, or rather, for their own glory and not for the firm concord of the Church, they divided the churches and made spectacles of the matter born from the difference. The same thing happened with Photius the Westerner: he too, as they say, sought to separate the churches, using the difference of opinion as a pretext, and again, he gave the agreements of the churches as the price of his own advantage, so that they might gain greater evil in return. I say more strongly than perhaps you do: all those who have failed in the truth of faith, and who in it have disturbed the peace of the Church, make it a mockery and draw everything to their own advantage. But they were not able to undertake this, since the ecumenical sentence held them in check, and the Latins were moved by the common scrutiny, or once for all he was at a loss whether things had been wrongly done... Nor should separation leave a pretext to those who come after, if nothing was harmful or frightening in the chief point of impiety of the Latins, but they had once been admitted, and the doubt was healed for the sake of the Spirit. For then perhaps the Latins would more easily have agreed, and would have changed their opinion alongside the common judgment of the Church, for many reasons, as anyone may readily understand. It seems that much contributes to the division of the churches when a man openly declares his opinion in a way that is not Latin, and then blames our people as if they condemned him without reason. For they always cast the symbol of faith on themselves as a reproach, and again the separation or taking away of the ... ; and if some of them in their own doctrine said the Spirit was in the ... and insisted that they did no wrong, as wisdom is openly said to be taught by teachers ... they, in saying nothing at all, confessed the common things, and as the common faith casts the words of the teachers to be understood... the unity of the essence, or rather it is better to marvel at the speaking of the Spirit in the Son.

units.la: Hoc de Spiritu discrimen hac ratione in Ecclesiam introductum, tum quidem primum pacem non nimis laedebat: sed statim atque Sexta Synodus celebrata est, apertius quam antea deprehensum, patentis diffidij initium extitit. Et licet prius ad tempus scinderentur, rursusque in unionem coirent, acsi illa differentia non essent de fide, sed postmodum scindere Ecclesiam cupientibus non absque ratione fuit obtentus, circa dogma Latinorum innovatio. Hinc nonnulli discrimen in fide, quod verum erat, & omnibus cognitum, arripientes Ecclesias scindebant, quod ita sibi in propriis causis commodum futurum existimarent, cum in similibus potestas in alios atque alios caderet, qui Ecclesiasticæ paci operam dabant, popotius in proprijs commodis, quam stabili Ecclesia unioni absque multarum rerum aggressione Ecclesiarum scandala dissolvebant, nullo de differentijs iudicio constituto. Hac eadem & in Photio tandem evenere. Nanque ipse, & dividere Ecclesias aggressus sub umbra opinionum differentia, rursumque Ecclesiarum conciliationem proprijs suis commodis lucrum fecit, ut malo malum peiori minus sibi compararet. Sic enim afferendum est potius, quam dici assolet.
units.tr: This division over the Spirit, introduced into the Church on this ground, did not at first greatly disturb the peace. But as soon as the Sixth Synod was held, and the matter was detected more clearly than before, it became the beginning of an open rift. Although the churches were at first split for a time and then came together again, as if that difference were not a matter of faith, a pretext was later found, not without reason, for those who wished to rend the Church: the innovation concerning the Latins' dogma. From this some people seized on a difference in faith, which was real and known to all, and split the churches, thinking it would serve their own interests. In similar cases power passed from one party to another, and those who worked for peace in the Church, preferring their own advantage to the stable unity of the Church, dissolved it, causing scandals to many churches and without any judgment being made on the differences. The same thing finally happened under Photius. He too, after trying to divide the churches under the cover of a difference of opinion, then profited from restoring their union for his own benefit, so that by one evil he might gain for himself a lesser evil. For this is better put in the way it is commonly said.

units.la: Omnes vero culpam commerebantur, tanquam qui fidei veritatem, & Ecclesiasticam pacem propriae gloriae postponerent, omniaque ad suam utilitatem traherent: sed oportebat ipsos universali iudicio differentiam committere, & innovatione Latinorum communi examini subiecta, vel semel ab ipsis disiungi, si male illi credebant, & in sententia contumaces perstisterent; aut nullum amplius in posterum successoribus divisionis obtentum relinquere, si in nihilo pietatis caput Latinorum innovatio vulnerabat: sed semel societate iunctos in ea unione perpetuo perdurare ob causam Spiritus. Tum enim fortasse & facilius persuasi fuissent Latini, & communi Ecclesia sententia Latini manus dedissent multas ob causas, quas unusquisque parvo negotio deprehenderit. Videtur porro absque multa indagine absolutis Ecclesia unionibus nimium tum temporis conducere potuisse, quod nec Latini ipsi aperte sententiam profiterentur, neque nostros criminarentur, nulla ratione eos accusantes. quin imo oppositum, adhortantes nempe, ut communem professionem exscularentur, semper enim Symbolum fidei proponebant manens in ipsis & praedicatum absque ulla additione, aut imminutione. Et licet apud ipsos nonnulli tenerent, Spiritum ex Filio quoque progredi, nulli aiebant voces illas iniurias esse, cum ita Patres ipsorum aperte docerent, semetipsos vero nihil praeterquam quod communi Ecclesiae sensu decretum fuerat tenere profitebantur, & ut communis fides Doctorum, intelligebant, hoc est unionem essentiae, non causam velle se indicare, cum afferrent Spiritum ex Filio. Et Niceta Cartophylax Nicaenus Auctor antiquior, de causis ob quas a Constantinopolitana Ecclesia Romana divisa est, Τίσσαρα [?] καὶ [?] τῶν Φωτίου [?] τῆς Κωνσταντινουπόλεως μέγα [?] τὸ σχίσμα, καὶ πολλὰ τὰ ἀπάσματα τῶν Ῥωμαίων, ὡς ἡ ἱστορία [?] τῆς [?] [?] ἐκκλησίας [?] . Γενομένης ἢ ἐνώσεως τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, ὡς ἡ αὐτὴ Φωτίου συνάγαγε Σωσθένης [?], καὶ ἐνωθέντος Ἰωάννης τῆς Ῥώμης, καὶ λαβόντες καινοτομίας τὰ ἀρχαῖα [?] ἐξ ἐκείνων [?] μὴ, ἃ Ῥωμαϊκὰ ἀπάσματα, ἃ καὶ ἡ ἐκτὸς Σωσθένης, ὡς ἀρχὴ [?], καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Φώτιος καλεῖ, ἐπὶ [?] πάντως αἰσχύνασθαι [?]. Ἐπὶ τὸ οὖν τῆς ἐκτῆς Σωσθένης μέχρι τῆς ἐβδόμης παρέδρομεν ἐν πλατυτέρων ὄντων [?], καὶ ἦσαν αἱ Ἐκκλησίαι λίωλωωλύσαι, καὶ ἡδὺς λόγος ἀεὶ τ σφαλμάτων τῆς Ρωμαίων, εἰ μὴ σωίβη ἡ εἰκονομαχικὴ αἵρεσις, ἀλλ' ἵνα καὶ μιδὴς ἐχίδνας[?]. Α'πὸ ἢ τῆς ἑβδόμης ὅτι τὰ ἀεὶ μέχρι καὶ Φωτίου, ἀλλ' ἔτι λόγος τῆς ἀεὶ αὐτῶν[?]. ὀργιμὼ Φωτίου μὴ πολλῷ καταβολῇ, καὶ πάλιν ἀπολυφαλμούς[?] παλιν ἰωάν[?] Ρωμαίοις, καὶ τῆς Ἐκκλησιῶν ἐνώσεως, κἂν ἔτι τὸ Σιρίας τὸ ὅτι τὸ Βουλγαρικὸν [?] λέγῃ[?] πάλιν χίσμα ἡμέας[?], καὶ ποίαν ἢ αἰτίαν ἀγνοῶ, δοκεῖ μήπω δῆλον εἶναι θεόν[?]. ἀλλ' εἰ μὴ ἄγνοια ἦν τῶν Ρωμαϊκῶν σφαλμάτων ἢ κοινωνίαν ἴσως ἐδὲς ἐμέμφετο.
units.tr: All, however, deserved blame, as men who put their own glory before the truth of the faith and the peace of the Church, and who turned everything to their own advantage. Instead, they ought to have committed the difference to a universal judgment, and, the innovation of the Latins being subjected to common examination, either have separated from them once and for all, if the Latins believed wrongly and persisted obstinately in their opinion; or else have left no pretext for division to their successors, if the Latins' innovation did not wound the chief point of piety at all. Once joined in fellowship they should have remained perpetually in that union for the sake of the Spirit. For then perhaps the Latins would have been more easily persuaded, and would have yielded to the common opinion of the Church for many reasons, which anyone may discover with little effort. It seems that, without much searching, after the unions of the Church had been settled, it could have been greatly to the advantage of that time, since the Latins themselves did not openly profess their opinion, nor did they accuse ours, accusing them on no ground at all. On the contrary, they urged them to adopt the common profession, for they always set forth the creed of faith remaining in its own form and preached without any addition or diminution. And although some among them held that the Spirit also proceeds from the Son, none said those words were wrongful, since their own Fathers taught this plainly. As for themselves, they professed that they held nothing beyond what had been decreed by the common sense of the Church, and they understood, as the common faith of the teachers does, that when they said the Spirit proceeds from the Son they meant to indicate the unity of essence, not a cause. And Niketas the Chartophylax of Nicaea, an older author, on the causes for which the Roman Church was separated from the Church of Constantinople, writes that the schism was great under Photius, and that there were many blemishes of the Romans, as the history of the Church relates. When the union of the Church was made, as the same Photius gathered it through Sosthenes, and John of Rome was united with it, and they received innovations from them... the Roman blemishes, which Sosthenes outside, as a beginning, and Photius himself calls, were altogether to be ashamed of. Therefore from the sixth to the seventh Synod they passed over these things in more ample form, and the churches were ... and there was always talk of the errors of the Romans, unless the Iconoclast heresy arose, but in order that ... of the vipers. From the seventh [Synod] ... until Photius ... but again a discourse of them... Photius, not by much foundation, and again the Romans were ... and the union of the Churches, even if still the Bulgarian ... says the schism again ... I do not know what cause, it seems not yet clear to God. But unless there was ignorance of the Roman errors, perhaps they did not blame the communion.

units.la: Ἐπεὶ ἢ ὅτο ἢ ἐκ τῆς Σωσιδὴς ἐγνώσθη, ἐ ὅτι τὸ Φωτίῳ ξανώτερον μεμπτέα ἡ ἕνωσις. ἐχελῶ ἡ ὁ ἐκείνων κακὸν, καὶ ἀποφρέφεις, ἢ ἀὁρθώ(ζα)σιν. εἰ τὴν δυνάμιν ὑπερέβαλες ἢ ἀὁρθωσις, τὼς ἐξ λόγων αὐτῆς ἐλῶν[?]. εἰ ἢ ἐλαπικὰ τὰ αἰπάμαία[?], ὅπερ ἀπίθυνον, ἀκόλαστα ἢ ταῦτα οἱ ἑώμενοι εἰς Ἕσπερον χρόνον, ἵνα τὶ καζεμένην[?] νῦν οἱ Λαῖνοι, ὀρθῶς φεγνεῖν λέγοντες.
units.tr: Since ... it was known from Sosthenes ... that the union was more blameworthy than under Photius. Rather, the evil of those men, and the correction, or ... If the correction exceeded its power, let it be judged from the words of it. If the ... things, which is absurd, the ones remaining into the western time, that is, the Latins, rightly say they are found in error.

units.la: Decimum quartum sub Photio Constantinopolitano magnum exortum est schisma, & multa in Romanos criminationes, vt Encyclica Epistola exhibet: subsecuta vero Ecclesiarum vnione, vti a Photio conflata Synodus edocet, & vnito Ioanne Romano, cum canonice antiquissima priuilegia obtinuisset, Romanae criminationes, quas & sancta Synodus, & Photius ipse in crimen adducunt, prorsus absque vllo examine silentio praeterita sunt. A sexta itaItaque Synodo ad septimam preterierunt anni quadraginta octo, & Ecclesia communicabant, & de Romanorum erroribus nullus sermo habitus est, nisi Iconoclastarum haeresis exorta fuisset, cuius causa rursum Ecclesia scissæ[?] sunt; a septima vero ad tempora subsequentia usque ad Photium, neque ullus pari modo de iisdem sermo fuit. Verum Photius post vehementem criminationem, & turbas absque multo negotio iterum cum Romanis societatem iniit, & similiter perdurabat Ecclesiarum unio, licet sub Sergio, qui Patriarchatum tenuit, sub Bulgaricida dicatur schisma renouatum. quam vero ob[?] causam ignoro; sed opinor causa sedium. Quod si Romanorum errores non innotescebant, nemo fortasse communionem criminabitur. Verum tamen cum a sexta Synodo iam paterent, & sub Photio magis ac magis, culpanda unio est: Addecebat[?] siquidem, quod malum indicauerant, vel vitare, vel saltem corrigere. Quod si supra facultatem correctio erat, minimum per sermones se opponere. Si tamen criminationes fidem non vulnerant, quod suaderi non ita facile est, qui illa per tot tempora indemnata relinquunt, qua de causa nunc Latini accusantur afferentes sese recte sentire? Et Auctor Anonymus, de iisdem dissidijs in Codice MS. Graeco Vaticano Num. 1150. Ἐπὶ Φωτίου, ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ἀντὶ πίστεως [illegible, ~12 letters] μεγάλη. ἀφίεσι δὲ [illegible, ~10 letters] φρασίικῶν σφαλμάτων, ὣς ἐπ' ὧν καὶ οἱ τῆς ἑκτης ἐπισημήναντο. ἀλλ' ἐνώσεως ἡρυομένης Φωτὸς [?] Ἰωάννης τῷ Πάπα, οὐ μόνον τὰ αἰτιάματα ὡς ἀὐθρώπινα παρ-έδραμον ἀσυζήτητα, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἀρχαῖα δίκαια τῆς Ῥώμης [?] ἐχ' ὦ νῦν ὑκ ἔχων ὀφείται. Ἀπὸ γοῦ τῆς ἑκτης ἄχρι ἰβδόμης ἐπὶ ἱβδόμη ἐπὶ ἐν τῇ ἱβδόμῃ ἡπάσθη οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι ἐπὶ τῇ ἑκτῃ σφάλματα.
units.tr: Under Photius of Constantinople there arose the great schism in the fourteenth century, and many accusations against the Romans, as the encyclical letter sets forth. But after the union of the churches was afterwards made, as the synod gathered by Photius teaches, and when John of Rome had been united, and had obtained the most ancient privileges by canon, the Roman accusations, which both the holy Synod and Photius himself brought as charges, were passed over in complete silence without any examination. From the sixth Synod to the seventh, forty-eight years passed, and the churches communicated, and no discourse was held about the errors of the Romans, unless the heresy of the Iconoclasts had arisen, on whose account the churches were again divided. From the seventh Synod to the times following, down to Photius, there was likewise no discussion of those matters. But Photius, after vehement accusation and disturbances, entered into fellowship again with the Romans without much difficulty, and the union of the churches continued in the same way, although under Sergius, who held the patriarchate, a schism is said to have been renewed under the Bulgarian business. But I do not know the cause, though I suppose it was a matter of the sees. If the errors of the Romans had not become known, perhaps no one would have blamed the communion. Yet since they had been laid open by the sixth Synod, and under Photius more and more, the union is to be blamed. For it was fitting either to avoid the evil they had pointed out, or at least to correct it. But if correction was beyond their power, at least they should have opposed it by their words. If, however, the accusations do not wound the faith, which is not so easy to persuade, why do those who leave them unpunished for so many ages now accuse the Latins, who claim to think rightly? And an anonymous author, on the same disagreements, in the Greek manuscript Codex Vaticanus number 1150, says: under Photius, as the Church ... great. But when the union was sought with the Pope John, they passed over the accusations as human, undisputed, and the ancient rights of Rome ... Hence from the sixth to the seventh, and again to the seventh, the Romans were charged with the errors of the sixth.

units.la: πάλιν ἀπὸ τῆς ἑκτης μέχρι Φωτίου ἱκανοῦ παρελθόντος χρόνου, ὥζαύτως ζήτησις ἡ συμβέβηκε, καὶ μάλιστα δὴ Φωτίου, ἐς ἀρχιερεὺς ἐχελῶ σφόδρα δὴ ἀλλοφωσάζασθαι τὰ ἰδιαῖα, καὶ ἔτως ἐνωθῶναι τοῖς Ῥωμαῖς. ἐπ' δὲ Σεργίῳ τῷ ὅτι τῷ Βουλγαρικῷ χρίσμα. εἰ μὲν δὴ τὰ σφάλματα τὰ Ῥωμαϊκὰ ἐπὶ πῶς ἀπεξέσεια ταῦτα ἀφαδραμόντες οἱ σεφολύων. εἰ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ τῆς σεφολουμένων, καὶ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῶν δικαίων ὑφιστάμενοι πολυθρυλούμενα ὁ βυλόμενος. ἰδὲ γὰρ καὶ ἡ ἐπὶ τὰ πνεύματα βλασφημία, καὶ ἡ τῆς ἀζύμων κατάχρησις, καὶ τῆς ἀβαπτίστων ἡ τήρησις, καὶ τὸ βλήλυκτον ἡγεῖσθαι πὲν τῆς ἱερῶν χάμον, καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐν τῇ εἰκωνλίῳ τῆς Φωτίῳ τῇ ἐπὶ τῆς μὴ Ἰωάννη τῷ Πάπα ἐνώσεως, καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐκτῇ ἐμφιέσοντα. Πῶς γοῦν λύων, ὅποε̈ρ μὴ τὰ ταύταν ἀλογοπάτων διαφορᾶ.
units.tr: Again, after a considerable lapse of time from the sixth [Synod] to Photius, a similar dispute arose, and especially under Photius, who was very eager to alter his own opinions and so unite with the Romans. And under Sergius came the schism over the Bulgarian chrism. If indeed these Roman errors had been wiped away in some way, they passed over them; but if they remained, and the Roman rights stood firm, let whoever wishes take up the much-repeated charges. For there is the blasphemy concerning the Spirit, the misuse of unleavened bread, the keeping of the unbaptized, the holding that the sacred ... is polluted, and the rest, which appear in the time of Photius, in the union under Pope John, and in the sixth [Synod]. How then, by resolving them, could one not refute these accusations as absurd differences?

units.la: Sub Photio, ut Epistola eius Encyclica personat, magnum diffidium exortum est propter errores Latinorum, quae Synodi sexta Patres indicarunt, sed unione Photij perfecta, & Papae Ioannis, non tantum criminationes velut res ludicras absque ullo examine obicuerunt, sed & pervetusta jura Romae confirmarunt, quae modo non possidet. Itaque a sexta Synodo usque ad septimam cum praeterissent anni centum quadraginta octo, neq; antea, neque in septima delati sunt impietatis Romani ob errores in sexta propositos. Rursumque a sexta ad Photium cum non paruum tempus intercessisset, similiter quaestio ulla mota non est. & potissimum sub Photio, quos Praesules oportebat antea similia corrigere, & postmodum unionem cum Romanis amplecti. Praeterea sub Sergio Patriarcha, qui praefuit sub Bulgarica sda[?] nouum dissidium exortum est. Si propter Latinorum errores, qua ratione illos praetereuntes uniti sunt, an vero propter privilegiorum, & jurium subreptionem, cuicunque id in animo est, curiosius perquirat. Ecce enim & de Spiritu blasphemia, & Azymorum abusus, & Sabbatorum observatio & inter abominanda reputare Sacerdotum matrimonia, & reliqua in Encyclica Epistola Photii ante unionem Joannis accensita, & in sexta Synodo relata. Qua ergo ratione post causam adeo justam, & dissidium uniti sunt usque dum non didici. Concludamus ergo in hac Octaua Photiana Synodo nullam habitam rationem dogmatis, Photium sua commoda non fidem circumspectasse, licet dogmata Latinorum Constantinopolitanis Patriarchis, aliisque Orienta-lilibus a Sexta Synodo innotuissent, quae post Photium apud Orientales per multos annos indemnata fuere. Ergo vel Photius impius est, & auitae suae fidei proditor, qui ab Hæreticis in thronum restitui procurauit, & cum ipsis associatus uti fratres, & Patres eos agnoscit, & laudat, & eorum se precibus ad Deum committit: vel hae postremae Synodi Actiones nullo modo sub Photio habitae sunt: & sic erunt figmenta, ac portenta posteriorum Schismaticorum impudenti solertia adinuenta.
units.tr: Under Photius, as his encyclical letter declares, a great dispute arose over the errors of the Latins, which the Fathers of the Sixth Synod had pointed out. But once Photius and Pope John were united, the Easterners not only let these charges drop, as though they were trifles, without any examination, but also confirmed the ancient rights of Rome, which they no longer hold. So from the Sixth Synod to the Seventh, one hundred and forty-eight years passed, and the Romans were neither previously nor at the Seventh Synod accused of impiety for the errors put forward at the Sixth. Again, from the Sixth Synod to Photius, a considerable time elapsed, and no such question was raised. Above all under Photius, the bishops who ought earlier to have corrected such things then embraced union with the Romans. Moreover, under the Patriarch Sergius, who presided when the Bulgarian ... a new dissension arose. If it was on account of the errors of the Latins, why did they unite with them while passing these over? Or was it rather on account of the usurpation of privileges and rights? Let anyone who wishes to know examine this more carefully. For see, the blasphemy concerning the Spirit, the abuse of unleavened bread, the observance of the Sabbaths, and the regarding of priests' marriages as abominations, and the rest, were all listed in Photius's encyclical letter before his union with John and were recorded in the Sixth Synod. By what reason, then, after so just a cause and so great a dissension, did they unite? I have not learned this. Let us conclude, therefore, that in this Eighth Synod under Photius no account was taken of doctrine; Photius looked to his own advantage, not to the faith. Although the doctrines of the Latins had become known to the Patriarchs of Constantinople and to other Easterners from the Sixth Synod, they were left unpunished among the Easterners for many years after Photius. So either Photius is impious and a traitor to his ancestral faith, who procured his restoration to the throne through heretics, associated with them as brothers, acknowledges and praises them as Fathers, and commits himself to their prayers before God; or these last acts of the Synod were in no way performed under Photius, and so they will be fictions and monstrous inventions of later schismatics, devised with shameless cleverness.

units.la: Neq; enim de Photio viro sanctissimo, & Catholicae fidei propugnatore aliud sentiendum est, qui Synodo Septimae illiusque decretis addictissimus, nunquam passus esset illius dogmata vel minimum violari, cum in ea a Tarasio Actione prima definitum legatur Τὸ κακὸν ἤδη κακόν ἐστι, ἢ μάλιστα ἐν Ἐκκλησιαστικοῖς πράγμασι [?]. τὸ γὰρ ἐν δόγματι εἴτε ἐν μικρῷ [?], εἴτε ἐν μεγάλῳ ἁμαρτάνειν, τοῦτο ἔστιν· ὡς ἀμφοτέρων γὰρ ὁ νόμος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπαγορεύει [?]. Quod malum est, iam utiq; malum est, & maxime in negotijs Ecclesiasticis. In dogmatum quippe causa, siue in parua, siue in magna peccare, id ipsum est: ex utrisque enim lex Dei improbatur. Quæ & Photium adnotasse, obseruasseque ex ipsius Epistola Encyclica cognoscimus: Καὶ γὰρ ἔχειν ὄντως κοινὰ πάντων· ἃ πάντας φυλάττειν ἐπάναγναῖκες. Καὶ ᾧδέ γε τῇ ἄλλων τὰ σφῇ τῆς πίστεως· ἵνα καὶ τὸ παρεισάγειν μικρόν, ὃ μὴ πρὸς ἓν ἀμφι-[?] νὰν τῶν ψυχῶν τὸν θάνατον. Nam revera communia omnibus sunt, quae omnes custodire necesse est, & ante alia quae de fide habemus, ubi vel paulum declinare, est mortifero se periculo obstringere. Compertum itaque erat Photio, quanti dogma Fidei aestimandum esset, videbatque certissimè, quantum illius, vel minima laesio damnum afferret Ecclesiae, & nihilominus sua commoda communi Ecclesiae bono, & salutì aeternae dignitatem terrenam praetulit sanctissimus vir.
units.tr: For we must not think otherwise of Photius, a most holy man and defender of the Catholic faith, who, being most devoted to the Seventh Synod and its decrees, would never have allowed its doctrines to be violated even in the slightest, since it is read there that the First Action of Tarasius defined: "What is evil is already evil, and especially in ecclesiastical matters. For to sin in doctrine, whether in a small matter or a great one, this is so, for the law of God forbids both." [Τὸ κακὸν ἤδη κακόν ἐστι, ἢ μάλιστα ἐν Ἐκκλησιαστικοῖς πράγμασι. τὸ γὰρ ἐν δόγματι εἴτε ἐν μικρῷ, εἴτε ἐν μεγάλῳ ἁμαρτάνειν, τοῦτο ἔστιν· ὡς ἀμφοτέρων γὰρ ὁ νόμος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπαγορεύει.] We know that Photius also noted and observed this from his own encyclical letter: "For indeed these are truly common to all, which all must keep; and before other things that we have concerning the faith, where even a little deviation binds one to a deadly peril." [Καὶ γὰρ ἔχειν ὄντως κοινὰ πάντων· ἃ πάντας φυλάττειν ἐπάναγκες.] Photius therefore knew well how highly the doctrine of the faith was to be valued, and he saw most clearly how great a loss to the Church even the smallest injury to it would bring; yet this most holy man preferred his own advantage to the common good of the Church and to eternal salvation, and set earthly dignity above them.

units.la: Illud quoque considerandum est, etiam si concludamus, dictas Actiones a Photio una cum Legatis Pontificijs habitas fuisse, nihil illas ad definiendum dogma de Processione Spiritus ex Filio pertinere, quod id nullo modo condemnatum est; cum nec alia, quae Trullana Synodus, quam supra sextam vocavit Nicetas cap. 13. 52. 55.; & 67. & Photius Latinis opposuit, condemnata sint, quod ex Niceta Nicaeno de dissidiis Graecorum, & Latinorum addiscimus. Et ego credam, in Actionibus hisce de dogmate actum fuisse, & quod magis est, sententiam Latinorum ex Filio condemnatam? Atrox flagitium est, quod apud suos Photinos Photius contrahit. Cui haeresis antea
units.tr: It must also be considered that, even if we conclude that the said Actions were held by Photius together with the Papal legates, they do not pertain at all to defining the doctrine of the Procession of the Spirit from the Son, since that was in no way condemned. For neither were those other things condemned which the Trullan Synod, which Nicetas called the Sixth, and which Photius opposed to the Latins (chapters 13, 52, 55, 67, as Nicetas cites), nor do we learn anything else from Nicetas of Nicaea about the disputes between the Greeks and the Latins. Am I to believe that doctrine was treated in these Actions, and, what is more, that the Latin opinion on the Filioque was condemned? It is a monstrous crime that Photius incurs among his own Photians. Heresy formerly...

units.la: O publipublice & voce, & scripto proclamata, errores, & crimina non multo ante Romanis inclementer obiecta, impietatisque manifesto modo prehensa, dum vno consensu cum Romanis iungitur, ludi sunt pueriles, & nugamenta, & vt res nullius momenti, adeo inconsiderate posthabentur, vna sola in Patriarchatu restitutione, quia optata contigit, vendidit Photius pietatem, Fidem, Ecclesiam, Christum: quae parentes, & progenitores sanguine, & vita per tot secula redemerunt, sola ambitione Photij turpissimo mercatu prostituuntur. Eant nunc Photiani, & sanctitatem nobis Photij, & sapientiam, & diuinum cultum, & pro Religione certamina, & reliqua, quae in hac Octaua Synodo ad nauseam repetitis clamoribus depraedicantur, insonent. Fides. Catholica infeliciter proscribitur, pietas conculcatur, Christus misere a nouo Iuda diuenditur, & haeresis, & errores profligati, vna cum restitutione Photij in Patriarchatum, in Ecclesiam, in fidelium animos restituuntur. Quamuis ipse Photianus non sim, ne[?] in eum inclementior videar, vocem pro eo mittam, & causam suscipiam. Vexatio dat intellectum: ideoque condemnatus, fugatus, proiectus in exilium, errans, & vndique exclusus, quam in prospera fortuna perdiderat sapientiam adipiscitur, & probra in Romanos iniuste a se iacta fuisse agnoscens, veritatem quam criminatus fuerat, etiam inuitus amplectitur, & cum non posset amouere, vulpino consilio excipit, & ore tacito insimulat, & cum non interponat damnationem, quod non erat, esse simulat. Non est ergo hisce Actionibus dogma damnatum. Quod si dogma non sanum reputatum fuisset, neque Photius, neque alij Græci, qui eum subsecuti sunt, unquam eorum societatem admisissent, quod supra annotauerat iam dictus Niceta.
units.tr: Errors and crimes which had shortly before been publicly and vocally and in writing proclaimed against the Romans without mercy, and impiety plainly grasped, are, once Photius joins with the Romans in one accord, set aside so carelessly as childish games, trifles, and matters of no moment. By the single restoration to the Patriarchate, which he obtained as he wished, Photius sold piety, faith, Church, and Christ. Those whom our forebears and progenitors redeemed through so many ages with blood and life are prostituted in a most shameful bargain, by the ambition of Photius alone. Let the Photians now go forth and sound out to us the holiness, wisdom, and divine worship of Photius, and his struggles for religion, and the rest that are extolled with clamours repeated to nausea in this Eighth Synod. The Catholic faith is unhappily proscribed, piety is trampled underfoot, Christ is wretchedly sold by a new Judas, and heresies and errors, once put to flight, are restored along with Photius's restoration to the Patriarchate, into the Church, into the minds of the faithful. Although I am not a Photian myself, lest I seem too harsh towards him, I will speak a word on his behalf and take up his cause. Affliction gives understanding: thus Photius, condemned, put to flight, cast into exile, wandering, and shut out on every side, has gained the wisdom he had lost in prosperity, and, acknowledging that the reproaches he had unjustly flung at the Romans were false, he embraces against his will the truth he had accused them of denying; and since he cannot remove it, he receives it with fox-like counsel, and, with a silent mouth, pretends to admit it, and, since he does not pronounce a condemnation, pretends that there was none to pronounce. Therefore no doctrine was condemned in these Actions. For if the doctrine had been judged unsound, neither Photius nor the other Greeks who followed him would ever have admitted communion with them, as the aforementioned Nicetas had already noted.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: Chapter XI.

units.la: In illa Synodo de Dogmate nullus sermo habitus est, nec Commonitorio Pontificio in omnibus obtemperatum, ideo facta omnia in dicta Synodo & potissimum in his Actioni- bus irrita, infectaque remanent.
units.tr: In that Synod no discussion of doctrine took place, and the Papal Commonitorium was not obeyed in all respects; therefore everything done in that Synod, and especially in these Acts, remains void and invalid.

units.la: SEd damnatur additio. Quid tum? Aliud est Processio Spiritus etiam ex Filio, aliud illius in Symbolo Additio. Processionem plerosque ex Græcis schismaticis non damnasse, tantummodo Additionem, fuse a nobis alibi probatum est. Sed cum damnatur additio in Symbolo, in Symbolo tum temporis additionem fuisse perspicuum est. Non puto. Tum enim in Ecclesia Romana Symbolum absque ea additione recitatum fuisse existimo, & videtur ex his Actionibus colligi. Ioannes enim decreta Leonis Papae non ita facile, nec tam cito abdicasset. Credidit Ioannes processionem Spiritus etiam ex Filio, sed illam in Symbolo recitasse non adeo facilis probationis est.
units.tr: But the addition is condemned. So what? The procession of the Spirit from the Son also is one thing, and the addition of it to the Creed is another. That most of the schismatic Greeks did not condemn the procession, but only the addition, I have proved at length elsewhere. But when the addition is condemned in the Creed, it is clear that the addition was then in the Creed. I do not think so. For I believe that at that time the Creed was recited in the Roman Church without that addition, and this seems to be gathered from these Acts. John did not so easily or so quickly renounce the decrees of Pope Leo. John believed in the procession of the Spirit from the Son also, but that he recited it in the Creed is not an easy thing to prove.

units.la: Καὶ μή τις τῶν ἐθελοκάκων συγχωρῶν ὁρμῇ ὡς ἐς ταῦτα λέγειν τὰ τῆς οἰκείας γνώμης ἐκτίθεια, ὡς πᾶν Φωτίῳ, καὶ τῇ Σωσόδῳ ἐ πέφασκται, καὶ κεκύρωται τῆς τῆς πίστεως συμβόλου [?] ἀπαγνωσθέντα ὡς τὴν Ῥωμαίων δὴ [?] εἰς τὸ αὐτὸ συνῳδευόντων· καὶ [?] συνῳδευμένων ἀθέσιν.
units.tr: Let none of the ill-disposed, yielding to impulse, presume to set forth on these matters the things of his own opinion, as if everything was declared and confirmed by Photius and Sosodus, and the Creed of faith [?] was rejected [?], as if the Romans, indeed, agreed with them in the same thing, and as if they were in harmony [?] with the rejection. [Καὶ μή τις τῶν ἐθελοκάκων συγχωρῶν ὁρμῇ ὡς ἐς ταῦτα λέγειν τὰ τῆς οἰκείας γνώμης ἐκτίθεια, ὡς πᾶν Φωτίῳ, καὶ τῇ Σωσόδῳ ἐ πέφασκται, καὶ κεκύρωται τῆς τῆς πίστεως συμβόλου [?] ἀπαγνωσθέντα ὡς τὴν Ῥωμαίων δὴ [?] εἰς τὸ αὐτὸ συνῳδευόντων· καὶ [?] συνῳδευμένων ἀθέσιν.]

units.la: Τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἔτι τὸ σύμβολον ὑπαναγνωσθῆναι δεχόμαι καὶ αὐτός, καὶ ὅπου τούτοις ζυγομαχήσω τινὶ, ἐς ἀ εἰδῶς εἶναι ἐν Ῥωμαίοις; καὶ κοινῇ μὲν ἡμῖν ἰδία κατὰ πάντας τὰς ἡμέρας ὠφελισμένας ἐκφωνοῦντας αὐτὸ καὶ ἡ ἀρχαία παράδοσις. τοῦτο δὲ βούλομαι γνῶναι ὡς εἰ δολιμαπικῶν λόγων κινηθέντων πρός τινας, εἰ καὶ πύρων χωρεῖς αὐξεπίσως, ὅπως ἐ ὡς; οἷον ὁμολογουμένῳ τῷ θεσπίσματι Ῥωμαίοι κακῶς φεγοῦντες, ὅπως τῆς τῆς ἀθεσίας [?] λόγοις ἐλέγχης, ἐ τῇ ταύτης ἀθεσίᾳ σωιέσθω, τὸ μαθεῖν ἐθέλω.
units.tr: For I myself also accept that the Creed was read again, and where I would contend with anyone about these things, knowing [them] among the Romans; and both commonly with us and privately, on all the days [of observance], the ancient tradition proclaims it. But I wish to know this: if, with deceitful words stirred up against certain people, you go on [?] with fire [?], how [?]... as if by agreeing with the decree the Romans are wrongly blamed; so that you may refute them with the words of their unbelief, I want to learn whether it is preserved by their unbelief. [Τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἔτι τὸ σύμβολον ὑπαναγνωσθῆναι δεχόμαι καὶ αὐτός, καὶ ὅπου τούτοις ζυγομαχήσω τινὶ, ἐς ἀ εἰδῶς εἶναι ἐν Ῥωμαίοις; καὶ κοινῇ μὲν ἡμῖν ἰδία κατὰ πάντας τὰς ἡμέρας ὠφελισμένας ἐκφωνοῦντας αὐτὸ καὶ ἡ ἀρχαία παράδοσις. τοῦτο δὲ βούλομαι γνῶναι ὡς εἰ δολιμαπικῶν λόγων κινηθέντων πρός τινας, εἰ καὶ πύρων χωρεῖς αὐξεπίσως, ὅπως ἐ ὡς; οἷον ὁμολογουμένῳ τῷ θεσπίσματι Ῥωμαίοι κακῶς φεγοῦντες, ὅπως τῆς τῆς ἀθεσίας [?] λόγοις ἐλέγχης, ἐ τῇ ταύτης ἀθεσίᾳ σωιέσθω, τὸ μαθεῖν ἐθέλω.]

units.la: Et nullus eorum, qui sponte deteriora capessendi impetu procedunt, ad haec propriae sententiae abortus enunciet, omnia a Synodo, & Photio absoluta esse & stabilita: cum fidei Symbolum absque additione recitatum fuisset, quasi vero Romani in illius consensissent, & conuenissent improbationem. Symbolum etenim eo modo lectum fuisse & ipse recipio, neque de eo cum aliquo contendam, donec video Romanos & communiter nobiscum, & priuatis certis praescriptis diebus recitantes illud secundum antiquam traditionem. Illud porro scire aueo, si tum temporis de dogmate sermones agitati sint, an vero iis neglectis absque vllo examine, & quasi res in confesso esset, Romani vti male sentientes de additione deprehensi sint, & illius improbationi assensum praestiterunt. Hoc vero scire aueo. Ioannes Veccus ad Sugdæae Theodorum lib. 3.
units.tr: And let none of those who rush headlong into worse things put forward, from this abortion of his own opinion, that everything was absolved and established by the Synod and by Photius, since the Creed had been recited without addition, as if the Romans had indeed agreed with and assented to its condemnation. I too admit that the Creed was read in that way, and I will not contend about it with anyone, until I see the Romans reciting it both in common with us and privately on certain prescribed days, according to the ancient tradition. Moreover, I am eager to know this: whether at that time matters of doctrine were debated, or whether, those matters being neglected without any examination, and as if the question were already settled, the Romans, caught holding wrong views about the addition, gave their assent to its condemnation. This I am eager to know. John Veccus, to Theodore of Sugdaea, book 3.

units.la: Ταῦτα λέγοντος ἐπισκοπῆς Φώτιον οἱ πρὸς ἡμᾶς σὺν λόγῳ πιέ-σαι, οἷον τῆς ἐχθρας τῷ ἐφιλίῳ αὐτῷ ἀντάλλαξαι, τὸ δὴ σὺν τῷ Πάπα Ἰωάννῃ Θεσσαλονίκης [?] ποπεμπείας τὸ ἀρχὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας αὐτοῦ ἀγαγωνιστὴν μόνον παρ᾽ ἡμῶν τῆς πίστεως σύμβολον [illegible, ~6 letters] ἀποφαίνεσθαι[?]. Τὸ δ᾽ ἐκ αὐτῆς τῆς ἀξιώσεως ἐπιβάλλειν ἐδόκει βάδιον εἰς πίστιν ἠγέραψαν. Ἐπειδὴ μηδὲ ἀδιαμαχήτος τοῖς λόγοις ἐν τῇ πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐξελίξει [?] ἐτὸ Σωσάφω ἀμείωσις [?] κινηθῆς· ἀλλ᾽ ἐπίκρυψις τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας ὡς ἀμῶς [?], καθ᾽ ὃ ἐν τῇ πάσης τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἀπὸ φθορᾶς τῷ Φωτίῳ ἀναμβόλλα [?]. Τὸν γὰρ ὀξὺ ἀπάντων λόγον ὑφεσσμένον Φωτίῳ, ἐφ᾽ οἷς τὲ ὑλῷ Πάπα Νικολάου μὴ ἀφεσιμένου αὐτὸν πᾶς ἢ Ῥωμαϊκῷ Ἐκκλησίας ἀφεὶς
units.tr: When the bishop Photius says these things, our side strive with reason, as if to exchange enmity for friendship: that with Pope John of Thessalonica ... the beginning of their church ... was the only champion, on our side, of the Creed of faith ... to declare. What seemed to follow from this very claim was easy to bring into the faith. Since the discussion was not stirred up without dispute in their own explanation of the Sosaphus ... but rather a concealment of the truth, in whatever way, from which, in the whole of the Roman Church, a corruption was thrown back upon Photius. For the sharp word of all was brought down upon Photius, on which account the Roman Church, in the person of Pope Nicholas, not having remitted it, ... everyone ... the Roman Church released. [Τὸν γὰρ ὀξὺ ἀπάντων λόγον ὑφεσσμένον Φωτίῳ, ἐφ᾽ οἷς τὲ ὑλῷ Πάπα Νικολάου μὴ ἀφεσιμένου αὐτὸν πᾶς ἢ Ῥωμαϊκῷ Ἐκκλησίας ἀφεὶς] [illegible in the original]

units.la: ᾧεἰς τὸ Θεὸν ἐξυβρίζας, καὶ ἀσεβῶς, καὶ ἀσεβῶς [?] ... ὠφελείας [?] τὸ ἢ Πάπα Ἰωάννῃ τῷ εἰς τὸν Πατριαρχικὸν θρόνον ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... σύμβολον, καὶ γνώμῃ, καὶ γλώσσῃ, καὶ χρῆσιν ἱερᾶς τῆς πίστεως ... [?] ... καὶ ὀμολογίαν, ... ὅπερ οὐδὲ ... ἐπίσκεψις μοι τὸ λόγο ... [?] ... ἀναγινωσκόμενον ... καὶ ὁμολογευκόν.
units.tr: ... insulting God, and impiously, and impiously ... of the benefit ... to Pope John for the Patriarchal throne ... [illegible, about twelve letters] ... the Creed, both in mind and in tongue, and the use of the holy faith ... and confession, ... which not even ... examination for me ... the word ... being read ... and confessing. [ᾧεἰς τὸ Θεὸν ἐξυβρίζας, καὶ ἀσεβῶς, καὶ ἀσεβῶς [?] ... ὠφελείας [?] τὸ ἢ Πάπα Ἰωάννῃ τῷ εἰς τὸν Πατριαρχικὸν θρόνον ... [illegible] ... σύμβολον, καὶ γνώμῃ, καὶ γλώσσῃ, καὶ χρῆσιν ἱερᾶς τῆς πίστεως ... [?] ... καὶ ὀμολογίαν, ... ὅπερ οὐδὲ ... ἐπίσκεψις μοι τὸ λόγο ... [?] ... ἀναγινωσκόμενον ... καὶ ὁμολογευκόν.]

units.la: Hæc cum inueniant Photium scribentem illi, cum quibus nobis ferino est, opinantur inimicitias cum pace commutasse, quod Papæ Ioannis piĳ locum tenentes absque additione, quod apud nos legitur, Symbolum subscripserint, & obsignauerint. Hoc verò nemo ex ijs, qui ad bene coniectandum idonei sunt, facile sibi credendum proponeret, cum nec dogmatica vlla oratio in ea Synodo, quæ pro pace sancienda coacta fuerat, repetiatur edita. Sed vera causa illud erat occultatio, propter quam cum vniuersa Romana Ecclesia fimultates, ac inimicitia Photio exorta fuerant. Cum enim vereretur, ne omnium reprehensionem incurreret, quod cum Papa eum Nicolaus non admitteret, Romanam Ecclesiam vniuersam in numen[?] iniuriam, impiam, & legum maxime praeuaricatricem nuncuparet; & cum Papa Ioannes in thronum Patriarchalem restitutioni illius assensum praebuisset, eandem sanctam, & pietatis magistram praedicaret, pro pace cum Ioanne inita, quasi apologiam contexens, per suos Locumtenentes Ioannem accepisse Symbolum, & mente, & lingua, & sacris illustrissimorum, & admirandorum hominum manibus subscripsisse, obsignasseque: Hoc autem ita ipsi persecere, veluti qui ante Papam Ioannem Romanam sedem ornarunt, hoc sanctum Symbolum, & pietate plenum profitebantur, & qui post eum ad haec usque tempora successere, & mente amplectuntur, & lingua praedicant. Et dictum meum demonstrabit Evangeliorum nulla facta immutatio, & omnia Patrum scripta, quae Spiritum tradunt, ex Patre procedere absque additione vlla ea apud illos & legi, & approbari. Quod si additio tempore Photij facta est in Symbolo, eam nusquam reprobatam fuisse probauimus alibi. Et post Photium inter Graecos, & Latinos vnio subsecuta per tot annos manifesto indicat, sententiam Latinorum, si facta non est approbatam fuisse; si additio facta est, etiam additionem veram, & rationabilem comprobatam suisse ad tempora usque Sergij Patriarchæ.
units.tr: When they find Photius writing to those with whom we are at odds, they think that enmity has been exchanged for peace, because the vicars of Pope John subscribed and sealed the Creed without the addition that is read among us. But no one among those fit to judge rightly would easily suppose this, since no doctrinal discourse is recorded as having been delivered in that Synod, which was convened to secure peace. The true cause was concealment, on account of which the whole Roman Church and the enmity and hostility arose against Photius. For since he feared that he would incur the blame of all, because Pope Nicholas did not admit him, he called the whole Roman Church an impious, injurious church, and a great breaker of laws; and when Pope John had given his assent to Photius's restoration to the patriarchal throne, he proclaimed the same church holy and the teacher of piety. In making peace with John, he wove an apology as it were: that through his vicars John had received the Creed, and with mind and tongue, and by the hands of most illustrious and admirable men, had subscribed and sealed it. They themselves professed this holy and pious Creed just as those who adorned the Roman see before Pope John, and as those who succeeded him down to the present time both embrace it in mind and proclaim it with tongue. And my statement will show that no change was made in the Gospels, and that all the writings of the Fathers which teach that the Spirit proceeds from the Father were read and approved by them without any addition. But if the addition was made in the Creed at the time of Photius, we have shown elsewhere that it was never rejected. And the union that followed between the Greeks and the Latins after Photius, lasting for so many years, clearly indicates that the opinion of the Latins was approved, if it was not made; if the addition was made, the true and reasonable addition was also approved up to the times of the Patriarch Sergius.

units.la: Dicunt, hanc nullo modo a Photianis confictam, sed re ipsa, & Oecumenicam cum omnibus suis partibus fuisse, cum in ea præsentes adfuerint Photius Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, Legati Pontificij Paulus, Eugenius, & Petrus, Locumtenentes reliquorum trium Patriarcharum, & Metropolitanorum, & Episcoporum, & aliorum non contemnendus numerus, & Imperator ipse Basilius cum filijs, eique assentientes subscripserint, nihilque in ea desideretur, quod Oecumenicam Synodum præfiniat.
units.tr: They say that this Synod was in no way fabricated by the Photians, but was in fact and in every part ecumenical, since present in it were Photius, Patriarch of Constantinople, the papal legates Paulus, Eugenius and Petrus, the vicars of the other three patriarchs, a not inconsiderable number of metropolitans and bishops and others, and the Emperor Basil himself with his sons; and that they, along with those assenting to him, subscribed, and that nothing is lacking in it which would prevent it being an ecumenical synod.

units.la: Hoc vero postremum probandum est, quod nunquam planum fiet. In ea Pontificij Legati seducti mandata sibi a Pontifice data violant, quibus violatis ( sic præmonet Pontifex ) reliqua pro infectis habeantur. Patriarcharum aliorum Oratores minis, atque pollicitationibus sevocati votis Photij, atque Imperatoris cedunt: alij Metropolitæ, & Episcopi partim sunt mancipia Photij, partim palpatores pessimi, partim excommunicationibus ob sacros Canones læsos irre-titi titi, ideoque a sententia ferenda in Synodo excluduntur. Imperator artibus Santabareni infatuatus, atque animo obcæcatus a iure dicendo repellitur: Photius ipse actor, ipse plurium scelerum reus, ipse iudex depositus, excommunicatus, exauctoratus, secularis, & apostata denunciatus. Et similis sceleratorum colluuies Synodus vocabitur, & inter Oecumenicas collocabitur?
units.tr: But this last point must be proved, and it will never be made plain. In that Synod the papal legates, led astray, violated the mandates given them by the Pontiff, and once these were violated (so the Pontiff warns) the rest are to be regarded as invalid. The envoys of the other patriarchs, called away by threats and promises, yielded to the wishes of Photius and the Emperor; the other metropolitans and bishops were partly the slaves of Photius, partly most wicked flatterers, partly entangled in excommunications for violating the sacred canons, and therefore excluded from pronouncing sentence in the Synod. The Emperor, befooled by the arts of Santabarenus and blinded in mind, was barred from giving judgment; Photius himself, the accuser, himself guilty of many crimes, himself deposed as judge, excommunicated, stripped of office, and declared a layman and apostate. And shall a filthy heap of criminals like this be called a Synod, and be placed among the ecumenical councils?

units.la: Examinemus singula. Mandatum Legatis a Ioanne Papa commissum, non aliud fuit, quam Photij reconciliatio in Ecclesia, & restitutio in thronum, si factis indoluerit, & pœnitentiam egerit. Prostat Commonitorium Legatis Paulo, & Eugenio datum, ex quo liquido apparet, ipsos Legatos Constantinopolim missos fuisse tantummodo pro Photij restitutione; Ioannes Epistola 203. ad Paulum, & Eugenium. Quatenus ea, quæ pro pace, & unitate Ecclesiæ Dei agenda sunt secundum Apostolicos nostræ auctoritatis apices, & secundum Commonitorii nostri tenorem capitulatim descriptum sagaci valde intuitu simul agatis, & ita definiatis. Et Epistola 250. quæ videtur missa Photio; Nam & ea, quæ pro causa tuæ restitutionis Synodali decreto Constantinopoli misericorditer acta sunt, recipimus: & si fortasse nostri Legati in eadem Synodo contra Apostolicam præceptionem egerunt nos nec recipimus, nec iudicamus alicuius esse firmitatis. Et Epistola 501. ad Augustos eadem verbo tenus exprimit. Ergo Commonitorium illud Legatis traditum nihil aliud continebat quam quod Ioannes Pontifex ante coactam Synodum, & postmodum toties repetit, restitutionem nempe Photij, quam misericorditer etiam peragendam mandat, non Photij nempe merito atque virtute, sed miseratione Pontificis. Et modum quoque praescribit Epistola ad Basilium, Constantinum, & Alexandrum, quamuis ea partim inuerterit, partim suppresserit Photius; Nunc itaque alijs Patriarchis Alexandrino videlicet, Antiocheno, & Hierosolymitano, atque omnibus Archiepiscopis, Metropolitis, Episcopis, & Sacerdotibus, cunctoque Clero Constantinopolitana sedis, qui de ordinatione B. Methodij, & Ignatij reuerendissimorum Patriarcharum existunt, vna voluntate pariterque voto consentientibus eiusdem Photium satisfaciendo, misericordiam, coram Synodo secundum consuetudinem postulantem in vera dilectione fratrem, & in Pontificali officio comministrum, atque coram Synodo misericordiam quaerendo in pastorali magisterio confacerdotem pro Ecclesia Dei pace, & utilitate amodo Christo faucnte [?], recipimus, & habemus. Ipsiq; etiam Photio indicauit Epistola 201. Et cum non sit reprehensibilis erga correctum quantacunque miseratio, si satisfaciens coram Synodo misericordiam secundum consuetudinem postulaueris, ac si euidenti correctione veteris, & peritiae non obliuiscens, nullius damna moliaris, quin potius auxilia eorum, qui tibi non velle consentire dicuntur, studiose dissolueris, eosque suis Ecclesijs, & honoribus restitueris: & si omnes vno voto, vno consensu, & vna concordia in tua restitutione convenerint, veniam pro pace sancta Constantinopolitana Ecclesia tibi concedimus, communionem quoque, & gradum coram Synodo misericordiam quaerendo nihilominus reddimus, & vt sancta Constantinopolitana Ecclesia praesse debeas, consentimus. Et cum tentata, & facta a Photio in ea Synodo vidisset non esse ad mentem Pontificis Ioannis, Marinus Episcopus, illius in sede successor, quae Photiani Synodice definierant dissoluens, annullansque per triginta dies in carceribus detinetur, sic referente Stephano Papa litteris ad Basilium Imperatorem. Et hoc antequam de factis Constantinopoli certior fuisset factus Ioannes; cum vero postmodum illi & astus Photij, & impudentia, & Praesulum inconsideratissima temeritas innotuissent, sententiam, quam misericorditer tulerat in Photium, revocauit, & Acta Concilij rescidit, & novo decreto Photium excommunicatum exauctorauit, & Legatos Romam reuersos in ambone anathemate damnatos deposuit. Et Acta Synodi rescidisse, irritaque declarasse tanquam quae contra Apostolicam præceptionem acta fuissent, testatur Formosus Papa Epistola ad Stylianum; Hanc sententiam promulgauit Papa Hadrianus, & Archidiaconus eius Ioannes, qui illi successor fuit, atque alta voce coram ipso ita proclamauit; In Photio completum videmus, Domine sanctissime, & Oecumenice Papa illud Psalmi; Dixit peccator ut delinquat in semetipso, non est timor Dei ante oculos eius. Posuit in Coelum os suum, & graueolens eius guttur aperuit Photius aduersus clauigerum Apostolicæ sedis. Accendatur itaque ut ignis zelus tuus, & accingere ut vir supra femur tuum, & contumeliam Apostolicæ sedis ut iustus iudex vindica, & falce sententiæ tuæ abscinde memoriam eius; & illos, qui eum sequuntur, vel tuentur, anathematis vinculis constringe, & nisi propria voce vel scriptione ipsum damnauerint, ut neque laicali communione recipiantur. Qui hæc dixit Ioannes, Hadriano in sede successit, & anathemate Photium damnauit, quando ille seduxit Eugenium, & eius socios, qui pro rebus Bulgariæ venerant. Cum enim accepisset Evangelium, & ambonem conscendisset omnibus audientibus ita dixit: Quicunque non habet damnatum Photium diuina sententia, sicut ipsum reliquit Nicolaus, & Hadrianus sanctissimi Papa praedecessores mei, sit anathema. Confirmatque haec Ioannes Nonus Epistola ad Stylianum verbis supra adductis.
units.tr: Let us examine each point in turn. The mandate that John the Pope gave to the legates was nothing other than the reconciliation of Photius in the Church and his restoration to the throne, if he grieved over his deeds and did penance. The Commonitorium given to the legates Paul and Eugenius survives, and from it it is clear that the legates were sent to Constantinople only for the restoration of Photius. John's Epistle 203 to Paul and Eugenius says: "Inasmuch as you are to consider with great care those matters which must be done for the peace and unity of God's Church, according to the Apostolic letters of our authority and the tenor of our Commonitorium set out point by point, and so to settle them." Epistle 250, which seems to have been sent to Photius, says: "For we accept those things which have been done mercifully at Constantinople by synodal decree for your restoration; and if perhaps our legates have acted in that Synod against the Apostolic precept, we neither accept those acts nor judge them to have any force." Epistle 501 to the Augusti expresses the same in words. Therefore that Commonitorium handed to the legates contained nothing other than what John the Pontiff repeatedly stated, both before the Synod was convened and afterwards: the restoration of Photius, which he also orders to be carried out "mercifully", not by Photius's merit and virtue but by the pity of the Pontiff.
