The Epistle to Basil, Constantine and Alexander also prescribes the manner, although Photius partly altered and partly suppressed it: "Now therefore, to the other Patriarchs, namely the Alexandrian, Antiochene and Jerusalemite, and to all archbishops, metropolitans, bishops, priests and the whole clergy of the see of Constantinople, who are concerned with the ordination of the blessed Methodius and Ignatius, the most reverend Patriarchs: with one will and one vote consenting, we receive and hold the said Photius, who asks mercy before the Synod according to custom, as a brother in true love and a fellow minister in the pontifical office, and as a fellow priest in the pastoral teaching, seeking mercy before the Synod, for the peace and benefit of God's Church, with Christ helping from now on." John indicated the same to Photius himself in Epistle 201: "Since mercy toward one who has been corrected is in no way blameworthy, if you ask for mercy before the Synod according to custom, and if, not forgetting the evident correction of the old offences and of your skill, you devise harm to no one but rather diligently release the aid of those who are said not to wish to agree with you, and restore them to their churches and honours; and if all agree in one vote, one consent and one harmony to your restoration, we grant pardon for the sake of the holy Church of Constantinople, we also restore communion and rank to you as you ask mercy before the Synod, and we consent that you should preside over the holy Church of Constantinople." When Marinus, bishop and successor of John in the see, saw that what Photius had attempted and done in that Synod was not according to the mind of Pope John, he dissolved and annulled what the Photian synod had defined, and was kept in prison for thirty days, as Pope Stephen reports in his letter to the Emperor Basil. This happened before John had been informed of the events at Constantinople. But when afterwards both the guile and impudence of Photius and the most inconsiderate rashness of the prelates became known to him, he revoked the sentence he had mercifully pronounced against Photius, rescinded the Acts of the Council, excommunicated Photius by a new decree, and deposed the legates, who had returned to Rome, having condemned them with anathema in the ambo. That he rescinded the Acts of the Synod and declared them void, as having been done against the Apostolic precept, Pope Formosus testifies in his letter to Stylianus. Pope Hadrian promulgated this sentence, and his archdeacon John, who succeeded him, proclaimed it aloud before him in these words: "In Photius, most holy Lord and Oecumenical Pope, we see fulfilled that psalm: 'The sinner has said that he may sin against himself; there is no fear of God before his eyes.' Photius has set his mouth against heaven and opened his foul throat against the keeper of the keys of the Apostolic see. Let your zeal therefore be kindled like fire, gird yourself like a man upon your thigh, avenge as a just judge the insult to the Apostolic see, and with the sickle of your sentence cut off his memory; and bind with the chains of anathema those who follow or defend him, and unless they condemn him by their own voice or writing, let them not be received even into lay communion." This John, who spoke these words, succeeded Hadrian and condemned Photius with anathema, when Photius had seduced Eugenius and his companions, who had come on the affairs of Bulgaria. For when he had received the Gospel and mounted the ambo, he said to all who heard: "Whoever does not hold Photius condemned by divine sentence, as my most holy predecessors Nicholas and Hadrian left him, let him be anathema." John IX confirms this in his letter to Stylianus, in the words quoted above.

units.la: Hinc palam arguitur, alia Legatis suis praecepisse Ioannem, & in Commonitorio digessisse, alia a Photio, & Legatis, eaque longissime diuersa peracta; & Commonitorium suetis Photio corruptelis, vti & Epistolas ipsius Ioannis, & antea Nicolai depravatum fuisse, idque vt melius agnoscatur Commonitorium ipsum, vti lectum est in Synodo, apponamus. Act. 3. Πέτρῳ ὁ Θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος, καὶ Καρδινάλις, εἶπε. Τὸ Διαγνωστικὸν Ἀποπληξίας λόγιον, τὸ φάσκον, ὅτι ἐγὼ τὴν δόξαν μὲν οὐ ζητῶ. ἔστιν ὁ ζητῶν, καὶ κεῖνον. ἀλλὰ τὰ μὲν ὡς πρότων ὁ καιρὸς ἐδοκίμασεν. ἃ δοκεῖ δὲ τῇ ἁγίᾳ ταύτῃ, καὶ εἰρηνικωτάτῃ Συνόδῳ, ἀναγνωσθῆναι τὸ ὑπὸ ἡμῶν Κομμονιτώριον, ὅπερ ἐντάλμα, ὥσπερ τῷ ἀμωτάτῳ οἰκουμενικῷ Πάπα Ἰωάννῃ, ἐν ᾧ καὶ πάντες οἱ καθ' ἡμᾶς Ἀρχιερεῖς, καὶ Ἐπίσκοποι ὑπέσφαλλαν. Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος εἶπεν. Ἀναγνωσθήτω. καὶ δὴ ἀνάγνωσις Πέτρῳ ὁ Θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος, καὶ Καρδινάλις Λέοντος Περιταταθαρίου, καὶ ἑρμηνεύς αἰτῶ. Κομμονιτώριον τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς Παύλῳ, καὶ Εὐλφίῳ τῆς Ἐπισκόπου, ὡς αὐτοὺς ἡ Πέτρῳ Πρεσβυτέρῳ, καὶ Καρδιναλι ἡμῖν τῆς ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλ[?] λ[?] ἀπεσταλμένοις[?]· α'. Μετὰ τὰς τῷ Θεῷ βοηθείας, ἐπὶ πρεσβευόντων τῶν ἀγίων Ἀποστόλων. ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει εἰσερχομένων ὑμῖν, ὅπως προσεύξῃ ὁ Βασιλεύς, ἐκεῖσε μεταπέμπηται, καὶ ἀφεὶ τῇ τὸν Βασιλέα Θεσσαλίας, ἄλλῳ τινὶ τὰς Ἀποστολικὰς ἐπιστολὰς μὴ ἀποδοῦναι [?] δοῦναι[?]. Ὡσπερ ὑμῖν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Βασιλέως, τὰς ἐπιστολὰς ἀποδώσειν, τοιούτοις ῥήμασιν αὐτῷ προσφθέγξομαι. Περσκυνῶ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἐκ Θεοῦ βασιλείαν ὁ πνευματικὸς ἡμῶν πατὴρ ὁ κύριος Γωαίνης ὁ Ἀποστολικὸς Πάπας. Τὸ ὑμέτερον ἐκ Θεοῦ κράτος τῆς αὐτῆς καθ' ἑκάστην ἱκεσίας [?] ἀποχαρίζομαι τῷ ἁγίῳ Θεῷ, ἵνα ὁ τοιαύτην ὑμῖν ἐπιθυμίαν δῷς, ἐξ ἃ τὸ προσῆμα τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς εἰρήνης αὐτὸ καταζαπέμψῃ ὑμῖν τὴν χάριν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀφωμοιωθήσεται ὑμᾶς τῇ αὐτῇ καταδοσῇ, καὶ τῆ ἀγάπῃ ἐν ἀγαθοῖς τὸ ἔλεος ὑμῶν.
units.tr: Hence it is plainly shown that John ordered one thing to his legates and set it down in the Commonitorium, while Photius and the legates carried out something else, and something far different. It is also shown that the Commonitorium, like John's own Epistles and earlier those of Nicholas, was corrupted by Photius's usual tricks. So that the Commonitorium itself may be better recognised, we set it out as it was read in the Synod. Act. 3. Peter, the most devout presbyter and cardinal, said: "The saying of the Apostle, 'I do not seek my own glory', is indeed a word that someone seeks it; but times have tested these things as they were. Since it seems good to this holy and most peaceful Synod, let the Commonitorium which we were commanded by the most holy Oecumenical Pope John be read, in which all our archbishops and bishops also fell." The holy Synod said: "Let it be read." And so it was read by Peter, the most devout presbyter and cardinal and legate of Leo of Perithatharium, as follows: "Commonitorium to the brothers Paul and Eugenius, bishops, sent by us to Constantinople with Peter the presbyter and cardinal. 1. After God's help, while the holy Apostles intercede, when you arrive at Constantinople, the Emperor is to be summoned that he may pray; and the Emperor of Thessaly, who is to give the Apostolic letters to no other person, shall be let go. As you are to give the letters to the Emperor in person, I shall address him in such words: 'The spiritual father of us all, our Lord John, the Apostolic Pope, worships your reign from God.' May your power from God be given to the holy God in every such supplication, so that he may grant you such desire, from which the bond of ecclesiastical peace may send down grace to you, and may make you like the same, and in love grant your mercy among good things." (The Greek here is too corrupt to render with certainty.)

units.la: β'. Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ Βασιλεὺς, ἀφὶ τὰ τὰς ὀλισθηλὰς ἀναλύονται τὰ τῆς ἀποκειμένως ἡμῶν αἱ αἱματωθεῖσαι κεφάλαια, τοιούτοις ῥήμασιν αὐτῷ προσείπατε. εἰ κελεύει ἡ βασιλεία ὑμῖν, ἰδίως τὰς ὀλισθηλάς. Ἐὰν ἔπη, τί ἐξιλεύουσιν αἱ ὀλισθηλαί, ἀποκειῖνται αὐτῷ, προσζωνύοντες πρὸς τὴν ὑμετέραν [?] ἀθῶσιν, καὶ λόγους τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς εἰρήνης συνκεφαλιῶντας τὸν συμβουλισμὸν, καὶ πάντα ζῶπῳ καλῶς ἀποπληρωῦντας.
units.tr: 2. If the Emperor is willing, after the slips of those who are released from the things taken from us, the chapters that have been cut off shall be declared to him in such words: "If your kingdom commands, let the slips be [dealt with] specially. If the slips ask what the penalties are, let them be told to him, adding to your acquittal, and words of ecclesiastical peace uniting the counsel, and fulfilling all things well in the Lord."

units.la: γ'. Τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ ἡμέρᾳ φωσαγορεύοντες Φωτὶ πρὸ ἀνωτάτω δικάζοντε τὴν ὀλισθηλὴν, ἀπαγγέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀφεντὸς τοιούτοις ῥήμασιν, Προσκυνῶ σε ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Γωαίνης ὁ Ἀποστολικὸς Πάπας, ἡ θλιβεῖσα ἐξ ἀδελφῶν, καὶ συλλεπτεύσας.
units.tr: 3. On the next day, going to Photius, who was judged in the highest manner, announcing him as released with such words: "I worship you, our Lord John, the Apostolic Pope, who has been afflicted by brothers and has suffered with you."

units.la: δ'. Καθὼς ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Βασιλεὺς, ἵνα δέξωμαι τὴν εἰρήνην τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἀποδεξάμεθα τ̔ ἀγιώτατον Πατριάρχην Φώτιον ἀδελφόν, καὶ συλλειτουργὸν ἡμῖν, εἰσηκούσαμεν τῆς στήσεως ὑμῶν, καὶ ἡδέωμεν, ἵνα ἐκ̔πον ὑμῖν ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν Σύνοδον [?], ἡ ἀποδέξηται αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἐκκλησία καὶ τὴν διάταξιν τῆς Γραμμάτων ἡμῶν, ἀποδέξηται αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμεῖς συνοικοινωνὸν καὶ συλλειτουργὸν, καὶ ἵνα ἀσφαλείας, καὶ ἐλέ[?]τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν Ῥωμαίων προσφέρειν.
units.tr: 4. As the Emperor has sent, that I may receive the peace of the Church, we receive the most holy Patriarch Photius, brother and fellow minister with us; we have heard of your standing, and we are glad that he should come to you to the Synod, so that the whole Church and the arrangement of our letters may receive him, and you too may receive him as fellow communicant and fellow minister, and that the Roman Church may offer security and mercy.

units.la: ε'. Ἀναστάντες ἅπαντ̔ αὐτῷ. Κ[?] ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ὁ ἀγιώτατος Πάπας, ἵνα παίτης οἱ ἐν διαφόρους ὄντες Τόπους [?] Ἐπίσκοποι, ἢ Πρεσβύτεροι, ἢ ἄλλοι τινὲς, καὶ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν τῶ παρόντων κοινωνῆσαι μετ᾽ ὑμῶν, δέξ τὰ μυθῆ ὑμῶν ἐνωθῶσι τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ τὸ Χεῖρε, καὶ ἡγώντας ἐν μετ᾽ ὑμῶν. Ἐρχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν, ἀποδέξεται αὐτὸν ὡς πατὴρ πίνα, καὶ νουθετίσει αὐτὸν πολλάκις, ἵνα δέξ τὴν εἰρήνην τῆς τῇ Θεῷ Ἐκκλησίας ὁμονοήσωσι μετὰ τῆς Ἀποστολικῆς, καὶ κεφαλῆσωσι μὴ αὐτὸ ἐν Σῆλημα ἀποδεχόμενοι Φώτιον τὸν ἀγιώτατον Πατριάρχην, καὶ γνώμενοι αὐτῷ συνοικονωσί. οἱ δὲ ἐρχόμενοι ὅσοι μὲν φερεχθεῖσ[?]τη[?], ἵνα ἀπὸ λάβωσι ζῶν ἀφ᾽ ὑμῶν [?]. οἱ δὲ ἐχάπως ἀρεσκόντες ἄλλοι ἐκ τ̔ αὐτῶν Ἐπισκόπων διαφορὰς ἢ σπερμάσματα ἀρκεῦ-α.
units.tr: 5. Standing up, all of them together, our most holy lord the Pope [asks] that those bishops, presbyters, or others who are in various places and did not wish to share in the present proceedings with you, should, upon receiving our letters, be reunited with the Church and join with us. When they come, he will receive them as a father would, and will often admonish them, so that they may agree with the Church of God and the Apostolic See, and not hold to the schismatic [council] receiving Photius the most holy patriarch, but rather communicate with him as fellow-members. Those who come, however, [are to receive whatever is due to them] from you. Other bishops of their party who have differences or seeds of dissension [are to be dealt with].

units.la: ς'. Καθὼ[?]ἐ[?]ἀπὸ[?]τῆς Σινόδου μὴ τὸ φεγόμενον ἀγιωτάτη Πατριάρχου, καὶ τὴν ἡμῶν τῆς ἀπατηλῆς [?] ζῶ μὴ, ἅμα τοῖς λοιποῖς Ἀρχιεπισκόποις, ἢ Μητροπολίτας, καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς Ἱερεῦσι τῆς Κωνσταντινουπόλεως Ἐκκλησίας, προσέζον αἰαΓναθήτως αἱ ἐπισολαὶ αἱ πρὸς τὴν βασιλείαν ὑποσα-λεῖαν, καὶ ἐφθασμηθήτω ἡ Σωσθόσ, εἰ ἀποδέχεται αὐτὰς, καὶ ἐαν φυλάττωσι τὰ μαρτυρίας, ὡς ὀφείλει ἡ ὑπισολὴ, ἐπεκείνα μαρτυρῶν αὐτῆ, ἐπαρτε. Ὁ κυρίος ἡμῶν ὁ ἀξιώτατος Πάπας, πασῶν τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν φροντίδα ποιεῖσθε, καὶ τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας, καὶ ἐνώσεως, καὶ εἰρήνης πειρμηθῆμεν, ἀπέσλεν ἡμᾶς ζῶν ὁμῶν [?] ἢ ... ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὅπως ὁ κυρίος ἐκαλέσατο, ἐκ τῆς ἐλαίας τῆς Ἐκκλησίας χύεσα ὁρέξωμεν, ὅπως καταβραγμένως ἀνοξθώσωμεν, ἵνα πάντες ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι δοξάζωμεν τὸν Πατέρα σὺν υἱῷ, καὶ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι. ἵστε τὸ καλὸν, ἡ ὑμῆ; Ἡ ἁγία Σωσθόσ εἶπεν, Ὅσα ἀφεῖς εἰρήνην, καὶ ὁμόνοιαν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας οἴσι, καὶ καλά, καὶ ἀποδεκτὰ ἡγούμεθα.
units.tr: 6. Since the most holy patriarch Photius was condemned by the synod, and our letter was [read] against the deceptive ... together with the other archbishops, metropolitans, and all the priests of the Church of Constantinople, let the letters sent to the emperor be read aloud and let the [present] synod be asked whether it accepts them, and whether they keep the testimonies as the letter requires; let it bear witness to them accordingly. Our most worthy lord the Pope, who takes care of all the churches and desires your salvation, unity, and peace, has sent us to you ... so that, being gathered from the sheep of the Church, we may draw near and be restored, so that all in one body may glorify the Father with the Son and the Holy Spirit. Do you know this is good? The holy synod said: We regard as good and acceptable whatever brings peace and concord to the Church.

units.la: ζ'. Τὰς δὲ διαλυόντας ἐν τῇ αὐτῶν ἀυθαδίᾳ, ἡ ἐσχυχῆ, καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐνώσιν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ τ᾽ ἀδήφων μὴ θέλοντας συνελθεῖν, μὴ δὲ ἡ σωσθεσμον τὴν ἀγάπης διαφυλάξαι, μὴ ἀδυτίσκειν, καὶ ξεῖτην νυσῶσιν ὑμῖν π, καὶ τὴν ἀγίας Σωσθόσθ ποιήσαται αὐτὰς ἀκοινωνήτως, καὶ παντὸς τάγματος Ἐκκλησιαστικοῦ ἀφορίζεται, ἕως ἂν ἐνωθῶσι τῇ οἰκείῳ Πατρίαρχῇ, καὶ τῇ καταυτῶν Ἐκκλησίᾳ.
units.tr: 7. As for those who persist in their own obstinacy and who, when called to the unity of the Church, refuse to come together, and do not keep the bond of love, let them not be [spared]; if they persist in this, the holy synod shall exclude them from communion and separate them from every ecclesiastical order until they are reunited with their own patriarch and their own Church.

units.la: ι'. Ἐξακολουθοῦντες τοῖς κανόσι τῶν ἁγίων Πατέρων, λέγομεν ἵνα μὴ τὴν ἀποβίωσιν Φωτὸς τῆς ἀξιωτάτης Πατρίαρχου, μηδὲις ἀπὸ κοσμικοῦ ἀξιώματος εἰς τὸν Θεῖον Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἀπελθῇ, καθὼς, καὶ αἱ ἐπισολαὶ ἡμῶν μαρτυροῦσι.
units.tr: 10. Following the canons of the holy Fathers, we declare that no one shall pass from secular office to the see of Constantinople in place of the deposed Photius, the most worthy patriarch, as our letters also testify.

units.la: ιά'. Θέλομεν ἐνώπιον τῆς Σωσθόσ, ἵνα τὸν θεοφιλῆ Φώτιον τὸν ἀξιώτατον Πατρίαρχην ἀποκαλέσητε, σπῆ, μήτε ὠμόφωρον εἰς Βυλγαρείαν ἀποστέλλαι, μήτε χειροτονῆσαι ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπαρχίᾳ, ἐὰν γὰρ τοῦτο ποιήσῃ, ἐλέγξαι αὐτὸν ἐκ τρόμου κανονικῶς. ι'. Θέλομεν ἐωσὰν τῆς ἀνδημιώσεως Συνόδου ἀνακηρυχθῆναι, ἵνα ἡ Συνόδος ἡ γεγονυῖα ἐπὶ τοῦ προειρημένου Πατριάρχου Φωτίου ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς Ἀδριανοῦ τοῦ ἁγιωτάτου Πάπα ἐν τῇ Ῥώμῃ, καὶ ἐν Κωνσταντινουπόλει ἀπὸ τῶν παρόντων ἢ ἐξωσρακισμένων, καὶ ἀνυεγῶ, καὶ ἀβέβαιον, ἢ μὴ σωαριθμῆταί αὐτῇ μετὰ ἑτέρας ἁγίας Συνόδου. Ἡ ἁγία Συνόδος ἀπεκρίθη. Ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐρῶν ἀπεκηρύξαμεν, καὶ ἀπεβαλόμεθα, καὶ ἀνεθεματίζομεν τὴν παρ᾽ ὑμῶν λεγομένην Σύνοδον, ἐνωθέντες Φωτίῳ τῷ ἁγιωτάτῳ ἡμῶν Πατριάρχῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀποβαλλομένης τὰ κατ᾽ αὐτὴν ἐαφέντες, ἡ λαληθέντα ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ῥηθείσῃ παρ᾽ ὑμῶν Συνόδῳ, τῶν ἀναθεμάτων [illegible, ~6 letters]. Ἡλίας Μητροπολίτης Μαρτυρυπόλεως, καὶ Ἡλίας Ἱεροσολύμων τοποτηρητὴς εἶπον. Καὶ πῶς ἂν Σινόδος ῥηθείη, ἡ μυρίων χισμάτων τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν πληρώσασα, τῆς ὀνομάσθη Σινόδου, τὴν Σαρακηνῶν ἀποκειμένας κείμενον[?], καὶ νομοθέτας καθίζασαν; ποίας Σινοδοῦς ἀριθμηθείη, ἡ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων Συνόδων ἐναντία ζωλμήσασα. ἡ οὖν αὐθέντες, καὶ χωρὶς τῆς οἰκουμένης ποτὲ ἐξεταύσεως καταδικάσασα. ἡ πάντας θεσμοὺς Ἐκκλησιαστικοὺς, καὶ πολιτικὰς συγχύσασα, καὶ καθαιρέσασα ... δὲ τῶτα δὲ οἱ τῆς αἱρετολῆς ἀγωνίσαντοι θεῖοι ἀποκηρύκτους τὰς φωνᾶξις, καὶ ἀποβλήτους ἐποίησαντο, καὶ τὰ ἀναθέματα παιστέμψαντο. ιά. Βλέπεσεν γὰρ ἐν τῇ Ἐνγαλμα
units.tr: 11. We wish, in the presence of the synod, that you shall call the God-beloved Photius, the most worthy patriarch, [a usurper?], and that he shall not be sent to Bulgaria, nor ordained in the same province; for if he does this, he shall be canonically convicted of the crime. 12. We wish that the synod which was held under the aforesaid Photius in the time of Adrian, the most holy Pope, at Rome and at Constantinople, be proclaimed null, void, and unstable by those present or absent, and not be counted among the other holy synods. The holy synod answered: We too have declared it void, rejected it, and anathematized the so-called synod of yours, in union with Photius our most holy patriarch; and it cannot be cast out, since it has set aside what was said in it... of the anathemas. Elias, metropolitan of Martyropolis, and Elias, locum tenens of Jerusalem, said: And how could that be called a synod which filled the Church with countless schisms, which set up a Saracen [?] and lawgivers, and what synod could be numbered which dared to oppose all the holy synods? It condemned without any examination, by its own authority, and overthrew all ecclesiastical and civil laws ... The divine champions of the orthodox faith declared those voices void, cast them out, and set aside its anathemas. 11. For I see in the ...

units.la: μὰ ἡμῶν ὕπας [?] εἰπατίσητε, [?] μήτε διὰ σωμα-πακθῆτε, μήτε δι᾽ κολακείαν, ἢ φόβου ἐκκλίνητε δίξιὰ, ἢ ἀρίστερὰ, ἀλλὰ βασιλικὴν ὁδὸν προδίωντε, ὡς τὸν τόπον, [?] τὴν οἰκουσίαν ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὑμῖν δι᾽ τὴν εἰρήνην τῆς Ἐκκλησίας διαλαμβάνωσιν ἔχοντες.
units.tr: Let us not be ... neither swayed by bribery nor by flattery, nor turn aside from fear to right or left, but follow the royal road, as the place of our authority requires, so that you may hold peace with the Church.

units.la: ἵνα δι᾽ τὰ ὑμέτερα νόσῃ, [?] ἀξίως ἡμῶν μόνῃ, τὴν χάριν ἡμῶν, καὶ τὰ Ἀποστολικὰ Θεσμὰ ἔχητε, [?] τῆς ἡμετέρας κοινωνίας [?] γνώσεται ἀπαλλαγόμεθα. Ἡ ἀγία Σωδος [?] ἀπεν.
units.tr: So that, for your part, you may have our grace and the apostolic ordinances, and so that we may be released from [the burden] of our communion. The holy synod said.

units.la: Ἰδοὺ ὁρῶμεν ὑμᾶς [?] πάντα τὴν Ἐντολὴν τὰ ἀμωτάτῃ Πάπα ἐξακολουθοῦντας. ἐπ᾽ ἀληθείας γὰρ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως μεγάλου [?] τοὺς [?] ἂν [?] τυπτυπεντας. Νικήτας ὁ Στοφιλίκτος Μοζοπολίτης Σμύρνης [?] ἐπιν.
units.tr: Behold, we see you all following the commands of the most holy Pope; for truly the great high priest... Nicetas, Stiphilus, metropolitan of Smyrna, said.

units.la: Ὁ Θεὸς ἔπως ἐπύποιεν ἐξεὶν ὑμᾶς τὰ ποσέσματα, ἵνα κἂν δίλη τῆς ἐξωδη τῆς ἐντολῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τὴν ὡς ἡμ. γυμάτων τὰ ἀμωτάτῃ Πάπα ἐξεπατῶζα, μὴ δείσῃ φεύφαιν. καὶ ὅτε τὰ ποσέσματα [?] αὐτὰ ἐκεῖνα [?] ἀλαμίζωσι, [?] τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ προδίωσι, [?] δὲ οἱ ἔχοντες φωλὰς γνώμας δίωσι [?] ἐωνίας [?] τῆς ποσέσματα ἐλθῶ.
units.tr: May God grant that the councils persuade you that, if you stray from God's commandment and from the most holy Pope's [authority], you need not fear to flee. And when the councils themselves wander, [let them] follow the way of God; but those who have false opinions ... of these councils may come.

units.la: πόσω οὖν μᾶλλον οἱ ἔχοντες τὴν δίξιαν ἀπὸν πάσῃ αὐτῇ καταπονσμένην, [?] δὲ δυνάμενοι ὅπως παντῶς ἐκκλίνειν δίξια, ἢ ἀρίστερὰ τὸ δήμα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὑπεντὸ ἐξαλμάπων τὰ Ἀρχιερέως τῆς Ῥώμης. Οἱ ἀγιώτατοι [?] τοπτυπεντ[?] τῆς Περσβυτέρας Ῥώμης ἔπον.
units.tr: How much more, then, should those who hold the right way, being firmly rooted in it, be able to avoid by every means turning aside right or left from the word of God, and from the commands of the Roman high priest. The most holy ... of the Presbyter of Rome said.

units.la: Ὁ Περφήτης λέγ[?] εἰς παῖδα ὅσα ἀποστέλλω ἡμᾶς ποσέδεῖτε, [?] ἐὰν ἀλλὰ ἀλλοῦ πληρῶζωι [?] μὴ τὸ θάνημα τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἡμῖν τῷ ἀμωτάτῳ Πάπα.
units.tr: The Prophet says to the servant: Wherever I send you, you shall go; if in another place ... the will of God, and the same to us and to the most holy Pope.

units.la: Ἡ ἀγία Σωζοδὸς [?] εἶπεν. Ἐναρλῶς ἐλίπομεν, ὅπ[?] τὸ θέλημα τῦ Θεῦ, ὅ τε ὑποστέλλαιτ ὑμᾶς Ἀρ-χιερέως πληρῶτε. Φῶτ[?]ῳ ὁ ἀγιώτατῳ Παξιαρ-χῇ ἅπα. Ἐὰν θέλημά ὁςι τὸ κατ᾽ ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἵνα καταλλαχῇ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον γένος τῷ Θεῷ εἰς τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ ἐκκοσμοπολιμωμένων χρόνοις πολλοῖς ἐμφανέσθαι, ὁ νῦν ἐρᾶ σωθῆναι ἡμῶν ἡ ὑμετέρα ἀγιωσύνη ὅπ κῇ τὸ θέλημα, καὶ τῷ ἐγγελῶν τῆ ἀγιωτάτῃ Πάπᾳ πάντα συνήλθον. καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα ἐδὲν ἔχει, καὶ συνεδράμε τῇ ἐκείνῳ γνώμῃ καὶ ἡ τῆς φύσεως φύσις. Οἱ ἀγιώτατοι Τοποτηρηταὶ ἄπαν. Τὸ ἱερὸν ἡμῶν τοῦτό ἐστι, ἵνα δὴ ἀξίως καὶ μέχρι ἐνώσωμεν τῇ κατ᾽ ὑμᾶς Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Δῆ τοῦτο καὶ πολλοῖς κόποις ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ὑπομένομεν· ὅμως οἱ ἄγιοι καὶ ἀνδρες ἐξ κόπου ἡρέας τῆς Χερσῷ. Φῶτι⊙ ὁ ἀγιώτατος Παξιάρχης ἔπεν. ἐστι μεταποδότης ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἀξίων μεγάλους μικρὰς, καὶ ἀκεπάτες ταμιεύομεν ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ. Πέξῳ ὁ θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος, καὶ Καρδινάλις ἔπεν. Ι᾽ δὲ ἔπιστεφαι τῆς Ἐπισκόπων, ὅπως ὠμονόας, καὶ ἀπεδέξαντο Φώτιον τὸν ἀγιώτατον Παξιάρχην σὺν πάσῃ τῇ ἁγίᾳ τῇ Ρωμαίων Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Ζαχαρίας Ἐπίσκοπος Ἐκκλησίας Ἀναγνῶν, καὶ Βιβλιοθήκης τὰ Ἀποστολικὰ Θέρμε, ἐν τούτῳ πρὸς Κομμονιτάιφ ἐαρ δὲ ἀποδοχῆς Φωτίῳ τῇ ἀγιωτάτῃ Παξιάρχῃ, ἰδιοχείρως ὑπέγραψεν. Ἡ Μαρῆνος Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Νεαπόλεως, ὁμοίως ὑπέγραψεν. Δομίνικος Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Τευθένης, ὁμοίως. Φλῶ-
units.tr: The holy synod said: We have clearly declared that it is the will of God, and that you should fulfil the commands of the high priest. To Photius the most holy patriarch, all. If it is the will of God in our Church that the human race be reconciled to God, its Father, which for many times has appeared in the world, we now ask that your holiness also agree with this will, and join all the others with the most holy Pope. And the same Spirit is in you, and the nature of the thing ran together with his judgment. The most holy locum tenens, all. This is our sacred purpose: that we may worthily unite with your Church. For this reason we endure many labours on the way; yet holy men have come with us from the land of ... Photius the most holy patriarch said: God is the one who changes great and small, and we keep watch for you in his kingdom without ceasing. Pesso, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, said: Since the bishops have agreed in harmony, let them receive Photius the most holy patriarch together with the whole holy Church of the Romans. Zacharias, bishop of the Church of Anagni, and librarian of the Apostolic See, has subscribed this in his own hand, with the agreement of Communitas to Photius the most holy patriarch. Marinus, bishop of the Church of Naples, likewise subscribed. Dominicus, bishop of the Church of Teuthenis, likewise. Flo-

units.la: ꝯ Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας Μανδυελίνου, ὁμοίως ἰδιοχειρως ὑπέγραψεν.
units.tr: ... bishop of the holy Church of Mandyelinus, likewise subscribed in his own hand.

units.la: Γαυδίεχος Ἐπίσκοπος Βελιτήρνε, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Gaudiechus, bishop of Velitrae, likewise.

units.la: Σπίφανος Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας Φερεσίνης, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Stephanus, bishop of the holy Church of Feresine, likewise.

units.la: Λέων Ἐπίσκοπος Γαβέσσης Μάσος, καὶ Ἀπόκεισαρίῳ τῷ ὑποσολικοῦ Θέσσῃ [?] ὁμοίως ὑπέγραψεν ἰδιοχείρως.
units.tr: Leo, bishop of Gabessa, Masos, and Apocisiarius of the Apostolic See, likewise subscribed in his own hand.

units.la: Πέτρος Ἐπίσκοπος Φορσοφορνένσου, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Peter, bishop of Forsoforne, likewise.

units.la: Οὐάλπερτος ἡ ἁγίας Πέξου Ἐκκλησίας, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Walpert, of the holy church of Pezo, likewise.

units.la: Συμεὼν Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας Φοωνδύ-ρων, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Symeon, bishop of the holy church of Phoondyra, likewise.

units.la: Ἰωάννης Ἐπίσκοπος ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας Σιλίνων, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: John, bishop of the holy church of Silinum, likewise.

units.la: Βενέδικτος Ἐπίσκοπος, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Benedict, bishop, likewise.

units.la: Γρηγόριος Ἐπίσκοπος τῆς ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας Σολβοκανδλά [?], ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Gregory, bishop of the holy church of Solbocandla, likewise.

units.la: Βονιφάτιος Ἐπίσκοπος ἁγίας τῆς Βλερσίων Ἐκκλησίας, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Boniface, bishop of the holy church of the Vlersii, likewise.

units.la: Στέφανος Ἐπίσκοπος ἁγίας τῆς Νεπισίνων Ἐκκλησίας, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Stephen, bishop of the holy church of the Nepisini, likewise.

units.la: Γερμανὸς Πρεσβύτερος τῷ ἁγίῳ Παύλῳ, καὶ Ἰωάννου, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Germanus, presbyter of St Paul and of John, likewise.

units.la: Πέτρος Πρεσβύτερος, τῷ ἁγίου Χρυσο-ζόνου [?], ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Peter, presbyter of St Chrysogonus, likewise.

units.la: Βενέδικτος Πρεσβύτερος τῆς ἁγίας Βαλβίνης, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Benedict, presbyter of the holy Balbina, likewise.

units.la: Ἀδριανὸς Πρεσβύτε-ρος τῷ ἁγίῳ Λαυρεντίῳ, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Adrian, presbyter of St Laurence, likewise.

units.la: Λέων Πρεσβύτερος, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Leo, presbyter, likewise.

units.la: Ἰωάννης Πρεσβύτερος τῆς ἁγίας Κικιλίας, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: John, presbyter of the holy Cecilia, likewise.

units.la: Παῦλος Διάκονος, ὁμοίως ὑπέγραψεν.
units.tr: Paul, deacon, likewise signed.

units.la: Λέων Διάκονος, ὁμοίως.
units.tr: Leo, deacon, likewise.

units.la: Μετὰ τὴν συμπλήρωσιν τῷ Κομμονιτῷ Πέτρος ὁ διοσεβίσατος Πρεσβύτερος, καὶ Καρολινάλις εἶπεν.
units.tr: After the completion of the Commonitorium, Peter, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, spoke.

units.la: Ἀρέσκει τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ἁγιωσύνῃ; καὶ ἡ ἁγία Σωσοδ ἀπηκεῖσθαι. Ἀρέσκει. καὶ μάλιστα, αἱ [illegible, ~14 letters] ὑποσεφαλίσαι τῆς κοινῆς εἰρήνης, καὶ ὁμοιοίας τῆς ἁγίας τῆ Θεοῦ Ἐκκλησίας, ἐ ἐπὶ τῆς ἀποδοχῆς Φωνῆς τῆ ἀμωμήτῳ[?], ἐ οἰκουμενικοῦ Πατριάρχου[?]. Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπόντος[?], ἐπευφήμησαν[?]. Petrus piissimus Presbyter, & Cardinalis dixit. Euangelicum comple eloquium, Ego gloriam meam non quæro: est qui quærit, & iudicat. sed ea, quæ circa hæc euenere, tempus probauit. Si autem placuerit sanctissimæ huic & perquam pacatissimæ Synodo, legatur traditum nobis Commonitorium, siue Præceptio a sanctissimo, & Oecumenico Papa Ioanne, quod omnes nostri Præsules, & Episcopi subscripsere. Sancta Synodus dixit: Legatur. Et assurgens Petrus piissimus Presbyter, & Cardinalis per Leonem Protospatharium, & interpretem legit. Commonitorium fratribus Paulo, & Eugenio Episcopis, similiter & Petro Presbytero, & Cardinali nostris Constantinopolim missis. I. Divino auxilio, & precibus sanctorum Apostolorum Constantinopolim ingressi, quocunque iusserit Imperator, vos conferte, & antequam Imperatorem inuisatis, Apostolicas literas nemini tradatis. Cum vero præsentes astiteritis Imperatori, literas consignate, his verbis Imperatorem alloquentes: Vestram ex Deo maiestatem veneratur spiritualis. vester Pater Dominus Ioannes Apostolicus Papa, vestrum ex Deo Imperium singulis diebus inter orandum sancta Deo committens, vt qui vestrum desiderium excitavit ad pacem Ecclesia conciliandam, retribuat vobis suam gratiam, & consoletur vos prosperis rerum euentibus, & vestram voluntatem in bonis perficiat. II. Si voluerit Imperator, antequam legat Epistolas, vestrae missionis capita addiscere, hisce verbis illi respondebitis; Si jubet vestra maiestas, percurrat Epistolas. Et si quaesierit, quid illae contineant, respondete; Erga vestram pietatem, reverentiam, & sermones unionis Ecclesiasticae vinculum approbantes, & modis omnibus bene perficientes.
units.tr: Does it please your holiness? And let the holy synod be dismissed. It pleases. And especially, since the common peace and the harmony of the holy Church of God are to be secured, whether by the acceptance of ... or of the oecumenical patriarch. When these things had been said, they acclaimed. Peter, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, said: "Fulfil the word of the gospel: I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks and judges" (John 8:50). But the things that have happened concerning these matters, time has proved. If it pleases this most holy and most peaceful synod, let the Commonitorium handed to us be read, or the precept of the most holy and oecumenical Pope John, which all our prelates and bishops have subscribed. The holy synod said: Let it be read. Then Peter, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, rising, read it through Leo the protospatharius and an interpreter. The Commonitorium to our brothers Paul and Eugenius, bishops, and likewise to Peter, presbyter and cardinal, sent by us to Constantinople. I. By divine help and the prayers of the holy apostles, having entered Constantinople, go wherever the emperor directs, and before you visit the emperor, do not hand the apostolic letters to anyone. When you are present before the emperor, deliver the letters, addressing him in these words: "Your spiritual father, our lord John, the apostolic Pope, venerates your majesty as given by God, and entrusts your empire, given by God, to holy prayers every day, that he who has stirred your desire to win peace for the Church may repay you with his grace, comfort you with prosperous outcomes, and bring your will to fulfilment in good things." II. If the emperor wishes, before he reads the letters, to learn the heads of your mission, you will answer him in these words: "If your majesty commands, let him run through the letters." And if he asks what they contain, answer: "We approve, with regard to your piety, reverence and words, the bond of ecclesiastical unity, and we are bringing it to completion in every way."

units.la: III. Altero die inuisentes sanctissimum Photium porrigite Epistolam, salutantes ipsum, ut addecet, in hunc modum; Veneratur te Dominus noster Joannes Apostolicus Papa, & vult te habere fratrem, & comministrum.
units.tr: III. On the next day, visiting the most holy Photius, hand him the letter, greeting him as is fitting in this manner: "Our lord John, the apostolic Pope, greets you and wishes to have you as brother and fellow minister."

units.la: IV. Modo quo misit ad nos Imperator pro reconcilianda Ecclesia pace, ut recipiamus sanctissimum Patriarcham Photium fratrem, & comministrum nostrum, supplicationem vestram exaudiuimus, & jubemus, ut coram vobis in Synodum progrediatur, & recipiat ipsum universa Ecclesia secundum ordinem nostrarum literarum: recipiatis vos quoque eum in vestra communione, & ministerio, ut Eucharistiam, & misericordiam Ecclesiae Graecorum offerat.
units.tr: IV. In the manner in which the emperor sent to us to restore peace to the Church, we have heard your request that we receive the most holy Patriarch Photius, our brother and fellow minister, and we command that he come forward before you into the synod and that the whole Church receive him according to the order of our letters. You also are to receive him into your communion and ministry, so that he may offer the Eucharist and the mercy of the Greek Church.

units.la: V. Assurgentes ipsi dicite. Mandat Dominus noster sanctissimus Papa, ut omnes, qui variis in locis extorres a solo patrio exulant, sive Epi-scoscopi, siue Sacerdotes, siue alterius ordinis, qui ad hunc diem vna cum vobis communicare noluerunt, vestro studio ac labore vniantur Christi Ecclesiae, fiantq; vnum cum vobis, quos aduenientes suscipiet vti parens natos, sepiusque ipsos commonebit, vt causa pacis Ecclesiae Dei conueniant cum Apostolico, habeantque cum eo vnam voluntatem, excipientes Photium sanctissimum Patriarcham, & communicantes cum ipso. Accedentes vero quotquot antea ordinati sunt, restituantur suis sedibus, qui deinceps habeant ex ijsdem Episcopis alimenta, & indumenta necessaria.
units.tr: V. Rising, say to them: "Our lord, the most holy Pope, commands that all who are exiled from their native soil in various places, whether bishops, priests, or of another order, who until this day have refused to communicate with you, be united by your zeal and labour to the Church of Christ and become one with you. He will receive them as a parent receives children when they come, and will often admonish them to come together with the Apostolic See for the sake of the peace of the Church of God, to have one will with him, receiving the most holy Patriarch Photius and communicating with him. Those who were previously ordained and who come forward are to be restored to their sees, and from then on they are to have from those same bishops the necessary food and clothing."

units.la: VI. Cum sederitis in Synodo cum praedicto sanctissimo Patriarcha, & Orientalium locumtenentibus, & reliquis Archiepiscopis, ac Metropolitis, & vniuersis Sacerdotibus Ecclesiae Constantinopolitanae, ante omnia legantur Epistolae ad Imperatorem, & interrogetur Synodus, An eas recipiat, & an obseruet testimonia in eis contenta. Cum responderit, subnectite: Dominus noster sanctissimus Papa, omnium Ecclesiarum curam habens, & vestram salutem, & vnionem, & pacem procurans, misit nos seruos suos, vt dispersos congregemus, & alienatos animis reconciliemus, & Ecclesiae misericordiae opem feramus, & accisos erigamus, vt omnes vno ore glorificemus Patrem cum Filio, & Spiritu sancto. Est ne hoc bonum, an malum? Sancta Synodus respondit; Quæcunque ad pacem & concordiam Ecclesiæ faciunt, & bona sunt, & recipienda esse existimamus. VII. Perseverantes vero in propria pertinacia, & inquiete, & in unitatem Ecclesiæ & fratrum convenire, & unitatis vinculum conseruare renuentes post secundam, & tertiam admonitionem vestram, & sanctæ Synodi, eiicite e vestra communione, & separate eos ab omni Ecclesiastico ordine, quousque vniantur proprio Patriarchæ, & illius Ecclesiæ. VIII. Vestigijs insistentes sanctorum Patrum, & decretis dicimus, post obitum sanctissimi Patriarchæ Photij nullus ex seculari dignitate ad sedem Constantinopolitanam ascendat vti nostræ Epistolæ testantur. IX. Volumus coram Synodo moneri prædictum Photium sanctissimum Patriarcham, vt neque Omophorum in Bulgariam mittat, neque in illa Dioecesi ordinationem teneat. Si aliter fecerit Canonum præscriptis poenis subiacebit. X. Volumus coram Synodo congregata denunciari, Synodum coactam contra prædictum Patriarcham Photium sub Adriano sanctissimo Papa Romæ, & in urbe Constantinopolitana, ex nunc esse expunctam, irritam, & infirmam, eamque cum aliis sanctis Synodis non collocari. XI. Sancta Synodus respondit. Nos opere ipso expunximus, & eiecimus, & anathemati subiecimus, quam vos vocatis Synodum, communicantes Photio nostro sansanctissimo Patriarchæ, & non eiicientes[?], quæ contra ipsum scripta, aut dicta sunt in ipsa commemorata a vobis Synodo, anathematizamus . Elias Metropolita Martyrcopolitanus, & Elias Hierosolymitani locumtenens, dixerunt. Et quanam ratione Synodus vocabitur, quæ innumeris dissidiis Ecclesiam repleuit. Quis Synodum illam nuncupabit, quæ sibi Saracenorum Apocrisiarios iudices, & legum latores constituit? Quibus cum Synodis annumerabitur, quæ omnibus sanctis contraria ausa est? quæ innoxios absque ullo examine condemnauit? Quæ leges omnes Ecclesiasticas confudit, & pessum dedit? Etenim propter hæc Orientis sanctissimi throni facta illius expunxerunt, atque infirmarunt, & anathemati tradiderunt.
units.tr: VI. When you have taken your seats in the synod with the aforesaid most holy Patriarch, and with the lieutenants of the East, the remaining archbishops and metropolitans, and all the priests of the Church of Constantinople, first the letters to the emperor are to be read, and the synod is to be asked whether it accepts them and whether it will observe the testimonies contained in them. When it has answered, add: "Our lord, the most holy Pope, having care of all the Churches and procuring your salvation, union and peace, has sent us, his servants, to gather the scattered, reconcile the estranged in mind, bring help to the Church's mercy and raise up the fallen, so that we may all with one mouth glorify the Father with the Son and the Holy Spirit. Is this good or bad?" The holy synod answered: "Whatever works for the peace and concord of the Church is good, and we judge it to be received." VII. But those who persist in their own obstinacy and restlessness, and refuse to come together into the unity of the Church and of the brethren and to keep the bond of unity, after your second and third admonition and that of the holy synod, you are to cast out of your communion and separate from every ecclesiastical order, until they are united with their own patriarch and his Church. VIII. Following the footsteps of the holy Fathers and their decrees, we say that after the death of the most holy Patriarch Photius, no one from the secular dignity is to ascend to the see of Constantinople, as our letters testify. IX. We wish the aforesaid most holy Patriarch Photius to be warned in the presence of the synod that he is neither to send the omophorion into Bulgaria nor to hold ordination in that diocese. If he acts otherwise, he will be subject to the penalties prescribed by the canons. X. We wish it to be announced before the assembled synod that the synod convened against the aforesaid Patriarch Photius under the most holy Pope Adrian at Rome and in the city of Constantinople is from now on expunged, void and invalid, and is not to be counted among the other holy synods. XI. The holy synod answered: "We by the act itself have expunged, cast out and subjected to anathema that which you call a synod, and we, communicating with our most holy Patriarch Photius, anathematize whatever was written or said against him in that synod commemorated by you, and we do not cast it out." Elias, metropolitan of Martyropolis, and Elias, lieutenant of Jerusalem, said: "And by what reasoning will that be called a synod which has filled the Church with countless dissensions? Who will name that synod which made Saracen envoys its judges and lawgivers? With what synods will it be numbered, which has dared to act against all the saints? Which condemned the innocent without any examination? Which has confounded and destroyed all the ecclesiastical laws? For these reasons the acts of the most holy throne of the East have expunged, weakened and handed over to anathema that synod's acts."

units.la: XII. Cauete ut secundum hoc nostrum Commonitorium inambuletis, neque donis, aut illecebris, aut minis seducti dextrorsum, aut sinistrorsum deflectatis; sed regia via incedite, uti qui locum nostrum & auctoritatem, quam vobis causa Ecclesiasticæ pacis exhibuimus, possidetis, ut vestro labore, ac studio in rem collatis nostram gratiam, & Apostolicæ sedis consequi, & nostræ communionis participes fieri possitis. Sancta Synodus dixit, En jam videmus vos sanctissimi Papæ vestigiis insistere: reipsa siquidem talis magnique Præsulis Legatos tales esse addecebat. Nicetas Dei amantissimus Metro-polipolita Smyrnensis dixit: Deus effecit, vt vos ita dispositas res inueniretis, adeo vt si quis voluerit extra praeceptionem Dei, & sanctissimi Papae praecepta incedere, illi nullus pretextus relinquatur, & res ipsa cogunt, praeter viam Dei aberrare, neque qui male sentiunt, contraria rebus pertentare. Multo itaque minus qui bonam mentem virtutum omni genere collustratam possident, & nullo modo dextrorsum, aut sinistrorsum extra Dei voluntatem, & praecepta Romani Pontificis declinabunt. Sanctissimi locumtenentes senioris Romae dixerunt. Prophetā [?] dixit, in omnia, ad quae mitto vos, procedite. Huc accessimus tantummodo, vt voluntatem Dei, & Domini nostri sanctissimi Papae compleremus. Sancta Synodus dixit. Plane consspicimus, vos Dei, & cuius vos misit Pontificis voluntatem complere. Photius sanctissimus Patriarcha dixit. Diuina voluntas est illius, qui de Coelo descendit, & nostram naturam assumpsit, & genus humanum abalienatum a Deo multos ante annos cum Patre reconciliaret. Et nunc videt cum nobis vestra sanctitas secundum voluntatem, & praeceptionem sanctissimi Papae omnia conuenisse, & nihil fuisse quod contra veniat, sed naturam etiam rerum cum ipsius sententia vna pariter confluxisse. Sanctissimi locumtenentes dixerunt. Hoc fuit opus nostrum, vt cum contentione atque labore vestra uniremur Ecclesia. Propterea & multos labores in agendo itinere sustinuimus. Sancti quoque viri laborando Christo complacuit sunt. Photius Patriarcha dixit. Deus mercedis dator dat mercedes ingentes, quae nunquam exinaniuntur, vobis in regno Cælorum recondens.
units.tr: XII. Take care to walk according to this our Commonitorium, and do not be turned to right or left, led astray by gifts, enticements or threats; but proceed on the royal road, as those who hold our place and the authority which we have granted you for the sake of ecclesiastical peace, so that by your labour and zeal, brought to bear on the matter, you may obtain our grace and that of the Apostolic See, and be made partakers of our communion. The holy synod said: "Now indeed we see you following the footsteps of the most holy Pope, since envoys of so great a prelate ought to be such." Nicetas, most beloved of God, metropolitan of Smyrna, said: "God has so arranged matters that you found things in such a state that, if anyone wished to proceed outside the command of God and the precepts of the most holy Pope, no pretext would be left to him, and the facts themselves compel him to stray from the way of God, nor would those who think ill attempt to oppose the facts. Much less, then, will those who possess a good mind, adorned with every kind of virtue, turn aside to right or left, outside the will of God and the precepts of the Roman Pontiff." The most holy lieutenants of the Elder Rome said: "The prophet said: go forward in all things to which I send you. We have come here only so that we may fulfil the will of God and of our lord, the most holy Pope." The holy synod said: "Clearly we see that you are fulfilling the will of God and of the Pontiff who sent you." Photius, the most holy Patriarch, said: "It is the divine will of him who came down from heaven, took our nature, and reconciled the human race, long estranged from God, with the Father. And now your holiness sees with us that everything has agreed with the will and precept of the most holy Pope, and that nothing has been found that runs counter to it, but that the very nature of things has flowed together into one with his judgement." The most holy lieutenants said: "This was our task: that we might be united with your Church through contention and labour. For this reason we also endured many labours in the course of the journey. Holy men too have pleased Christ by labouring." Patriarch Photius said: "May God, the giver of rewards, bestow great rewards, which are never exhausted, storing them up for you in the kingdom of heaven."

units.la: Petrus piissimus Presbyter, & Cardinalis dixit: En & subscriptiones Episcoporum, quibus se omnis animis recepisse Photium sanctissimum Patriarcham significatur cum universa sancta Romana Ecclesia: Zacharias Episcopus Ecclesiæ Anagninæ, & Apostolicæ sedis Bibliothecarius in hoc Commonitorio pro receptione sanctissimi Patriarchæ Photii propria manu subscripsit, Martinus Episcopus Ecclesiæ Narconfi similiter subscripsi. Dominicus Episcopus Ecclesiæ Trinuensi similiter. Florus Episcopus Ecclesiæ Mandurësis[?] similiter propria manu subscripsi. Gaudericus[?] Episcopus Veliterni similiter. Stephanus Episcopus S. Ecclesiæ Ferentina similiter. Leo Episcopus Gabensis missus, & Apocrisiarius Apostolicæ sedis similiter manu propria subscripsi. Petrus Episcopus Forosemproniensis similiter. Valpertus sancti Petri Ecclesiæ similiter. Simeon Episcopus S. Ecclesiæ Fundanæ & Ioannes Episcopus S. Ecclesiæ Sininæ[?] similiter. Benedictus Episcopus similiter. Gregorius Episcopus S. Ecclesiæ Silvæ Candidæ similiter. Bonifacius Episcopus S. Ecclesiæ Blerenæ similiter.
units.tr: Peter, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, said: "Here are also the signatures of the bishops, by which it is declared that all of them with their whole heart received the most holy Patriarch Photius, together with the whole holy Roman Church. Zacharias, bishop of the Church of Anagni and librarian of the Apostolic See, subscribed this Commonitorium in his own hand for the reception of the most holy Patriarch Photius. Martin, bishop of the Church of Narni, likewise subscribed. Dominicus, bishop of the Church of Trinus, likewise. Florus, bishop of the Church of Mandura[?], likewise subscribed in his own hand. Gaudericus[?], bishop of Velletri, likewise. Stephen, bishop of the holy Church of Ferentino, likewise. Leo, bishop of Gabii, sent and apocrisiary of the Apostolic See, likewise subscribed in his own hand. Peter, bishop of Forosempronio, likewise. Valpert of the Church of St Peter, likewise. Simeon, bishop of the holy Church of Fondi, and John, bishop of the holy Church of Sinna[?], likewise. Benedict, bishop, likewise. Gregory, bishop of the holy Church of Silva Candida, likewise. Boniface, bishop of the holy Church of Blera, likewise."

units.la: Stephanus Episcopus S. Nepesinorum Ecclesiæ similiter. Germanus Presbyter S. Pauli & Ioannis similiter. Petrus Presbyter S. Chrysogoni similiter. Benedictus Presbyter sanctæ Balbinæ similiter. Adrianus Presbyter sancti Laurentij similiter. Leo Presbyter similiter. Ioannes Presbyter sanctæ Ceciliæ similiter. Paulus Diaconus similiter subscripsi. Leo Diaconus similiter. Commonitorio completo Petrus pissimus Presbyter, & Cardinalis dixit; Placet ne vestræ Sanctitati? Sancta Synodus respondit, Placet, & potissimum subscriptiones factæ pro communi pace, & concordia sanctæ Dei Ecclesiæ, & de receptione Photij sanctissimi, & Oecumenici Patriarchæ. Et his dictis laudantes, fausta precati sunt.
units.tr: Stephen, bishop of the holy Church of Nepi, likewise. Germanus, presbyter of Sts Paul and John, likewise. Peter, presbyter of St Chrysogonus, likewise. Benedict, presbyter of St Balbina, likewise. Adrian, presbyter of St Lawrence, likewise. Leo, presbyter, likewise. John, presbyter of St Cecilia, likewise. Paul, deacon, likewise subscribed. Leo, deacon, likewise. When the Commonitorium had been completed, Peter, the most pious presbyter and cardinal, said: "Does it please your Holiness?" The holy Synod replied: "It pleases us, and especially the subscriptions made for the common peace and concord of the holy Church of God, and for the reception of the most holy Photius, Patriarch and Ecumenical Patriarch." And with these words, praising him, they prayed for his prosperity.

units.la: Hic ut vides contenta voce profitentur, subscriptum fuisse hoc Commonitorium, sive a Synodo Romana dictatum, sive Photianis artibus conceptum, sive a Romano sermone aliis additis, vel detractis malitiose in Græcum transfusum, pro pace, & unione Ecclesiis conciliandâ, & restitutione Photii, nulla facta mentione de dogmate. Ergo postremæ istæ Actiones, in quibus agitur de dogmate, a Photianis confictæ sunt & additæ, quod est præter mentem, & præceptionem Pontificis Romani, qui mandat, extra contenta in Commonitorio nihil aliud audendum, & postulata etiam ab Imperatore, qui nihil aliud rogat, quam restitutionem Photij ob pacem Ecclesiarum, clamante quoque Synodo; [?]Ὅσα [?]ἀ[?]ιλώ[?]ω, [?]Ἐ[?]ιμόνοιαν δὲ Ἐ[?]κκλησίας [?]ἀ[?]ὶ [?]καὶ [?]τ[?]ῆ[?]ς [?]ἁγί[?]ας [?]ὑπ[?]ο[?]ο[?]ῖ[?]α. Quaecunque ad pacem & concordiam Ecclesiae faciunt, & bona sunt, & recipienda esse existimamus. Ergo vel ista Synodus, vel hae postremae Actiones Synodus non sunt, sed Photianorum commenta. Et nullam tum fuisse quaestionem de dogmate, ex ipso Photio manifeste elicitur. Latinos Processionem Spiritus etiam ex Filio profiteri non nesciebat Photius. pellitur Ignatius. Photius substituitur, & petit confirmari a Nicolao, multa eloquentissime in sui defensionem congerens, ut constat ex Epistola ipsius ad Nicolaum. nullum ibi est verbum de dogmate. Nicolaus causae momenta examinat, tum inuasorem declarans Photium condemnat. Sic Photius exauctoratus in rabiem versus inter alia, dogma quoque Latinorum de Processione Spiritus criminatur. Si dogma Latinorum error, aut haeresis est, quare petit suam confirmationem ab Haeretico, qua vel sola stabilitatem in throno sibi promittit? Si haeresis non est, improbum se gerit cum Romanis, dum illis opponit crimen, quod crimen non est. Et modo in hac Synodo restitutus a Ioanne, Ioanni crimen obijceret: quod si crimen esse pro certo in Ecclesia haberetur, iam ipsa sua restitutio per Ioannem haereticum facta, in discrimen veniret, & pror. fusrueret. Est ergo Ioannes Catholicus pro. cessionem Spiritus etiam ex Filio clamitaris, & Photium restituens, & ab eodem Photio laudibus in hac eadem Synodo exornatus. Quare Actiones istae additiciae sunt, ne reconciliatio Photij vertatur in dubium.
units.tr: Here, as you see, they openly declare that this Commonitorium was subscribed, whether it was dictated by the Roman Synod, or devised by the arts of the Photians, or maliciously translated into Greek from a Roman text with additions or omissions, for the sake of bringing about peace and union of the Churches and the restoration of Photius, with no mention made of doctrine at all. Therefore those last Acts, in which doctrine is discussed, were invented and added by the Photians. This is contrary to the intention and instruction of the Roman Pontiff, who orders that nothing beyond what is contained in the Commonitorium be attempted, and contrary to the request of the Emperor, who asks for nothing but the restoration of Photius for the peace of the Churches; the Synod also shouted: "Whatever brings about peace and harmony of the Church, we consider good and to be received." [Ὅσα ... ἐιμόνοιαν δὲ Ἐκκλησίας ... ὑπο... as printed] Therefore either this is not a Synod, or these last Acts are not from the Synod, but inventions of the Photians. And it is clearly drawn from Photius himself that there was then no question about doctrine. Photius was not unaware that the Latins also confess the procession of the Spirit from the Son. Ignatius is driven out; Photius is put in his place and asks to be confirmed by Nicholas, heaping up in his own defence many very eloquent arguments, as is clear from his letter to Nicholas. There is not a word about doctrine in it. Nicholas examines the grounds of the case, then declares Photius an usurper and condemns him. Thus Photius, deposed, raged and, among other things, accused the Latin doctrine of the procession of the Spirit. If the Latin doctrine is an error or heresy, why does he ask his confirmation from a heretic, by which alone he promises himself stability on the throne? If it is not heresy, he acts dishonestly with the Romans, since he charges them with a crime which is no crime. And recently, restored in this Synod by John, he would have charged John with this crime; but if it were certainly held in the Church to be a crime, his very restoration by a heretical John would have been put in jeopardy and would have collapsed. Therefore John was a Catholic, who declared the procession of the Spirit also from the Son, and who restored Photius and was himself praised by the same Photius in this same Synod. Therefore those Acts are spurious, lest the reconciliation of Photius be called into doubt.

units.la: Sed neglectis in Commonitorio minutioribus, consideremus, an Synodus praecepta sibi a Ioanne compleuerit, quibus non completis Ioannes ipse Acta confringens, reddit irrita, licet nonnulla de his supra adnotauerimus. Primum est, ne in posterum Constantinopolitanus in Bulgariam ordinationes teneat, neque Sacerdotes mittat; si contraeuenerit, non abibit inultus, sed Canonum praescripto castigabitur. Non obediunt Photiani, alia atq; alia causantes, & negotium ad Imperatorem remittunt.
units.tr: But, setting aside the minor points in the Commonitorium, let us consider whether the Synod fulfilled the conditions laid on it by John, and, since these were not fulfilled, John himself, breaking the Acts, made them void, although I have noted some of these above. The first is that henceforth the Constantinopolitan shall not hold ordinations in Bulgaria, nor send priests there; if he acts against this, he will not go unpunished but will be chastised according to the prescription of the Canons. The Photians do not obey, offering one excuse after another, and refer the matter back to the Emperor.

units.la: Act. 4. Ἡ ἁγία Σύνοδος ἅπαν ἡμῖν ἐ ἀπολύ[?] τῇ ἡμῶν ἀξιώσει, ἐ πάλιν λέγομεν, [illegible, ~12 letters] ἀλλ' ὁ λόγος [?] παρούσῃ διέστησεν, [illegible, ~14 letters] τὸν Βυζαντίου βασιλεία [?] ὡς [illegible, ~8 letters] σὴ αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς ἐ ποιήσῃ, τ̀ ϑεῶν, ᾗ ἴσον κανό-[?] νων συμπεσόντων, ἐ διαζωμένων ἡμῖν, περὶ ὧν [illegible, ~8 letters] ἡμᾶς. Sancta Synodus dixit. Nos ante etiam vestra Sanctitati diximus, rursusque dicimus, longe esse ab hoc argumento de Dioecesibus quaestionem, & tempus proprium, & opportunum exquirere. Nihilominus vobiscum vna piissimum nostrum Imperatorem precamur, vt decernat de hoc, vti ipsum Deus direxerit, & ordinauerit, dummodo sacrosanctorum Canonum consensum, atque vnitatem nobis seruauerit: tum etenim illius decreta excipiemus, illisque calculum addemus. Secundum, ne quis in posterum ex laico in sacros ordines promoueatur, quod & in Epistolis id inculcauerat, contra leges Ecclesiasticas esse. Respondent Photiani, id non esse contra legem Ecclesiasticam, ideoque morem vniuscuiusque Ecclesiae seruandum: Βασιλεὺς ὁ Θεοφιλέστατος Μητροπολίτης Μαρτυρο-πόλεως καὶ τοποτηρητὴς, καὶ Ἡλίας ὁ Θεοσεβέστατος Πρεσβύτερος καὶ τοποτηρητὴς, ἐπὶ ᾗ καὶ Κοσμᾶς Διάκονος ἀπέρ[?]ιο. Ἀλεξανδρίας εἶπον. τῶν κατ' ἀὐτὴν ἐκκλησιαστικῶν [?]. Καὶ ᾗ δὲ καὶ ἡ Ἀλεξανδρέων [?] ὁ Πατριάρχης τῆς Ἀντιοχείας Θεοῦ; ἀλλὰ μὲν ἡ ἡ τῆς αὐτίας πόλεως, ἐν οἷω δ' αὖ τάγμα ἐ τὸ λεγόμενον, ἐ πολιτικῶν [illegible, ~10 letters] ἐπὶ τὸν ἐρχόμενον ἀκοῦν Θεόνον αὐαβιβάζειν ἢ παραπ-τῶνζωῶταί. ἡ γὰρ δὲ μόνως κληρικὸς καπήλθεν ὅτι γῆς ὁ Χειστός, ἀλλ' ἐν τούτοις μόνοις ἀπέκλεισε τὰ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἄθλα, ἀλλὰ πᾶσι τοῖς χειραγωγικοῖς πληρω-μασιν· τοῦτο οὖν εἰ ἀδοκιμάσθη ἀποκληθῆναι, πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερατικοὶ Θεῖοι εἰς ἐρήμωσιν, καὶ ἀπόλαβεῖν ἐχουσι κλεῖστν. οἱ γὰρ πλείως τῆς ἀλαμψάντων ἐν ἡμῖν ὑπὸ λαϊκῆς τάγματος οὖν ἀρχιερατικὸς καταπᾶς ὁ Ἀθηνοῦ θεύνης. ἡμεῖς δὲ τούτῳ σωαγρίζειν ἡ διωάμεθα, ἵνα μὴ τῇ τῆς ἀρχιερέων ἡμῖν φωταγωγῶμεν ταλμῶν ἐξαγόντες. ἡ ἀμία Σωσθ[?] ἔστιν. ἐκάστῳ Θεῷ ἔχει ἀρχαῖά τινα ἀποδεδομένα ἔδη. Καὶ ἐχρὴ πρὸς ἀλλήλους τε τῶν φιλονεικῶν καὶ εἰςζν. Φυλάττεται μὲν γὰρ ἡ τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησία τὸ εἶναι αὐτῆς, ὁ φυσικόν ὅτι. Φυλάττεται δὲ ἡ Κωνσταντινοπολίτη Ἐκκλησία ἰδίᾳ τινὰ ἔθη αὐτῶν ἀποδεδλαβῆσθαι. ὡς αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ τῆς αἱρετικῆς Θεῖοι. Εἰπὼν οὖν ἡ τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησία ἐλήποτε ἀπὸ Λαϊκῶν παρεληλυθὼς εἰς ἀρχιερεία, φυλάττει τὸ τοῦτο. φυσικὸν γὰρ ἔστιν ἔγκ πατέρων μὴ ἀποβαίνειν. ἐπεὶ ἢ ἔτι οἱ αἱρετικοὶ τὸ παρεφυ-λάξαντο, ἔτι ἡ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἀμα Κωνσταντινοπολίτη Ἐκκλησία, ἐχρῆσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς κληρικῶν, καὶ λαϊκῶν τοιοῦτος αὐαδίκυνδ. ὥστε τὸν ψῆφον τῆς ἀρχιερωσύνης ὑπ' αὐτὸς ἔχειν. Α' ἀν δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς μὴ ὤσι ζῶντοι, ἐν ᾗ πολλαϊκῇ τάγματι ἔπιπ-φαίνων. ἐδὲ τῆς διηποτέρως καταλιμπάνων, ἐδὲ οὖν ἀξιωτέρως, ἐς οὖν αἰεπτ-πής, καὶ ἐλάσεως ἕν τῶν ἀξίαν τῶν αὐτῆς παρελ-κύσῃ ψῆφον. Basilius Dei omantissimus Martyropolitanus Metropolita & Locumtenens, & Elias piissimus Presbyter & Locumtenens, Cosmas[?] item Apocrisiarius Alexandrini dixere; Hoc Ecclesiasticis Canonibus non adversatur; Nanque Alexandrinus, & Patriarchalis thronus Antiochenus, & similiter sancta Civitatis, in quocunque ordine sive seculari, sive clericali invenerint virtute reliquis aliys praestantiorem, ad archieraticam sedem promovere non dedignantur: neque enim ob solos Clericos Christus in terram descendit, neque illis solis virtutis praemia circumduxit, sed universo Christianorum complemento. Hoc itaque si approbatum fuerit receptumque, omnes Archieraticae sedes in desolationem atque interitum abibunt. Potior enim eorum pars, quae apud nostros inclaruit, ex laicali ordine ad Archieraticas sedes evecti sunt. Nos huic assensum praebere non possumus, ne contra nostros Praesules sententiam tulisse deprehendamur: Sancta Synodus dixit; Singulae sedes habent singulares suas proprias consuetudines, neque pro iis cum aliis in controversiam veniendum est, & decertandum. Observat siquidem Romana Ecclesia suas consuetudines, quod & convenit. Observat itidem & Constantinopolitana Ecclesia quasdam suas consuetudines ab antiquo tempore sibi traditas, similiter & throni Orientales. Quare si Romana Ecclesia nunquam ex laico in Praesulem admisit, id obseruet: nanque conuenit terminos maiorum non praeuertere. Veruntamen cum id neque Orientales throni, neque nostra sancta Constantinopolitana Ecclesia simile quid acceptanerit, supplices Deo continuo vota reddimus, vt ex Clericis, & Laicis tales proueniant, qui digne calculum Pra[?]sulatus in sese admittant: quod si inter Clericos tales non fuerint, & ex Laico ordine aptiores inuenti fuerint, nemo aptiores respuens, neque extraneos in ineptos & dignitate inferiores calculum suum proiciet. Quod erat tertium, non abfimili ratione eludunt. Ὥστε μὴ ἐξ ἄλλης Ἐκκλησίας προάγεσθαι εἰς ἀρχιερέα τῆς Κωνσταντινουπολιτῶν Ἐκκλησίας, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ Καρδ[?]ιωκαλίῳ, Πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ Διακόνων. ἡ ἁγία Σιὼν ἔστι. τὸ κεφάλαιον συμβαίνει τῷ ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... ὁ Θεὸς τῆς Κωνσταντινουπολίτων ἀγίας Ἐκκλησίας ἡμῖν ... [illegible, ~10 letters] ... φανῇ, ὥστε εἶναι ἐν αὐτῇ Πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ Διακόνων ... [illegible, ~8 letters] ... λαμπρὸν ἀπάντων τῶν ὑπὸ τὴν Ῥωμαϊκὴν ἀρχήν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν Ἱερέων, καὶ Διακόνων. ἵνα καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μόνων ὅτι τὸν μέγιστον Θεὸν τῆς ἀρχιερεύσεως ἀναβιβάζωμεν. εἰ δὲ ὁ κεχρισμένος [?] ... [illegible, ~14 letters] ... ἐξεζόμενον τῶν ἐν τοῖς μείζοσιν αὐτῆς ἐξεταζόμενον τῷ ἐν τοῖς ἐλάττοσιν. Non esse ex alia Ecclesia in Præsulem Constantinopolitanum, sed ex ipsius Cardinalibus, Presbyteris, & Diaconis promovendum. Sancta Synodus dixit. Hoc caput continetur in priori. Et utinam Deus concederet sanctæ Ecclesiæ Constantinopolitanæ sic nobilitari, & inclarescere, ut qui in ea sunt Diaconi, & Presbyteri, omnium, qui sub ditione Græcorum ac dominatu viviunt, omnibus Sacerdotibus, ac Diaconis præstantiores sint, ut ex iis solis in maximum hunc thronum promoveri possint. Quod si tempus tales non ostenderit ex Ecclesiasticis, qui virtute, & aliis prærogativis alios antecellant, ille regiæ urbis dignitatem archieraticam communi omnium calculo in se suscipiat, quem qui sibi iudicium assumant, uti maioribus virtutibus præditum, si cum eo, qui inferior est, comparetur, elegerint. Et hac ratione Synodus ista Photiana, restitutionem Photij, & sui confirmationem a Ioanne Pontifice Romano expectans, mandatis Pontificiis obtemperat; & ad nutum Ioannis præsto est. Cum ergo Synodus legitima non est, quæ mandata sibi a Romano non observat, concludamus, Photianam hanc haud morigeram Pontifici Synodum non esse, & consequenter Synodica illius attendenda non esse, neque Photium restitutum, cui si restitutio placita erat, quæ exigebantur a Romano, uti dignitate, & auctoritate antecedente, post delictorum confessionem, & peractam poenitentiam, & absolutionem acceptam, mandatis obtemperandum erat. Idq; cum non fecerit, mirum non est, si post compertas fraudes, & Legatorum praevaricationem, quidquid erat gestum in ea Ioannes infregit, & infectum esse declaravit.
units.tr: Act. 4. The holy Synod says: "We have already told your Holiness, and we say again, that the question of the dioceses is far from this subject, and that it needs its own proper and fitting time. Nevertheless, together with you we pray that our most pious Emperor decide this matter as God shall direct and ordain him, provided that he preserve for us the agreement and unity of the sacred Canons. Then indeed we will accept his decrees and add our vote to them." The second point: that from now on no one be promoted from the laity to the sacred orders, which the Pope had also pressed in his letters as contrary to the ecclesiastical laws. The Photians reply that this is not contrary to ecclesiastical law, and that each Church must therefore keep its own custom. [Basileus, the most God-beloved Metropolitan of Martyropolis and locum tenens, and Elias, the most pious Presbyter and locum tenens, and likewise Cosmas, the deacon and apocrisiarius of Alexandria, said: "This is not opposed to the ecclesiastical Canons. For the Alexandrian and Antiochene patriarchal thrones, and likewise the holy city, do not disdain to raise to the archiepiscopal see whoever, in any order, whether lay or clerical, they find superior to the rest in virtue. For Christ did not come down to earth for clerics alone, nor did he offer the prizes of virtue to them alone, but to the whole body of Christians. So if this is approved and accepted, all the archiepiscopal sees will go to desolation and ruin. For the greater part of those who have shone among us were raised from the lay order to the archiepiscopal sees. We cannot give our assent to this, lest we be found to have passed a judgment against our own prelates."] The holy Synod says: "Each see has its own particular customs, and we must not come into dispute and contention with others about them. The Roman Church keeps its customs, and rightly so; likewise the Constantinopolitan Church keeps certain customs handed down to it from ancient times, and so do the Eastern thrones. Therefore, if the Roman Church has never admitted a layman as prelate, let it keep that practice, for it is fitting not to overstep the boundaries set by our elders. Yet since neither the Eastern thrones nor our holy Constantinopolitan Church have accepted anything similar, we continually offer prayers to God that there may arise from the clergy and the laity such men as worthily admit the vote for the prelacy into themselves. But if there are no such men among the clergy, and more suitable men are found in the lay order, no one, rejecting the more suitable, shall cast his vote away on unfit men of lesser dignity and on outsiders." The third point they elude in a not dissimilar way. [That no one be promoted from another Church to be archbishop of the Constantinopolitan Church, but from among its own presbyters and deacons: "the holy Sion is" ... "God grant us that the holy Church of Constantinople be seen..."; "that there be in it presbyters and deacons ... brilliant above all who are under the Roman rule and authority of priests and deacons, so that from them alone we may raise up the greatest of the priesthood." "But if the anointed ..."] It is not to be examined from another Church for the Constantinopolitan Presulate, but to be promoted from its own cardinals, presbyters and deacons. The holy Synod says: "This point is contained in the earlier one. Would that God grant that the holy Church of Constantinople be so ennobled and so renowned that those who are deacons and presbyters in it be more distinguished than all the priests and deacons who live under the rule of the Greeks, so that the most exalted throne might be filled from them alone. But if the time does not show such men from among the ecclesiastics, who excel the others in virtue and other prerogatives, then let him take on the archiepiscopal dignity of the royal city by the common vote of all, whom they have judged, having compared him with the one who is inferior, to be endowed with greater virtues." And by this reasoning this Photian Synod, expecting the restoration of Photius and its own confirmation from John, the Roman Pontiff, obeys the Pontifical commands and is at the nod of John. Therefore, since a synod that does not observe the commands laid on it by the Roman is not a lawful synod, let us conclude that this Photian synod, which is not compliant with the Pontiff, is not a synod, and consequently that its synodal acts are not to be heeded, nor is Photius restored. If restoration was pleasing to him, then, once the things demanded by the Roman had been done, after the confession of his offences, the completed penance, and the absolution received, he ought to have obeyed the commands, as one of prior dignity and authority. Since he did not do so, it is no wonder that, after the frauds were discovered and the Legates' prevarication, John broke whatever had been done in it and declared it undone.

units.la: CAPUT XII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII.

units.la: Ioannis Henrici Hottingeri, Ioannis Henrici Boecleri, & Roberti Creyghtoni de Pho- tio mendacia recluduntur, & redarguuntur.
units.tr: The lies of Johann Heinrich Hottinger, Johann Heinrich Boeckler and Robert Creighton about Photius are exposed and refuted.

units.la: EXpedirem exitum meae differtationis, nisi Magistellus ex Zuingliana schola Tigurinus solemni suo more, ut in aliis omnibus immaniter insaniret, cum de dissidiis inter Pontifices Romanos Nicolaum & Adrianum, & Photium agit. Scribit: Fuit illi, Photio, lucta cum Ignatio eiusque sectatoribus, qui eum accusabant, quod non recte successisset Ignatio contra ius, & Canones deposito. Deinde etiam cum Pontifice Romano ipsi ea de re certamen fuit ingens, quod is ex ambitione dominatum sibi super Ecclesias vindicaret, ac omnes controversias ad suum fofilius arbitrium, & sententiam definiri contenderet, & scripsit librum contra Nicolaum Pontificem, quem a pluribus Episcopis subscribi curauerat, vt patet ex libro Pontificali in vita Adriani II. Tertio cum Basilio Imperatore parricida, qui eum ab officio remouit, dissimulans causam veram, & prætendens aliam, quod alienam sedem nimirum Ignatij iniuste obtineret: & iussit eum Romæ coram Adriano II. litigare. Misit etiam librum illius contra Nicolaum, scriptum ad Adrianum, qui isthic in Synodo damnatus, & exutus est, ac missi Legati Constantinopoli in Synodo Photium declararunt depositum, & excommunicatum, vt patet ex Actis eius Synodi. Postea tamen cum Basilius fraudes Romanas agnouisset, & Ignatius e vinculis sublatus esset, Photium restituit in pristinam sedem, unde iterum expulit Leo Philosophus Imperator, ac in Armeniorum Monasterium relegauit, vbi videtur esse mortuus.
units.tr: I would finish my treatise now, were it not that the little teacher from the Zwinglian school at Zurich, in his usual solemn manner, raves monstrously in everything else, as he treats of the quarrels between the Roman Pontiffs Nicholas and Hadrian and Photius. He writes: Photius had a struggle with Ignatius and his followers, who accused him of having succeeded Ignatius wrongly, against law and the canons, since Ignatius had been deposed. Then he also had a great contest with the Roman Pontiff himself over this matter, because the Pontiff, out of ambition, claimed lordship over the Churches and tried to have all controversies decided by his own judgment and opinion. Photius wrote a book against Pope Nicholas, which he had caused to be signed by several bishops, as appears from the Liber Pontificalis in the life of Hadrian II. Thirdly, with Basil the parricide emperor, who removed him from office, concealing the true cause and pretending another, namely that he unjustly held the see that belonged to Ignatius; and Basil ordered him to dispute at Rome before Hadrian II. He also sent Photius's book against Nicholas, written to Hadrian, which was condemned and deprived in that synod there; and the legates sent to Constantinople declared Photius deposed and excommunicated in the synod, as appears from the Acts of that synod. Later, however, when Basil had recognised the Roman frauds, and Ignatius had been released from his chains, Basil restored Photius to his former see; from there Leo the Philosopher emperor expelled him again and relegated him to the monastery of the Armenians, where he is thought to have died.

units.la: Et hic nugipolyloquides, licet aphoristice scribat, vel legisse historias, vel lectas non intellexisse, velrerum momenta nullo pacto examinasse dicetur. Credant scioli, credant festiui Saperdæ. Recte ergo tulerit Hottingerus, si post tot sua mendacia, atque impostEnsuras de rebus Ecclesiasticis Græcorum in duabus non magnis paginulis a nobis discussas, atque diffamatas, hic quoque novis hisce apophoretis accumulari. Scripserat supra, Basilius a Photio tanquam homicida excommunicatus sacris fuit prohibitus. Sequitur Zonaram, qui ad hæc tempora inauditam eiectionis Photianæ causam ex Georgij Hamartoli Historia, vt puto, extraxit, vt videre potes, si huiusce historiam præ manibus habes, sin minus, beabo te, si verba exscripsero. Sunt vero. Τῆ δὲ Βασιλίως ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀπαλλαγεὶς, ἡ τῆς ἀρχαίας θυσίας μετάλαβὼν βασιλεύοντος, ὁ Παλαιολόγος Φωτίος τῆς Θεᾶς αὐτὸν ἀπορρήξεως μεγάλης ἀνεφόβουν ἀνάξιον. ἐπ' οἷς Θυμωθεὶς ὁ Βασιλεὺς ἐκ Ῥώμης ἐπισκόπους ἐλθεῖν παρεκάλεσε, Τόμον ἐπιφέροντας τὸ Πάπα, καὶ τὸ Πατριαρχικὸν θρόνον ἐξωθῆσαι, Ἰγνάτιον δὲ τὸν ἐξωθηθέντα πατριάρχην ἀπεδείξατο τὸ δεύτερον. Cum vero in Ecclesiam ingressus esset Imperator, & immaculati Sacrificij particeps fieri vellet, Patriarcha Photius a diuina Communione exturbauit, homicidam vocitans & prædonem, et immaculatorum Mysteriorum indignum. Quibus exasperatus Imperator, Romā Episcopos Byzantium aduocauit Tomum Pontificis ferentes, & sic eum e Patriarchali sede expulit: Sanctum vero Ignatium Patriarcham secundo promouit. Basilium nempe a Photio uti homicidam a piorum societate, & communione fuisse seseclusum, ideoque Photij abdicationem procurasse: nec advertit tot aliorum illius temporis scriptorum, quibus res similes exploratissimæ fuerunt, seclusionis similis nulla habita ratione, aliam atque aliam causam in medium attulisse, Nicolaum Papam, Acta Concilij octaui, Nicetam, Stylianum, Constantinum Porphyrogennetam, Basilium ipsum, & alios. Et tamen si conferatur ad hos imi subsellij vir, longe post hæc tempora vixit. Si licuit Zonaræ schismatico auctorem schismatis Photium fingendo alia omnia commentitio præsidio tutari, liceat nunc quoque Hottingero Hæretico fabuloso mendacio innixum historiam, quam ex vero proferre profitetur, præuertere, & Photij diuini cultus impetum debuccinare, qui intra unius morulæ, ut ita dicam, spatium causam examinauit, homicidij reum Imperatorem comperit, & in eum uti homicidam sententiam ferendo e sacris exclusit. Michaël siquidem vigesimo quarto die Septembris occiditur, Photius vigesimo septimo eiusdem mensis procurante Basilio eijcitur, & restituitur Ignatius. Non est hæc via iuris, & ratio, sed turbulenta rerum omnium concussio. His adde,etiam si male affectus in Basilium Photius effet, id minus conficere, & addere exextremum actum fabulae perexiguum tempus non concessisse. Nanque statim atque summam Imperij Basilius tenuit, & vt ita dicam, eodem ipso momento legatos a Photio ad Pontificem reuocauit, & absque vllo decreto Pontificio eijcit Photium, & audiens ob dienfque Nicolao presso tenore exauctoratum in Monasterium Scepem dictum relegat, & Ignatium etiam absentem restituit, quod mihi sanctissimus item & eloquentissimus illius aeui scriptor Michael Syncellus uno verbulo significauit, παραχρῆμα, continuo, subito, simul atque in potestate sua dominium fuit.
units.tr: Here this babbler of nonsense, although he writes in aphorisms, would be said either to have read histories without understanding what he read, or to have never weighed the importance of the facts at all. Let the half-learned believe it, let the jesting Saperdas believe it. Hottinger therefore deserved what he got, if after so many of his lies and impostures about the ecclesiastical affairs of the Greeks, which we examined and exposed in two not large pages, he is here also loaded with new trifles. Above he had written that Basil, excommunicated by Photius as a murderer, was barred from the sacred rites. He follows Zonaras, who, as I think, drew from the History of George Hamartolus the cause of Photius's expulsion, unheard of up to those times. You can see this if you have that history at hand; if not, I will spare you by copying out the words. They are these: [Τῆ δὲ Βασιλίως ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀπαλλαγεὶς, ἡ τῆς ἀρχαίας θυσίας μετάλαβὼν βασιλεύοντος, ὁ Παλαιολόγος Φωτίος τῆς Θεᾶς αὐτὸν ἀπορρήξεως μεγάλης ἀνεφόβουν ἀνάξιον. ἐπ' οἷς Θυμωθεὶς ὁ Βασιλεὺς ἐκ Ῥώμης ἐπισκόπους ἐλθεῖν παρεκάλεσε, Τόμον ἐπιφέροντας τὸ Πάπα, καὶ τὸ Πατριαρχικὸν θρόνον ἐξωθῆσαι, Ἰγνάτιον δὲ τὸν ἐξωθηθέντα πατριάρχην ἀπεδείξατο τὸ δεύτερον.] Translated: when the emperor entered the Church and wished to partake of the sacrifice that had been offered, Patriarch Photius cast him out from divine communion, calling him a murderer and robber, unworthy of the immaculate mysteries. Enraged at this, the emperor asked bishops to come from Rome, bringing the Pope's Tome, and to drive Photius from the patriarchal throne; and he appointed Ignatius, the patriarch who had been expelled, a second time. When indeed the emperor had entered the Church and wished to share in the immaculate sacrifice, Patriarch Photius cast him out from divine communion, calling him a murderer and a robber and unworthy of the immaculate mysteries. Exasperated by this, the emperor summoned bishops from Rome to Byzantium, bearing the Pope's Tome, and thus drove him from the patriarchal see; and he restored the holy Ignatius as patriarch a second time. That Basil was shut out by Photius from the fellowship and communion of the pious as a murderer, and that Photius's deposition was therefore brought about, is what he says; but he did not notice that the many other writers of that time, for whom these matters were thoroughly established, brought forward different causes, never mentioning any such exclusion: Pope Nicholas, the Acts of the Eighth Council, Nicetas, Stylianus, Constantine Porphyrogenitus, Basil himself, and others. And yet, if he is compared with these, Zonaras, a man of the lowest rank of the bench, lived long after those times. If it was allowed to Zonaras, a schismatic, to shield with an invented pretext everything else, by making Photius the author of the schism, let it now also be allowed to Hottinger, a heretic, to forestall with a fabulous lie the history he professes to give from the truth, and to trumpet abroad Photius's zeal for divine worship, who within the space, as I may say, of a short delay examined the case, found the emperor guilty of murder, and by pronouncing sentence on him as a murderer shut him out of the sacred rites. For Michael was killed on the twenty-fourth day of September; Photius was cast out on the twenty-seventh of the same month through Basil's agency, and Ignatius was restored. This is not the way of law and reason, but a turbulent upheaval of all things. Add to this that even if Photius had been ill-disposed towards Basil, this would make little difference, and that the final act of the drama did not allow a very short time. For as soon as Basil held the supreme power, and, as I may say, at that very moment, he recalled the envoys from Photius to the Pope; and without any papal decree he cast out Photius, and, as Nicholas had pressed, Photius was deprived and relegated to a monastery called Scepe; and he also restored Ignatius, though absent. The most holy and eloquent writer of that age, Michael Syncellus, signified this to me in one word, parachrēma [παραχρῆμα], at once, immediately, as soon as dominion was in his power.

units.la: Audiatur, Ὁ δ᾽ ἀδίκως καταχειρισθεὶς μὲν Φωτίου τῆς ἐπιφανείας τὴν [?]ἀρχιερωσύνην [?], τὸ ἐκ Μακεδόνων Βασιλέως τὸν Θεόφιλον τῆς βασιλείας τλωικαῦτα παρελθὼν [?]. Οὓς καὶ παραδὼν τὸν μέγαν, καὶ νέον Θεοφόρον Ἰγνάτιον ἐκ τῆς πολιτείας ἐξορίας αὐτ[?]ανακαλεῖται, καὶ τῇ τε λαῷ πατρὸς αἰτήσει πρέσβεις, λαμπρῶς, καὶ μὲ ὅσης ἐπὶ ἐν ἵνα πυρὸς εἰς τὸν Παλαιολόγειον ἀναβιβάζει θρόνον[?].
units.tr: Let us hear him: "He who had been unjustly installed by Photius in the high priesthood of the Epiphany, having passed over Theophilus of the Macedonian imperial line in favour of himself; and having handed over to him the great and new God-bearing Ignatius, recalled from exile, and with the people's request, brilliantly, and with the greatest splendour, raises him up to the Palaiologan throne..." [Ὁ δ᾽ ἀδίκως καταχειρισθεὶς μὲν Φωτίου τῆς ἐπιφανείας τὴν ἀρχιερωσύνην, τὸ ἐκ Μακεδόνων Βασιλέως τὸν Θεόφιλον τῆς βασιλείας τλωικαῦτα παρελθὼν. Οὓς καὶ παραδὼν τὸν μέγαν, καὶ νέον Θεοφόρον Ἰγνάτιον ἐκ τῆς πολιτείας ἐξορίας αὐτανακαλεῖται, καὶ τῇ τε λαῷ πατρὸς αἰτήσει πρέσβεις, λαμπρῶς, καὶ μὲ ὅσης ἐπὶ ἐν ἵνα πυρὸς εἰς τὸν Παλαιολόγειον ἀναβιβάζει θρόνον.]

units.la: Iniqua vero sententia damnatus Ignatius ingenti cum gloria sacram sedem recuperauit, simul ac Basilius Macedo imperium accepit, qui continuo eximium, & nouum hunc Deiferum Ignatium, ex diuturno exilio reuocatum, permotus universi populi postulatis summo cum honore, summaque veneratione in Patriarchium restituit. Et tempora ad unguem Niceta Paphlago subdistinxit; Καὶ ὁ Μιχαὴλ ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἐκ-κλησίας κυρίε, πεποιηκὼς [illegible, ~10 letters] ἐν δικτιῶν ἔχει ἀρχῶ [?] ἡ [?] πατρίκιος ὁ Σιπ[?]μβ[?]ε[?]ι[?]. καὶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς εἰς τὰ βασίλεια κατ[?]ὰ [?]ὠ[?]μ[?]ν, Αὐτοκράτωρ ἀνηρέθετο. παρὰ δὲ ἡ πέμψας εἰς καὶ ζαδρομὼ [?] τὸν Ζαχαρίαν Χαλκηδόνος ἐν μέσῳ ἀπέστρεψε τὴν ὁδὸν. Τῇ ἐξῆς δὲ μετὰ τὴν ἀναχώρησιν τὰ Πατριαρχικὰ θέρῃ τὸν Φώτιον καταβιβάζει, ἐν Μοναστηρίῳ τινὶ καλουμένῳ Σκέπῃ τὴν ὄνομα ἐξορίζει, καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον Ἡλίας ὁ ἀναφανέστατος τῆς βασιλικῆς σόλου [illegible, ~8 letters] ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλικῶν δρόμων πρὸς τὸν ἀμωμότατον Πατριάρχην, ὅπως αὐτὸν ἐκ τῆς νήσου πρὸς τὴν βασιλίδα μετὰ τῆς ὀφειλομένης τιμῆς [illegible, ~3 letters]. Cumque malum fecisset Michael in conspectu Ecclesiæ Dei, periit initio indictionis primæ, IX. Kal. Octobris, Basilius regia occupata Imperator est consalutatus; qui missis ad renocandum ex itinere Zachariam, illum e media via retraxit. Posteroque die quam renunciatus erat Imperator, Photium de throno deturbatum in Monasterium Scepen appellatum eijcit. Postridieque Eliam splendidissimum regiæ classis Drungarium cum Dromone regio, seu celoce ad sanctissimum Patriarcham ex Insula Constantinopolim ea, qua par est, honoris pompa reducendum, mittit. Idemmet Imperator Basilius in suo Epanagnostico dedeclarat, ante communes Reipublicæ curas dediffe operam, vt Ecclesiasticæ controuersiæ componerentur; Τῆς Θείας ἐφιλανθρωπίας φρονήσεως τὰ πολλὰ δ' οἰκουμένης ὀλκάδος ἡμῶν ἐξηρέσεως, πᾶς ἐνιαυτοῦ[?] ἰδιώματι[?] ἀναλαμβάνω, καὶ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς[?] τῆς Δημοσίων φροντίδων[?] τὰς ἐκκλησιαστικὰς ἐρευνὰς[?] ἐξελαύνει[?].
units.tr: Ignatius, condemned by an unjust sentence, recovered the sacred see with great glory as soon as Basil the Macedonian received the empire; who at once, moved by the petitions of the whole people, restored the outstanding and new God-bearing Ignatius, recalled from long exile, to the patriarchate with great honour and the highest veneration. Niceta Paphlago also set out these times exactly: [Καὶ ὁ Μιχαὴλ ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἐκκλησίας κυρίε, πεποιηκὼς ἐν δικτιῶν ἔχει ἀρχῶ ἡ πατρίκιος ὁ Σιπμβε ι. καὶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς εἰς τὰ βασίλεια κατὰ ὠμν, Αὐτοκράτωρ ἀνηρέθετο. παρὰ δὲ ἡ πέμψας εἰς καὶ ζαδρομὼ τὸν Ζαχαρίαν Χαλκηδόνος ἐν μέσῳ ἀπέστρεψε τὴν ὁδὸν. Τῇ ἐξῆς δὲ μετὰ τὴν ἀναχώρησιν τὰ Πατριαρχικὰ θέρῃ τὸν Φώτιον καταβιβάζει, ἐν Μοναστηρίῳ τινὶ καλουμένῳ Σκέπῃ τὴν ὄνομα ἐξορίζει, καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον Ἡλίας ὁ ἀναφανέστατος τῆς βασιλικῆς σόλου ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλικῶν δρόμων πρὸς τὸν ἀμωμότατον Πατριάρχην, ὅπως αὐτὸν ἐκ τῆς νήσου πρὸς τὴν βασιλίδα μετὰ τῆς ὀφειλομένης τιμῆς.] Translated: "And Michael, having done evil in the sight of the Church of God, perished at the beginning of the first indiction, on the ninth day before the Kalends of October. Basil, with the palace seized, was saluted emperor; who, having sent to recall Zacharias from his journey, drew him back from the middle of the road. On the day after he was proclaimed emperor, he removed Photius from the patriarchal throne and exiled him to a monastery called Scepe. On the following day Elias, the most distinguished admiral of the imperial fleet, went along the imperial roads to the most blameless Patriarch, to bring him back from the island to the capital with the honour due to him." The Latin reads: Since Michael had done evil in the sight of the Church of God, he died at the beginning of the first indiction, on the ninth day before the Kalends of October; Basil, having occupied the palace, was acclaimed emperor, and sent to recall Zacharias from the journey, and drew him back from the middle of the road.
