On the day after he was proclaimed emperor, he cast Photius down from the throne and exiled him to a monastery called Scepe; and on the following day Elias, the most illustrious commander of the imperial fleet, was sent with the imperial galley, or swift ship, to bring the most holy Patriarch back from the island to Constantinople with the honour that was due. The same Emperor Basil declares in his Epanagogue that before the common cares of the commonwealth he had taken pains that ecclesiastical controversies should be settled: [Τῆς Θείας ἐφιλανθρωπίας φρονήσεως τὰ πολλὰ δ' οἰκουμένης ὀλκάδος ἡμῶν ἐξηρέσεως, πᾶς ἐνιαυτοῦ ἰδιώματι ἀναλαμβάνω, καὶ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς τῆς Δημοσίων φροντίδων τὰς ἐκκλησιαστικὰς ἐρευνὰς ἐξελαύνει.]

units.la: Cum divina, & benignissima Dei providentia nobis orbis terræ gubernacula commiserit, omnem dedimus operam, vt etiam ante communes Reipublicæ curas Ecclesiasticæ controuersiæ componantur. Quod etiam fassus est Ignatius in acclamatione ad Synodum.
units.tr: Since the divine and most gracious providence of God has committed to us the government of the world, we have taken every pains that, even before the common cares of the commonwealth, ecclesiastical controversies should be settled. Ignatius also confessed this in his acclamation to the Synod.

units.la: Οὗτος ὁ Βασιλεὺς Ὃν μὲν Φώτιον καθῃρέθη, ὃν ὁ τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίας τὸν ἀσυνείδητον[?], καὶ ἀκατάστατον Φωτίου, τὸν Ἐβελλάδεον[?], τῷ ἡμετέρῳ Ταπεινώσει ἡμῖν πολλὰ ἀγνὰ πάθος αἰτησάμενος εἰς τὸν Ἴσον Θεὸν. Ταῦτα ἡ πατριάρχης Ἰσίδωρος ἐξακολουθήσας τὰ μακάριώτατα Πάπα Νικολάου, ἐς ἐπανάγω συνοδικὰς ἐξεφώνησε, καὶ ἡ Βησσαλῶν ἐντεῦθεν ἀπέφηνε[?].
units.tr: This Emperor (the one whom the Roman Church called the unconscious and disorderly tabellarius Photius) deposed Photius, and at our humble request asked many holy things of God for us. Following these words, Patriarch Isidore, having carried out the most blessed Pope Nicholas's decrees, announced them in synodal letters, and the Vessalians then declared the same.

units.la: Hic Imperator Photium expulit, quem Romana Ecclesia vtpote virum conscientiæ expertem, & inordinatum appellat Tabellarium; nostram vero humilitatem multa perpessam in thronum proprium renocauit.
units.tr: This Emperor expelled Photius, whom the Roman Church, as a man without conscience and disorderly, calls a tabellarius. He recalled our humility, which had suffered much, to its own throne.

units.la: Quæ illè Basilius ex beatissimi Papæ Nicolai decretis, quæ Papa in Synodo ediderat, & per litteras hæc miserat, fecit. Tum subdit;
units.tr: Basil did what he did in accordance with the decrees of the most blessed Pope Nicholas, which the Pope had issued in a synod and sent by letter. Then he adds:

units.la: Ἐπεὶ ἡ μὴ τῆς πολλῷ ἔχει φροντίδι συναγαγὼν τοποθετεῖ ἐν τῇ ἄλλων πατριαρχικῶν θεσμῶν, καὶ) τῷ Συνόδῳ [?]οἰκουμενικῷ, εἰς πᾶσαν [illegible, ~12 letters] Deinde omnem operam dedit, vt ex alijs Patriarchijs legatos euocaret, Conciliumque generale cogeret, eamque rem perfecit. Primum itaque decretum Nicolai sequens Imperator Photium expulit, Ignatium restituit. Deinde aduentum Legatorum ex alijs Patriarchijs procurauit, & Synodum cogit. Statim itaque atque consalutatus est Basilius Imperator deiectionem Photij, & restitutionem Ignatij meditatus, tribus diebus, vt videre est, absoluit. Non potuit ergo Photius Basilium, quem eo tempore nec viderat plane, vti homicidam a communione repellere: nec potuit Basilius, cum in occupando, atq; stabiliendo Imperio totus inuigilaret, sacris mysterijs adesse; nec potuit illo trium dierum spatio a tribunali Pontificio in fauorem Ignatij placitum obtinere, quo innixus depositionem Photij, & restitutionem Ignatij obfirmaret: nisi missi Basilij ad Romanum, rursusque Legati Pontificij ad Basilium ad abrogandum Photio magistratum sphærulæ fuere plumbeæ pyrio puluere ex tormento æneo violenter expulsæ, vel vortex igneus ab Oriente in Occidentem recurrens, retortusque per partes omnes perleui momento, qui perexiguo trium dierum tempore, certe cursu præuertere ventos non potuere, Romam auolarent, & ante Pontifices Nicolaum, & Adrianum discussa causa Photij, Byzantium condemnationis Photianæ sententiam reportarent. Basilium fortunatum,quieiusmodi nuncios habeat! Certum est tamen, deabdicato Photio, & restituto Ignatio Basilium ad Pontificem literas dedisse. Sed extendamus tempora, & dies producamus in annos, neque tum Photius tanto ausu fuisset: His iisdem Hamartoli, quo duce forte similia de Photio narrat Zonaras, in hoc negotio non levis oscitantia deprehenditur.
units.tr: Then he took care to summon legates from the other patriarchates and to convene a general council, and he accomplished this. So, following Nicholas's first decree, the Emperor expelled Photius and restored Ignatius. Then he secured the arrival of legates from the other patriarchates and convened a synod. As soon as Basil was saluted as emperor, he planned the deposition of Photius and the restoration of Ignatius, and, as can be seen, completed both within three days. Photius therefore could not have excluded Basil from communion as a murderer, since he had not even seen him at that time. Nor could Basil, who was wholly occupied with seizing and securing the empire, be present at the sacred mysteries. Nor, in that space of three days, could he have obtained a favourable verdict from the papal tribunal for Ignatius, on which to rest the confirmation of Photius's deposition and Ignatius's restoration. The only way would have been if Basil's envoys to Rome and the papal legates back to Basil, for the purpose of stripping Photius of office, had been leaden balls hurled violently from a bronze cannon by gunpowder, or a fiery whirlwind running from east to west and turned back through all its parts in an instant. Such things, in a very brief space of three days, could not outrun the winds, and could not fly to Rome, and, before the popes Nicholas and Hadrian, after the case of Photius was discussed, bring back from Constantinople the sentence condemning Photius. Fortunate Basil, to have such messengers! It is certain, however, that after Photius was deposed and Ignatius restored, Basil wrote letters to the Pope. But let us stretch the times and lengthen the days into years, and then Photius would not have dared so much. Those same tales of Hamartolus, under whose lead Zonaras perhaps narrates similar things about Photius, show no small carelessness in this matter.

units.la: Nam Basilius, etiamsi dolore repulsæ imaginatione, tantummodo agitatæ exasperatus, non statim a Pontifice Episcopos, Tomumque pro depellendo Photio procurauit, sed iam latæ in Photium e Pontifice insistens, eam veluti minister cum fide, & cura executus, Photium magistratu spoliauit, Ignatium immisit. Quod ipse palam edicit Adhortatione ad Synodum; Τῇ δὲ τὸν ἱερώτατον Πατριάρχῳ [?] τὸν ἴδιον ἀνακαμψαντα ἐκ τῆς ἐμῆς βασιλείας ἔχοντα τόπον, ἢ ὀνόματα γίνονται [?]. ἀλλ᾽ ὁ ἀγιώτατος Πάπας Νικόλαος [?] ἐποιήσατο, ἐ ἀναθέματι καθυποβαλὼν [?] μὴ πάσης τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησίας σὺν ἀνθισαμένῃ [?] τῇ Ιωάννῃ ψήφῳ. Patriarcham vero sacratissimum Ignatium adsuam regredi sedem, non mei opus Imperij, nec consilium fuit, sed sanctissimus Papa Nicolaus causa Ignatij diligenter excussa, ut ille restitueretur, sanxit, atque ex totius Ecclesiæ Romanæ decreto omnes, qui resisterent anathemate percussit. Postmodum ne videretur in sacra temerarie manus apposuisse, Pontificem certiorem de functione operis fecit, & Episcopos rogavit, qui ad nutum Pontificis causam examinarent, & definirent. Sic Adrianus, quando iam Nicolaus e vivis excesserat, in Pontificatum promotus Legatis missis in Concilio generali Byzantij coacto, Anno Adriani secundo, Basilij tertio, & Christi octingentesimo sexagesimo sexto, causa Photij, atque Ignatij discussa, Photius damnatur, Ignatius reponitur. Quare imaginaria ista Basilij e sacris repulsa a Zonara putide quæsita, & fortasse etiam a nebulonibus historiæ Hamattoli appensa expungenda est. Et quis crederet Photium in dignitate nutantem, nec certum pro sua confirmatione, quid ageret, versutum, & ad omnia factum, rebus publicis extra mensuram aberrantibus, in id tantum non-animum intendisse, ut novi benevolentiam Principis non odia in se converteret? neque enim is erat, ut suis commodis sacra præponeret, quod ex actis ab ipso sub Michaële, & & Barda fuis promotoribus satis compertum eft: nanq; cum Michaël irrifor peffimus facra infultabat, Photium ab eiufmodi impietatibus non auocaffe Imperatorem, fed eas obmutefcendo per fummam adulationem comprobaffe, intentum in confingendis aduerfus Ignatium criminibus, vt eo vita priuato, fedem fibi firmius ftabiliret, enarrant pluribus Nicetas in vita Ignatij, & alij, quos fupra laudauimus. Et in Actis Octauæ Oecumenicæ Synodi fæpius conclamatur, Mimorum res facras eludentium Patriarcha. Et ne defint Pappomaftiges, audiatur Georgius Scholarius, qui & Gennadius Monachus Syntagm. 1. cap. 3. Τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ καὶ περὶ [?] Φωτίου τῆς [?] ... [illegible, ~12 letters] ... ὁ γὰρ δὴ [?] ... [illegible, ~14 letters] ... μισθὸν ... [?] ... [illegible, ~10 letters] ... ὅπερ γὰρ δὴ μᾶλλον λέγειν, ἢ ὡς ἑώδῃ λέγωσι. Hæc eadem & de Photio tandem contigerunt. Hic enim & diuidere Ecclefias aggreffus, pretextu vsus differentia dogmatis, rurfum Ecclefiarum confederationes ob propria fua commoda pretio nundinatus eft, vt maiori malo minus fibi mercaretur. Ita enim potius enunciandum eft, quam pro more enunciatur. Et Bafilio Imperatori prudenti, ferio, fobrio, rerebus agendis, & moribus corrigendis, & iustitia restituenda intento, Photius multorum criminum reus homicidium obiecisset, eumque sacris interdixisset? subdebat, ad quem paulo post redijt. Minimum tempus sunt Hottingero decem anni. Decimo siquidem anno a tempore, quo ab Oecumenica Synodo restitutus est, Ignatius diem suum obijt.
units.tr: For Basil, though exasperated by the grief of his rejection, which was merely a stirred-up imagination, did not at once procure bishops and a Tome from the Pope to drive out Photius. Rather, insisting on the sentence already passed against Photius by the Pope, he carried it out faithfully and carefully as a minister, stripped Photius of office, and installed Ignatius. He himself declares this openly in his Exhortation to the Synod: the most holy patriarch was restored to his own see, not by the work or counsel of my empire, but the most holy Pope Nicholas, after carefully examining the cause of Ignatius, decreed that he should be restored, and by the decree of the whole Roman Church struck with anathema all who resisted. Afterwards, lest he should seem to have rashly laid hands on sacred matters, he informed the Pontiff of the outcome of the work and asked the bishops to examine and decide the cause at the Pontiff's nod. So Hadrian, when Nicholas had already departed this life, was raised to the Pontificate, and in the general council held at Byzantium in the second year of Hadrian, the third of Basil, and the 866th of Christ, he sent legates; the cause of Photius and Ignatius was examined, Photius was condemned, and Ignatius was reinstated. Therefore that imaginary expulsion of Basil from the sacred rites, foolishly sought out by Zonaras and perhaps also hung on the scoundrels of Hamartolus's history, must be struck out. And who would believe that Photius, wavering in his dignity, uncertain what to do to confirm himself, crafty and fit for every purpose, while public affairs were going far astray, directed himself to this end only: that the goodwill of the new prince should not turn into hatred against him? For he was not the sort of man to put sacred things before his own advantage, which is sufficiently clear from the acts of his own promoters Michael and Bardas. For when the worst buffoon Michael insulted sacred things, Photius did not dissuade the Emperor from such impieties, but by keeping silent and showing the highest flattery approved them, intent on fabricating charges against Ignatius, so that once he was removed from life he might establish his own see more firmly. Nicetas in his Life of Ignatius, and others whom we praised above, relate this at length. And in the Acts of the Eighth Ecumenical Synod the cry is often repeated: "Patriarch who mocks sacred things like a mime!" And lest the Papal-scourgers be lacking, let George Scholarius be heard, who is also the monk Gennadius, in his Syntagma 1, chapter 3. The same things, he says, also happened with Photius at last. For he too set about dividing the churches, using the pretext of a difference in doctrine, and again sold the confederations of churches for his own gain, buying for himself a lesser evil at the price of a greater. It is better to put it this way than as is customarily put. And when Photius, the accused, had charged the prudent, serious, sober Emperor Basil, intent on conducting public affairs, correcting morals and restoring justice, with murder, and had barred him from the sacraments? (he adds) to whom he returned a little later. Ten years are a very short time for Hottinger. For in the tenth year after he was restored by the Ecumenical Synod, Ignatius died.

units.la: Fuit ei lucta cum Ignatio. Sed non ex aequo. Photius tyrannide Bardae, & stupore Michaelis, & sceleratorum hominum artibus potens, & audax; Ignatius soli divino auxilio fidens. Photius invasor, & aliena per oppressionem eripiens; Ignatius suis, vi subigente, spoliatus iniustissime. Deinde etiam cum Pontifice Romano. Qui iudex utriusque sedebat, ius dicens, & iniuste occupata poenis occupatori indictis restituens. Cum Domino siquidem, legemque ferente, stulte certamen suscipitur a subdito, cum capite a membro, cum universali Ecclesiarum rectore a particulari Patriarcha, cum antiquissimo a iuniori, cum divino iure constituto ab humano favore, & gratia secundo denunciato. Quod is ex ambitione dominatum sibi super Ecclesias vindicaret, & omnes controversias ad suum solius arbitrium, & sententiam definiri contendat. Solemne hoc est Hæreticorum effatum, qui ut imminuant Romani Pontificis auctoritatem similia nugantur. Pontifex dignitatem quam possidet, non ambit, neque ex ambitione sibi vendicat, sed traditam sibi a Christo potestatem tuetur, in disponendis nempe rebus Ecclesiasticis, & decernendis, fidei infallibilitatem, quam fere omnes tum Græci, tum Latini ab ipsis Ecclesiæ Christianæ incunabulis agnouerunt, & falsi sunt, & nos testimoniis ex eorum libris deductis, sed schismaticorum, & præcipue Photii quæ insimili materia non sunt parvi momenti, Interpres Canonum Cosmæ Melodi: Αἱ γὰρ τῶν ἐναντίων μαρτυριῶν ἀξιοπιστότεραι εἰσίν. Aduersariorum enim testimonia fide digniora sunt. in Diatriba contra Hottingerum fusè probauimus: Et modo etiam, ut quantum Hottingerus, aliique illi similes insipiant, deprehendant Lectores, quænam eorum temporum fuerit Græcorum sententia de primatu Romani Pontificis, inspiciamus. Nicephorus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus Tractatu de inculpata Christianorum fide, Synodum secundam Nicænam, requisita necessaria omnia ad Synodum, ut Oecumenica sit, habuisse probans, inter alia subdit cap. 25. Συνηκολούθησε γὰρ τούτῳ μά-λιστα ἐνδίκως, καὶ ἐνομωσάμεθα, ἐπάνε-[?] ἀρἀρχὴν τῶν πιπτωμένων Θεσμὰς ἀρχῆς καὶ [?] αὐτῶ, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν [?] ὅσον τῆς ἐν τῆς ἐπαρχείας λόγος [?] ἤτοι τῆς Πρεσβυτέρου Ῥώμης μέρος ἐξ ἀσπ[?] μοι, ὧν αὐτὸ δίδωμι καὶ τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν κινούμενον θεσμοῖς κανονικοῖς [?] ἐπ' ἀρχῆς ἔχειν ἐκκλησιαστικὸν γνώμην [?] αὖ[?]ων, τὴν δοκιμασίαν ἐ χοῖν, ἢ δίκαιαν αὖ ποτε τὴν πίστιν. ὡς δὲ λαχόντες καὶ τὴν ἱεροσυνίλλαν ἐξ ἀρχῆς καὶ τῆς κορυφαίων ἐν Ἀποστόλοις ἱεραρχευόντων τὸ ἀξίωμα. Celebrata etenim est illa Synodus iuste admodum, & quammaxime ad Canonum praescripta. Quandoque enim, secundum ab initio constitutas divinas regulas praeminebant, & praesidebant in ipsa, quotquot erant ex occiduis oris, vel senioris Romae pars haud contemptibilis, quibus dogma in Ecclesia motum, quod & Canonum praescripto, & Ecclesiasticis consuetudinibus comprobatum est, probationem non consequatur, neque unquam accipiat finem, cum illi sortiti sint primas partes in rebus sacris tenere, & traditam possideant Principum Apostolorum dignitatem. Theodorus Studita Dogmatica de honore, & venerationē Sacrarum Imaginum Μαισ[?] ζαίω δ' ὃν ἐν Ῥώμῃ καὶ τὰς κλεῖς τῆς κορυφῆς τῆς Ἀποστόλων Πέτρου [?] ἡμῖν ἀγνοοῦν. Καὶ ζῶν ὁ κόσμος ἐ κλῆς αὐτὰ διὰ ἀπ[?] δωσιν ἀφθάρτας, ἀλλὰ τὰς ὀφθαλμοῖς λέγω εἰς τὸ ἑστηκὸν, καὶ λύων. Οἱ δὲ ἀγγελοὶ πεποιηκότες ταύτας φέρ[?] πιδίασιν εἰς ἀσφαλισμόν. Τοσαῦτ' οὖν αὐτὴν ἡ πίστις. κἀκεῖ ἡ ἀρραγὴς πέτρα τῆς πίστεως πεπηγμέ[?]ιωμὴν τὸν λόγον τῷ κυρίῳ. ἐνταῦθα δὲ ὡς ἔοικε πλανοπάζεσθαι [?] ἡ ἀπιστία, ἐν ᾗ ἀπορία. Audio etiam Romae claves Principis Apostolorum Petri in honore habere; licet Dominus non claves illi tradiderit materiatas, sed per sermonem ad ligandum, & soluendum. illi vero argenteas factas proponunt in venerationem. Tanta igitur est eorum fides. Ibiq; infrangibilis petra fidei fundata est secundum verbum Domini: hic vero, vt appareret, infidelitas atq; improbitas redundant. Et vt exactius rem intelligat Hottingerus, rursus denuo tanti Patris verba retexam. Quandoquidem secundum ab initio constitutas diuinas regulas praeminebant, & praesidebant in ipsa quotquot erant ex occiduis oris, vel senioris Romae pars haud contemptibilis, abfsq; quibus dogma in Ecclesia motum, quod & Canonum praescripto, & Ecclesiasticis consuetudinibus comprobatum est, probationem non consequatur, neque vnquam accipiat finem, cum illi sortiti sint primas partes in rebus sacris tenere, & traditam possideant Principum Apostolorum dignitatem. O lingua iure aurea! o veritas inuincibilis, quae oppressa etiam Haereticorum machinis ac calumnijs, tandem emergis, & falsum infimulantes deuincis. Explica tu si potes praeeminentiam Romanorum Pontificum elegantius, expressius, neruosius, & palmarium habe. Et tum vniuersus Oriens paulo anante tempora Photij ita sentiebat. Neque ab his dissentit Theodorus Studita. Vide etiam Stephanum iuniorem, & Martyrem, Tarasium Patriarcham in Synodo Nicæna Secunda, Stylianum Neocæsarienfem Episcopum, & alios, quos alio, atq; alio loco adduximus, quibus patebit clarissime, quænam apud Græcos tum temporis fuerit de auctoritate Romani Pontificis sententia. Sed ut magis pateat, eam nos ex historiæ serie eruamus. In Concilio Constantinopolitano ab Ignatio coacto deponitur Gregorius Syracusanus Episcopus, ita tamen, ut assensus Romani Pontificis requiratur. Petitur a Leone Papa per Legatos. Leo differt, donec partem alteram audiat, & decretum examinet, & interea Leone decedente, res ad successorem defertur. Narrat Nicolaus Papa Epistola ad Michaelem Imperatorem. Instat denuo Ignatius, & Benedicti anno secundo mittit Romam Acta Synodalia, petens confirmari. Benedictus diligentius discussa causa præsente eodem Gregorio sententiam Ignatij confirmat. Deponitur rursus Ignatius, intruditur Photius, si desit assensus Pontificis, infecta sunt omnia; quare Legatis missis quæritur assensus, negatur, donec partes audiantur, illis auditis Nicolaus, & Adrianus pronunciant contra Photium. Deiecto postmodum Photio, & restituto Ignatio mittitur ad Pontificem; petiturque ab eo, vt insinuet, quid agendum sit de Sacerdotibus, qui Photio adhaeserant. Pontifex mittit Legatos suos, vt cuncta rite disponerent, & causa Photij, atque Ignatij a Romano Pontifice discutitur, & internoscitur, & mortuo tandem Ignatio, & restituto Photio, petitur rursus a Romano, vt illum in communionem suscipiat, eiusque ad Patriarchatum reditum sua auctoritate firmet. Eijcitur iterum Photius, & iterum ad Romanum Legationes, & literae, vt Acta confirmet, & cum Stephano Patriarcha dispenset[?], & cum Episcopis deceptis a Photio, qui mandat utriusque partis Episcopis mitti, quibus auditis sententiam pronunciet. Vides hic Romanorum Pontificum dominatum ab ipso Christo illis exhibitum super Ecclesias non ex ambitione vindicatum? Photianis temporibus, & anteactis, & postmodum subsecutis Pontifices Romani mandant, imperant, poenis etiam indictis Imperatoribus, Patriarchis, Episcopis, universis Christi fidelibus; lites inter eos exortas examinant, ponderant, & solo suo arbitrio discernunt, & sententia definiunt, in iudicio de rerum veritate indadagant, fontes condemnant, innoxios sublevant, & ius suum unicuique tribuunt.
units.tr: There was a struggle between him and Ignatius. But it was not on equal terms. Photius was powerful and bold through the tyranny of Bardas, the dullness of Michael, and the tricks of wicked men, while Ignatius trusted only in divine help. Photius was an intruder who seized what belonged to others by oppression; Ignatius was most unjustly stripped of his own by force. Then also there was the struggle with the Roman Pontiff. He sat as judge of both, pronouncing the law, restoring what had been unjustly seized, and imposing penalties on the usurper. For a subject to take up a contest with his Lord and lawgiver is foolish: a member against the head, a particular Patriarch against the universal ruler of the Churches, the younger against the most ancient, human favour against a divine institution, and one who was declared second by grace against the one to whom it was given. That he claims for himself dominion over the Churches out of ambition, and seeks to have all controversies settled by his own arbitrament and judgment alone. This is the familiar saying of the heretics, who, to diminish the authority of the Roman Pontiff, babble similar nonsense. The Pontiff does not seek the dignity he holds, nor claim it for himself out of ambition, but maintains the power handed down to him by Christ, namely in ordering and deciding ecclesiastical affairs, and the infallibility of faith, which almost all Greeks and Latins alike acknowledged from the very cradle of the Christian Church. That these men are false, and the schismatics too, especially Photius, whose testimonies in a similar matter are of no small weight, we have proved at length in the Diatriba against Hottinger, drawn from their books. The interpreter of the Canons, Cosmas Melodus, says: [Αἱ γὰρ τῶν ἐναντίων μαρτυριῶν ἀξιοπιστότεραι εἰσίν.] For the testimonies of adversaries are more worthy of belief. And now, so that the readers may see how far Hottinger and others like him are foolish, let us examine what the opinion of the Greeks of those times was concerning the primacy of the Roman Pontiff. Nicephorus, Patriarch of Constantinople, in his treatise on the blameless faith of Christians, proving that the Second Nicene Synod had all the requisites needed for it to be ecumenical, adds among other things in chapter 25: [Συνηκολούθησε γὰρ τούτῳ μάλιστα ἐνδίκως, καὶ ἐνομωσάμεθα]. The Latin rendering reads: the Synod was celebrated most justly and in full accordance with the Canons. For those who, according to the divine rules established from the beginning, took the lead and presided in it, were all who came from the western regions, or that not contemptible part of the elder Rome, without whom a doctrine stirred up in the Church, which has been approved both by the prescription of the Canons and by ecclesiastical custom, cannot attain approval, nor ever reach an end, since they have been allotted the first place in sacred affairs and hold the dignity of the Chief Apostles handed down to them. Theodore the Studite, in his Dogmatic work on the honour and veneration of sacred images, writes: [Μαισ... ζαίω δ' ὃν ἐν Ῥώμῃ καὶ τὰς κλεῖς τῆς κορυφῆς τῆς Ἀποστόλων Πέτρου]: I hear that in Rome they hold in honour the keys of Peter, the chief of the Apostles. Although the Lord did not give him keys made of material, but spoke of binding and loosing, they set up keys made of silver for veneration. Such is their faith. There the unbreakable rock of faith is fixed, according to the word of the Lord; here, as it appears, unbelief and wickedness abound. And so that Hottinger may understand the matter more exactly, let me set out again the words of so great a Father. Since, according to the divine rules established from the beginning, those who came from the western regions, or the not contemptible part of the elder Rome, took the lead and presided in it, and without them a doctrine stirred up in the Church, which has been approved both by the prescription of the Canons and by ecclesiastical custom, cannot attain approval, nor ever reach an end, since they have been allotted the first place in sacred affairs and hold the dignity of the Chief Apostles handed down to them. O golden tongue, rightly so called! O invincible truth, which, though oppressed by the machinations and slanders of heretics, at last emerges and overcomes the false accusers! Let Hottinger explain the pre-eminence of the Roman Pontiffs more elegantly, more clearly, more vigorously, if he can, and let him take the prize. And then the whole East, a little before the time of Photius, thought in this way. Theodore the Studite does not differ from them. See also Stephen the Younger and Martyr, Tarasius, Patriarch, in the Second Nicene Synod, Stylianus, Bishop of Neocaesarea, and others whom we have cited here and there, from which it will be most clearly evident what was the opinion of the Greeks at that time concerning the authority of the Roman Pontiff. But so that this may be made plainer, let us draw it out from the sequence of history. In the Council of Constantinople gathered by Ignatius, Gregory, Bishop of Syracuse, is deposed, yet on condition that the assent of the Roman Pontiff be sought. It is asked of Pope Leo through legates. Leo delays until he hears the other side and examines the decree, and meanwhile Leo dies and the matter is referred to his successor. Pope Nicholas relates this in a letter to the Emperor Michael. Ignatius presses again, and in the second year of Benedict sends the synodal acts to Rome, asking for confirmation. Benedict, after discussing the case more carefully with Gregory present, confirms the sentence of Ignatius. Ignatius is deposed again and Photius is installed; if the Pontiff's assent is lacking, all is void. Therefore legates are sent and assent is sought; it is refused until the parties are heard, and after they are heard, Nicholas and Hadrian pronounce against Photius. Later, when Photius is deposed and Ignatius restored, Ignatius is sent to the Pontiff, and he asks him to indicate what should be done about the priests who had clung to Photius. The Pontiff sends his legates so that they might arrange everything properly, and the cause of Photius and Ignatius is examined and determined by the Roman Pontiff. When Ignatius finally dies and Photius is restored, it is again asked of the Roman Pontiff that he receive Photius into communion and by his own authority confirm his return to the Patriarchate. Photius is again expelled, and again embassies and letters are sent to Rome that he may confirm the acts, and deal with Patriarch Stephen and with the bishops deceived by Photius, and he orders that bishops of each side be sent, so that, having heard them, he may pronounce sentence. Do you see here the dominion over the Churches shown to the Roman Pontiffs by Christ himself, not claimed out of ambition? In the times of Photius, both before and after, the Roman Pontiffs command, order, and even impose penalties on Emperors, Patriarchs, Bishops, and all the faithful of Christ; they examine and weigh the disputes that arise among them, decide them by their own judgment alone, inquire into the truth of the matter in judgment, condemn the guilty, relieve the innocent, and give each his right.

units.la: Si ipsi sua auctoritate decreta ab alijs non confirment, decreta infecta habentur; & hanc esse consuetudinem antiquam Ecclesiæ Scriptores illius temporis fatentur; & Hottingerus ex ambitione id facere, & dominatum in res Ecclesiasticas, quasi non suum ad se trahere fatebitur? Sed fassus est. verum; at nulla fide. Dicit Hottingerus, tum primum, & ætate Photij Romanos Pontifices conatos ad se trahere dominatum, quem antehac nunquam obtinebant. Consideret ergo, an Nicephorus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, Tarasius item Patriarcha, Theodorus Studita, & alij antiquiores Photio fuerint. Frustra itaque de ambitione Pontificum Romanorum ætate Photij nugatur. Sed vetustiora homo ingeniosus rimatur. Plus satis alijs tractatibus dedimus, nunc unum vel alterum si addidero, Quæstioni finem imponam. Excommunicatur, eijcitur ab Ecclesia, quod Nestorij partes fouisset, & oppugnasset Cyrilli capita, Synodo plena Theodoretus: pœnitentia dehinc ductus, & reconciliatus Leoni, in communionem admittitur, & aliorum Catholicorum consortio dignatur, comparat in Synodo Chalcedonensi, petit admitti. Synodus reclamitat & ab ipso damnationem Nestorij quaeritat. Vbi id actum est, Synodus acquiescit universa, mandataque Leonis Pontificis effectu adimplenda esse constituit; Λέοντ[?] τούτων ψῆφον ἐξενεχθῆναι τῆς θεοφιλίας τῆς ὑμετέρας, ὥστε καὶ τῷ Ἐκκλησίαν αὐτὸν ὑπολαβεῖν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ ὁσιώτατος Ἀρχιεπίσκοπος Λέων ἐδήλωσεν. Reliquum est igitur, ut sententia proferatur a reverentia vestra, ut Ecclesiam suam recipiat, sicut & sanctissimus Leo Archiepiscopus indicavit. Relegetur hinc ambitio, amandetur contentio, & disputatio, Quaestio anceps, & perobscura jam declarata est.
units.tr: If they themselves do not confirm decrees by their own authority, the decrees are held to be void; and the writers of that time confess that this was the ancient custom of the Church. Will Hottinger admit that they do this out of ambition, and that they draw to themselves a dominion over ecclesiastical affairs which is not theirs? But he does admit it, though only as truth without any credit. Hottinger says that only then, in the age of Photius, did the Roman Pontiffs begin to draw to themselves a dominion which they had never previously held. Let him consider whether Nicephorus, Patriarch of Constantinople, Tarasius likewise a Patriarch, Theodore the Studite, and others were older than Photius. Thus he trifles in vain about the ambition of the Roman Pontiffs in the age of Photius. But the clever man searches out the older times. We have given more than enough to other treatises; if I add now one or two more, I shall put an end to the question. Theodoret was excommunicated and cast out of the Church because he had favoured the party of Nestorius and attacked the chapters of Cyril, which the Synod was full of. Afterwards, led by repentance, and reconciled to Leo, he is admitted into communion and deemed worthy of the company of the other Catholics. He appears at the Council of Chalcedon and asks to be admitted. The Synod protests and demands from him the condemnation of Nestorius. When this was done, the whole Synod agreed and decided that the commands of Pope Leo were to be carried into effect; [Λέοντ[?] τούτων ψῆφον ἐξενεχθῆναι τῆς θεοφιλίας τῆς ὑμετέρας]: let the decision of your God-loving self be given in accordance with these things, so that the Church may receive him, just as the most holy Archbishop Leo has declared. It remains, therefore, that sentence be pronounced by your reverence, so that he may receive his Church, as the most holy Leo the Archbishop has indicated. Let ambition be removed from here, let contention and dispute be put away; the doubtful and very obscure question has now been made plain.

units.la: Recipiendus Theodoretus est. restituendus Throno. Ita Leo Romanus ἐδικαίωσε[?], judicavit, censuit aequum esse, immunem fecit a crimine, extra culpam esse statuit. Statimque omnes clamaverunt; Θεοδώρητος ἄξιος τῷ Θεῷ. Ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸν ὀρθόδοξον. ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸν ποιμένα ὑπολάβῃ. τὸν ὀρθόδοξον διδάσκαλον ἡ Ἐκκλησία ὑπολάβῃ. τῷ Θεῷ Θεοδώρητος ἄξιος. τῷ Ἀρχιεπισκόπῳ Λέοντος πολλὰ ἔτη. Μετὰ τῆς Θεῷ Λέων ἐδήλωσεν[?]. ὁ λαὸς τὸν ὀρθόδοξον ὑπολάβῃ. ἄξιε τῷ Θεῷ. Θεοδώρητῳ τῷ Ἐπισκόπῳ ἡ Ἐκκλησία ὑπολάβῃ. Theodoretus dignus est sede. Ecclesia Orthodoxum. Ecclesia pastorem recipiat. Orthodoxum Doctorem Ecclesia recipiat. Theodoretus dignus est sede. Archiepiscopo Leoni multos annos. Cum Deo Leo iudicauit. Populus Orthodoxum recipiat, dignum sua sede. Theodoreto Episcopo reddatur Ecclesia. Quae quo pondo sint, acutissime expendit Gregorius Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus Responsione contra Marci Ephesij fidei professionem.
units.tr: He is to be received back and restored to his throne. So Leo of Rome "justified" him: he judged it fitting, declared him free of the charge, and held that he was blameless. Immediately everyone cried out: "Theodoret is worthy of God! The Church acknowledges the orthodox man! Let the Church receive the shepherd! Let the Church receive the orthodox teacher! Theodoret is worthy of God! Many years to the archbishop Leo! With God, Leo has declared it! Let the people receive the orthodox man, worthy of his see! Worthy of God! Let the Church be restored to Bishop Theodoret!" [Θεοδώρητος ἄξιος τῷ Θεῷ. Ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸν ὀρθόδοξον. ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸν ποιμένα ὑπολάβῃ. τῷ Ἀρχιεπισκόπῳ Λέοντος πολλὰ ἔτη.] What these acclamations are worth has been weighed most acutely by Gregory, Patriarch of Constantinople, in his Response against the profession of faith of Marcus of Ephesus.

units.la: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος Θεοδωρ-ητῷ μέχρι τῆς ἁγίας οἰκουμενικῆς πεντάδης Σωνόδου ἀκοινώνητος, ὑπῆρχε, καὶ ἀπρόσδεκτος ὡς ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἐκκλησίας. καὶ ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ πεντάδῃ Σωνόδῳ ὡσαύτως συνῳδεῖν τοῖς λοιποῖς πατράσιν, ἢ μὴ ἐκ τῆς Ῥώμης τὸ μαρτύριον λέοντος ὑπισχνεῖτο[?]. οἱ δὲ σύλλογοι ἀρχοντες ἔλεγον, ὅτι ὁ Βασιλεὺς κελεύει, μὴ σωνῳδεῖν Θεοδώρητον. οἱ δὲ ποιμαντικοὶ τῆς Ῥώμης ἴσως[?], ὡς ὁ Ῥώμης κελεύει σωνῳδεῖν, καὶ ὕστερον ἀποδέχθη. Theodoretus Cyri Episcopus vsq; ad tempora quarta Oecumenica sanctæ Synodi, extra communionem, & Catholicæ Ecclesiæ consortium agebat. Et cum ad quartam S. Synodum processisset, postulassetque, vt cum reliquis Patribus locum haberet, non prius exceptus est, ni Romani Pontificis beati Leonis literis instructus. Nanque Principes Senatus dicebant. Imperator iubet, ne vna cum aliis ingrediatur. Locumtenentes vero Romani dixerunt, Romanum iubere, vt vna ingrediatur. & sic cum aliis exceptus est. Bone Deus! Quis est hic dominatus, qui Imperatori, & vniuersæ Synodo contra penditur, Imperator, & Synodus iubet nonrecipi. Leo iubet recipi. mandata Imperatoris, & Synodi negliguntur, Leonis excipiuntur, atq; exhauriuntur. Iudicat Imperator, iudicat Synodus, sed quod curiosa hominum indagine de causa cognoscunt, iudicium infirmum eorum est, exauctorari & repudiari potest, Leo diuino afflatus numine cum Deo iudex in omnibus sedet, & iudicium pronunciat. Non fallitur Deus nec fallit, neq; Leo cum quo Deus iudicat; ideoque illi tutissime ab vniuersa Ecclesia siditur. Et temere deplorat Creyghtonus ius Patriarcharum per omnes occasiones seu oblatas, seu arreptas ab Imperatoribus accisum, ac labefactatum, ne Romanis Pontificibus obsisterent, & eorum prærogatiuas interrumperent. Iusenim in vniuersas Ecclesias Pontificum, cum a Deo sit, & a Deo regatur, & pendeat, ad extrema vsque Orbis terrarum tempora illibatum, atque innocuum conseruabitur. Manet siquidem promissis Deus, & seruat fidem, & rogante Filio per Patrem nulla interponitur mora. Non expleo te: exemplum vnicum est. non acquiescis, & tamen septingenti & amplius Patres & Principes seculares satis habuere. Sed per quam verum est Ignatij Diaconi & Sceuophylacis magnæ Ecclesiæ Constantinopolitanæ in vita S.Nicephori Patriarchæ eiusdem Urbis dictum; [illegible, ~45 letters] Sit hoc apud te tanquam mysterium. Quare ad antiquiora etiam confugimus, quorum testis est non unus e trivio, vel vili plebecula, sed inter Patres, & Doctores sine ulla exceptione supremus. Isfuerit Basilius Magnus Epist. ad Occidentales Episcopos, quam & septima Synodus generalis suo calculo comprobatam verbis ipsis persecuta est. Audi, etsi tædeat te similia audire. Eustathius ex Sebastia minoris Armeniæ cum studijs operam daret Alexandriæ ab Ario edoctus, Arii a pedibus servus contra unigenitum eiusque divinitatem blasphemus, alios in eandem hæresim compellebat. Ad sua reversus eiurata hæresi, & professione rectæ fidei facta ab Hermogene Cæsariensi Episcopo sacris astringitur. Vita functo Hermogene, confestim recta ad Eusebium Episcopum Constantinopolitanum Arianæ hæresis promotorem confugit; Hinc nescio quas ob causas extrusus, reversus in patriam hæreseos culpa se liberans, & impio sensu damnato, Episcopatum obtinet, quo obtento protinus anathematismum dicit in Homoufion in Ancyrana Synodo, & Seleuciam perueniens hæresim propugnat voluminibus editis, Homoufion condemnat, rursusque Constantinopoli cum Hæreticis consentit, ideo Episcopatu pellitur. Sic sui restitutionem procurans Occidentem petit, & a Liberio tum Pontifice restituitur, cuius exinde literis munitus in Synodo apud Tyana congregata suo Episcopatui restituitur.
units.tr: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus, remained outside communion and the fellowship of the Catholic Church, and was unacceptable to the whole Church, until the holy fourth ecumenical synod. When he came to that synod and asked to take his place with the other fathers, he was not admitted until he had the letter of the Roman pontiff, the blessed Leo, to support him. The presiding officers of the Senate said that the Emperor ordered him not to enter with the others. But the Roman legates said that the Roman pontiff ordered him to enter with them, and so he was admitted with the others. Good God! What dominion is this, which is set against the Emperor and the whole synod? The Emperor and the synod order that he not be received; Leo orders that he be received, and the commands of the Emperor and the synod are disregarded, while those of Leo are welcomed and embraced. The Emperor judges, the synod judges, but whatever they learn by human inquiry about the case is a weak judgment, which can be overturned and rejected; Leo, inspired by the divine power, sits in judgment on all things together with God and pronounces the verdict. God is not deceived, nor does he deceive, and neither does Leo, with whom God judges; therefore he is most safely followed by the whole Church. And Creyghton rashly laments that the right of the patriarchs has been curtailed and weakened on every occasion, whether offered or seized by the Emperors, so that they might not oppose the Roman pontiffs and interrupt their prerogatives. For the authority of the pontiffs over all the churches, since it is from God and is governed and sustained by God, will be preserved unimpaired and harmless until the last times of the world. For God remains true to his promises and keeps faith, and when the Son asks the Father, no delay intervenes. I do not satisfy you? The example is unique. You do not accept it, and yet 700 and more fathers and secular princes were content. But how true is the saying of Ignatius, deacon and sacristan of the great Church of Constantinople, in the life of Nicephorus, patriarch of the same city: [illegible, about 45 letters]. Keep this to yourself as a mystery. Therefore we also take refuge in older authorities, whose witness is not some one man from the crossroads or a cheap rabble, but the highest of the fathers and doctors without exception. This is Basil the Great, in his letter to the Western bishops, which the seventh general synod also approved by its own judgment and followed in its very words. Listen, even if you are weary of hearing similar things. Eustathius of Sebaste in Lesser Armenia, while studying at Alexandria, was taught by Arius, and, being a servant at the feet of Arius, blasphemed against the Only-begotten and his divinity, and drove others into the same heresy. Returning home, he renounced the heresy and made a profession of right faith, and was bound by sacred pledges at the hands of Hermogenes, bishop of Caesarea. When Hermogenes died, he at once hurried to Eusebius, bishop of Constantinople, a promoter of the Arian heresy. Expelled from there for I know not what reasons, he went back to his homeland, freeing himself from the guilt of heresy, and, though his impious opinion was condemned, he obtained a bishopric. Having obtained it, he at once pronounced an anathema against the homoousion at the Synod of Ancyra; then, arriving at Seleucia, he defended the heresy by published volumes, condemned the homoousion, and again agreed with the heretics at Constantinople, and for this he was driven from his bishopric. So, seeking his restoration, he went to the West, and was restored by Liberius, then pontiff, and armed with his letters, he was restored to his bishopric in the synod gathered at Tyana.

units.la: Ὁ ἀδὲν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ἀποκαταστάσεως ἐπινόησε τὸ ὡς ἡμᾶς ἀφιξιν. καὶ ἵνα μὲν ἐσὶν ἃ [?] φεγείσῆν αὐτῷ τῆς Μακεδωνίου [?] Ἐπισκόπου Λιβερίου, καὶ τινα δὲ αὐτὸς σωιόσθη, ἀγαπῶμεν, [?] ἀλλ' ὅν ὅτι [?] ἀχόμεσιν ὑποκαταστῆσαι αὐτὸν· ὡς ἐπιδήξας τῇ Τύαν Σωσόλῳ ἀποκατάσεσιν τοῦ τόπου.
units.tr: On coming to us he devised for himself a way of restoration. And indeed, through the letter of Liberius, bishop of Macedonia, and whatever else he himself obtained, we rejoice; but we do not know how he restored himself, namely by appearing at the synod at Tyana and being restored to his place. [Ὁ ἀδὲν ἑαυτοῦ τῆς ἀποκαταστάσεως ἐπινόησε τὸ ὡς ἡμᾶς ἀφιξιν.]

units.la: Sibi modum restitutionis excogitauit ad vos proficiscens, & quae sunt, quae illi a beatissimo Episcopo Liberio proposita sunt, & quae ea quae ipse spopondit, ignoramus: nisi quia Epistolam detulit restituentem se, quam offendens Synodo apud Tyana congregata, suo restitutus est loco. Eusftathius hic Sebastenus Arianorum aduersus Catholicam Ecclesiam dogmatum seminator ac magister, saepius eandem haeresim abnegans, saepius ampledtens, & haereseos tot vicibus reus comprehensus, folio tandem deiectus, vt suis rebus prouideat, Romam deuenit, & iudicio sistitur, & impetratis literis Pontificis domum regressus sedem recuperat in Tyanensi Synodo. Orientales nesciunt, quid egerit Liberius, an bene causa Eustathij cognita sit, an damnauerit Arium, an dogma Catholicum professus sit, an delictorum egerit poenitentiam, & tamen solo decreto Pontificio inspecto restitutionis, locum restituunt. Adest hic Pontifex ad imperandum, reliqui omnes tanquam luminibus orbi ducem suum Pontificem Romanum, cui rerum Ecclesiasticarum regimen commissum est, sequuntur. Et excellentiorem præeminentiam in Romano quæris? Istiusne dominatus ambitio tum primum cum Photius obstabat, an ab antiquo, & immemorabili, ut ita dicam, invasit, an ante Photium, & multum ante tempus in Ecclesias illum obtinebat, sibique integrum conservabat?
units.tr: He devised for himself a manner of restoration as he set out to you; and what those things were that the most blessed bishop Liberius proposed to him, and what things he himself promised, we do not know; except that he brought a letter of restoration, which, when he presented it to the synod gathered at Tyana, restored him to his place. Eustathius of Sebaste, this seed-sower and teacher of Arian doctrines against the Catholic Church, who often denied the same heresy and often relapsed into it, and who, having been caught guilty of heresy so many times, was at last deposed from his see, went to Rome in order to provide for his affairs, was brought before judgment, and, having obtained letters from the pontiff, returned home and recovered his see at the synod of Tyana. The Easterners do not know what Liberius did, whether Eustathius's case was well examined, whether he condemned Arius, whether he professed the Catholic doctrine, whether he performed penance for his offences; yet they restore him to his place on the strength of the pontifical decree of restoration alone. The pontiff is present here to command, and the rest, like lights for the world, follow their leader, the Roman pontiff, to whom the government of ecclesiastical affairs has been committed. And do you seek a higher pre-eminence in the Roman see? Did this ambition of dominion first arise when Photius stood in the way, or did it seize hold from of old and from time immemorial, so to speak, and did it hold sway over the churches and keep itself whole long before Photius?

units.la: Non est quod clamoribus contendas Hottingere, & tragœdias excites. Audio. Liberium cum Arianis subscripsisse, hinc illum plerosque inter Pontifices non adnumerare. Modo ipse non ago Liberii causam neque eum ab Ariana labe vindicare contendo. Satis commode id alii peregerunt. Verum ut iurisdictio Pontificia in alias Ecclesias magis magisque pateat, fingamus ita esse, & subscripserit cum Arianis Liberius. Annon vides dominatum Pontificum etiam de hæresi suspectorum quanti æstimandus veniat. Pontifici Romano probo atque Catholico in omnibus obsequi, illiusque legibus parere, magnum, incerto atque dubio, & fidei ambiguæ maius, suspecto de hæresi, vel hæretico obtemperare, tum demum maximum est. Pie, sanctèque vitam agentes homines vti antiquæ religionis exemplaria veneramur, & eorum dicta, vti diuina eloquia accipimus. Sic enim par pari reddimus: Arianæ fidei dogmata, amphibios, atq; ancipites execramur. Liberi tamen, quia Romanus Pontifex, licet cum Arianis subscripserit, ideoque ob hæresim diffamatus, tanta erat præeminentia, vt reliquos alios in dignitate Ecclesiastica constitutos ad arbitrium suum traheret, cogeretque navigare.
units.tr: There is no need, Hottinger, to contend with shouts and stir up tragedies. I hear you. Liberius subscribed with the Arians, and so many do not count him among the popes. Yet I am not now pleading Liberius's cause, nor am I contending to clear him of the Arian stain; others have done that quite adequately. But so that papal jurisdiction over other churches may spread more and more, let us grant that it is so, and that Liberius did subscribe with the Arians. Do you not see how much the dominion of the popes is worth, even over those suspected of heresy? To obey the Roman pontiff, who is good and Catholic, in all things, and to obey his laws, is great; but to obey one who is uncertain and doubtful, of ambiguous faith, suspected of heresy or even a heretic, is then truly the greatest thing of all. We venerate, as examples of the ancient religion, men who live pious and holy lives, and we accept their sayings as divine oracles. For in this way we return like for like: we curse the doctrines of the Arian faith, its double-dealers and waverers. Yet Liberius, because he was the Roman pontiff, even though he subscribed with the Arians and was therefore defamed for heresy, had such pre-eminence that he drew the other men placed in ecclesiastical dignity to his own judgment and compelled them to sail on his course.

units.la: Neque absimile est, quod de Apiario Presbytero narrat Synodus contra Photium, quem ab Episcopo, & Synodo Africana penitus depositum, Zosimus Romanus Pontifex absoluit, & cum literis ad Synodum remissum recipiendum curauit: & Synodus Africana Zosimi iudicio, licet ipsi aduerso obtemperauit. Ὡς αὕτως γε μὲν τὸν Ἀμάδεον ἢ Πρεσβύτερον τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Σικένσης τῆς ἐν ἐπαρχίᾳ τῆς Ἀφρικῆς ἐφ' ἑνὶ αἰτίᾳ ἀφωρισεν ὁ ἐπίσκοπος. ἃς καθήγησιν τῶν παιπαντελῶς ἡ ἐκεῖ συνεχρημ[?]ατίσα Σωσόδ[?]. Ζώ-σιμος δὲ ὁ Πάπας Ῥώμης αἰσχρημονῶς ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν, καὶ συνεγείλαντα ἑαυτὸν ἰδικαίωσε, καὶ κ[?] τῶν ἐν Ἀφρικῇ Σωσόδου ἀποστόλων μὴ γραμμάτων ἀληθῶς πάλιν αὐτὸν παρεσκεύασεν, ἀπολογιζα-μένης τῆς Σωσόδ[?] αἰτησεφόων Βονιφατίῳ τῷ μὴ Ζώσιμον Πάπα Ῥώμης ἀφ᾽ ἧς τ[?] Ἀπαρίου καθαρίσεως, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς ἀδικαιώσεως. Καὶ ἕως νῦν ἀδικημαμένων αὐτὸν ἡγέμβα. Κικεί[?]ημένῳ μὴ ἐκεχάνων αὐτὸν τὸ τὸ Πρεσβυτέρῳ ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ Σικένοι δι᾽ τὸ ἀκολουθῶντα σκάνδαλα, ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἄλλαις Ἐκκλησίαις ἱεροτυργῶν. Ὥςπερ τόπων ἡ ἐν Ἀφρικῇ Σωσόδου πεδαρχίαν κάλλον τῆ κείσ Ζωσίμε. Eadem ratione Apiarii Sicensis Ecclesiae, quae in Africana provincia est, Presbyterum, loci illius Episcopus quandam ob causam a coetu fidelium exclusit, eundemque postea Synodus ibi coacta penitus depositit, quem Zosimus Papa Romanus ad se confugientem, suamque causam illi probantem absoluit, & cum literis ad Synodum remissum recipiendum curauit. Rationem vero reddens per apologeticum scriptum Synodus Africana Apiarij depositi, & rursus iustificati causa apud Bonifacium Papam Romanum, Zosimi successorem. Apiarium, inquit, etiam hodie absolutum iudicamus. Censuimus tamen ei propter scandala consecuta in Ecclesia Sicensi Presbyteri officium non esse obeundum, at in alijs EcEcclesiis rem ei divinam facere licere. Synodum ergo Africanam Zosimi judicio potius obtemperasse compertum est. Hæc Metrophanes Smyrnensis Metropolita ad Zachariam a Photio creatum Chalcedonensem Metropolitam falso afferentem, dictum Apiarium a Præfulibus Romanis absolutum Synodum Africanam non iustificasse. Synodus siquidem mandato Pontificio potius quam suo judicio nixa Apiarium absoluit, & munus sui Presbyteratus obire permisit in aliis Ecclesiis, licet in Sicensi ob scandala ibi exorta. obire negaverit, & huiusce suæ negationis per scriptum Apologeticum causam Bonifacio reddidit, quod solent facere secundi, & inferioris conditionis homines, & subiecti, uti ita dicam, servitio apud præstantissimos & nemini mancipatos Dominos. Nanque ἀπατᾶται ὁ νομίζων μαθητὴς εἶναι ἑαυτοῦ ὑπὲρ τὸν διδ-[?] δάσκαλον, καὶ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.[?]
units.tr: Nor is what the Synod against Photius relates about Apiarius the presbyter any less similar. Although the bishop and the African synod had completely deposed him, Zosimus, the Roman pontiff, absolved him and arranged for him to be received back by the synod with letters. The African synod, however, obeyed Zosimus's judgment, though against its own view. The Greek text of this passage is badly garbled in the scan. Its sense is that the bishop of the place excluded Apiarius, presbyter of the church of Sicca in the African province, from the assembly of the faithful for a certain offence; that the synod gathered there later deposed him entirely; that Zosimus, the Roman pontiff, absolved him when he fled to him and proved his cause; and that he arranged for him to be received back by the synod with letters. The African synod, giving its reasons in an apologetic writing to Boniface, Zosimus's successor, concerning the cause of Apiarius, deposed and then restored, said: "We judge that Apiarius too is today absolved. Nevertheless, we have decided that because of the scandals that followed in the church of Sicca he is not to perform the office of presbyter there, but that he may perform the divine office in other churches. It is therefore established that the African synod yielded to Zosimus's judgment rather than to its own." Metrophanes, Metropolitan of Smyrna, says this in reply to Zacharias, the Metropolitan of Chalcedon created by Photius, who falsely asserted that the synod had not confirmed Apiarius's absolution by the Roman prelates. For the synod, leaning on the pontifical mandate rather than its own judgment, absolved Apiarius and permitted him to discharge his presbyterate in other churches, though it refused him that office in Sicca because of the scandals that had arisen there. By its apologetic writing it gave Boniface the reason for this refusal. This is what second-rank men of lower condition, and as it were servants bound to the most distinguished masters who belong to no one, are accustomed to do. For "he who thinks himself a disciple above his teacher, and a slave above his lord, is deceived" [ἀπατᾶται ὁ νομίζων μαθητὴς εἶναι ἑαυτοῦ ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον, καὶ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ].

units.la: Et Hottingerus sub Photio affectati honoris crimen Pontificibus Romanis appingit.
units.tr: And Hottinger charges the Roman pontiffs with the crime of seeking honour under Photius.

units.la: At fides mihi vel nuncianti fit. Levia sunt hæc in Romanam maiestatem Hæreticorum vulnera, quæ verae historiæ limpidis limphis facillime abluuntur. Pergit Hottingerus. Postea tamen cum Basilius fraudes Romanas agnovisset, & Ignatius e vivis sublatus esset, Photium restituit. E vivis sublato Ignatio Basilius Photij fraudibus, & Santabareni præstigijs de statu mentis deturbatus Photium restituit, non ita tamen, vt restitutionis confirmationem a Romano Pontifice non petierit, cui cum indulsisset Pontifex, & certis conditionibus consensisset, si vera sunt quæ in Photiana hac Synodo digeruntur, cum illas non obseruasset Photius, assensum quoque suum retraxit, & auocauit, & Photium eadem ipsa anathematis sententia, qua eum Præcessores sui innodauerant, acta contra eum omnia confirmando alligatum declarauit, quam Græci ipsi vti a vero proprioq; rerum Ecclesiasticarum iudice latam, exceptis nonnullis, approbarunt, quidquid ineptiat Hottingerus.
units.tr: But I am not persuaded even by the one who reports it. These are light wounds inflicted by heretics on the Roman majesty, and they are very easily washed away by the clear waters of true history. Hottinger goes on: "Afterwards, however, when Basil had recognised the Roman frauds, and Ignatius had been removed from the living, he restored Photius. When Ignatius had been removed from the living, Basil, deprived of his mental balance by the frauds of Photius and the tricks of Santabarenus, restored Photius." Yet he did not seek confirmation of the restoration from the Roman pontiff, who granted it and agreed to it on certain conditions. If the things set out in this Photian synod are true, then, since Photius did not observe those conditions, the pontiff withdrew and revoked his assent, and declared Photius bound by the same sentence of anathema by which his predecessors had bound him, confirming all the acts against him. The Greeks themselves approved this sentence, with a few exceptions, as one given by the true and proper judge of ecclesiastical affairs. Whatever Hottinger may babble.

units.la: Neque in his cordatior dignoscitur Ioannes Henricus Boeclerus Commentario de rebus seculi a Christo nato &c. pag. 152. in qua notat; Notari autem debet, historiam huius Tragediæ variis dubitationibus, partim ex serie rei gestæ, partim studio eorum, quibus nihil liquet in historia, nisi quod ad curiæ Romanæ scenam compositum accommodatumque est, bodieque implicari, specimen eius rei possis capere ex Leonis Allatij disputatione, quam 'artificioso suo Commentario de Ecclesia Occidentalis, atque Orientalis perpetua consensione inserit, lib. 2. cap. 4. 5. 6. ubi multa & scripta & facta circa hanc rem, eo quo dixi proposito, in dubium vocat, ad quae accuratius consideranda non patitur instituti ratio, ut digrediamur. Fiet forte opportuniore loco, & tempore. Et quando opportunior hic locus & tempus? Utinam ante quam ipse hinc demigrem. Iterum utinam & quam oriffime. Rei geftae feriem in turbulentissimis Photii agitationibus ferio examine, partium studio neglecto, exploraui, & quod rem ipsam loquebatur, in medium protuli testimonii Scriptorum, & vero proximioribus ftabilitum. Quare hoc sibi ex Allatio habeat Boeclerus, quod & Hottingero antea indixerat, non versari illum in comprobando dogmate vel consuetudinibus Ecclesiasticis a calumniis Haereticorum eruendis. Esto sit falsum dogma. sint praue consuetudines. Liceat per me Boeclero, quidquid in mentem venerit etiam inconsiderate effutire. Propositum Allatii est, Ecclesiae Romanae Graecaeque consensionem demonstrare, eamq; perpetuam. Id sane aptissime probabitur, si & Romanos & Graecos eadem dicere, eadem probare, eadem profiteri, quod ex libris eorum ritualibus, illiusque gentis Scriptoribus, & potissimum si Schismaticorum consensus accedat, ni caecutire velimus, in rebus clarissimis, ostenditur.
units.tr: Nor is John Henry Boeckler more discerning in this matter, in his Commentary on the affairs of the century since Christ's birth, p. 152, where he notes: "It must be observed that the history of this tragedy is open to various doubts, partly from the sequence of events and partly from the zeal of those for whom nothing in history is clear except what has been composed and adapted to the stage of the Roman court. A sample of this you may take from the disputation of Leo Allatius, which he inserts in his skilful Commentary on the perpetual agreement of the Western and Eastern Church, book 2, chapters 4, 5 and 6, where he calls into doubt, for the purpose I have mentioned, many things both written and done concerning this matter. The plan of my work does not allow me to examine these more carefully here, so that we may digress. Perhaps it will be done in a more suitable place and time. And when will this place and time be more suitable? Would that it were before I depart from here. Again I wish it were as soon as possible. I have investigated the sequence of events in the most turbulent agitations of Photius with a serious examination, setting aside zeal for either party, and I have brought forward into the open what the matter itself says, as established by the testimony of writers and those nearest to the events." Let Boeckler therefore take from Allatius what he had earlier imputed to Hottinger: that Allatius was not engaged in proving doctrine or ecclesiastical customs against the calumnies of heretics. Suppose the doctrine is false and the customs are wicked. Let Boeckler, through me, blurt out whatever comes into his mind, even if he does so without thought. Allatius's aim is to demonstrate the agreement of the Roman and Greek Church, and that it is perpetual. This will certainly be proved most aptly if the Romans and the Greeks say the same things, prove the same things and profess the same things. This is shown from their ritual books and from the writers of that nation, and especially if the consent of the schismatics is added, unless we wish to be blind in matters that are perfectly clear.

units.la: Quare cum ipse ante & post tempora Photij testimonia Graecorum eo aeuo praeclarissimorum profert, eadem ipsa, quae & Pontificij dicunt, enunciantium, nemo nisi perfatuus consensionem, etiam si prava a nonnullis reputetur, in dubio ponet. Hinc concludo: Tarasius, Nicephorus Patriarchae Constantinopolitani, Theodorus Studita, Simeon Metaphrastes, Maximus Homologeta, Basilius, Leo Imperatores Graecorum, Pontifices ipsi Romani ad cosdem [?] Graecos scribentes, a quibus nullo negotio de mendacio, atque de usurpata indebite auctoritate argui poterant, ipse Photius Ecclesiae Romanae hostis infensissimus: hi omnes non ex trunco, aut stipite, sed cum primis illustres scientijs, virtutibus, & dignitatibus clari, & ab ipsis Graecis etiam schismaticis in maximo pretio habiti, & maxima veneratione culti, dictis factisque fatentur, Romanum Pontificem primas partes in universa Ecclesia obtinere, illius esse & Ecclesias corrigere, & corripere, dogmata stabilire, minis etiam & poenis inflictis Ecclesiasticas personas, cuiuscunque sint gradus & dignitatis, ad sua placita compellere, &, si mandatis non obtemperauerint, poenam ab eis ob contumaciam expetere, &, quidquid ipsi egerint, irritum declarare, ni ab illis postmodum confirmatum fuerit, & Concilia etiam ipsa generalia, & particularia nullam habere firmitatem, si ipsius assensus non accesserit, & similia. & haec omnia non scriptis tantum, sed factis etiam comprobant. Ergo Pontificia dignitas, & auctoritas, quam sibi Romanus in universam Ecclesiam exercet, debita est illi consensu Graecorum, & Latinorum unanimi, non ex ambitione circa tempora Photij vindicata, nec artificioso Allatij commentario implicata, ut Graeci cum Latinis coniuncti sententiis concinunt: & tu consensum pernegas, & criminis loco & artificij conatus Allatij obijcis? Dicta factaque prae oculis sunt; si audis & non comprehendis animo plane & dilucide loquentia, quare ipsa devoras? quare illis offundis tenebras? quare certa incerta reddis? Si non capis, si non recipis, fatere inscitiam tuam: si tenes, & negas, nec acquiescis, iam malignus es, improbus es, plenus sceleris es, extra Ecclesiam es, & eiurato Christianismo extra aram & fidem es.
units.tr: Therefore, since Allatius brings forward the testimonies of the most distinguished Greeks of that age, both before and after the time of Photius, who say exactly what the Papists also say, no one but a complete fool will call that agreement into doubt, even if some think it wicked. Hence I conclude: Tarasius; Nicephorus, Patriarchs of Constantinople; Theodore the Studite; Symeon Metaphrastes; Maximus the Confessor; Basil and Leo, Emperors of the Greeks; the Roman pontiffs themselves, writing to the Greeks, who could easily have been charged by them with lying and with unlawfully usurped authority; and Photius himself, the most bitter enemy of the Roman Church. All these, not as tree trunks or blocks, but as men eminent above all for learning, virtues and dignities, and held in the highest esteem and honoured with the greatest reverence even by the Greeks themselves, schismatics included, declare by word and deed that the Roman pontiff holds the first place in the whole Church. It belongs to him to correct and rebuke the churches, to establish doctrines, to compel ecclesiastical persons of whatever rank and dignity to his decrees by threats and penalties, and, if they do not obey his commands, to demand punishment from them for their contumacy; and whatever they have done he declares void, unless it is later confirmed by him. They also declare that general and particular councils have no firmness unless his assent is added, and similar things. And they prove all these things not only by writings but also by deeds. Therefore the pontifical dignity and authority which the Roman exercises over the whole Church is owed to the unanimous consent of Greeks and Latins. It was not claimed out of ambition around the time of Photius, nor is it entangled in Allatius's skilful commentary; rather, the Greeks, joined with the Latins, agree in their opinions. And do you deny the consent, and object to Allatius that it is a crime and a trick of his craft? The sayings and deeds lie before your eyes. If you hear them but do not grasp with your mind what they say so plainly and clearly, why do you devour them? Why do you cast darkness over them? Why do you make certain things uncertain? If you do not understand, if you do not accept, confess your ignorance. If you grasp them and deny them and do not yield, then you are malicious, you are wicked, you are full of crime, you are outside the Church, and with Christianity renounced you are outside the altar and the faith.

units.la: Hinc quoque assequimur immodicam Roberti Creyghtoni in historia infantiam, & immoderatam stultiloquentiam, ne dicam impietatem, & rerum sacrarum contemptum, qui praefatione ad Lectorem in Historia Concilij Florentini, quasi de Romanis Pontificibus triumphasset Photius, nimbos Septentrionis profundit: Et quid si mille Papæ Photium incursassent [?], seu Laicum, seu sacratum, seu vivum, seu mortuum? Photius non minus sui juris securus sedebat in solio a Paparum contumeliis, dum vixit, quam post mortem supinus iacebat in sepulchro. Jam mundus aetate proiectior vindicias dedit secundum libertatem; & mortales plurimi a Photij exemplo didicere, istos Salmoneas contemnere, qui tonitrua excitant in maiorem strepitum, quam stragem. Fulgur discurrens multa territat animalia, sed rarum cadit bidental. Et esse ne mentis integrae dicendus est hic vir? Ad incursandum Photium non fuere necessarij mille Papae. Quatuor nec illi coniunctim, sed unus post alium subsecutis temporibus in Romana cathedra confidentes, Nicolaus, Adrianus, Joannes, Marinus astum Photij, & immensam improbitatem, nec non Imperatorum, & Principum fauorem, & gratiam compresserunt, eumque de throno malis artibus occupato deiectum, in numerum sceleratorum, & impiorum hominum detrusum, & uti a Gregorio Syracusano ad sacros ordines promotum, laicum declaratum, a solo patrio extorrem, vagum, exulemque aberrare, dignitatibus imminutum iterum, atque iterum perinuitum, ac repugnantem coëgere. Et hoc est renitentibus mille Papis throni occupati securum, & ad Pontificum ictus tutum esse? Securitas ista, si mentis inops non est Creyghtonus, mera calamitas, crux mala maxima est. sic eiectus, afflictus cum reliqua omnia ad solandum eum defecissent, & artes ipsius retunderentur, ad Romanum recurrit, a quo tantummodo securitatem attendit, qui aerumnas illius deplorandas commiseratus, speransque eum ad sanam frugem reducere, Imperatoris quoque supplicationibus flexus, seseque ad illius mediocritatem demittens, illius reconciliationem cum Ecclesia Romana ita disponit, vt in Synodo Libellum exhibeat, indoleat de commissis, & misericordiam poscat, poenas etiam pro sceleribus promeritas, imponendas sibi persoluat. Quod cum ipse postmodum non perfecisset, poenis novis subactus, & extra thronum communione Catholica seclusus cum vita animum quoque inglorius amisit, profectus ad inferos. Sic triumphatur apud inconfideratissimos Haereticos de Pontificibus Romanis, & Salmonei similes plorare iubentur. Sic tonitrua ista non sunt strepitus, sed terror, fulgur discurrens, strages, & per dendensum cadens bidental. Bidental vides, fulminis vestigia, & ob illa constructam a Sacerdotibus aram, & fulminis ictum denegas? tantum ad terrorem proiectum contendis? Quod non potuit Michaël Imperator, Bardas Imperij arbiter, Basilius Macedo item Imperator nervis omnibus incumbentes, unus Romanus Pontifex habuit in sua potestate. Declarat reum Photium, pellit de throno, Sacris spoliat: si placuerit, modo quo vult, restituit, rursusque inobedientem pellit. Et Photius sui juris securus sedet in solio, etiam si mille Papae eum incursent? Sed esto etiam sedisset invitis Pontificibus. Vis, & tyrannis, & dementissima pro arbitratu suo imperitantium temeritas aliud poscit, aliud aequum & iustum. Imperatores vim vi repellunt: Pontifices Romani Ecclesiasticis armis sua defendunt, & criminibus obnoxios oppugnant.
units.tr: Hence we also see the immoderate childishness of Robert Creyghton in his history, and his unbridled silliness, not to say impiety and contempt for sacred things. In the preface to the Reader of his History of the Council of Florence, after boasting that Photius had triumphed over the Roman pontiffs, he pours out a storm from the north: And what if a thousand popes had attacked Photius, whether lay or clerical, living or dead? While he lived, Photius sat on his throne as securely, free from the insults of the popes, as he lay on his back in the tomb after death. Now the world, grown wiser with age, has vindicated true liberty, and most mortals have learned from Photius' example to despise those Salmoneuses who stir up thunder that makes more noise than damage. A flash of lightning frightens many animals, but it rarely strikes a bidental. Should this man be called sound in mind? A thousand popes were not needed to attack Photius. Four popes, not together but one after another, in successive times, sitting in the Roman chair (Nicholas, Hadrian, John, and Marinus), crushed Photius' cunning, his immense wickedness, and also the favour and grace of emperors and princes. They cast him down from a throne he had seized by evil arts, thrust him among the wicked and impious, and declared him a layman, though Gregory of Syracuse had promoted him to holy orders. They made him an exile and a wanderer, driven from his native soil, and again and again, though diminished in dignity and struggling against it, they forced him back. And is this what it means to be safe on a seized throne and secure against the blows of the pontiffs, even though a thousand popes resisted? If Creyghton is not destitute of sense, that security is sheer calamity, a very great evil. So cast down and afflicted, when all other means of consolation had failed and his arts were blunted, he ran back to the Roman pontiff, from whom alone he sought security. Pitying his miserable state, and hoping to bring him back to sound conduct, the pontiff, also moved by the emperor's entreaties and lowering himself to Photius' mediocrity, arranged his reconciliation with the Roman Church in such a way that, at a synod, he would present a written statement, lament his misdeeds, ask for mercy, and pay the penalties he had earned for his crimes. When he later failed to carry this out, he was subdued by new punishments, excluded from Catholic communion and from the throne, and he lost his life and his spirit without glory, departing to the lower world. Thus the most inconsiderate heretics boast about the Roman pontiffs, and Salmoneus-like men are bidden to weep. Thus those thunders are not noise but terror: a flash of lightning, slaughter, and a bidental falling through the air. You see the bidental, the traces of the lightning, and because of them the altar built by the priests, yet you deny that a stroke of lightning occurred and insist it was thrown only to terrify? What Emperor Michael, Bardas, arbiter of the empire, and Basil the Macedonian, likewise emperor, straining every nerve, could not do, one Roman pontiff had in his power. He declares Photius guilty, drives him from the throne, strips him of sacred office; if he pleases, he restores him in whatever manner he wishes, and again drives him out when he disobeys. And Photius sits securely on his throne, free from fear, even though a thousand popes attack him? But grant that he sat there even against the wishes of the pontiffs. Violence and tyranny, and the most insane recklessness of men who rule as they please, demand one thing, while what is fair and just demands another. Emperors repel force with force; the Roman pontiffs defend their own with ecclesiastical arms and assail those liable to crimes.

units.la: Jam vero, ut id quoque concedamus Schismaticis, sit sane ita. Synodus haec Photiana Oecumenica sit, Joanni Pontifici probata, ab Ecclesia tum Graeca, tum Latina agnita, & uti legitima excepta; iura, ac facultates aliis Synodis Oecumenicis indubitate concessas, & quod magis est, tantum sibi vindicet, justeq; possideat, ut & suturis Synodis Oecumenicis, & vniuersali Ecclesiæ legem, pœnis statutis, imponere valeat, quam si non seruauerint, ob delictum contra legem datam commissum plectendæ veniant: nunquid propterea Romana Ecclesia addens in Symbolo, Filioque, pœnas indictas persoluet? Nihil minus. Pendamus verba Synodi. Decretum est post Symbolum absq; additione pronunciatum: Si quis aliam fidem in hoc sancto Symbolo addiderit, vel aliquid dempserit, vel immutauerit, si ex sacratis Deo hominibus est, omnimodæ depositioni, si ex laicorum ordine, anathemati subiiciatur. Εἰ μὲν [?] ... [illegible, ~60 letters] ... ἀναθεματισμῷ ὑποβ[?]. Prohibetur alia fides, contraria nempe, scriptæ aduersans, repugnans, aliena, externa. Sed fidei in Symbolo Nicæno, vel Constantinopolitano traditæ, nullo modo aduersatur, neque repugnat additio Filioque, cum id multo ante Photiana tempora tenuerint atq; deprædicauerint Ecclesiæ Orientalis, & Occidentalis, Patres, & Doctores Ecclesiæ Græcæ, & Latinæ, & illius vestigia satisperspicua, & manifesta in sacris literis habeantur, vt alibi sæpius fuse probauimus. Non assicit ergo Romanam Ecclesiam cohærentem, aptam, & cõsentaneam Symbolo veritatem addentem Symbolo . quidquid in contra- rium conentur Schifmatici Photiani.
units.tr: Now indeed, to concede this also to the schismatics, let it be so. Let this Photian synod be counted ecumenical, approved by Pope John, accepted by both the Greek and Latin Churches as lawful, and let it claim for itself, and rightly possess, the rights and powers that have been undoubtedly granted to other ecumenical synods; and, what is more, let it be able to impose on future ecumenical synods and on the universal Church a law with penalties, which those who fail to keep would deservedly suffer for a transgression against the law given. Would the Roman Church, by adding Filioque to the Creed, therefore pay the penalties imposed? Not at all. Let us weigh the synod's own words. It was decreed, and proclaimed after the Creed without any addition: If anyone adds another faith to this holy Creed, or removes anything from it, or alters it, let him be subjected to total deposition if he is of the order of God's consecrated men, or to anathema if he is of the laity. [Greek sentence, largely illegible in the scan, about "anathema".] The Greek is forbidden: another faith, that is, one contrary to the written one, opposed, repugnant, foreign and alien. But the addition of Filioque is in no way contrary to the faith delivered in the Nicene or Constantinopolitan Creed, nor does it contradict it, since the Fathers and teachers of both the Greek and Latin Churches, in the East as well as the West, held and proclaimed this long before the time of Photius, and its traces are sufficiently clear and manifest in the sacred writings, as we have often proved at length elsewhere. Therefore the addition of a truth that agrees with and is consonant with the Creed does not touch the Roman Church, whatever the Photian schismatics may attempt to the contrary.

units.la: Tandemque hic adnectam verba Grego- rij Hieromonachi ex Responsione in Pro- fessionem fidei Marci Ephesij, quae toti du- bitationi finem imponant ; Ἡμεῖς ἢ καὶ τὰ θεωρικὰ τὰ ὀρθὰ τῆς Ἐφέσου ἀποκομιζόμενα, ὡς τῆς ὀρθῆς Σωσόδε[?] ἀξιόμεθα. Ἐν ᾧ καὶ ὡς λέγει ὑπομνήσει τῷ ἀγιωτάτῳ Πάπᾳ Ἰωάννῃ[?]· καὶ τί γε πολὺ τὸ ὑποπτον ἔχεις[?], ἐπεὶ δὲ ἄναγ ὅλως δι' ὅλου ἰλλωικλῶ τῷ γραφῷ, καὶ μηδὲν ἔχει ἐν ἑαυτῇ ἰδίωμά τι Λατινικόν. Ἀλλως τε ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ Σωσόδω θεῶτον ὠφέλει αὐτῇ ἀναγωνιζομένη[?], ἐὰ δὲ[?] ξιωθῆς τὸν Φώτιον τὰ ἰσχειζοντα τῷ καθέδρᾳ τῆς Κωνσταντινουπόλεως. Ὃ δὲ ἐχ' ἔπως ἐχρύετο[?]. Ἀλλ' ἅμα πρὸ τῷ ἀποφαλιζεῖ τοῦ Πάπα, καὶ τοῦ Φωτίου κομίζαι τὰ σαλέντα, τὸ ὁμοφόρον, καὶ τὸ σιχάζειον, καὶ ἃ σαρδάλια, μηδήμιας ἀφηγιζαμένης ἐξεταστέως[?]; δ' Θεὺς ὁ Φώτιος δίδηκ' ἀωόντ', ἃ δὲ κομιδέντα αὐτὸ, ὡς τὰ θεωρικὰ τῆς Σωσόδε ταύτης μάρτυρα. Καὶ τὸ, Χριστὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ἐπᾶν ὁ νεφέλας τὸν ἑαυτὸν ἀποβάλλων, καὶ τῷ ἡμετέρῳ φύσιν ἀπαχωρίζαι, καὶ καθάρας σολισάμενος, αὐτὸς τὸν ἀδῆγον, καὶ συλλαβεῖν[?], καὶ πνευματικὸν πάπιεα ἡμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῇ παρόντι βίῳ φέρει ἄδυλον, καὶ σωτηρίαν ἀσφαλῇ συλίζαι, καὶ τῷ μέλλοντι αἰῶνι τὸν νυμφι- κὸν παραβάλλοι χιτῶνα, ἄξιον τῆς μακαρίας ἐκκλησίας νυμφῶν ἀνασηκάς[?]. Εἰ δ' οὐκ ἀποστέρειν ἐν κοινῇ ἀπα-[?]
units.tr: Finally, I will add here the words of Gregory the Hieromonk from his Response to the Profession of Faith of Mark of Ephesus, which put an end to the whole doubt. [Greek passage, badly garbled in the scan; it contains a sharp reply to Mark: Gregory says that Mark's Ephesian letter, which he judged to be correct, is not wholly Latin in its manner, and that its supposed Latin features are absent; he speaks of the see of Constantinople, of Photius, of the holy Pope John, and of the Creed, and he warns that the tribe of the Latins should not be regarded as heretics for keeping their own custom, and he cites Peter's words about shepherding the flock willingly and not under compulsion.]

units.la: Ἐπεὶ δὲ = Signum Graecum: ill., several words of the Greek passage uncertain in this scan. ἀναγωγῶναι τῷ Θεσσαλονικεῖ, καὶ τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς πίστεως ἔγραφον λαβὼν, καὶ ἔπειτα τὸ ἐν τῇ ἀρχιερωσύνῃ ἀναχηρύξιν ἀπλῶς τὸ ἐκ τῆς ἀρχῆς ἴστατο [?]. Ὅμως γε μὴν ὑμᾶς, ὡς οἰκειότατα [?] αὐτῷ ἐχόμεθα ἀσμενέστατα, ὡς αὐτὸς καὶ τῷ Θεσσαλονικεῖ. Τί οὖν φησὶν αὕτη; οἶόμεθα ἢ μηδὲ τῷ σοφίᾳ εὐτυχοῦντι ἀγωνᾶν, ὡς ἂν νοννεχῆ τι, καὶ πλήθει ζοφίας, ὅπως τὸ ἐξ οὗ λοιποὺς ἡμῖν Ἐπισκόπους καταπαῦσαι ἐπὶ φρονεῖν, εἰς δυνάμενος ἡμῖν ἐμπίπτῃ, ὅτι ᾧ ἀγαλμάτῳ ἡ θέοτητι ἐπὶ ἔχεσα μεταβαλλὼν εἰς ἀπολᾶς καὶ ἀκόλουθος [?] συνηθείᾳ, εἰ καὶ βεβαιώτατος ἀχρὸν τῷ ἐναρξιν ἀληφθεῖς, καὶ ἐκ ἐστι παγιωτάτη ἐκ πολλῶν ἐμαυτῆς καὶ δι᾽ ταῦτα καλῶς ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν, ἵνα μὴ μὴ βίας ἀναγκαδῇ τῆς παρ᾽ ἡμῶν ἐάσαι τῷ προδόνλῳ, ὥστε ἐφθασεν ἐν τῷ Συμβόλῳ προδῶσαι, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον μὴ οἰκονομίας ἀζημιωτάτας, καὶ ἔτι ἀφαινουμένης ὑπισθίας τῆς βλασφημίας. Ποιμαίνειν γὰρ τὸ ἐν ὑμῖν ποίμνιον ἐκ ἀναγκαστῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ἑκόντως, ἐπ᾽ ὡς καταχυεί- ζουντες τὸ κλῆρος, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς τύποι γινόμενοι, ὁ ἄνεπος τῷ Ἀ ποσταλῶν Πέτρος ἔφη. καὶ ἐξ ἐξῆς. καὶ ταῦτα ἐκ τῆς Θησολλῆς. τίς δὲ ἐκ ἀκήκοεν, ὡς Λαοῦνοι ὅτι κακοδόξους ἐμὲ πυρὸς μᾶλλον δοκι- μάζεσθαι; πῶς ἢ ἐκ αἰσχυνόμενοι ἐπὶ βλασφη- μοῦντας; ποῦ ἢ ἐν τῇ κακοδοξίᾳ μᾶλλον ἀρμό- ζει τὸ μὴ καταχυεῖν τὸ κλῆρος; τοῦτο δὲ Ἄρεος καὶ Μακεδόνιος, καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτοῖς εἶπον αὐ, ὅπ γέγραπται, μὴ καταχυεῖσθαι τὸ κλῆρος, καὶ πάν- τας ὁμοίως οἱ τῶν ὀρθῶν δογμάτων ἀλλόξιοι. ποῦ ἢ ὁ ὁ καινὼν ὁ Διαπλίζων, ὁ κοινωνῶν πῷ ἀκοινωνήτῳ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἀκοινωνήτῳ ἔσω. ἕνλον ἓν ὡς ἐχ' αἱρε-σεως τὸ ἐκ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν τῷ Θεῷ Συμβόλῳ. ἀλλὰ δὲ αἱρέσεως ὧ τῆτο, οἱ ἔπι Φάλλοντες πῷ αἰα-θήματι καθυποβάλλοντο, ὁ καὶ τὸν πυεῖς δί-κλω διέφυγον.
units.tr: [Greek passage, largely illegible in this scan; several words are uncertain.] Gregory, in this section, argues that Mark's confession of faith was received and that his promotion to the priesthood was made in the light of the original decision. He nonetheless gladly holds you as very close to himself, as he does also the Thessalonian. What then does this man say? He thinks that one who is prosperous in wisdom should not contend over some small point, lest he fall into the company of those who, in their ignorance, wish to prevent the rest of us from being bishops. Those who have changed what was once held in the Godhead into an unnatural and wicked habit, though it was firmly grounded from the beginning, have been judged rightly by us, so that they should not be forced by our authority to betray the Creed, but rather pursue an innocuous economy, while the blasphemy remains exposed. For the flock among you is to be shepherded not under compulsion but willingly, not as lording it over the clergy but as becoming examples, as the apostle Peter said. Who has not heard that the Latins are judged more worthy of fire than heretics? How could they not be ashamed of blaspheming? Where does it fit better, in false doctrine, not to lord it over the clergy? Arius and Macedonius, and those with them, said the same, that the clergy must not be lorded over, and all alike who dissent from right doctrine. Where is the one who is consecrated for the Creed, who communes with the uncommunicated, and is himself uncommunicated within? One article, taken from the whole world, is not accepted as heresy in the Creed of God. But the heresy of this kind, the ones who fell under the anathema, were brought under condemnation, and they escaped the sword by fleeing.

units.la: Ἀλλ' ὁ μακαριώτατος Πάπας Ἰωάννης, καὶ ἡ ἐπὶ αὐτῶν Σωσθ. τῆς ἐκ ἐπίσ-κοπον, καὶ τοῦτο [?] ... καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικοῖς μεγίσης, ὡς καὶ ἀλλὰ τὸ συνέξει τὸ τῆς Ἀνθίμε ὄνομα ἐν τῆς ἐπιτύχοις τῶν ἀλαπλικῶ Ἐκκλησίαν ἐπιχειθλῶσ ὑπὸ ταύτης τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῷ Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Nos porro & Acta, quæ ab Ephesio producuntur, ac si Octauæ Synodi essent, recipiemus. Præterea etiam & quam ait Epistolam sanctissimi Papæ Ioannis, licet suspectissima sit, quod scriptio illa per omnia dictionem Græcam referat, & nullam in se contineat proprietatem Latini sermonis. Et absque dubio in ea Synodo ante alia omnia primum legenda erat, postmodum recipiendus Photius, admittendaque ea, quæ ipsum in cathedram Constantinopolitanam promouerent. Hoc vero ita peractum non est. Sed statim atque conuenissent Papæ locumtenentes, & præsentassent munera Omophorium, Sticharium, & Sandalia, nullo præuio examine, statim Photius ipsos recepit, & munera sibi missa, vt Acta Synodi testantur, nec non & illud; Christus Deus noster, qui cœlum nubibus circundat, & naturam nostram, vt eam reconslaret & repurgaret, amiciri voluit, ipse fratri, & communistro, & spirituali Patri nostro, & in vita præsenti custodiam tutam, & salutem sacrosanctam tribuat, & eum in futuro seculo sponsali tunica circumdet, dignum beati illius thalami ostendens. Addecebat itaque. primum Epistolam in omnium audientiam legere, & Legatorum confessionem scriptam accipere, tum demum ea, quæ restitutionem throni, & Pontificatus indicabant, admittere. Nihilominus nos illam perquam libentissime vti Oecumenicam suscipiemus, & eam ipsam Epistolam. Quæ porro in ea continentur?
