Cyprianus Epistola ad Iubaianum; Et idcirco, quia legitimum & Ecclesiasticum Baptismum consecuti fuerant, babaptizari eos vltra nono portebat : sed tantummodo quod deerat id a Petro, & Ioanne factum est, vt oratione pro eis habita, & manu impositą inuocaretur, & infunderetur super eos Spiritus sanctus. Quod nunc quoque apud nos geritur, vt qui in Ecclesia baptizantur Præpositis Ecclesia offerantur, & per nostram orationem, & manus impositionem Spiritum sanctum consequantur, & signaculo Dominico consummentur. Optatus Mileuitanus ; Oleum simplex est, & nomen suum vnum, & proprium habet, confectum iam Chrisma vocatur, in quo est suauitas, quæ cutem conscientiæ mollit, exclusa duritia peccatorum, quæ animum innouat leuem, quæ sedem Spiritui sancto parat, vt inuitatus illic, asperitate fugata, libenter inhabitare dignetur. Actum agerem, si ex Græcæ, Latinæqúe Ecclesiæ Patrum antiquorum testimonijs, antiquitatem Sacramenti Eucharistiæ in Ecclesia constabilire conarer. Agant id illi, quibus plus otij est. Neque puto id negari, nisi a male sanis hominibus.
units.tr: The number of the seven sacraments. Jeremias the Patriarch defends this number with more insistence than is needed. He does not, however, escape Allatius's censure, because he assigns the other sacraments apart from Baptism and the Lord's Supper to the institution of the Church alone. The Greek and Latin Churches agree about the number of the sacraments, about their institution, and about their grace. So this line of argument does not help the opponent much in overturning the agreement. But this is the dogma not of the ancient but of the more recent Greeks. Some John Damascene, a man of the eighth century, although he embraced all Christian theology in the work he wrote on the Orthodox faith, delivered no such division. Perhaps some rivalry with the Latins led them to this number of seven mysteries, so that they should not seem in any way inferior to them. These are the words of Daillé. So the more recent Greeks too, so as not to be inferior to the Latins in anything, therefore conform themselves to them and promote the agreement. We have already spoken about the sacraments and their antiquity against Hottinger. Now, for the sake of our opponents, we will add some points, so that it may be recognised how ancient the tradition of the mysteries in the Church is. Tertullian, in the book On the Resurrection, chapter 9, where he explains what happens to a man in the flesh when his soul is joined to God: The flesh is washed, so that the soul may be made spotless. Here is Baptism. The flesh is anointed, so that the soul may be consecrated. The flesh is signed, so that the soul may be fortified. The flesh is shadowed by the laying on of hands, so that the soul may be enlightened by it. Here is Confirmation. The flesh feeds on the body and blood of Christ, so that the soul too may be fattened on God. Here is the Eucharist. And in chapter 9 again: The flesh of man, which God fashioned with his own hands in his own image, and clothed with his sacraments and disciplines, will this flesh not rise again? And in the book On Prescription against Heretics, chapter 40: He too baptises certain believers and his faithful; he promises the forgiveness of sins through the bath, and so he initiates them still into Mithras. He seals his soldiers on their foreheads there; he celebrates also the offering of bread. Ambrose, in the book On Those Who Are Initiated into the Mysteries, chapter 7: Repeat what you have received: the spiritual seal, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness, the Spirit of holy fear; and keep what you have received. God the Father has sealed you; Christ the Lord has confirmed you and given the pledge of the Spirit in your hearts. And in the following chapter: Having been washed, the people hasten with the two marks to the altars of Christ; laying aside the garments of their old error, renewed like the eagle's youth, they hasten to approach that heavenly feast. And in book 3 On the Sacraments: There follows the special seal, which you heard read today, because after the font there remains that it be made perfect, when the Holy Spirit is poured in at the invocation of the priest. Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogical Catechesis 3: After we have come up from the waters of the holy laver, the chrism is given to us, which bears the image of that with which Christ was anointed. And Catechesis 4: The teaching of blessed Paul will be able to make you quite certain about the divine mysteries given to you, you who have become partakers of Christ's body and blood. On the chrism, Origen on chapter 6 of the Epistle to the Romans: We were all baptised according to the type handed down by the Church, in the visible waters themselves and with the visible chrism. Eusebius of Caesarea, History book 6, chapter 35: Novatus, having at last escaped his illness, did not obtain the other things which, according to the canon of the Church, ought to have been imbued after Baptism, and he was not sealed with the seal by the bishop. Since he did not attain these, how, I ask, did he obtain the Holy Spirit? The Synod of Laodicea, canon 39: Those who are being enlightened ought, after Baptism, to be anointed with the heavenly chrism and to be partakers of the heavenly kingdom. Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogical Catechesis 3: Just as the bread of the Eucharist, after that invocation of the Holy Spirit, is no longer common bread but the body of Christ, so this holy ointment is no longer plain ointment, nor, if anyone wishes to call it common, is it so after it has been consecrated; it is the chrism of Christ, which by the coming of the Holy Spirit has the energy of his divinity. With it your forehead and your other senses are anointed symbolically; and the body is indeed anointed with this visible ointment, but the soul is sanctified by the holy and life-giving Spirit. And first it is smeared on the forehead, so that it may wipe away from you the shame which the first transgressor carried about perpetually, and so that you may be able to behold the glory of the Lord with unveiled face. Theodoret on chapter 1 of the Song of Songs: Remember the mystery of holy Baptism, in which those who are initiated, after renouncing Satan and confessing God, are anointed with the chrism as with a sign and mark of royal spiritual ointment, and under that visible appearance of the ointment they receive the invisible grace of the most holy Spirit. Cyprian, Epistle to Jubaianus: And therefore, because they had obtained lawful and ecclesiastical Baptism, it was not necessary for them to be baptised again. What was lacking was done only by Peter and John, so that, prayer having been offered for them and hands laid on them, the Holy Spirit should be invoked and poured out upon them. This is also done now among us: those who are baptised in the Church are brought to the presidents of the Church, and through our prayer and the laying on of hands they obtain the Holy Spirit and are completed with the Lord's seal. Optatus of Milevis: Oil in its simple state has its own single and proper name; once it has been consecrated it is called chrism. In it there is a sweetness which softens the skin of the conscience, the hardness of sins being shut out; it renews the mind, making it light; it prepares a seat for the Holy Spirit, so that, invited there and the roughness being put to flight, he may deign to dwell there willingly. I would be doing something superfluous if I tried to establish the antiquity of the sacrament of the Eucharist in the Church from the testimonies of the ancient Fathers of the Greek and Latin Churches. Let those do it who have more leisure. Nor do I think this will be denied except by men of unsound mind.

units.la: De Pœnitentia Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 1. Pædagogi cap. 9. Pulchrum quidem certe est non peccare: pulchrum est etiam, vt qui peccat, ducatur pœnitentia. Quemadmodum optimum quidem semper esse sanum; bonum autem etiam a morbo conualescere. Idem lib. 2. Stromatum; Dedit ergo, cum sit multā[?] misericordia, ijs etiam, qui in fide in aliquod peccatum incidunt, secundam poenitentiam, quam, si quis tentatus fuerit post vocationem coactus, & callide circumuentus, vnam adhuc inpoenitendam acceperit poenitentiam. Origenes Homilia 9. in Numeros; Nostrum est ad emendationem otius festinare, ad poenitentiam sine dissimulatione conuerti, lugere praterita, cauere futura, inuocare auxilium Dei. Statim enim vt conuersus ingemueris, saluus eris; inuenies enim aduocatum, qui pro te interpellat Patrem, Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Dionysius Alexandrinus Epist. ad Fabium Antiochenum; Illi igitur diuini Martyres, dum erant apud nos, nonnullos e fratribus, in quibus crimen sacrificandi Idolis haerebat, quique a fide excidissent, cum conuersionem, ac poenitentiam eorum perspicerent, eamque posse acceptam fore ei, qui omnino non vult mortem peccatoris, satis exploratum haberent, ad se denuo admittunt, recipiunt in Ecclesiam, conuentus cum illis celebrant, ineunt societatem, precum, & epularum communione vna vtuntur, Concil. Neocaesariense Can. 1. Presbyter si fornicatus fuerit, vel adulterium commiserit, penitus extrudatur, & ad poenitentiam deducatur. Cyrillus Hierosolymitanus Catechesi 2. Si Manasses, qui Prophetam diffecuerat per poenitentiam saluatur, tu vero, qui nihil huiusmodi perpetrasti, non saluaberis? Caue ne virtuti poenitentiae frustradiffidas. Vis cognoscere quantam vim habeat poenitentia? vis nosse hoc fortia salutis arma, & discere, quam multis praualeat confessio? Centum octoginta millia hostium Ezechias per consessionem in fugam verterat. Magnum quidem id re vera, sed exiguum tamen respectu eorum, quae dicenda sunt. Divinam sententiam promulgatam hic idem per poenitentiam revocauit. Aegrotanti enim illi dixerat Esaias; Dispone domui tuae: Morieris enim tu, & non viues. Quae deinceps expectatio, quae spes salutis, Propheta dicente, quod morieris? Sed non abstinuit tamen a poenitentia Ezechias: recordatusque illius, quod scriptum est. Cum conuersus ingemueris, tunc saluaberis. &c. Gregorius Nyssenus Orat. in eos, qui durius, & acerbius aliós iudicant; Quid enim est aliud poenitentia, nisi dissolutio, & eversio praeteritorum, quae vel re, vel cogitatione sunt admissa. Qui vero cognita poenitentia utilitate adhuc in flagitiorum, & impietatis coeno volutatur, similis est illi servo, qui dominum sibi iratum sciens, in eius conspectu scelerate se gerit, peccatumque duplicat. Non plura referam. etiamnum leguntur de Poenitentia antiquorum Patrum sermones Tertulliani, Basilij Caesariensis, Ephraem Syri, Ambrosij Mediolanensis, Ioannis Chrysostomi, qui tibi de hoc argumento plura suppeditabunt.
units.tr: On Repentance. Clement of Alexandria, Paedagogus book 1, chapter 9: It is certainly a fine thing not to sin; it is also a fine thing that he who sins should be led to repentance, just as it is always best to be healthy, but good also to recover from sickness. The same, Stromata book 2: God, being abundant in mercy, has given a second repentance even to those who fall into some sin after faith; and if anyone, after his calling, has been tempted, forced, and cunningly circumvented, he has received one further repentance that must not be repeated. Origen, Homily 9 on Numbers: It is for us to hasten quickly to amendment, to turn to repentance without pretence, to mourn what is past, to beware of what is to come, to call upon the help of God. For as soon as you have turned and groaned, you will be saved; for you will find an advocate who intercedes for you with the Father, our Lord Jesus Christ. Dionysius of Alexandria, Epistle to Fabius of Antioch: Those divine martyrs, while they were among us, when they saw the conversion and repentance of some of the brothers, in whom the crime of sacrificing to idols clung, and who had fallen from the faith, and when they were quite sure that it would be accepted by him who does not at all wish the death of a sinner, admitted them again, received them into the Church, held meetings with them, entered into fellowship, and shared in common prayers and meals. Council of Neocaesarea, canon 1: If a presbyter has committed fornication or adultery, let him be utterly cast out and brought to repentance. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechesis 2: If Manasseh, who had cut in pieces the prophet, was saved through repentance, will you, who have committed nothing of the kind, not be saved? Take care not to distrust in vain the power of repentance. Would you know how great the power of repentance is? Would you learn these strong weapons of salvation, and how much confession prevails over many? Hezekiah, by confession, had put to flight a hundred and eighty thousand enemies. That is indeed a great thing, but small nonetheless compared with what must still be said. The same man, by repentance, revoked a divine sentence that had been pronounced. For Isaiah had said to him when he was sick: Set your house in order, for you shall die and not live. What expectation, what hope of salvation remained after the prophet had said that you would die? But Hezekiah did not refrain from repentance; and, remembering what is written, When you turn and groan, then you shall be saved, etc. Gregory of Nyssa, Oration against those who judge others too harshly and bitterly: For what else is repentance but the dissolution and overthrow of past things, whether admitted in deed or in thought? But he who, though he knows the usefulness of repentance, still wallows in the mire of crimes and impiety, is like that servant who, knowing his lord to be angry with him, behaves wickedly in his sight and doubles his sin. I will not report more. Still to be read on repentance are the sermons of the ancient Fathers: the works of Tertullian, Basil of Caesarea, Ephraem the Syrian, Ambrose of Milan, and John Chrysostom, which will supply you with more on this subject.

units.la: De Confessione auriculari, & expressione peccatorum singulorum egimus in Hottingero; quod eodem modo atque Græci exequuntur Pontificij. Et hæc est vera concordia, quam non convellit, neque quæstus Pontificius, neque intermissio Consessionis Sacerdotum Græcorum, neque alia singularia hominum dubia, cum concordia plurium fit, non unius, vel alterius disputantis, aut contendentis. Et cum dicit Latinus Confessionem exercendam absque quæstu, neque debito tempore intermittendam, & Græcus etiam hoc dicit, non soluit consensum, si quis parere dedignans hic quæstum inhiat, ille Confessionem intermittit: Neque enim omnes in Ecclesia præceptis Ecclesiasticis semper obediunt. Et quis animis rebellibus modum con-stituet? Raro tamen antecedentem scelestum deseruit pœna pede claudo, aiebat ille, cum ob simile delictum, sicut etiam alia a Deo, vel hominibus tarde, vel cito pœnæ expetantur.
units.tr: We have treated auricular confession and the enumeration of individual sins in Hottinger, where the Papists carry them out in the same way as the Greeks. This is the true agreement, which is not shaken either by the Papal profit-seeking, or by the Greek priests' omission of confession, or by other individual doubts of men. For agreement belongs to the many, not to one or another disputant or contender. When the Latin says that confession is to be practised without profit and not to be omitted at the proper time, and the Greek says this too, the agreement is not broken if one man, disdaining to obey, pursues profit here while another omits confession. For not all in the Church always obey the ecclesiastical precepts. And who will set a limit to rebellious minds? Yet, as that man used to say, punishment, though lame of foot, seldom abandons the wicked who went before, since for a similar offence both God and men seek punishments for other things too, sometimes late and sometimes soon.

units.la: De Extrema unctione Verba illa Iacobi: Si quis infirmatur, vocet Presbyteros Ecclesiæ, & imponant ei manus, ungentes eum oleo in nomine Domini, & oratio Fidei salvabit infirmum, etsi in peccatis fuerit, remittentur ei. De infirmitate corporali accipiunt Ioannes Chrysostomus, Cyrillus Alexandrinus, Victor Antiochenus, Augustinus Sermone 214. de tempore; Quoties aliqua infirmitas superuenerit, corpus, & sanguinem Christi ille, qui aegrotat, accipiat, & inde corpusculum suum vngat, vt illud, quod scriptum est, impleatur in eo; Infirmatur aliquis. &c. Videte fratres, quia qui in infirmitate ad Ecclesiam cucurrerit, & corporis sanitatem recipere, & peccatorum indulgentiam merebitur obtinere. Idem lib. 2. de Visitatione infirmorum cap. 4. Nec praetermittendum est illud Apostoli Iacobi praeceptum, Infirmatur quis in vobis? &c. Ergo sic roges de te, & pro te fieri, sicut dixit Apostolus Iacobus, imo per Apostolum suum Dominus: ipsa videlicet olei sacrati delibutio intelligitur Spiritus sancti typicalis vnctio. Idem in Tractatu de rectitudine Catholicae conuersationis; Quoties aliquid infirmitas occurrerit alicui, non quaerantur praecantatores, non diuini, non sortilegi, non carcarij, neq; per sontes, aut arbores, aut biuia Phylacteria exerceantur: sed qui aegrotat in sola Dei misericordia confidat, & Eucharistiam cum fide, & deuotione accipiat, oleumque benedictum fideliter ab Ecclesia petat, vnde corpus suum vngatur, & secundum Apostolum, oratio Fidei saluabit infirmum, & alleuabit eum Dominus, non solum corporis, sed & animæ sanitatem accipiet.
units.tr: On extreme unction: the words of James, If any man is sick, let him call for the elders of the Church, and let them lay their hands upon him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord, and the prayer of faith shall save the sick man; and if he has committed sins, they shall be forgiven him, are taken of bodily sickness by John Chrysostom, Cyril of Alexandria, Victor of Antioch, and Augustine in Sermon 214 on the time: As often as any sickness comes upon someone, let the one who is ill receive the body and blood of Christ, and let him anoint his little body with it, so that what is written may be fulfilled in him: Is anyone sick? etc. See, brothers, that whoever in sickness runs to the Church shall deserve to receive bodily health and to obtain forgiveness of sins. The same in book 2, On the Visitation of the Sick, chapter 4: Nor is that precept of the Apostle James to be passed over, Is anyone among you sick? etc. So let him ask, and let prayer be made for him, as the Apostle James said, or rather the Lord through his Apostle: that is, the very anointing with consecrated oil is understood as the typical anointing of the Holy Spirit. The same in his Treatise on the Uprightness of Catholic Conduct: As often as any sickness befalls anyone, let them not seek enchanters, diviners, sorcerers, or charmers, nor practise anything through trees, springs, or phylacteries; but let the one who is sick trust in the mercy of God alone, receive the Eucharist with faith and devotion, and faithfully ask the Church for blessed oil, with which his body may be anointed, and, according to the Apostle, the prayer of faith shall save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up, and he shall receive health not only of body but also of soul.

units.la: De Ordine. Origenes Homilia 7. in Ieremiam; Utilitas quippe Clericatus, non in eo est, si aliquis in agmine sedeat Presbyterorum, sed si iuxta locum suum, & iuxta præcepta Domini dignus incedat. Plus a me exigitur, quam a Diacono, plus a Diacono, quam a Laico. Qui vero totius Ecclesiæ arcem obtinet, pro omni Ecclesia reddet rationem. Concilium Ancyranum Can. 13. Chorepiscopis non licet Diaconos ordinare, sed nec Presbyteris ciuitatis sine præcepto Episcopi, vel literis in unaquaque Parochia aliquid imperare. Gregorius Nyssenus Oratione de S. Baptismate; Eadem etiam verbi vis Sacerdotem angustum, & venerandum facit, nouitate benedictionis a communitate vulgi segregatum. Cum enim heri, ac tempore superiori unus e multitudine ac plebe esset, repente redditur præceptor, præses, doctor pietatis, mysteriorum latentium Præsul, eaque contingunt eo, cum nihil vel corpore, vel forma mutatus: sed quod ad speciem externam attinet, ille sit qui erat, inuisibili quadam vi, & gratia inuisibilem animam in melius transformatam gerens. Ioannes Chrysostomus lib. 3. de Sacerdotio; Sacerdotium in terra peragitur, sed in rerum cœlestium classem ordinemque referendum est. Atque id per quam merito: quippe non mortalis quispiam, non Angelus, non Archangelus, non alia quaevis creata potentia, sed ipse Paracletus eiusmodi ordinem disposuit. &c.
units.tr: On Order. Origen, Homily 7 on Jeremiah: For the usefulness of the clerical office does not lie in a man's sitting in the ranks of the presbyters, but in his walking worthily in his own place and according to the precepts of the Lord. More is required of me than of a deacon, more of a deacon than of a layman. But he who holds the stronghold of the whole Church will render account for the whole Church. The Council of Ancyra, canon 13: Country bishops may not ordain deacons, nor may they, without the bishop's command or letters, order anything in any parish, even as presbyters of a city. Gregory of Nyssa, in his oration On Holy Baptism: The very force of the word also makes the priest reverend and venerable, set apart from the common crowd of the people by the newness of the blessing. For though yesterday, and in earlier time, he was one of the multitude and the common people, suddenly he is made a teacher, a president, a doctor of piety, and a leader in the hidden mysteries; and this happens to him though he has changed nothing in body or form, but as regards outward appearance is the same man as before, bearing by some invisible power and grace an invisible soul transformed for the better. John Chrysostom, book 3 On the Priesthood: The priesthood is carried on upon earth, but it is to be referred to the order and rank of heavenly things. And this with good reason: for no mortal, no angel, no archangel, no other created power whatever, but the Paraclete himself, has established such an order. Etc.

units.la: Cyprianus de Cardinalibus Christi operibus; Docemur, quae fit Baptismi, & aliorum Sacramentorum stabilitas. Nam Baptismum repeti Ecclesiastica prohibent regulae, & semel sanctificatis, nulla deinceps manus iterum consecrans praesumit accedere; nemo sacros ordines semel datos iterum renovat: nemo sacro oleo lita iterum linit, aut consecrat: nemo impositioni manuum, vel ministerio derogat Sacerdotum.
units.tr: Cyprian, On the Cardinal Works of Christ: We are taught how stable Baptism and the other Sacraments are. For the rules of the Church forbid Baptism to be repeated, and once it has been sanctified, no hand that consecrates again presumes to approach; no one renews holy orders once given; no one anoints again with holy oil, or consecrates; no one detracts from the laying on of hands or from the ministry of the priests.

units.la: Augustinus lib. 1. de Baptismo contra Donatistas. Sacramentum Baptismi est, quod habet, qui baptizatur, & Sacramentum dandi Baptismi est, quod habet, qui ordinatur. Sicut autem baptizatus, si ab unitate recesserit, Sacramentum Baptismi non amittit, sic etiam ordinatus, si ab unitate recesserit, Sacramentum dandi Baptismi non amittit. Nulli enim Sacramento iniuria facienda est. Si discedit a malis, utrumque discedit; si permanet in malis, utrumque permanent.
units.tr: Augustine, book 1 On Baptism against the Donatists: The Sacrament of Baptism is what the one who is baptized has, and the Sacrament of giving Baptism is what the one who is ordained has. Just as a baptized man, if he has departed from unity, does not lose the Sacrament of Baptism, so also an ordained man, if he has departed from unity, does not lose the Sacrament of giving Baptism. For no injury is to be done to any Sacrament. If he departs from evil, both depart; if he remains in evil, both remain.

units.la: De Matrimonio. Clemens Alexandrinus lib. 3. Stromatum; Quod si lex sancta est, sanctum est matrimonium, Sacramentum ergo ad hoc Christum, & Ecclesiam ducit Apostolus. Quemadmodum, quod ex carne generatur, caro est: ita quod ex Spiritu spiritus, non solum inpariendo, sed etiam in discendo. Jam sancti sunt filij, Deo gratae oblationes verborum Dominicorum, quae desponderunt animam. Athanasius sermone contra omnes Haereticos; Nunquid auscultas in Euangelio Dominum in Cana ad nuptias vocatum, easque benedixisse, & ex aqua vinum fecisse? & rursus alibi Judaeis dicentibus, sibi Mosen concessisse libellum repudij, Christum respondere, quos Deus coniunxit, homo non separet? Quomodo potest ramus consistere, si non subsit radix? Quomodo virgo esse potuerit, si non habeat patrem, & matrem? Similia habet Epiphanius Haeresi 67. Vide de hac eadem re Methodij Martyris Symposium decem Virginum, & nuper a nobis editum Graece & Latine, & Gregorium Nyssenum de Virginitate. Tertullianus de Monogamia cap. 5. Christus unam habens Ecclesiam sponsam, secundum Adae & Eua figuram, quam Apostolus in illud magnum Sacramentum interpretatur in Christum & Ecclesiam competisse. Plura hic etiam ex Patribus possent produci pro septenario numero Sacramentorum, & illorum antiquitate in Ecclesia, sed ista in Sacramentorum, numero, & eorum quoque antiquitate in Ecclesia Latina & Graeca, ut consensus colligatur, sufficiunt. In quibus, cum totus orbis Christianus Occidens & Oriens hactenus consenserunt, contra disputare infolentissimæ insaniæ effet. Præsertim, cum nullum in antiquitate vestigium appareat, quo tempore unum ex his Sacramentis de novo in Ecclesiam introductum, & institutum fuerit: ideoque eorum origo ad prima tempora, Christi scilicet institutionem, & Apostolorum promulgationem referenda est. Neque refert, quod nuspiam apud Patres antiquiores expresse eorum numerus septenarius legatur: neque enim illis erat propositum Sacramentorum numerum recolligere, cum neque in dubium vocarentur; ideoque recensebant Sacramenta modo plura, modo pauciora suo instituto inseruientia. Sic frequentissime apud eos reperitur trium Sacramentorum Baptismi, Confirmationis, & Eucharistiæ commemoratio, quia hæc cuilibet ad Ecclesiam Christi recepto, & ad illius consecrationem, atque perfectionem magis necessaria, & ordine quodam conferebantur, ut videre est ex supra adductis.
units.tr: On Marriage. Clement of Alexandria, book 3 of the Stromata: If the law is holy, then marriage is holy; the Apostle therefore leads this Sacrament to Christ and the Church. As what is born of the flesh is flesh, so what is born of the Spirit is spirit, not only in begetting but also in teaching. Now the children are holy, pleasing offerings to God of the words of the Lord, which have betrothed the soul. Athanasius, in a sermon against all heretics: Do you not hear in the Gospel that the Lord was called to the wedding at Cana, and blessed them, and made wine from water? And again elsewhere, when the Jews said that Moses had granted them a bill of divorce, Christ answered: What God has joined together, let no man put asunder? How can a branch stand, if it has no root? How could a virgin have been, if she had no father and mother? Epiphanius has similar things in Heresy 67. See on this same matter the Symposium of the Ten Virgins by the martyr Methodius, recently published by us in Greek and Latin, and Gregory of Nyssa On Virginity. Tertullian, On Monogamy, chapter 5: Christ, having one Church as his bride, according to the figure of Adam and Eve, which the Apostle interprets as applying to Christ and the Church in that great Sacrament. Many more passages from the Fathers could be brought forward here for the septenary number of the Sacraments and their antiquity in the Church; but those cited suffice to gather the consensus concerning the number of the Sacraments and their antiquity in the Latin and Greek Church. Since the whole Christian world, West and East, has so far agreed on these, to dispute against them would be the height of most insolent madness. Especially since no trace appears in antiquity of any time when one of these Sacraments was newly introduced into the Church and instituted; and therefore their origin must be referred to the earliest times, namely to Christ's institution and the Apostles' promulgation. Nor does it matter that nowhere in the earlier Fathers is their septenary number expressly read; for it was not their purpose to collect the number of the Sacraments, since these were not called in doubt. Therefore they listed the Sacraments sometimes more and sometimes fewer, as suited their purpose. Thus among them the mention of the three Sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist is found very frequently, because these were conferred on anyone received into the Church of Christ, and were more necessary for his consecration and perfection, and in a certain order, as may be seen from what has been cited above.

units.la: Sed de septenario Sacramentorum numero recentiorum tamen Græcorum dogma est. Septenariam illam Sacramentorum divisionem nullus tradidit, nec diligentissimus Goar ullum eius auctorem, vel testem edit Simeone Thessalonicensi, & Matthæo Blastari vetustiorem. Quidquid alij dixerint . Sit nouum Græcorum dogma; nulla apud Græcos Septenarij ante millesimum mentio habeatur. Concludo fecundum Dallæum, ab anno millesimo, ad hæc tempora in hoc numero Sacramentorum inter Græcos, & Latinos consensionem fuisse, & contra Chemnitium pro Arcudio. ante Florentinam Synodum nos proferimus Synodum antiquiorem, in qua septenarius iste numerus digestus est; modus item dicta Sacramenta administrandi, ex antiquorum Conciliorum, Patrumq; scriptis collectus describitur. Ea est Synodus Cypria sub Germano Amathuntis Episcopo,ac summi Græcorum in Insula Cypri Antistitis Anno Domini 1260. inter viuos agentis. Probant hæc hunc septenarium numerum Sacramentorum Simeone Theffalonicensi, & Matthæo Blastari multo antiquiorem esse, & ante millesimum ex Codice Euchologij Patriarchali vetustissimo, qui anno octingentesimo eruditorum omnium iudicio, & antiquitatis peritissimorum scriptus, literarum ipsarum forma tractuq; & multis aliis deprehenditur,ex Bibliotheca S.Marci Florentini in Bibliothecam amplissimam Cardinalis Barberini translatus, & cuique obuius propositus, cui ipse non absimilia, & multo etiam vetustiora in Monachorū Monafterijs obseruaui, quorum ob vetustatem literæ, vt plurimum exciderunt. Et vt plurimum, subdis, Synodice sub Cyrillo Berrhoensi, & Parthenio ratum esse iubeant, nihilo tamen seriùs in plurimis ijsque substantialibus, tam longe a Latinis dissentire, vt non sine tædio altercationes, & conciliationes in scriptis Arcudij, Allatij, Goaris legas, quos ea propter optimo iure perstringit Dallæus. Id primo probandum erat, quod de more silentio prætereuehitur, in plurimis ijsque substantialibus longe a Latinis dissentire, quod cum non probauerit Dallæus pessimo iure perstringit memoratos viros. Pontificij quoq; multis se quæstionibus, & altercationibus exagitant in materia Sacramentorum, sed cum numerum integrum seruant, & substantialia non destruant, laudem sibi nanciscuntur inter Catholicos, tantum abest, vt a Pontificijs dissentire reputentur. Sed Allatij altercationes in scriptis Arcudij, & Goaris. Neq; Arcudius, neq; Allatius, neque Goar etiam post mille annos efficient, substantialia non esse substantialia, & contra. Et mirum est homines, qui Theologiæ vel minimam operam navant, inter ea discrimen ad hunc diem non agnoscere.
units.tr: But the septenary number of the Sacraments is the dogma of the more recent Greeks. No one has handed down that septenary division; nor has the most diligent Goar published any author or witness of it earlier than Simeon of Thessalonica and Matthew Blastares. Whatever others have said, let it be the new dogma of the Greeks; no mention of a septenary is found among the Greeks before the year one thousand. I conclude, following Dallaeus, that from the year one thousand to these times there was agreement between Greeks and Latins on this number of the Sacraments; and against Chemnitz, on behalf of Arcudius, we produce an older Synod before the Florentine Synod, in which this septenary number was set out; likewise the manner of administering the said Sacraments is described, collected from the writings of the ancient Councils and Fathers. This is the Synod of Cyprus under Germanus, bishop of Amathus and the highest prelate of the Greeks in the island of Cyprus, in the year of the Lord 1260, while he was still living. These things prove that this septenary number of the Sacraments is much older than Simeon of Thessalonica and Matthew Blastares, and before the year one thousand, from the very ancient Euchologion manuscript of the Patriarchate, which was written in the year 800, by the judgement of all learned men and of the most expert in antiquity, as is shown by the form and style of the letters and by many other signs; it was transferred from the Library of St Mark at Florence into the very ample Library of Cardinal Barberini, and is laid open to anyone who meets it. To this I myself have observed not dissimilar, and even much older, manuscripts in the monasteries of monks, whose letters for the most part have perished through age. And for the most part, you add, the Synodicon under Cyril of Berrhoea and Parthenius bids it be held as valid, yet no less late in very many and those substantial matters, the Greeks dissent so far from the Latins that one cannot read the disputes and reconciliations in the writings of Arcudius, Allatius, and Goar without weariness, whom Dallaeus rightly and justly takes to task. This was the first thing to be proved, which is by custom passed over in silence: that in very many and those substantial matters the Greeks dissent far from the Latins. Since Dallaeus has not proved it, he takes those men to task on the worst grounds. The Papists too harass themselves with many questions and disputes on the matter of the Sacraments; but since they keep the full number and do not overturn the substantial matters, they win praise for themselves among the Catholics, so far is it from the case that they are reckoned to dissent from the Papists. But the disputes of Allatius in the writings of Arcudius and Goar. Neither Arcudius, nor Allatius, nor Goar, even after a thousand years, will make the non-substantial into the substantial, or the reverse. And it is strange that men who devote even the smallest effort to theology do not to this day recognise the distinction between these things.

units.la: De alijs capitibus, nempe, Idololatria, Artolatria, Oenolatria, Staurolatria, Hagiolatria, Angelolatria, Lipsanolatria, & præcipue Mariolatria, Monopolio Episcopali in electione ministrorum Ecclesiæ, Libero arbitrio, immani elogio vitæ Monasticæ, ac denique transubstantiatione, Parua ne sunt hæc? Auctore opponente, Ecclesia Græca & Latina eadem sentiunt, & explanationem Græcæ & Latinæ Ecclesiæ consensionem exquirimus? Fides est certa, atq; indubitata, & ambarum una. Quid enim refert si in tanta hominum turba, & magno fidelium numero idem sentientium, & enuntiantium unus aliquis sit adeo pervicax, & perdita mente, ut etiam Salvatoris imaginem Latinis tantum inscriptam literis adorare renuat, & a sculptilibus, tanquam ab Idolis abhorreat? Quod damnum unioni afferre potest, si alius atque alius, dum Sacerdos munera non dum consecrata, sed consecranda adoret, etiam adoratione latriæ, dicatque, Memento mei Domine, cum veneris in regno tuo, Annon etiam apud Pontificios a quibusdam docetur, munera consecranda ante consecrationem adoratione latriæ posse coli? Quid si de ligno Crucis nugaces homines alia, atque alia garriunt? Quid si Græci [illegible, ~13 letters] nuncupantur? Quid si ministrans Sacerdos sacratissimam Virginem invocat? Quid si stultus quispiam sub illa particula, quam dicunt παναγίαν[?] corpus B. Mariæ contineri credat? Quid si pluribus apud Græcos, illisque præstantissimis Maria sanctissima innotescit? Quid si excluditur plebs, & Magistratus ciuilis in electione ministrorum Ecclesiæ? Quid si Ieremias Patriarcha nihil, quod obiectiones Tubigenses ferìat, asserat? Quid immane elogium vitæ Monasticæ? Quid si tria, aut quatuor sint Monachorum genera? Quid si in recipiendis iuuenibus a nonnullis sciolis præuaricentur Canones? Quid si a quibusdam eadem vis tribuatur peccata dimittendi habitui Monachico, & Baptismo? Quid si Schismatici sunt in monte Atho, eoque laudatissimo? Quid si panem consecratum pretiosissimum corpus Christi in muro appendunt, & non sine veneratione conseruant? Quid si verbis transubstantiationis, alias quoque preces adnectunt, verbis Domini inuiolatis seruatis? Quid si Chemnitius dicit,antiquitatem non facere pro transubstantiatione, & fateatur ætate Damasceni, & Teophylacti factam? Quid tot aliæ ex cœnosa colluuie ineptiæ recollectæ?
units.tr: Concerning the other chapters, namely idolatry, artolatry, oenolatry, staurolatry, hagiolatry, angelolatry, lipsanolatry, and above all mariolatry, the episcopal monopoly in the election of the ministers of the Church, free will, the monstrous praise of monastic life, and finally transubstantiation: Are these trifles? The objector says: do the Greek and Latin Churches agree on these points, and do we seek agreement between the Greek and Latin Churches? The faith is certain and undoubted, and one for both. For what does it matter if, in so great a crowd of people and a large number of believers who think and speak alike, some one man is so stubborn and so perverse in mind that he refuses to worship the image of the Saviour inscribed only in Latin letters, and shrinks from images carved in wood as if from idols? What harm can it do to unity if one priest or another, while adoring the gifts not yet consecrated but to be consecrated, even does so with the adoration of latria, and says, Remember me, Lord, when you come into your kingdom? Is it not taught by some even among the Papists that the gifts to be consecrated may be worshipped with the adoration of latria before consecration? What if foolish men chatter one thing and another about the wood of the Cross? What if the Greeks are called [illegible]? What if the minister at the altar invokes the most holy Virgin? What if some fool believes that the body of the blessed Mary is contained under that little particle which they call the Panagia [παναγίαν]? What if the most holy Mary is known to many among the Greeks, and to the most distinguished of them? What if the common people and the civil magistrate are shut out from the election of the ministers of the Church? What if Patriarch Jeremias asserts nothing that could strike at the Tübingen objections? What of the monstrous praise of monastic life? What if there are three or four kinds of monks? What if some half-learned men break the canons in admitting young men? What if some ascribe the same power of forgiving sins to the monastic habit as to baptism? What if the schismatics are on Mount Athos, that most praised mountain? What if they hang the consecrated bread, the most precious body of Christ, in a wall and keep it with no little veneration? What if they add other prayers to the words of transubstantiation, while keeping the words of the Lord unviolated? What if Chemnitz says that antiquity does not favour transubstantiation, and yet admits that it was made in the time of Damascene and Theophylact? What of so many other trifles gathered from that foul filth?

units.la: Meretur hoc loco castigationem cruenta Allatij vox, qua pronunciat. Haeretici negant, (scilicet, Crucem Christi ad nostra usque tempora servatam durare) quid ad nos? Negant Verbum Dei. &c. O calumniam. certe eorum amasiæ[?] sanguine, & ignibus expienda. Et quis calumniæ crimen inferet Allatio, dum legit in Luthero de Veteri testamento; Mosen neque audire, neque videre volumus: nam ille Iudaico solum populo datus est, neque quicquam ad nos pertinet. Si quis tibi Mosen cum suis legibus proponat, teque cogere volet, ut eas observes, tum dicas; Abi ad Iudaeos cum tuo Mose. Ego Iudaeus non sum. Ne me cum Mose involuas. Et; Mosem cum sua lege non suscipiam: Nam hostis Christi est. Et Moses omnium carnificum Magister est, conscientias dire agreditur, corda terret, torquet, lacerat. Et; Apage cum Mose ad pertinaces, ferosque homines, & superbos sanctos, quos terrefaciat, & humiliet. Et; Moses habuit labia, sed profana, infecunda, impedita, irata, in quibus non est verbum gratiæ, sed iræ, mortis, peccati. Colligite omnes sapientias Mosi, Gentium, Philosophorum, & inuenietis eas coram Deo esse vel Idolatriam, vel sapientiam hypocriticam, vel si est politica, sapientiam iræ. Et Sebastiano Castalione de Canticis Canticorum; Canticum illud esse colloquium Salomonis cum amica quadam Sulamitha. De scriptura, & Verbo Dei in genere, in Thoma Muncero. Scripturam æternumque Verbum, non esse verum Dei Verbum, sed solum testimonium veri Verbi: hoc autem internum & cœleste esse, & immediate ex ipso Dei ore prodire, & hoc interius docere oportere, non autem scripturis, & concionibus. In Dauide Georgio; Omnem doctrinam hactenus a Deo per Mosen, Prophetas, ipsum Iesum Christum, eiusque Apostolos, & Discipulos traditam esse mancam, imperfectam, & inutilem ad perfectam consequendam felicitatem: suam autem doctrinam perfectam esse, & efficacem ad hominem, qui eam susceperit, beandum, Gasparo Swenckfeldio; Deum non agere nobiscum per scripturas: & fidem nostram non debere dirigi iuxta sacram Scripturam, sed sacra Scriptura regatur iuxta fidem nostram. Scriptura est humana vox, sonitus, strepitus, & mortua litera. Et; Doctrina Euangelij est humanum Euangelium. Scriptura est incerta, & flexibilis doctrina, quæ patitur se in varios sensus trahi. Carolo Molinæo; Hæc verba limitant, vt tantum Christus audiatur, id est, verbum eius solius prædicetur: & cum ait Christus, qui vos audit, me audit, non loquitur de quibusuis verbis Apostolorum, sed de præscripto mandato legationis suæ. Plures hic similes Heterodoxorum blasphemiæ addi possent ad vindicandum Allatium a calumnia, sed hæ satis sint.
units.tr: The bloody remark of Allatius deserves rebuke in this place, in which he declares: "The heretics deny" (namely, that the Cross of Christ has survived to our own times). "What is that to us? They deny the Word of God," etc. O calumny! Surely it must be atoned for with the blood and fires of those lovers of theirs. And who will bring the charge of calumny against Allatius, when he reads in Luther about the Old Testament: "We do not want to hear or see Moses; for he was given only to the Jewish people, and nothing pertains to us. If anyone sets Moses with his laws before you and wants to compel you to observe them, then say: Go to the Jews with your Moses. I am not a Jew. Do not entangle me with Moses. And: I will not receive Moses with his law, for he is an enemy of Christ. Moses is the master of all executioners; he attacks consciences, terrifies hearts, tortures and tears them. And: Away with Moses and his stubborn, savage and proud men, whom he terrifies and humbles. And: Moses had lips, but profane, barren, halting and angry lips, in which there is no word of grace, but of wrath, death and sin. Gather all the wisdom of Moses, of the Gentiles and of the philosophers, and you will find that before God it is either idolatry, or hypocritical wisdom, or, if it is political, the wisdom of wrath." And with Sebastian Castellio on the Song of Songs: that that song is a conversation of Solomon with a certain lover, a Shulammite woman. On Scripture and the Word of God in general, in Thomas Müntzer: that Scripture and the eternal Word are not the true Word of God, but only a testimony to the true Word; that this true Word is inward and heavenly, and comes forth immediately from the very mouth of God, and that it ought to teach inwardly, not by Scriptures and sermons. In David Joris: that all doctrine hitherto delivered by God through Moses, the Prophets, Jesus Christ himself, and his Apostles and disciples is incomplete, imperfect, and useless for attaining perfect happiness; but that his own doctrine is perfect and effective for making blessed the man who receives it. To Caspar Schwenckfeld: that God does not deal with us through the Scriptures, and that our faith ought not to be directed according to holy Scripture, but holy Scripture ought to be governed according to our faith. Scripture is a human voice, a sound, a noise, and a dead letter. And: The doctrine of the Gospel is a human gospel. Scripture is an uncertain and pliable doctrine, which allows itself to be drawn into various senses. To Charles Dumoulin: These words limit things so that only Christ is heard, that is, that his word alone is preached; and when Christ says, "He who hears you hears me," he does not speak of any words of the Apostles whatever, but of the prescribed command of his own mission. Many similar blasphemies of the heterodox could be added here to clear Allatius of calumny, but these are enough.

units.la: Certe eorum ἀπίσια[?] sanguine, & ignibus expiauda. Mitius, mitius mi Allati, mansuesce quamlibet Leo fis. Propenso animo acquiescerem, & mitius agerem, & cum primis tecum. Etiam si velim non queo. Imperatores, Patres antiqui, recentiores, Concilia, ipsi quoque Schismatici, & Haeretici sanciunt poenas contumacibus, & ne in me offensionem tuam contraham, & me inclementius contra Haereticos verba facere conqueraris, audi. Constantinus Imperator apud Nicephorum Califtum lib. 8. cap. 25. Si quis libellum aliquem ab Ario conscriptum celare, nec continuo igni comburere deprehensus fuerit, supplicium et mortis esse constitutum. illico nanque in crimine tali comprehensus, poenam sustinebit capitalem. Theodosius, & Valentinianus Imperatores. Qui seruum, vel ingenuum invitum, seu sua sione fleCtendo excultu religionis Christianae in nefandam sectam utcunque transduxerit cum dispendio fortunarum capite puniendum esse censemus. Et; Manichaei de civitatibus pellantur, ac ultimo supplicio tradantur. Necnon; Illis etiam omnibus in sua manentibus firmitate, quae de militia poenisque variis, deque diversis sunt Haereticis promulgata, est nec speciale quidem beneficium adversus leges valeat impetratum. Sic; Cernet praeterea bona sua proscripta poena mox sanguinis destinandus, qui fidem alterius expugnavit perversa doctrina. &c, Valentinianus, &c. & Martianus AA. ad Palladium Præfectum Prætorij; Etiam supplicio coërceantur, qui illicita docere tentauerunt. Hoc idem decernit Cyrillus lib. 8. de Spiritu sancto, Procopius Gazæus in Exodum; Mors autem Hæreticis pœna statuitur, Etin Leuiticum; Eodem modo Hæretici condignam a Iudice sustinent mortem. Theodorus Lector narrat lib. 2. Theodoricum Afrum Diaconum suum Orthodoxum, & a se vehementer dilectum, cum gratificaturus Theodorico relicta Catholica Fide cum Arianis consensisset, confestim capite truncauisse. Cyprianus de exhortatione Martyrij; Cuius præcepti, & vigoris memor Mathathias interfecit eum, qui ad arcam sacrificaturus accesserat, quod si ante aduentum Christi circa Deum colendum, & Idola spernenda hæc præcepta seruata sunt, quanto magis post aduentum Christi seruanda sunt. Optatus Milevitanus lib. 3. respondens calumniæ Hæreticorum, qui ægerrime ferebant, duos ex suis a Macario Præfecto interfectos esse. Videtis, inquit, a Mose, & Phinees, & Helia, & Macario similia esse facta, quia ab omnibus unius Dei præcepta sunt vindicata. Sed Leo dicit, ignibus quoque esse expiandos. Dixit. Sed ante ipsum dixerunt alij. Rheginus Cyprius Homilia Ephesi habita post exauctoratum Nestorium: Enim vero ad manifestam impietatis tuæ redargutionem ante cum pascua adhuc erant, que ausus es, igni terraque hiatu, teque, tuosque conatus compescere debebamus. Euagrius Histor. lib. 5. cap. 18. Hæreticos quosdam populus diuino quodam zelo incensus, naui piscatoria impositos viuos ignis tradidit incendio. Ioannes Damascenus Dialogo aduersus Manichæos. Non Manichæos morte afficimus, non flammis absumimus ? Ioannes Zonaras in Historia; Alexius Comnenus Basilium professione medicum, habitu monachum, Bogomilorum nefariæ sectæ auctorem, deprehensum communi suffragio in equestri Theatro comburi iussit. Cæsarius Heisterbachius lib. 5. cap. 19. Sub Ar-noldo Colonia plures sunt Hæretici comprehensi, qui a literatis viris examinati, & victi per iudicium seculare damnati sunt, & data sententia duƈti ad ignem. Nec mitiora sunt, quæ tradunt Hæretici tui. Philippus Melanchthon Disputatione de delirijs, & furoribus Anabaptistarum; Cum Anabaptistæ palam sint seditiosi, Magistratus publice eos coërcere, ac punire tanquam latrones debent. Theodorus Beza lib. de Hæreticis a ciuili magistratu puniendis. Sed qua pœna fit scelus hoc (hæreseos) vindicandum, quorsum attinet obsecro hu-manis coniecturis probare, cum plura, & aperta testimonijs in verbo ipsius legantur. Sic enim ait, ait, qui sacrificat diis alienis, praeter quam soli Deo, morietur. &c. Budnæus Ebionita Trinitarius Annotationibus in nouum Testamentum, cuius sententiæ fuerit Beza & Calvinus aperte docuit; Ipse miser Beza in hoc Diabolo seruiet, non Erasmus, qui manifestam veritatem conatur extinguere, & falsitatem sustinere, qui etiam cum Antichristo Romano seruos Dei interfecit, sicut ante annos aliquot Valentinum Gentilem virum pium, & accuratum diuinæ veritatis indagatorem ad supplicium adegit, & paulo ante Calvinus præceptor eius Michaelem Seruetum. Conradus Scluffelburgius lib. 2. Catalogo Hæreticorum de Seruetianis narrat ex actis publicis; Michael Servetus deprehensus Genevæ, carceri mancipatus, atque ad dicendum causam postulatus est. Calvino eum de impijs Dogmatibus accusante, vt idem met Calvinus in sua defensione recenset, cum perseueraret in hæresi à Senatu Genevensi, consultis Helueticis ministris, pronunciauit, eum capitis supplicio afficiendum esse: cum in erroribus obstinatus perstitisset, igni traditur anno 1555. Sed libet hic exscribere historiam supplicij Valentini Gentilis Trinitarij, quam refert idem Conradus ex Actis editis a Benedicto Aretio Bernensis Ecclesiæ Pastore, Tandem Valentinus Gentilis de horrendissimis in Deum blasphemijs de diffeminatis manifestis, ac perniciosis erroribus, de seditiosis turbis & de periurio iudicium sententia pronunciatur, vt ad præcauenda dissidia, & eliminandos tam tetros errores capite plecteretur. Ductus igitur ad supplicium, pertinax in errore perseueraut, & subinde gloriatus est, more omnium hæresiarcharum, & falsorum Doctorum se pro gloria altissimi Dei pati. donec capite plexus, & viuere, & blasphemias in Deum euomere maledico ore desineret. Ioannes quoque Syluanus Gentilis huiusce hæresifeos sectator capitali supplicio affectus est. Et similes poenas ab Hæreticis expetendis laudat Philippus Melanchthon in locis communibus Manlij cap. de Ecclesia; Senatus Geneuensis rectè fecit, quod blasphemum hominem Seruetum interfecit. Est enim vnum ex præcipuis officijs Magistratus, facere executionem corporalibus pœnis contra deprauatores prima, & secunda Tabula; quando aliquis colit Idola, & Diabolicum venenum in homines infundit. Tunc Magistratus iuste facit, si eum tollit: quia mandatum Dei est, vt textus seuere præcepit; Ne parcas ei. Debet esse nemesis, & sæua diligentia. Qua ergo ratione adhortaris Allatium, vt contra Leges, Canones, decreta Conciliorum, & Patrum, ipsorum etiam Schismaticorum, & Hæreticorum præscripta, cum Hæreticis mitius agat. Non est id in mea potestate. Quæ fieri possunt impera. Concludo. Mihi sane non videtur, nescio an & tibi, quod sit factum lege diuina, rescindi posse ab Allatio. Deuteron. 13. Quod si rogauerit te frater tuus, aut filius tuus, aut filia tua, &c. latenter dicens: Eamus, & seruiamus Diis gentium, non consenties ei, & non exaudies eum, & non parcet oculus tuus super eum, & non celabis eum, annuncians annunciabis de illo: manus tua erit super eum in primis, interficere eum, & manus omnis populi: postremo & lapidabunt eum, & morietur: quoniam quæsiuit auertere te a Domino Deo tuo, &c. Sed hic non est sermo de Hæreticis, sed de ijs, qui ad Idolorum cultum, Christianum seducendo conuertunt. Hoc vero idem est: & ad Idolorum cultum ex Christiana religione conuertere hominem, & ex recta fidei regula ad hæreticorum prauas opiniones. Marcellinus ad Imper. Valentin. Theod. & Arcad. epist.; Et ad maiorem iam incaluit insaniam impietas, tum facile strage multitudinis, non hoc minus sacrilegii est, non hæc minor impietas, quam si sub persecutore gentili Idolo sacrificatum esset, quia & in hæresi perterritum subscribere, Dæmoniis sacrificare. Et siquidem docentibus Scripturis, doctrina Dæmoniorum est hæresis, sicut & Idolatria. Inique ergo a me, quod præceptum est diuinis, atq; humanis legibus, rescindi postulas.
units.tr: Surely their unbelief [ἀπιστία] must be expiated with blood and fire. Gentler, gentler, my Allatius, be mild, though you are a lion. I would gladly agree and treat them more mildly, and above all you, but even if I wished to, I cannot. Emperors, the Fathers, both earlier and later, Councils, and the schismatics and heretics themselves all decree punishments for the obstinate. So that you may not say I am harsher against heretics than I should be, hear this. The Emperor Constantine, in Nicephorus Callistus, book 8, chapter 25: If anyone is found to have concealed a little book written by Arius, and not to have burned it straightaway in the fire, the penalty of death is laid down for him; for whoever is caught in such a crime will suffer capital punishment at once. The Emperors Theodosius and Valentinian: We decree that whoever leads a slave or a freeborn person, against his will or by his own bending, from the worship of the Christian religion into any abominable sect, shall be punished by death with the loss of his property. And: Manichaeans are to be driven from the cities and handed over to the final punishment. Again: For all those who remain firm in their position, the regulations promulgated against heretics concerning military service and various penalties, no special privilege obtained against the laws shall avail. So also: Moreover, whoever has tried to overthrow another's faith by a perverse doctrine shall see his goods confiscated, and he himself shall soon be destined for the shedding of blood. Etc. Valentinian, etc., and the Emperors Martian and Augustus to Palladius, Praetorian Prefect: Even those who have attempted to teach unlawful things are to be restrained by punishment. Cyril, book 8 on the Holy Spirit, decrees the same, and Procopius of Gaza on Exodus: Death is appointed as the penalty for heretics. And on Leviticus: In the same way, heretics suffer the death they deserve at the judge's hands. Theodorus the Lector relates in book 2 that Theodoric, when he wished to do a favour to Theodoric the Arian, cut off the head of his own deacon Afer, an orthodox man whom he loved greatly, because Afer had left the Catholic Faith and gone over to the Arians. Cyprian, On the Exhortation to Martyrdom: Mindful of this command and its force, Mattathias killed the man who had come up to sacrifice at the altar. If these precepts were kept before the coming of Christ, concerning the worship of God and the rejection of idols, how much more must they be kept after the coming of Christ. Optatus of Milevis, book 3, answering the slander of the heretics, who were very bitter that two of their men had been killed by the prefect Macarius: You see, he says, that similar things were done by Moses, Phinehas, Elijah and Macarius, because these precepts were avenged by all for the sake of the one God. But Leo says that they must also be expiated by fire. He said it; but others said it before him. Rhegius of Cyprus, in a homily delivered at Ephesus after Nestorius was deposed: Indeed, for the manifest refutation of your impiety, while the pastures were still there, you who dared such things ought to have been restrained by fire and by the opening of the earth, and you and your attempts should have been checked. Evagrius, Ecclesiastical History, book 5, chapter 18: The people, inflamed with a certain divine zeal, placed some heretics alive on a fishing boat and handed them over to the fire to be burned. John Damascene, in the Dialogue against the Manichaeans: Do we not put the Manichaeans to death, do we not consume them with flames? John Zonaras in his History: Alexius Comnenus, when he had caught Basil, a physician by profession and a monk in dress, the author of the wicked sect of the Bogomils, ordered him to be burned in the horse-racing arena by common consent. Caesarius of Heisterbach, book 5, chapter 19: Under Arnold, many heretics were apprehended at Cologne; examined by learned men and convicted, they were condemned by secular judgment, and once sentence was given they were led to the fire. What your heretics hand down is no milder. Philip Melanchthon, in the Disputation on the Madness and Frenzies of the Anabaptists: Since the Anabaptists are openly seditious, the magistrate ought publicly to restrain and punish them like robbers. Theodore Beza, in his book on heretics to be punished by the civil magistrate: But by what punishment this crime of heresy is to be avenged, I beg you, what is the point of proving it by human conjectures, when more and plainer testimonies are read in the Word itself? For thus he says: he who sacrifices to other gods, besides to the Lord alone, shall die, etc. Budaeus, the Trinitarian Ebionite, in his Notes on the New Testament, clearly taught whose opinion Beza and Calvin shared: Wretched Beza himself will serve the devil in this, not Erasmus, who tries to extinguish the manifest truth and to uphold falsehood, who together with the Roman Antichrist has also killed the servants of God, as some years ago he drove to execution Valentine Gentile, a pious man and a careful investigator of divine truth, and shortly before him Calvin, his teacher, did the same to Michael Servetus. Konrad Schlüsselburg, book 2 of the Catalogue of Heretics, on the Servetians, relates from the public records: Michael Servetus was apprehended at Geneva, put in prison, and called upon to plead his case. Calvin accused him of impious dogmas, as Calvin himself recounts in his defence. When he persisted in heresy, the Senate of Geneva, having consulted the Helvetic ministers, pronounced that he was to be punished by execution. As he remained obstinate in his errors, he was handed over to the fire in the year 1555. But it is worth copying here the account of the execution of the Trinitarian Valentine Gentile, which the same Konrad gives from the records published by Benedict Aretius, pastor of the Church of Bern: At last sentence was pronounced against Valentine Gentile for most horrible blasphemies against God, for spreading manifest and pernicious errors, for seditious tumults and for perjury, that he should be punished by death, so as to prevent dissensions and to root out such foul errors. Led therefore to the execution, he persisted obstinately in his error, and, after the manner of all heresiarchs and false teachers, he boasted that he suffered for the glory of the Most High God, until, beheaded, he ceased with his cursing mouth to live and to vomit blasphemies against God. John Silvanus Gentile, a follower of this heresy, was also subjected to capital punishment. Philip Melanchthon, in the Loci communes of Manlius, chapter on the Church, praises similar penalties to be sought against heretics: the Senate of Geneva acted rightly in killing the blasphemer Servetus. For it is one of the chief duties of the magistrate to carry out bodily punishments against the corrupters of the first and second Tables, when someone worships idols and pours diabolical poison into men. Then the magistrate acts justly if he removes such a man, because it is God's command, as the text strictly orders: Thou shalt not spare him. There must be vengeance and unrelenting diligence. Why then do you urge Allatius to treat heretics more mildly, contrary to the laws, canons, decrees of Councils and Fathers, and the prescriptions even of the schismatics and heretics themselves? That is not in my power. Command what can be done. I conclude. It does not seem to me, nor I think to you, that what has been done by divine law can be annulled by Allatius. Deuteronomy 13: If your brother, or your son, or your daughter, etc., entice you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve the gods of the nations, you shall not consent to him nor listen to him, and your eye shall not spare him, nor shall you conceal him, but you shall surely reveal him; your hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and the hand of all the people afterwards; and they shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, etc. But this passage is not speaking of heretics, but of those who, by seducing a Christian, turn him to the worship of idols. Yet it is the same thing to turn a man from the Christian religion to the worship of idols, and from the right rule of faith to the wicked opinions of heretics. Marcellinus, in his letter to the Emperors Valentinian, Theodosius and Arcadius: And when impiety has grown into a still greater madness, then the slaughter of a multitude is no less a sacrilege, no less an impiety, than if sacrifice had been offered to an idol under a pagan persecutor, because to subscribe to heresy in terror is to sacrifice to demons. And indeed, as the Scriptures teach, the doctrine of demons is heresy, just as idolatry is. Therefore you unjustly demand that what has been commanded by divine and human laws be annulled by me.

units.la: Trina immersionis in Baptismo mandatum. Salis usus in Baptismo. Chrismatis immediata cum Baptismo coniunctio. Panis azymi necessitas. Suffocati abstinentia judaizans praecepta. Grana aquae calidae in sacro Calice jam consecrato. Ieiunij praecipue quadragesimalis non sine reprehensione rigidior celebratio. Hæc plane adiaphora sunt. Trina siquidem immersio in Baptismo licet mandata, & hodierno usu recepta sit, & a nonnullis Schismati addictis ita defensa, ut unica damnata sit, sicuti illud de usu salis in eodem Baptismo, nihilominus unionem non lædunt, cum non sint ex ijs, quæ substantiam Baptismi destruant. Manentibus siquidem materia, forma, & intentione ministri, valide, quidquid de alijs sit, Baptismus confertur. Et ut res planius pateat, ritus apud Latinos, & ceremoniæ sunt, Exufflatio in frontem infantis baptizandi, salis modici immissio in os, Signum Crucis pollice in fronte, & manuum compositio in capite, stolæ super infantem impositio, saliva ministri, & tactus aurium & narium, unctio pectoris ex oleo Catechumenorum, Stolæ violaceæ in albam mutatio, infusio trina aquæ super caput, tandem appositio linteoli albi in capite. Horum pleraque apud Græcos in usu sunt, & perpaucula non in utrisque confpi-cies cies, quæ, cum ad Sacramentum attineant, sacramentalia nuncupantur. Non ea tamen sunt, vt si aliquod deerit, Sacramentum irritum fit, cum ad illius validitatem necessario tria solummodo flagitentur, quæ vocantur essentialia. Vis Sacramentum illibatum, sartumtectum, atque omnibus suis partibus integrum? hæc tria quærito, his animum applica, reliqua si negligat minister, prætereatque ex malitia, Minister quidem peccat, & lethaliter, sed Sacramento non officit, quod idem fuerit, ac si neglectum nihil fuisset: quod si ex negligentia tantum; nec scandalum subortum est, peccat, sed leuiuscule. Idem sequitur si formam mutauerit, sententiam in alium sensum non subtrahens, vel aliqua ipsius verba, quæ sensui referendo non officiunt, mutatio cum fit accidentalis, non essentialis, siue substantialis, vt si pro baptizo dicat, abluo. sic si in forma omittatur, ego, vel in forma Eucharistiæ, enim, si sine scandalo, & contemptu fuerit, veniale tantum peccatum fore ob materiæ leuitatem dicunt Pontificij, neque destrui Sacramentum. Tria itaque dicta conseruata Sacramenta semper conficiunt. Et quod iam cum Scholasticis decernimus, Ministri intentionem sufficere confusam, atque implicatam, cum facere tendit, quod Christus instituit, vel Ecclesia facit, etiam si cum eiusmodi intentione coniunctus sit error speculatiuus, & illi errori correspondeat vitiosa intentio male conferendi Sacramentum, vel ministrandi Baptisinum per Filium Patre minorem: cum enim haec intentio conditionalis sit, seu ex suppositione exisimationis falsae, quod haec ipsa sit Christi institutio, ideo superatur ab alia confusa, & generali, quae absoluta est, faciendi quod Christus instituit. Colligitur ex Concilio Arelatensi primo can. 8. Si ad Ecclesiam aliqui de haeresi Ariana venerint, interrogent eos nostrae fidei Sacerdotes Symbolum, & si prauiderint[?] in Patre, & Filio, & Spiritu sancto eos baptizatos, manus tantum eis imponentur, ut recipiant Spiritum sanctum. Et Augustinus libro 4. contra Donatistas capite 25. Satis ostendimus ad Baptismum, qui verbis Euangelicis consecratur, non pertinere cuiusque, vel dantis, vel recipientis errorem, sive de Patre, sive de Filio, sive de Spiritu sancto aliter sentiat, quam caelestis doctrina insinuat. Vides? Baptizati ab Arianis, veram verborum formam retinentibus ad Ecclesiam Catholicam reuersi non fuerunt denuo baptizati. Requiritur tamen in hoc casu, ut Minister actuali contraria opinione non excludat veritatem Sacramenti, nempe si Minister nolet baptismum conferri, nisi Pater sit maior Filio, et si Græcus nolit Eucharistiam conficere, nisi panis sit fermentatus, qui sit de necessitate Sacramenti tali casu ob defectum intentionis Sacramentum irritum est, multoqz magis si error contra veritatem Sacramenti exprimatur in forma: tum enim dicitur esse & est essentialis formæ mutatio. Id habeo ex Athan. Orat. 3. contra Arianos, & Greg. lib. 9. epist. 61. ad Quirinum. ceremoniæ itaqz & ritus in administratione non variant essentiam; ideoqz neqz Ecclesias illos alio atque alio modo vsurpantes separant, & diversas efficiunt. Hæc Pontificij dicunt, hæc Græci prædicant. Male ergo disfidia hariolamur inter Græcos, & Pontificios in Baptismo ex eo quod Ecclesia Græca trina immersione vtatur, Latina infusione. Sed id obijciunt Latinis Ieremias Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, & præterea vsum salis Michaël Cerularius. Obijciunt. Quid tum? Nos non disputamus de re, an bene, vel male peragatur, sed tantum de dissidio: si libera hæc sunt, & ex vtriusque arbitrio pendent, ergo sive baptismus conferatur per infusionem aquæ, sive per immersionem hominis, eamqe sive trinam, sive vnicam, sive cum sale, sive sine sale, sive hoc modo, sive alio, cum ad Sacramenti sub-stanstantiam quæuis corporis ablutio per aquam facta sufficiat, valide baptifinus confertur, & consequenter male assignatur dissidium.
units.tr: Three immersions commanded in baptism. Use of salt in baptism. Immediate connection of chrism with baptism. Necessity of unleavened bread. Abstinence from what is strangled, a Judaizing precept. Grains of warm water in the sacred chalice already consecrated. Stricter observance of fasting, especially the Lenten fast, not without censure. These are plainly matters indifferent. Although the threefold immersion in baptism is commanded and is received in present practice, and some men devoted to the Schism have defended it so strongly that the single immersion has been condemned, and likewise the use of salt in the same baptism, they nevertheless do not harm the union, since they are not among those things that destroy the substance of baptism. For so long as the matter, form and intention of the minister remain, baptism is validly conferred, whatever may be said of the rest. To make the matter plainer: the rites and ceremonies among the Latins are these: the breathing upon the forehead of the infant to be baptized, the placing of a little salt on the mouth, the sign of the cross with the thumb on the forehead, the laying on of hands on the head, the putting of a stole over the infant, the spittle of the minister, the touching of the ears and nostrils, the anointing of the breast with oil of the catechumens, the change of the violet stole to a white one, the threefold pouring of water over the head, and finally the placing of a white linen cloth on the head. Most of these are in use among the Greeks too, and a very few are seen in one church and not in the other; these, since they pertain to the sacrament, are called sacramentals. Yet they are not such that, if any of them is lacking, the sacrament is void, since for its validity only three things are necessarily required, which are called essentials. Do you want the sacrament whole, intact, and complete in all its parts? Ask these three things, and fix your mind on them. If the minister neglects the rest, or passes them over out of malice, the minister indeed sins, and mortally, but it does not harm the sacrament, which is the same as if nothing had been omitted; if it is only from negligence, and no scandal has arisen, he sins, but venially. The same follows if he has changed the form without withdrawing the meaning into another sense, or changed some words of it which do not hinder the meaning when it is referred back; when the change is accidental, not essential or substantial, as if he should say abluo for baptizo. So too if ego is omitted in the form, or enim in the form of the Eucharist, the Papists say that if it is without scandal and contempt, it is only a venial sin because of the lightness of the matter, and the sacrament is not destroyed. Therefore, so long as the three said things are preserved, the sacraments always take effect. And what we now decide with the Scholastics: the intention of the minister is sufficient even if it is confused and entangled, provided it aims at doing what Christ instituted or what the Church does. This holds even if an erroneous speculative belief is joined with such an intention, and a faulty intention to confer the sacrament badly, or to administer baptism through the Son who is less than the Father, corresponds to that error. For since this intention is conditional, or depends on the supposition of a false judgement that this very thing is Christ's institution, it is therefore overcome by another, confused and general intention, which is absolute, of doing what Christ instituted. This is gathered from the First Council of Arles, canon 8: If some come to the Church from the Arian heresy, let the priests of our faith question them about the Creed, and if they perceive that they were baptized in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, hands alone shall be laid upon them, so that they may receive the Holy Spirit. And Augustine, book 4 against the Donatists, chapter 25: We have sufficiently shown that the baptism which is consecrated by the words of the Gospel does not depend on the error of anyone, whether of the giver or of the recipient, whether he thinks otherwise about the Father, or about the Son, or about the Holy Spirit, than heavenly doctrine teaches. Do you see? Those baptized by the Arians, who kept the true form of words, and who returned to the Catholic Church, were not baptized again. Yet in this case it is required that the minister, by a present contrary opinion, does not exclude the truth of the sacrament: namely, if the minister would not wish baptism to be conferred unless the Father is greater than the Son, or if a Greek would not wish to consecrate the Eucharist unless the bread is leavened, which is by necessity of the sacrament. In such a case the sacrament is void because of a defect of intention; and much more so if an error contrary to the truth of the sacrament is expressed in the form. For then it is said, and it is, a change of the essential form. I have this from Athanasius, Oration 3 against the Arians, and from Gregory, book 9, letter 61 to Quirinus. Ceremonies and rites in the administration therefore do not alter the essence; and so the Churches which use them in one way or another do not separate or become divided. This is what the Papists say, this is what the Greeks proclaim. So we idly and wrongly conjecture a dissension between Greeks and Papists over baptism, because the Greek Church uses threefold immersion and the Latin infusion. But Jeremias, Patriarch of Constantinople, objects this to the Latins, and besides him Michael Cerularius objects the use of salt. They object. So what? We are not disputing whether it is done well or badly, but only about the dissension. If these things are free and depend on the judgement of each side, then whether baptism is conferred by pouring water or by immersing the man, and whether it is done threefold or single, with salt or without salt, in this way or that, since any washing of the body with water suffices for the substance of the sacrament, baptism is validly conferred, and consequently a dissension is wrongly assigned.

units.la: Adde his præterea. Ritus in Baptismo seruandos sæpesæpius urgente necessitate, nempe cum mors fœtui imminet, vel periculum urget, vel priuatim confertur, vel alia etiam causa omissos, cōstat ex praxi Ecclesiæ postmodum in Ecclesia supplendos esse, licet ex Pontificiis non nemo tenuerit, sacrilegium fore, & maximam Sacramenti iniuriam, si Parochus puero priuatim baptizato postea exorcismos ad Dæmonem profligandum adhibeat. De ommittendis hisce ritibus vsus, maxime pestilentia crassante obseruatur, cum infantes ex matribus peste infectis editi, magno in discrimine sint. Cessante postmodum pestilentia in Ecclesia supplentur. Sic etiam ab Hæreticis absque talium ceremoniarum solemnitate baptizatis, si in rectam fidem venerint, non sunt in Ecclesia supplendi, ne populus existimet Hæreticorum baptisma, tanquam minus validum improbari. Quod aliter fit, si scandalum non obstat. Tum sic; Baptismus absque ceremoniis collatus vere Baptismus est, & ceremoniæ non ideo supplentur, vt Baptismum irritum, validum efficiant, cum validus sit per se. Ergo illæ ceremoniæ ad Baptismum, ut iam diximus, ex arbitrio hominum pendent, nec inter illas Ecclesias alio, atque alio modo illas usurpantes diffidium pariunt. Et quod addis ex sententia Syropuli, Latinos ἀβαπτίστως[?] esse, perridiculum plane est. Neque enim id contendit Syropulus, sed ex disputatione Proto-syncelli cum Petro Calabro recitat: Syropulus enim, ut in calculo ferendo inconstantiam redargueret Proto-syncelli, & facto aliquo ridiculo dictum illius, & assensum imminuisset, illud confinxisse existimatur. Fruftra siquidem de Latinorum Baptismo, nec de quo Græcis nullum unquam dubium fuit, dubitatum fuisset. sic quæstio illa exorta, & resoluta est, quasi per iocum.
units.tr: Add to these as well. That the rites to be observed in baptism are often omitted under pressing necessity, namely when death threatens the infant, or danger presses, or it is conferred privately, or for some other cause, and that they must afterwards be supplied in the Church, is established by the practice of the Church. Although some of the Papists have held that it would be sacrilege and the greatest injury to the sacrament if a parish priest afterwards applied exorcisms to drive out the devil from a boy privately baptized. The omission of these rites is especially observed when pestilence is thick, since infants born of mothers infected with plague are in great peril. When the pestilence has afterwards ceased, they are supplied in the Church. So too those baptized by heretics without the solemnity of such ceremonies, if they come to the true faith, are not to be supplied in the Church, lest the people think the baptism of heretics is rejected as less valid. It is otherwise if scandal does not stand in the way. Then it goes thus: baptism conferred without ceremonies is truly baptism, and the ceremonies are not supplied so as to make an invalid baptism valid, since it is valid in itself. Therefore those ceremonies in baptism, as we have now said, depend on the judgement of men, and the churches which use them in one way or another do not cause a dissension between them. And what you add from the opinion of Syropulus, that the Latins are unbaptized [ἀβαπτίστως], is quite ridiculous. For Syropulus does not contend this; he recites it from the dispute of the Proto-syncellus with Peter of Calabria. For it is thought that Syropulus invented it, in order to expose the inconsistency of the Proto-syncellus in reckoning, and by some ridiculous act to diminish both his saying and his assent. For it would be in vain to have doubted about the baptism of the Latins, about which the Greeks never had any doubt. Thus that question arose and was settled as if in jest.

units.la: Chrismatis immediata cum Baptismo coniunctio. Hoc verum est. Hinc scripserat Alatius, nullum esse, qui Sacramento Baptismi accepto, domum absque Sacramento Confirmationis redire. Sed hanc administrationem falsam, & Hæreticam vocat Arcudius. Quid dixerit Arcudius non examino. Hoc scio in Ecclesia tum Orientali, cum Occidentali, olim in more positum fuisse, ut infantibus statim post Baptismum, Chrisma conferretur. Nunc vero in Ecclesia Romana usu receptum est, ut infantes, antequam ad rationis usum perveniant, quod fere septimo ætatis anno contingit, non confirmentur. Cum enim in prima Ecclesia extra mortis periculum, tum paruulis dum adultis Pafchate, & Pentecoste, cum etiam adessent Episcopi, confirmationem conferri solitum effet, aucta postmodum Ecclesia, cum Baptismus omnibus anni temporibus ministrari coepit, factum est, vt statim post Baptismum commodiore tempore infantes confirmarentur. Materiam huius Confirmationis, tum in Græca, tum Latina Ecclesia benedicit Episcopus. Esto; sed in Græca inungit Presbyter: id in Latina prohibetur Presbytero, vindicatur Epifcopo. Cum Minister habet facultatem, collatum ab ipso Sacramentum validum est. Et Pontifices aliquibus Ecclesijs hanc facultatem concessisse, disco ex Decreto Eugenij IV. in Concilio Florentino, Legitur aliquando per Apostolicæ Sedis dispensationem ex rationabili, & urgente admodum causa, simplicem Sacerdotem Chrismate per Epifcopum confecto administrasse Confirmationis Sacramentum. Vide locum Gregorij Magni. Hæc est doctrina Theologorum Græcorum & Latinorum, quæ cum eadem fit, confensum vnanimem in collatione Chrismatis, non diffensum elicimus. Sed hic mirari liceat Lutherum, Melanchthonem, Caluinum, Magdeburgenses, & reliquos, qui ex Ecclesiæ Orientalis, atque Occidentalis Sacramentorum numero Chrismatis Sacramentum eliminant, quod factum sit ex manuum impositione, quod sit prorsus otiosa Ceremonia, quod virtus eius confícta[?], quod conferat ad gratiæ augmentum in Baptismo collatæ ad innocentiam, quod non Verbum Dei Spiritus sancti præsentiam promittit, quod non in aliarum, quam in Occidentalium legatur; & tamen de ea uti Sacramenta reliqua gratiam conferente legitur in Clemente Alexandrino, Origene, Eusebio Cæsariense, Synodo Laodicena, Cyrillo Hierofolymitano, Gregorio Nazianzeno, Epiphanio, Ioanne Chrysostomo, Cyrillo Alexandrino, Isidoro Pelusiota, Theodoreto, & ex recentioribus, Theophylacto, Oecumenio, Balsamone, Niceta Choniata, Simeone Thessalonicensi, Ieremia Patriarcha Constantinopolitano, & aliis, quorum verba, cum publici iuris sint, petat sibi quisque, si placet. Sed in hoc etiam est discrimen. imo consensus. Cum enim essentiam Sacramenti non lædat, parum refert, an statim post Baptismum, vel post sex annos, aut plures conferatur. Nanque dicitur etiam num in Hispania infantes duorum, vel trium annorum pueros confirmari. Sic ante septennium in mortis periculo constituti pueri atque infantuli rectissime confirmantur, cum confirmationis sunt capaces, & digni.
units.tr: Immediate connection of chrism with baptism. This is true. Hence Allatius wrote that there is no one who, having received the sacrament of baptism, returns home without the sacrament of confirmation. But Arcudius calls this administration false and heretical. What Arcudius said I do not examine. This I know: in both the Eastern and the Western Church it was formerly the custom that chrism was conferred on infants immediately after baptism.
