units.la: BIna illa Opuscula, quæ nuper ad me misisti, Clarissime Leo, nostri sæculi Literatorum decus, & ornamentum; Vnum Iohannis Henrici Hottingeri Tigurini inscriptum: Disputatio Apologetica de euidenti Ecclesia Orientalis, & Occidentalis, tam in dogmatibus, quam in ritibus dissensu; Alterum, cui titulus est: Exercitatio HistoricoTheologica de Ecclesia Græcanica hodierna, M. Eliæ Veielij Vlmensis, legi, atque perlegi, eamque præsertim partem, in qua vterque scripta mea exagitat circa variarum Syrorum, Arabumque Christianarum Sectarum consensum tam inter se, quam cum Ecclesia Romana de ritibus, & dogmatibus, quæ nos inter & Reformatos in controuersiam vocantur. Id enim vnum est, quod a me planè exigis, & cuius gratia Opuscula illa pro tua in me humanitate, & beneuolentia misisti. Tuis itaque morem gerens iussibus, eruditissime Leo, paucis apeaperiam, unde utrique tanta bilis in me etiam est. Scripseram olim in notis ad Synopsim, & Praefationem Arabicam Concilij Nicæni, necnon in Notis ad Catalogum librorum Chaldæorum: Hebediesu, eos Fidei articulos, in quibus conueniunt Nationes illæ Orientales, tam inter se quam cum Ecclesia Romana, necessario ad ipsos Apostolos, & primæuæ Ecclesiæ æuum suum referre originem, ac in nullam confictionis cadere posse suspicionem. Ratio quidem mea est, quia si post suborta schismata conficta fuissent, necesse profecto esset, ut id vel ab omnibus illis Sectis simul, Romana etiam consentiente Ecclesia, factitatum fuisset, vel ab vna tantum istarum Sectarum seorsim: Sed cum neutrum fieri posset, ad ipsos Apostolos, & primæuæ Ecclesiæ æuum referenda omnino esse oportebit. Quemadmodum cordatus nemo, & sanæ mentis non concedit, & ultro largitur, ea dogmata, & Religionis articulos, in quibus conveniunt tot Protestantium Sectæ, tam inter sese, quam cum Ecclesia Romana, suam referre originem ad aureum illud sæculum, in quo Ecclesia vna erat ante Lutherum, Caluinum, aliosque tot malorum, ac turbarum auctores. Quod quidem Argumentum, cum sit maximi ponderis, ac momenti, iamdudum ante ipse, eruditissime Leo, inculcasti ex Græcorum, & Latinorum consensu, quod plurimum Reformatorum latera vrget, & pectora ferit. Videns dein
units.tr: Those little works that you lately sent me, most distinguished Leo, the glory and ornament of our age among scholars, I have read and reread: one entitled by Johann Heinrich Hottinger of Zurich, Apologetic Disputation on the Evident Disagreement of the Eastern and Western Church, in Doctrines as Well as in Rites; the other, titled Historical-Theological Exercise on the Present Greek Church, by M. Elias Veiel of Ulm. I read especially that part in which both of them attack my writings on the agreement of the various Syrian and Arab Christian sects, both among themselves and with the Roman Church, in rites and doctrines, which are disputed between us and the Reformed. This is the one thing you ask of me plainly, and it is for its sake that you sent those works, out of your kindness and goodwill toward me. So, obeying your commands, most learned Leo, I will explain briefly why both of them are so bitterly angry with me. I had written earlier, in the notes to the Synopsis and in the Arabic preface to the Council of Nicaea, and also in the notes to the Catalogue of Chaldean books of Hebediesu, that those articles of faith in which those Eastern nations agree, both with one another and with the Roman Church, necessarily trace their origin to the Apostles themselves and the age of the earliest Church, and cannot fall under any suspicion of invention. My reasoning is this: if these had been invented after the schisms arose, it would necessarily have had to be done either by all those sects together, with the Roman Church also consenting, or by only one of those sects separately. But since neither could happen, they must without doubt be referred to the Apostles and the age of the primitive Church. Just as no sensible and sound-minded person denies, and indeed willingly grants, that those doctrines and articles of religion in which so many Protestant sects agree, both among themselves and with the Roman Church, trace their origin to that golden age in which the Church was one, before Luther, Calvin, and the others, authors of so many evils and disturbances. This argument, since it is of very great weight and importance, you, most learned Leo, have long ago pressed on us from the consent of the Greeks and Latins, which presses hard on the flanks and strikes the chests of most of the Reformed. Seeing then

units.la: Bartholdus Nihusius ذو الذكر الـمـالـك [?]
units.tr: Bartholdus Nihusius, dhu-l-dhikr al-malik [?],

units.la: quisque pro bono Ecclesiæ longiori vita dignus erat, idem hoc argumentum maiores sumere vires ex aliorum Orientalium consensione, duo nostro Hebediesu, dum illum vna cum nostris notis recudi curauit Moguntiæ, adiecit programmata ad Academicos Protestantes, quibus eos prouocat ad singulare hoc certamen. Præsertim cum non defuerint apud ipsos, qui meris, & nudis assertionibus Orientalium hunc consensum sibi vindicare sint conati, vti testis vberrimus, & omni exceptione maior, nobis esse potest vir clarissimus Iulius Blumius, qui vna nobiscum plures huius generis assertiones contulit Parisijs. Huius autem argumenti ex consensione tot populorum adstructum, vim, & efficaciam effugere, atq; euitare volentes Veielius, & Hottingerus, opposita prorsus diuerticula, & flexiones arripiunt, eodem tamen collimantes, neminem veritatem ipsam eludere. Veielius enim, vt se hinc citius expediat, hunc irridet, & improbat consensum, ita pag. 2. scribens:
units.tr: who was worthy of a longer life for the good of the Church, that same argument, while he took care to have Hebediesu reprinted at Mainz together with our notes, gathered greater strength from the agreement of other Easterners, and added programmes to the Protestant academics, by which he challenges them to this singular contest. Especially since there were not lacking among them those who tried to claim this agreement of the Easterners for themselves by bare and mere assertions. As an abundant witness, beyond all exception, we have the most distinguished man Julius Blum, who with us collected many assertions of this kind at Paris. Veiel and Hottinger, wishing to escape and avoid the force and efficacy of this argument, drawn from the agreement of so many peoples, seize upon entirely opposed side-paths and evasions, yet aiming at the same goal, that no one should evade the truth itself. For Veiel, in order to extricate himself more quickly from this, mocks and rejects the agreement, writing thus at page 2:

units.la: Hinc nuper prodit libellus Abrahami Ecchellenfis Maronitæ Professoris in Gymnasio Romano, de concordia Nationum Christianarum per Asiam, & Africam, cum Ecclesia Latina contra Protest. cum notis ad Catalogum librorum Chaldaeorum Hebediesu, quem in Germania nobis curauit officiendo officiosissimus Nihufius, adiectis 2. ad Academicos Protestantes programmatibus. Quæ sunt autem illæ Nationes Christianæ in Asia, Africa? Sunt Hæretici, Armeni, Nestoriani, Melchitæ, Iacobitæ, &c. ut habet titulus, & asseritur in Epistola Abrahami Ecchellensis, tam inter se, quàm cum Romana Ecclesia inueterata, & incredibilia exercentes odia. Improbat is quidem, sed improbando nostri argumenti rationem corroborat potius, quam soluit; quia fieri omnino nequit, ut tot Nationes tam inter se, quam cum Ecclesia Romana inueterata, & incredibilia exercentes odia, convenire possint ad aliquod adstruendum commentum. Unde Tertullianus: Quod apud multos inuenitur, non est erratum, sed traditum. Et Arist. lib. 7. mor. Nic. c. 13. Non prorsus fama illa perit, quam multa per Orbem turba hominum celebrat. Quod enim omnibus videtur, id esse affirmamus. Hinc scriptum reliquit Iacobus Arminius, primariæ auctoritatis inter Reformatos, Difput. priuat. Thes. 13. de obiecto Christianae Religionis num 14. Accedit denique perpetuus, & universalis omnium populorum consensus, qui instar legis, imo Oraculi divini habendus est. Et Oratione 3. de certitudine sacro-sanctae Theologiae: Negare miracula, quae Gentilium, & Iudaeorum testimonia habent, manifestae impudentiae est, & execrandi stuporis. Quantae igitur impudentiae, & quidem manifestissimae, & execrandi stuporis erit, vel ex ipsorum Reformatorum sententia, negare perpetuum, & universalem consensum non solum Iudaeorum, & Mohammedanorum, sed tot etiam Christianorum Orientis populorum? Ad huius autem consensus originem, & rationem velim respondeat Veielius, eiusque Reuerend: Fhelauius; & quomodo ad aliquod commune mendacium confingendum conspirare possunt tot Nationes longissimae terrarum [?]dissitae spatiis, variis imbutae moribus, diversis utentes linguis, & persuasionibus, atque inveterata caeteroquin exercentes odia. Dicat praeterea Veielius: si Orientales illi populi in hisce articulis, de quibus Reformati controversiam nobiscum habent, convenirent cum ipsis, quas ille excitaret adversus nos turbas? quos ad astra usque extolleret clamores? quas vociferationes in foro suorum Reformatorum emitteret? Sane tot, quot Hottingerus, licet falso, & fallaciter, vt mox infra patebit, & forte maiores. Imo iam titubat Veielius, iam canit palinodiam, animos resumit nouos, Hottingeri fretus armis, & auxilio; adeoque quem supraimprobauit consensum, paulo post comprobat, vt ostendat omnibus, se nequaquam sibi esse compotem, qua falsæ, & vagæ causæ est patronus. Nam postquam verba quædam mea, quibus suos Protestantes prouoco ad singulare hoc certamen de consensu Orientalium populorum, statim subdit: Quam prouocationem Nihusius lepida simul, & Thrasonica innuitatione, ad exemplum Rabsacis 2. Regum 18. 23. 24. progr. f. 7. 55. ornat. Quam vero non cohorrescant ad istiusmodi gloriantes abunde iam docuisse celeber. Hottingerus praesat. in Lex. har. & Topograph. Ecclesiæ Orient. contra Ecchellensem, postquam hæc scripsissem, vidi. Igitur postquam vidit, quæ scripsit eius celeberrimus Hottingerus de consensu Orientalium, illum sibi, & suis adscisens, accedit libenter Veielius, & nos cohorrescere iubet tanquam falso hunc consensum nobis vindicantes. Res igitur cum ad Orientalium consensum redeat, redeamus & nos ad Hottingerum, qui eum sibi vindicat, & suis, ac singulas eius assertiones expendamus ad Orientalium trutinam, momentifque suis ponderemus, & videamus, quinam cohorrescere debeant, nos, an Veielius, Hot. tingerus, & qui ab ipsorum in hoc argumento stant partibus.
units.tr: Recently there has appeared a little book by Abraham Ecchellensis, a Maronite, Professor in the Roman Gymnasium, on the agreement of the Christian nations throughout Asia and Africa with the Latin Church against the Protestants, with notes to the Catalogue of Chaldean books of Hebediesu, which the most obliging Nihusius has kindly had reprinted for us in Germany, with two programmes added to the Protestant academics. But what are those Christian nations in Asia and Africa? They are the heretics, Armenians, Nestorians, Melkites, Jacobites, etc. as the title has it and as is asserted in the letter of Abraham Ecchellensis, who are, both among themselves and with the Roman Church, carrying on ancient and incredible hatreds. He indeed rejects it, but in rejecting it he strengthens the reasoning of our argument rather than dissolving it; for it is entirely impossible that so many nations, carrying on ancient and incredible hatreds both among themselves and with the Roman Church, could agree to devise some fiction. Whence Tertullian: What is found among many is not an error but a tradition. And Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics book 7, chapter 13: That fame does not perish altogether, which a great crowd of men throughout the world celebrates; for what seems so to all, we affirm to be so. Hence James Arminius, of the first authority among the Reformed, left this written in his private disputation, thesis 13, on the object of the Christian religion, number 14: Finally, there is added the perpetual and universal consent of all peoples, which is to be held as a law, indeed as a divine oracle. And in his third oration, on the certainty of sacred theology: To deny miracles, which have the testimony of Gentiles and Jews, is a manifest impudence and a detestable stupidity. What, then, of impudence, and indeed most manifest impudence, and detestable stupidity, will it be, even by the judgment of the Reformers themselves, to deny the perpetual and universal consent not only of Jews and Muslims, but also of so many Christian peoples of the East? Let Veiel and his reverend Fhelavius say what the origin and reason of this consent is, and how so many nations, separated by the widest spaces of the lands, imbued with various customs, using different languages and persuasions, and otherwise carrying on ancient hatreds, could conspire to fabricate some common lie. Let Veiel further say: if those Eastern peoples agreed with us on these articles about which the Reformed have controversy with us, what uproars would he stir up against us? What shouts would he raise to the stars? What outcries would he utter in the forum of his Reformed? Surely as many as Hottinger, though falsely and deceptively, as will shortly be shown below, and perhaps more. Indeed Veiel now staggers, now sings a palinode, takes up new courage, relying on Hottinger's arms and help; and so the consent he rejected above, shortly afterwards he approves, so as to show everyone that he is by no means master of himself, since he is the defender of a false and vague cause. For after I had written certain words of mine by which I challenge my Protestants to this singular contest about the agreement of the Eastern peoples, he immediately adds: Nihusius adorns this challenge with a witty and boastful taunt, after the manner of Rabshakeh, 2 Kings 18:23-24, progr. f. 7, 55, ornat. But that the celebrated Hottinger has already sufficiently taught that such boasters should not be dreaded, in his preface to the Lexicon and Topography of the Eastern Church against Ecchellensis, I saw after I had written these things. Therefore, after he saw what his most celebrated Hottinger wrote about the agreement of the Easterners, Veiel, taking him and his into his fold, gladly comes over, and bids us to shudder as though we falsely claim this agreement for ourselves. Since the matter, then, returns to the agreement of the Easterners, let us also return to Hottinger, who claims it for himself and for his side, and let us weigh each of his assertions in the Eastern balance, and ponder them with their proper weights, and see who ought to shudder: we, or Veiel, Hottinger, and those who stand on their side in this matter.

units.la: Hottingerus itaque in atenam animose descendens, postquam pag. 28. num. 28. plura in genere sine vlla probatione, testimonio, vel auctoritate garriuit de Orientalium consensu cum Reformatis in capitibus fidei, ritibus, ac regimine Ecclesiastico, ad speciem tandem deueniens haec subdit: In specie vero vbi ad singulorum dogmatum dequentum fuerit examen, obseruamus, Orientales, vel Reformatis per omnia accedere, vel in circumstantijs tantum variare; vel vbi Pontificijs videntur fauere partibus; illud aut ex principijs fluere, Pontificiorum etiam opinione erroneis, aut φαγουδῶς potius quam ὄντως, verbis, quam rebus assensum testari maiorem. Atque sic non negamus, Orientales Ecclesias cum Romana aliquid habere simile (idem, difficulter obtinebunt). Hisitaq; vult Hottingerus, Orientales Ecclesias cum Romana aliquid habere simile, at non idem; φαγουδῶς, & non ὄντως; cum Reformatis vero ὄντως, & rebus. Hinc vero ad articulorum, in quibus consentiunt Orientales cum Reformatis, vt ait, concedens enumerationem ita scribit: Plura tamen nobiscum sic 1. occurrunt in Orientalium, Gracorum cumprimis, & Syrorum scriptis varie formule ad B. V. Mariam concepte; vel etiam ad alios Sanctos, quibus tamen superstitionibus auctissima Pontificiorum ἀχολαξεία non defenditur. Magnum enim utrinque est ἁγίσμα[?], vel in eo saltem, quod singulis urbibus, morbis, Prouincijs patronum suum Romani præficiunt.
units.tr: Hottinger, then, descending boldly into the arena, after having at page 28, number 28, chattered at length in general, without any proof, testimony, or authority, about the agreement of the Easterners with the Reformed in the heads of faith, in rites, and in ecclesiastical government, at last comes down to particulars and adds this: But in particular, where there is an examination of individual doctrines in turn, we observe that the Easterners either agree with the Reformed in all things, or differ only in circumstances; or where they seem to favour the Papist side, this flows from principles which are erroneous even in the opinion of the Papists, or they attest a greater assent seemingly [φαγουδῶς] rather than in truth [ὄντως], in words rather than in things. And so we do not deny that the Eastern Churches have something similar to the Roman Church (the same they will hardly obtain). In this way Hottinger wants the Eastern Churches to have something similar to the Roman Church, but not the same; seemingly [φαγουδῶς], and not in truth [ὄντως]; but with the Reformed in truth [ὄντως] and in things. Hence, conceding the enumeration of the articles in which, as he says, the Easterners agree with the Reformed, he writes thus: Several points, nevertheless, occur with us in this way: in the writings of the Easterners, especially of the Greeks and the Syrians, various formulas composed to the Blessed Virgin Mary, or also to other saints, in which, however, the very great slavish adherence [ἀχολαξεία] of the Papists is not defended by such superstitions. For on both sides there is a great hallowing [ἁγίσμα], or at least in this, that the Romanists set a patron over each city, disease, and province.

units.la: Hic non ratiocinatur Hottingerus, sed plane insanit. Nam vel conveniunt cum Orientalibus Reformati in eiusdem modi formulis, vel non. Si conveniunt, vt contendit ille, qua ratione impius non erit in se, suosque Reformatos, eas appellans formulas superstitiones, in quibus conveniunt Orientales cum Reformatis ex ipsius sententia? Si vero non conveniunt, qua fronte, qua impudentia, & qua cauteriata conscientia, eos convenire, dicit? Suis itaque capitur paralogismis, & dilemmate concluditur; apparetque inde luculentissime, eum ex fraude, fallacijs, ac mendacijs constare totum. Et quis proinde erit, vel sit Reformatus, qui eum apertissimi, ac turpissimi mendacij, fraudis, & contradictionis non arguet, & convincet? Quam autem hic vocat auctissimam ἀχολαξείαν Pontificiorum Hottingerus, nullæ caitæ[?] Christianæ auaures sine indignatione, & stomacho excipere possunt; cum eadem haec sit summorum heroum primaeuae Ecclesiae sententia de SS. invocatione, ut infinita, quae occurrunt passim, ipsorum id comprobant testimonia. Sed quae adhuc Hottingeri impudentia, & insania est, qui eodem asserto condemnat omnes Orientales, quos hic pro se laudat? Ex quo plane patet, eum non ratione duci, & veritatem sequi, sed effraenata quadam rabie, & furiosa rapi. Porro qui non cohorreat impius cum Veielio, Sanctorum invocationes condemnans, ad has sui Lutheri execrandas voces, & formulas, non ad B. V. Mariam, aliosque Sanctos conceptas, sed ad ipsum Sathanam in Colloquiis ita intonantis: Sancte Sathan ora pro nobis: minime tamen contra te peccavimus clementissime Diabole? Haec est, quae Hottingero arridet Diaboli λατρεία, non B. V. & aliorum Sanctorum δουλεία. Magnum verò illud [illegible, ~8 letters], quod ponit, magnum quidem eius impudentiae argumentum est, quia omnes Christiani Orientales eodem prorsus modo, ac Romani, & urbibus, & morbis, & Prouinciis suos praeficiunt patronos. Sic Antiochia patronum agnoscit D. Petrum, Alexandria Marcum, Hierusalem Iacobum, Damascus Paulum, Berytus Georgium, Mesopotamia Addæum, & sic de aliis. Item S. Antonius Abbas præficitur Energumenis, & a Diabolo vexatis, Romanus Paralysi, Lucius oculorum ægritudinibus, & alii aliis morbis. Et quidem illud saltem ad quod saltat, plane vanitatem eius pronunciati de illis formulis indicat; est enim titubantis, & inconstantis animi constantissimum argumentum. Nullum igitur in hisce διάσημα[?] agnoscendum est, nisi quod Hottingerum inter, & ipsam veritatem interest, quod quidem maximum esse, oportet, cum tantum sit, quantum ab ipsa veritate distat mendacium.
units.tr: Hottinger does not reason here at all; he plainly raves. Either the Reformed agree with the Orientals in such formulas, or they do not. If they agree, as he maintains, how is he not impious himself, and how can he call these formulas superstitions in which the Orientals agree with the Reformed on his own account? If they do not agree, with what brow, what impudence, and what seared conscience does he say that they do? He is therefore caught in his own paralogisms and refuted by his own dilemma, and it is most clearly evident that he is made up entirely of fraud, deceit, and lies. Who, then, among the Reformed would not charge him with, and convict him of, a most manifest and shameful lie, fraud, and self-contradiction? As for what Hottinger here calls the most abundant servile fawning [ἀχολαξεία] of the Papists, no Christian ears can hear it without indignation and disgust, since it is the very opinion of the greatest heroes of the primitive Church concerning the invocation of the saints, as the countless testimonies that occur everywhere prove. But what further impudence and madness is this of Hottinger's, who by the same assertion condemns all the Orientals whom he here praises as his own? From this it is plain that he is not led by reason or follows the truth, but is carried off by a certain unbridled rage and frenzy. Moreover, who would not shudder, with Veielius condemning the invocations of the saints, at those execrable words and formulas of his Luther, not addressed to the Blessed Virgin Mary or other saints, but to Satan himself, thundered out thus in the Table Talk: Holy Satan, pray for us; yet we have by no means sinned against you, most merciful Devil? This is the worship [λατρεία] of the Devil that pleases Hottinger, not the service [δουλεία] of the Blessed Virgin and the other saints. As for that "great" [illegible] which he sets down, it is indeed a great proof of his impudence, since all Eastern Christians, in exactly the same way as the Romanists, appoint patrons for cities, diseases, and provinces. Thus Antioch acknowledges St Peter as patron, Alexandria Mark, Jerusalem James, Damascus Paul, Beirut George, Mesopotamia Addai, and so on for others. Likewise St Antony the Abbot is appointed over the possessed and those vexed by the devil, St Roch over paralysis, St Lucy over diseases of the eyes, and others over other diseases. Indeed that word at least, on which he leaps, plainly reveals the vanity of his assertion about those formulas, for it is the surest sign of a wavering and inconstant mind. Nothing, therefore, is to be recognised in these matters beyond the gap between Hottinger and the truth itself, which must be very great, since a lie is as far from the truth as it is distant from it.

units.la: Pergit Hottingerus: Illæ generales sunt, & apostrophæ potiùs encomiastica; hæ sæpe impiæ, & cum dedecore Nominis divini coniunctæ.
units.tr: Hottinger goes on: Those are general, and rather encomiastic apostrophes; these are often impious, and joined with dishonour to the divine Name.

units.la: De formulis generalibus, & encomiasticis non est hic nobis laborandum, quia passim occurrunt etiam in Ecclesiæ Romanæ Officiis, & scriptis symbolicis, adeoque conveniunt in illis cum Occidentalibus Orientales. De specialibus itaque videamus, an Orientales quoque habeant ad B. V. Mariam, aliosque nominatim Sanctos conceptas, quibus illos invocant, eorum implo-rantopem, atque deprecantur, ut sibi adsint, pro se orent, & apud Deum intercedant.
units.tr: We need not labour here over general and encomiastic formulas, since they occur everywhere, even in the Offices and symbolic writings of the Roman Church, and so the Orientals agree with the Westerners in them. Let us therefore look at the particular ones: whether the Orientals also have prayers addressed by name to the Blessed Virgin Mary and other saints, by which they invoke them, implore their help, and beseech them to be present, to pray for them, and to intercede with God.

units.la: Primo autem loco accedant Melchitæ, quos hic Græcos appellat Hottingerus, & pro se primo loco laudat. Isti itaque in Troparijs ad Deiparam Mariam per circulum totius anni inter cetera hoc recitant ad vesperas Dominicæ in primo tono: [illegible, ~3 letters]
units.tr: Let us first take the Melchites, whom Hottinger calls Greeks and praises first. In their troparia to the Mother of God, which they recite through the whole cycle of the year, they say among other things this at Sunday vespers in the first tone:

units.la: [illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters] Mirabilissimum mirabilium obstupefacientium conspicit creatura, & lætatur ideo, atque exultat concipiente te sine semine, o gratia plena, quæ peperisti partum tuum ineffabilem, in quem Archangeli respicere non possunt, deprecare illum pro animabus nostris. Item ad Vesperas feriæ 2. in primo tono: [illegible, ~3 letters]
units.tr: [illegible] The creature beholds the most wonderful of wonders, and is astonished and rejoices, and exults, because you conceived without seed, O full of grace, and bore your ineffable child, into whom the Archangels cannot look; intercede with him for our souls. Likewise at vespers on the second feria in the first tone:

units.la: [illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters][illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters] Concepisti absque combustione ab igne Divinitatis, & peperisti sine semine Dominum fontem vite. O Dei genetrix, gratia plena, salua magnificantes te. Item ad Vesperas fer. 3. in tono 3.
units.tr: [illegible] You conceived without burning from the fire of the Godhead, and you bore without seed the Lord, the fountain of life. O Mother of God, full of grace, save those who magnify you. Likewise at vespers on the third feria in the third tone:

units.la: انتي ملجانا وقوتنا يا والدة الاله يا معونة العالم القويه بشفاعتك استرى عبيدك من كل شدة اذتهيا المباركه وحدك
units.tr: Anti malja'na wa-quwwatuna, ya walidat al-ilah, ya ma'unat al-'alam al-qawiyyah, bi-shafa'atik astiri 'abidaka min kulli shiddah, idh tahayya al-mubaraka wahdaka. [Transliterated from Arabic.]

units.la: Tu es Refugium nostrum, & virtus nostra, o Deipara, o forte Mundi auxilium, tuis intercessionibus protege feruos tuos ab omni afflictione, o sola benedicta. Item in Menologio die 4. Septembris in Tropario commemorationis S. Moysis Prophetae:
units.tr: You are our refuge and our strength, O Mother of God, O mighty help of the world; by your intercessions protect your servants from every affliction, O only blessed one. Likewise in the Menologion, on 4 September, in the troparion for the commemoration of the holy prophet Moses:

units.la: اننا معيدون لتذكار نبيك موسى وبه نتوسل اليك يا رب خلص بطلباته نفوسنا:
units.tr: Inna-na mu'idun li-tadhkar nabiyyika Musa, wa-bihi natawassal ilayka ya Rabb, khallis bi-talibatihi nufusana. [Transliterated from Arabic.]

units.la: Vtique festum agimus commemorationis Prophetae tui Moysis, per quem te supplicamus Domine, vt saluos precibus illius animas nostras. Eodem die de S. Babila Antiocheno.
units.tr: Indeed we keep the feast of the commemoration of your prophet Moses, through whom we beseech you, O Lord, that by his prayers you save our souls. On the same day, concerning St Babila of Antioch:

units.la: ايها الشهيد فى الكهنه بابيلا لما وضعت فى قلبك عظايم الايمان وحفظتها لم تجزع من المغتصب ولم ترهب من المعاند فلذلك احفظنا يا خادم
units.tr: Ayyuha al-shahid fi al-kahanah Babila, lamma wada'ta fi qalbika 'azaim al-iman wa-hafiztaha, lam tajza' min al-maghtasib, wa-lam tarhab min al-ma'nid, fa-li-dhalika ihfazna ya khadim [...]. [Transliterated from Arabic.]

units.la: المسيح ومونسا [?] O Martyr inter Sacer-
units.tr: al-Masih wa-Munsa [?] O martyr among the priests

units.la: dotes Babila, cum posueris in corde tuo magnalia Dei, & custodieris ea, neque quam timuisti tyrannum, neque metuisti aduersarium, pro-pterea ferua nos, o Minister Christi, & custodi nos .
units.tr: Babila, since you placed the great things of God in your heart and kept them, and neither feared the tyrant you dreaded nor the adversary, therefore keep us, O minister of Christ, and guard us.

units.la: Ἐυχολόγιον [?] cap. 82. cuius titulus est: ملاة تقال على مريض معذب من الارواح النجسه Oratio dicenda super ægroto vexato à spiritibus immundis :
units.tr: Euchologion [?] chapter 82, whose title is: Prayer to be said over a sick person tormented by unclean spirits. [Arabic title transliterated: salah tuqal 'ala marid mu'adhdhab min al-arwah al-najisah.]

units.la: يا مراتب قواة الملايكه الغير هيولانيين مع الرسل والشهدا دوسلوا ميتهلين الى سيد الكل ان ينجى عبده هذا من هذه الشده الثقيله جدا . ايتها الميده الدائمه المتوليه عليها المومنين ايتها المعونه القويه لنا من عبيدك بشفاعاتك خلصني من عبدك مسن هذه الشده الحاضره :
units.tr: Ya maratib quwwat al-mala'ika al-ghair hayulaniyin, ma'a al-rusul wa-al-shuhada, tawassalu mutadarri'in ila sayyid al-kull, an yunji 'abdahu hadha min hadhihi al-shiddah al-thaqilah jiddan. Ayyatuha al-sayyida al-da'imah al-batuliyyah, al-mutawalliyah 'alayha al-mu'minun, ayyatuha al-ma'unah al-qawiyyah lana min 'abidika bi-shafa'atik, khallisni min 'abdika hadha min hadhihi al-shiddah al-hadirah. [Transliterated from Arabic.]

units.la: O ordines Virtutum Angelorum immaterialium, cum Apostolis, & Martyribus, deprecemini supplicantes Dominum omnium, ut eripiat famulum hunc suum ab hac grauissima, afflictione. O Domina semper virgo, refugium fidelium, & fortissimum nostrum seruorum tuorum auxilium, tuis intercessionibus libera famulum hunc tuum à præsenti afflictione.
units.tr: O orders of the angelic powers, immaterial, together with the Apostles and Martyrs, entreat and supplicate the Lord of all to rescue this his servant from this very heavy affliction. O Lady, ever virgin, who presides over the faithful, O strong help for us your servants, by your intercessions deliver this your servant from the present affliction.

units.la: Maronitæ, qui Syri sunt, & Syriaca in sacris functionibus utuntur lingua, obiasque quoque eiusmodi ad B. Virginem Mariam, aliosque Sanctos formulas habent, ex quibus paucas. In Proœmio primæ stationis Nocturni Dominicæ simplicis Officij sic ad B. Virginem orant: [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters]
units.tr: The Maronites, who are Syrians and use the Syriac language in their sacred services, also have many such formulas addressed to the Blessed Virgin Mary and other saints, of which here are a few. In the proem of the first station of the Nocturn of the simple Sunday Office they pray thus to the Blessed Virgin: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: Te autem supplicamus, o mater vitæ, & fons lætitiarum, ut quemadmomodum per te nobis evenerunt omnia bona decalo, ita & preces nostras, atque humiles supplicationes cum suffitu hoc thymiamatum, illi, qui invariabiliter, & qua Deum decet, ex te natus est, offeras pro salute, & liberatione animarum nostrarum, & corporum. Ibidem statione 2. ad sanctos Prophetas, Apostolos, & Martyres. [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters]
units.tr: But we beseech you, O mother of life and fountain of joys, that as through you all good things have come to us from heaven, so you would offer our prayers and humble supplications, with this incense of perfumes, to him who was invariably born of you, as befits God, for the salvation and deliverance of our souls and bodies. Likewise at the second station, to the holy Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: Oeconomi estis Prophetae, Apostoli, & Martyres, Aperite thesaurum precum vestrarum, & auxilia prabete egentibus. Item in hymno S. Iacobi, qui legitur in commemoratione Beatae Virginis Mariae ad Missam: [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters]
units.tr: You are the stewards, O Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs: open the treasury of your prayers and give help to the needy. Likewise in the hymn of St James, which is read at the Mass commemorating the Blessed Virgin Mary: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: Perfice in nobis amorem tuum precibus matris tuae, que te supplicat, ut offeramus tibi thura pura in die illius commemorationis. Concede nonobis Domine nostra orationibus illius remissio-nem debitorum, necnon ipsius precibus parce omnia crimina.
units.tr: Perfect your love in us through the prayers of your mother, who asks you that we may offer you pure incense on the day of her commemoration. Grant to us, Lord our God, through her prayers the remission of our debts, and through her own entreaties spare us all our sins.

units.la: Moyses Princeps Veteris, & Simon Nove, ambo sibi sunt similes. Moyses descendere fecit tabulas Legis; & Simon accepit claves Regni: Moyses edificavit Tabernaculum temporis; Simon vero edificavit Ecclesiam ex Veteri, & Nova. Tibi laus Domine, Alleluia, oratio eorum auxilietur nobis.
units.tr: Moses was the prince of the Old, and Simon of the New; both are like each other. Moses caused the tablets of the Law to be brought down; and Simon received the keys of the kingdom. Moses built the tabernacle of the age; but Simon built the Church out of the Old and the New. Praise to you, Lord, Alleluia; may their prayer come to our aid.

units.la: Nestoriani in Officio diurno ad Vespe-ras in commemoratione B. Virginis Mariæ:
units.tr: The Nestorians, in their daily office at Vespers, in the commemoration of the Blessed Virgin Mary:

units.la: Oratio, Domine, Virginis Sanctæ, & precacatio Matris benedicta, supplicatio, ac deprecatio gratia plena Beata Maria sit nobis semper alta moenia, & munitum refugium, liberet, vindicet, & custodiat animas nostras a Malo, eiusque satellitibus omnibus temporibus, & momentis. Ibidem in commemoratione SS.
units.tr: By the prayer of the holy Virgin, the blessed intercession of the Mother, and the supplication and entreaty of the Blessed Mary, full of grace: may she always be for us a high wall and a fortified refuge, and may she free, defend and keep our souls from the Evil One and all his minions, at every time and moment. There, in the commemoration of the SS.

units.la: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: Oratio, Domine, Doctorum veracium, & deprecatio Iustorum perficientium voluntatem tuam supplicet pro nobis iustitiam tuam, ut concilies nobis tranquillitatem, & pacem tuam omnibus diebus vitae nostrae. Ibidem ad B. Virginem:
units.tr: Prayer, Lord, of the true teachers, and entreaty of the just who perform your will, may they plead for us your righteousness, so that you may grant us tranquillity and your peace all the days of our life. Likewise, to the Blessed Virgin:

units.la: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~13 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~12 letters] Maria Virgo Sancta, Mater Iesu Saluatoris nostri, supplica, & deprecare misericordias peccatoribus, ne pereant. Qui ad tuas orationes confugiunt, oratio tua sit illis murus in hoc Mundo, atque in futuro. Ibidem ad Sanctos: [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: [illegible] Holy Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus our Saviour, intercede and entreat mercy for sinners, that they may not perish. May your prayer be a wall to those who take refuge in your prayers, in this world and in the world to come. Likewise, to the saints: [illegible]

units.la: Beati sunt iusti, qui dilexerunt te, Seruator noster, & mandata custodierunt tua, ac voluntatem perfecerunt. Virtus abdita in ipsis custodiat Mundum, sintque in Ecclesia scaturigines auxiliorum. Infirmi sanentur, & curentur, claudi ambulent, & erigantur ab auxiliis officium ipsorum.
units.tr: Blessed are the righteous who have loved you, our Saviour, and kept your commandments and done your will. May the hidden power in them guard the world, and may there be in the Church springs of help. May the sick be healed and cured, the lame walk and be raised up by their aid in their office.

units.la: Quid plura? omnia sane Orientalium, quos pro se laudat Hottingerus, sine ulla tamen probatione, symbolica scripta huiusmodi formulis refertissima[?] sunt. Quamobrem unam producamus nunc, vel alteram formulam ex ijs, quibus Romana vtitur Ecclesia, ut collatione facta cum mox allatis, videant aequi, & probi Lectores, & iudicent, in quo consistat magnum Hortingeri [illegible, ~6 letters]. Oratio ex Officio paruo B.V.Mariæ ad Laudes: Deus, qui de B.Maria Virginis vtero, Verbum tuum, Angelo nunciante, carnem suscipere voluisti: præsta supplicibus tuis, vt qui vere eam Genitricem Dei credimus, eius apud te intercessionibus adiuvemur. Alia ad Primum: Deus, qui salutis æternæ B. Mariæ virginitate fecundæ, humano generi premia præstitisti: tribue quæsumus, vt ipsam pro nobis intercedere sentiamus, per quam meruimus Auctorem vitæ suscipere Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum filium tuum.
units.tr: What more is there? Certainly all these formulas of the Orientals, whom Hottinger praises for them without any proof, are symbolic writings crammed full of such formulas. Therefore let us now produce one or another formula from those used by the Roman Church, so that, once the comparison is made with those just cited, fair and honest readers may see and judge in what the great thing of Hottinger's [illegible] consists. A prayer from the Little Office of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Lauds: God, who willed that your Word, announced by an angel, should take flesh from the womb of the Blessed Virgin Mary, grant to your suppliants that we, who truly believe her to be the Mother of God, may be helped by her intercession with you. Another at Prime: God, who through the virginity of the Blessed Mary, fruitful in eternal salvation, bestowed rewards on the human race, grant, we pray, that we may feel her interceding for us, through whom we have deserved to receive the Author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

units.la: Pergit deinde Hottingerus: 2. Petri Apostoli, Sedisque veteris Romanæ honorifica hincinde apud Syros, Arabes &c: fit mentio, frustra tamen ad Monarchiam rapitur Pontificiam.
units.tr: Hottinger then goes on: the Apostle Peter, and the honourable seat of old Rome, are mentioned here and there among the Syrians, Arabs, etc.; yet it is dragged in vainly to establish the Papal monarchy.

units.la: Si verba profundere inania, & garrire duntaxat, esset probare, egregie profecto hanc suam assertionem probauit mugiendulus, sed cum non verbis inanibus, & meris assertionibus hic certandum sit, quis sanæ mentis compos, & æquus veritatis indagator non videt, Aduersarium desperatæ causæ esse patronum, & cæca tantum duci animi libidine? Etenim qui ad Monarchiam Pontificiam id rapi dicitur, quod omnium Orientalium mirifico consensu, & suffragio Pontifici Romano ex Nicæni Concilij decreto, & Canone decernitur?
units.tr: If it were enough to pour out empty words and merely chatter, this fellow, that bleating creature, would certainly have proved his assertion splendidly. But since this contest is not to be settled with empty words and bare assertions, who of sound mind and fair seeker of truth does not see that the opponent is the advocate of a lost cause, led only by the blind desire of his own mind? For how is it said that this is snatched away to a papal monarchy, which by the wonderful agreement and vote of all the Orientals is decreed for the Roman Pontiff by the decree of the Council of Nicaea?

units.la: وان ينظر البطريرك في كل امر عسل به احد من مطارنته او اساقفته في بلدانهم التي يلونها: فان وجد منهـا شيا على غيرما يمبغى فليغيره ويامر فيه بما يرى لانه ايدو جميعهم وبهم بقوة وانما المطران في رياسته عليهم وتوقيرهم ايساه بمنزلة الاخ الكبير الذى يقدمونه اخوذ ويوجبون طاعته بحسن سياسته وحكمته: فاما البطريرك فانه بمنزلة الاب في سلطانه على بنيه: وكما ان للبطريرك سلطان على من تحت يديه فكذلك يكون لماحسني رومية سلطان على سايير البطارکه مثل بطرس فيما كان لـــ من السلطان على جميع روسا النصرانيـه وجماعة اهلها لانــه خليفـــة المسيح على بيعته وكنايسه وشعوبه ومن خالف هذه المنه جماعـة السونذوس [illegible, ~4 letters]
units.tr: "The patriarch shall examine every matter which any of his metropolitans or bishops has handled in the lands they govern. If he finds anything in them not as it ought to be, let him change it and order what he thinks fit, for he is the strength of them all, and they are strengthened by him. The metropolitan's headship over them, and their honouring of him, is like that of an elder brother whom they put first, and they hold obedience to him obligatory because of his good governance and wisdom. But the patriarch is like a father in his authority over his sons. And just as the patriarch has authority over those under his hands, so the see of Rome has authority over the other patriarchs, such as Peter, in the authority he had over all the heads of the Christian nations and their peoples, because he is the successor of Christ over his church, his churches and his peoples. Whoever opposes this rule is of the company of the Sonthodus [illegible]." [Arabic transliterated: wa-an yanzur al-batriyark fi kull amr 'amila bihi ahad min matranatihi aw asaqifatihi fi buldanihim allati yulunaha; fa-in wajad minha shay'an 'ala ghayr ma yanbaghi fal-yughayyirhu wa-yamur fihi bima yara li-annahu 'adiduhum jami'an wa-bihim bi-quwwa...]

units.la: Patriarcha igitur inspiciat quodcunque negotium fecerit aliquis suorum Metropolitarum, siue Episcoporum in suis Provinciis, quibus praesunt. Si autem invenerit ex illis quicquam, quod non decet, permutet illud, ac de illo constituat, prout sibi videtur; etenim omnium ipsorum pater est, & illi filii sunt ipsius. Metropolitae autem principatum supra se agnoscere, eumque venerari debent instar fratris maioris, quem sibi anteponunt fratres, illique parere ducunt ob eius optimum regimen (seu officium) & maioritatem. Patriarcha porro instar patris est in sua iurisdictione super filios suos.
units.tr: The patriarch, therefore, shall examine whatever business any of his metropolitans or bishops has transacted in their provinces, over which they preside. If he finds anything there that is not fitting, let him alter it and determine about it as he sees fit; for he is the father of them all, and they are his sons. The metropolitans, moreover, ought to acknowledge a principate above themselves and venerate him as an elder brother, whom the brothers place before themselves, and they consider it right to obey him on account of his excellent rule (or office) and his greatness. The patriarch, moreover, is in his jurisdiction like a father over his sons.

units.la: Quemadmodum vero Patriarcha potestatem habet super subditos suos: ita quoque potestatem habet Romanus Pontifex super universos Patriarchas, quemadmodum habebat Petrus super universos Christianitatis Principes, & Concilia ipsorum; quoniam Christi Vicarius est super redemptionem, Ecclesias, & cunctos populos eius. Quicunque autem Sanctioni huic contradixerit, Patres Synodi illum anathemate percellunt.
units.tr: Just as the patriarch has authority over his subjects, so too the Roman Pontiff has authority over all the patriarchs, just as Peter had over all the princes of the Christians and their councils; since he is the Vicar of Christ over the redemption, the Churches and all his peoples. Whoever contradicts this sanction, the Fathers of the synod strike with anathema.

units.la: Frustra ne id rapitur ad Pontificiam Monarchiam statuendam, an vero clarissimis verbis, & Solis radiis scriptis asseritur ab Orientalibus eiusmodi Monarchia? Nec cauilletur Hottingerus, vel quispiam alius eiusdem farinae dicéns: Canonem hunc non esse verum, ac legitimum Concilij Nicæni. De hoc enim nobis cum Hottingero, & Symmystis inpræsens controuersia non est: Sed utrum Romani Pontificis Monarchiam in suis Symbolicis scriptis asserant Orientales illæ Nationes, an vero cum Reformatis in hoc conueniant? Nobis enim satis est inpræsens ostendere, Canonem hunc pro vero, ac legitimo Nicæno haberi a Chaldæis, Syris, & Arabibus, nempe Melchitis, Maronitis, Iacobitis, Nestorianis & Coptitis, quibus adde Æthiopes, in quorum omnium Conciliorum editionibus hic extat Canon, & pro Nicæno habetur; refertur que præterea in suarum Ecclesiarum Constitutionibus cap. De Patriarchis. De hoc vide quæ diximus par. 2. cap. 14. & seqq. nostri Eutychij vindicati. Garrit igitur Hottingerus hic, vt & alibi, atque gannit, suaque conficitur rabie, nulla veritatis habita ratione; nihil tamen in Christum Domini proficiens. Quamobrem audiat illud Arabis Poëtæ, in ipsum pene compositum.
units.tr: Is it in vain, then, that this is snatched away to establish a papal monarchy? Or is such a monarchy asserted by the Orientals in the clearest words and as plain as the sun's rays? Let Hottinger not wriggle out, nor anyone else of the same stripe, saying that this canon is not a true and legitimate canon of the Council of Nicaea. For the present controversy is not with Hottinger and his fellow-travellers on that point. The question is whether those Oriental nations assert the monarchy of the Roman Pontiff in their confessional writings, or whether they agree with the Reformed on this. For it is enough for us at present to show that this canon is held to be the true and legitimate Nicene canon by the Chaldeans, Syrians and Arabs, namely the Melchites, Maronites, Jacobites, Nestorians and Copts, to whom add the Ethiopians. In the editions of the councils of all of these the canon stands and is regarded as Nicene, and it is also cited in the Constitutions of their Churches, chapter "On Patriarchs." On this see what we said in part 2, chapter 14 and following, of our vindicated Eutychius. Hottinger therefore babbles here, as elsewhere, and snarls, and is consumed by his rage, with no regard for the truth, yet accomplishing nothing against Christ the Lord. Wherefore let him hear that verse of the Arab poet, composed almost against him.

units.la: اصبر على حين الحسود فـ[?]اني صبرك قاتله فالنار تأكل بعضها ان لم تجد ما تأكله
units.tr: Isbir 'ala hini al-hasud, fa-inna sabraka qatilah, fa-al-nar ta'kulu ba'duha in lam tajid ma ta'kulah. [Endure patiently the time of the envious; for your patience kills him. Fire eats itself if it finds nothing to eat.]

units.la: Innvidi sustine petulantiam, Patientia enim tua illum interimit: Ignis enim sese consumit, Si quid consumat, non reperit.
units.tr: Bear with the petulance of the envious man: your patience destroys him. For fire consumes itself, if it finds nothing else to consume.

units.la: Prosequitur Hottingerus illud suum tam celebre; Plura tamen nobiscuui sic: 3. habent & Orientales suos Monachos, & Monasteria, nec tamen sine discrimine.
units.tr: Hottinger pursues his point, so often repeated: Yet we have more in common in this respect too: 3. the Orientals also have their monks and monasteries, though not without distinction.

units.la: Habent profecto Orientales suos Monachos, qui paupertatem observant, Castitatem servant, Obedientiam suis praestant Praesulibus, quae sunt praecipua, ac palmaria huius professionis, & instituti capita. Sed haec eadem sancte, ac religiose coluntur a Monachis Pontificijs: Ergo in hisce nullum est inter utrosque discrimen. Agunt Monachi Orientales communem vitam, sunt cucullati, calceati aliqui, nonnulli discalceati; septem persoluunt canonicas horas, Beatissimam Virginem Mariam, aliosque invocant Sanctos, eorum venerantur reliquias, iuge offerunt sacro-sanctum Missae sacrificium, tam pro Vivis, quam pro Defunctis; plura habent peculiaria ieiunia, & eiusmodi. Sed haec omnia sancte praestant Monachi Pontificij, ergo in hisce nullum etiam est discrimen. Orientalium Monachi quidam pro parente, & duce habent D. Antonium Abbatem, quidam Diuum Basilium, quidam Pachomium, & juxta regulas ab his traditas, suos instituunt mores, & vestigia sequuntur, eodem plane modo, ac Pontificij, quorum aliqui pro parente S. Benedictum agnoscunt; nonnulli S. Augustinum, alij D. Bernardum, alij D. Dominicum, alij D. Franciscum, & alij alios; Ergo nullum agnoscitur discrimen. Si vero aliquid interfit, tam inter ipsos Orientalium Monachos, quam cum Pontificijs discrimen, id sane erit in rebus adiaphoris, & supererogatorijs, vti sunt quaedam jejunia, abstinentiae, ciborum delectus, vestitus asperior, & eiusmodi. Nunc assignet ipse Hottingerus, quos habent Reformati Monachos, & in quibus convenient cum Orientalium Monachis, cum praemittat hunc enumerans articulum: Plura tamen nobiscum sit, nisi in medium proferat Apostatas suos Lutheros, Oetolampadios, & eiusmodi alios, qui abiecto cucullo, & abiurato Monachatu, in omnium vitiorum illuviem sese dederunt.
units.tr: The Eastern Christians certainly have their monks, who observe poverty, keep chastity, and render obedience to their prelates. These are the chief and outstanding marks of this profession and way of life. But the Papist monks observe these same things just as devoutly and religiously. So in these matters there is no distinction between the two. The Eastern monks lead a common life. They wear cowls, some wear shoes, and some go barefoot. They recite the seven canonical hours, invoke the Blessed Virgin Mary and other saints, venerate their relics, and continually offer the most holy sacrifice of the Mass, both for the living and for the dead. They also have several special fasts and the like. But the Papist monks observe all these things devoutly, so in these matters too there is no distinction. Some Eastern monks take St Anthony the Abbot as their father and leader, some St Basil, some Pachomius, and they shape their way of life by the rules handed down by these men and follow their footsteps in exactly the same way as the Papists. Some of the Papists acknowledge St Benedict as their father, some St Augustine, others St Bernard, others St Dominic, others St Francis, and others still others. So no distinction is recognised here either. If there is any difference, both among the Eastern monks themselves and between them and the Papists, it will certainly lie in matters indifferent and supererogatory, such as certain fasts, abstinences, choice of food, rougher clothing, and the like. Now let Hottinger himself name the monks the Reformed have, and where they agree with the Eastern monks, since he begins by listing this article: Yet we have more in common. Unless he brings forward his own apostates, Luther, Oecolampadius, and others of that kind, who, having cast off the cowl and renounced monastic life, gave themselves over to a filth of every vice.

units.la: Pergit adhuc Hottingerus: 4. Patrum mentio, & allegata obvia sunt in Aethyopum, Syrorum, & Gracorum scriptis, neque tamen vt Cynosura, & Canon.
units.tr: Hottinger goes on: 4. Mention and citations of the Fathers are common in the writings of the Ethiopians, Syrians and Greeks, yet not as a Cynosure and canon.

units.la: Si semel mendax, suspectus in omnibus habenduseft, vel ex ipsiusmet Lucheri sentententia in Assertion. Teuton . art. 21. Qui semel mentitur, hic certissime ex Deo non est, & suspectus in omnibus habetur, quantus mendax habendus erit Hottingerus, ex hoc sui Lutheri placito, qui non semel, sed bis, terque, quaterque, imo semper mendax deprehensus est? Et quidem, si
units.tr: If a man who has lied once must be held suspect in everything, as even Luther's own opinion in his Assertion of the Teutonic articles, art. 21, has it: He who lies once is certainly not from God, and is held suspect in everything. How great a liar, then, must Hottinger be held to be by this maxim of his Luther, who was caught lying not once, but twice, three times, four times, indeed always?

units.la: Quo semel est imbuta recens seruabit odorem, Testa diu,
units.tr: A fresh jar will keep the scent of whatever it was first steeped in for a long time.

units.la: Quanto magis diutissime mendacis imbutus foedissimis Hottingerus, Cacabus, mendaciorum seruabit foetorem. Etenim nihil aliud Arabibus denotat الطبخه [?] Hottinger, quam Cacabus, Olla. Unde egregie Poëta Arab de Hominum cognomine,
units.tr: How much more will Hottinger, steeped for so long in the foulest lies, keep the stench of his lies, like a jar (Cacabus). For the Arabic word al-ṭabkha [?] signifies nothing other to the Arabs than Cacabus, a cooking pot. Whence the Arab poet excellently says, concerning the surname of men,

units.la: وقل ما ابصرت عيناك من رجلإلا ومعناه ان قشت في لقمه [?]
units.tr: wa-qalla mā abṣarat ʿaynāka min rajulin illā wa-maʿnāhu an qashshat fī luqmah

units.la: Pauci sunt, quos tui vident oculi, homines,Quorum notionem, si perquisieris, non designat cognomen.
units.tr: Few are the men your eyes behold whose meaning, if you inquire, their nickname does not express.

units.la: Asserit itaque الطبخه [?] Hottinger, Patrum mentionem, & allegata obvia esse apud Orientales, non haberi tamen ab eis, vt Cynosuram, & Canonem; Sed habentur; ergo mentitur, & ex illo foetidissimo Cacabo, hoc putidum profert mendacium, non autem ex Orientalium monumentis. Oftendamus, & primo ex Græcorum, seu Melchitarum Symbolicis scriptis.
units.tr: Hottinger therefore asserts that al-ṭabkha [?] has no mention of the Fathers, and that the passages he cites are found among the Orientals but are not held by them as authoritative, as the Cynosure and the Canon are. But they are held. Therefore he lies, and from that most foul pot he brings forth this rotten falsehood, not from the monuments of the Orientals. Let us show this, and first from the symbolic writings of the Greeks, or Melchites.

units.la: Melchitæ in Menologio, sub dienona Iunij hoc de sancto Cyrillo Archiepiscopo Alexandriæ recitant Troparium.
units.tr: The Melkites, in the Menologion, under the ninth day of June, recite this troparion concerning St Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria:

units.la: [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~24 letters] [illegible, ~24 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: Extitisti, o divino inflammate amore, Cyrille, director ad fidem Orthodoxam, Doctor illustris Religionis, Dux ad puritatem, & CYNOSURA Orbi habitabili, ac decus Principibus Sacerdotum, o Sapiens divine, documentisque tuis illuminasti Universum cognitione Spiritus. Quamobrem intercede apud Christum Deum pro salute animarum nostrarum. En Cynosura, Hottingere. Quo etiam titulo decoratur ibidem S. Gregorius Archiepiscopus Armenorum, sub die 30. Septembris; eodem S. Philippus Diaconus, sub die 11. Octobris; sanctus Nicander Episcopus Myræ, sub die 4. Novembris; sanctus Paulus Archiepiscopus Constantinopolitanus, sub die 6. eiusdem mensis; sanctus Theodorus Abbas, sub die 11. eiusdem; Sanctus Ioannes Damascenus, sub die 4. Decembris; Sanctus Maximus, sub die 21. Ianuarij. Eodem ferme omnes sancti Patres Ecclesiæ Doctores.
units.tr: You have appeared, O Cyril, inflamed with divine love, director to the Orthodox faith, illustrious teacher of religion, guide to purity, and CYNOSURE for the inhabited world, and ornament of the princes of priests; O divine wise one, who by your teachings have enlightened the whole universe with knowledge of the Spirit. Therefore intercede with Christ God for the salvation of our souls. Behold the Cynosure, Hottinger. With the same title St Gregory, Archbishop of the Armenians, is adorned there under 30 September; likewise St Philip the Deacon under 11 October; St Nicander, Bishop of Myra, under 4 November; St Paul, Archbishop of Constantinople, under the 6th of the same month; St Theodore the Abbot under the 11th of the same; St John of Damascus under 4 December; and St Maximus under 21 January. Almost all the holy Fathers and Doctors of the Church are so adorned.

units.la: Eosdem etiam Patres esse Fidei Canonem, idem testatur Menologium. Sic enim sub die decima octava Februarij legimus de sancto Leone Papa:
units.tr: The same Menologion testifies that these Fathers are also the canon of the faith. For under the eighteenth day of February we read thus of St Leo the Pope:

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] اطْهِرتـك افعـال الـــــق لرعيتـــــــك قانونـــا للامانه وصورة للوداعـــه ومعلمـــا للمساك ايها الاب لاون لاجل هـــذا اقتنيت بالتواضع الرفعـــه وبالمسكنـــه الغنـــا فتشفـــع الى المسيح الالـــه أن يغلـــص من نفوسـ ـــــــــــ [?]
units.tr: [illegible] aṭhharatka af‘āl al-ḥaqq li-raʿiyyatika qānūnan lil-amānah wa-ṣūrat lil-wadāʿah wa-muʿallimān lil-masākīn, ayyuha al-ab Lāwun; li-hādhā iqtanayta bi-l-tawāḍuʿ al-rifʿah wa-bi-l-maskanah al-ghinā, fa-tashaffaʿ ilā al-Masīḥ al-Ilāh an yakhlaṣa min nufūsinā [?] [Translation: The works of truth have made you a canon of faith for your flock, a pattern of meekness, and a teacher of the poor, O Father Leo. Therefore by humility you acquired exaltation, and by poverty riches. Intercede, then, with Christ God that he may save our souls.]

units.la: Profecto te promulgarunt opera veritatis gregi tuo CANONEM ad fidem, & exemplar ad mansuetudinem, atque Doctorem continentiæ, O Pater Leo; quapropter comparasti humilitate exaltationem, & paupertate diuitias, quamobrem intercede apud Christum Deum, vt saluet Animas nostras. En CANON. quo etiam adiuncto ornatur S. Nicolaus Episcopus Myrae, sub die 6. Decembris; sanctus Syluester Papa, sub die 2. Ianuarij; S. Leo Episcopus Catanensis, sub die 20. Februarij; sanctus Tharasius Archiepiscopus Constantinopolitanus, sub die 25. eiusdem. S. Porphyrius Episcopus Gazae, sub die 26. eiusdem; sanctus Nicephorus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, sub die secunda Iunij; S. Metrophanes Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, sub die 4. eiusdem; sanctus Andreas Cretensis, sub die 4. Iulij. Eodem, & omnes fere sancti Patres. Garrit igitur ex more Hottingerus, & suos Reformatos, male cautos suis lactat mendacijs.
units.tr: Indeed the works of truth have made you, for your flock, a canon of the faith, an example of gentleness, and a teacher of continence, O Father Leo. Therefore you acquired exaltation through humility and riches through poverty; intercede, then, with Christ God that he may save our souls. Behold the CANON. With this also is adorned St Nicholas, Bishop of Myra, under 6 December; St Sylvester the Pope under 2 January; St Leo, Bishop of Catania, under 20 February; St Tarasius, Archbishop of Constantinople, under the 25th of the same; St Porphyry, Bishop of Gaza, under the 26th of the same; St Nicephorus, Patriarch of Constantinople, under the second day of June; St Methodius, Patriarch of Constantinople, under the 4th of the same; St Andrew of Crete under 4 July. Likewise almost all the holy Fathers. So Hottinger chatters on as usual, and feeds his ill-guarded Reformed with his lies.

units.la: Ex Maronitis D. Ioannes Maro in præsatione Commentariorum ad Liturgiam sancti Iacobi, sic de Patrum iudicat doctrinam: [illegible, ~60 letters]
units.tr: Among the Maronites, Dom John Maro, in the preface to his commentaries on the Liturgy of St James, judges thus concerning the teaching of the Fathers: [illegible]

units.la: Custodite itaque diligenter quod vobis tradi-tum est ab Ecclesia sancta Catholica, quemadmodum didicit illa a Prophetis, atque Apostolis, & consignauit ipsi tertius Chorus Sanctorum Doctorum, qui omni tempore clarueruunt[?] in vera fide Orthodoxa, ac tanquam Sydera dirigentia in ea illuxerunt,
units.tr: Therefore keep carefully what has been handed down to you by the holy Catholic Church, as she learned it from the Prophets and Apostles, and as the third choir of holy Doctors has set its seal upon it. They have shone in every age in the true Orthodox faith, and have gleamed in it like guiding stars,

units.la: Imo sancti Patres sunt ipsis Maronitis Lampades. Officium sanctorum Basilij, & Gregorij ad Vesperas: [illegible, ~45 letters] [illegible, ~45 letters] [illegible, ~45 letters] [illegible, ~25 letters]

units.la: Benedictus est Christus, qui sibi elegit pra-cones fidei, ac tanquam lampades constituit, & illuminata est ab eis tota creatura.
units.tr: Blessed is Christ, who chose for himself heralds of the faith and set them up as lamps, and the whole creation has been enlightened by them.

units.tr: Christ, the light of truth, who has illuminated the earth with his rays through the holy Fathers and the orthodox Doctors, and those illuminated by him shone like the sun and, going forth, drove out the darkness of error.

units.tr: In you has been fulfilled that word which the Lord of truth spoke: You are the Light of the World, which was obscured by sin.

Jacobo, cum Divo Marone.
units.tr: In the holy Church is preached that faith which the holy Fathers taught us: the builders of the Church, true ministers, approved teachers and overthrowers of all heresies, Basil with great Gregory, Athanasius, and Cyril, the tower of truth, Eustathius, and John Chrysostom, with the chosen Ephrem, and Saint James, with the divine Maro.
