units.tr: Jacobites. The bishop, in the Homology which he gives to those being ordained, after commemorating the three Synods (for they reject the fourth, which was gathered against their heresy), speaks thus of the other Fathers:

units.la: Nominatim vero, & peculiariter suscipiatis, & agnoscatis Iacobum Episcopum Hierusalem Apostolum, & Martyrem, Linum Romanum, Anacletum Romanum, Clementem Romanum, Timotheum Ephesinum, Titum Cretensem, Ignatium Antiochenum, Polycarpum Smyrnensem, Dionysium Atheniensem, Hypolitum Romanum, Petrum Alexandrinum, Gregorium Neocaesariensem; Athanasium Alexandrinum, Basilium Caesariensem, Gregorium Nazianzenum, Gregorium Nyssenum, Meletium Antiochenum; Dionysium Alexandrinum, Eustathium Antiochenum, Nectarium Constantinopolitanum, ArArsacium Constantinopolitanum, Ioannem Constantinopolitanum, Theophilum Alexandrinum, Amphilochium Iconij, Cyprianum Carthaginensem, Irenaeum Lugdunensem, Methodium Olympiadis, Ephrem Doctorem, Isaac Doctorem &c. His volumus adhaereatis, & amplexemini, eorumque doctrinas puras, & probatas diligatis, & amplectamini, quicquid praestiterunt in Ecclesia sancta Dei ab eorum ortu usque ad finem vitae, sive in Canonibus, sive in scriptionibus, sive in Decisionibus, sive in excommunicationibus.
units.tr: You shall receive and acknowledge by name and in particular: James, bishop of Jerusalem, apostle and martyr; Linus of Rome; Anacletus of Rome; Clement of Rome; Timothy of Ephesus; Titus of Crete; Ignatius of Antioch; Polycarp of Smyrna; Dionysius of Athens; Hippolytus of Rome; Peter of Alexandria; Gregory of Neocaesarea; Athanasius of Alexandria; Basil of Caesarea; Gregory Nazianzen; Gregory of Nyssa; Meletius of Antioch; Dionysius of Alexandria; Eustathius of Antioch; Nectarius of Constantinople; Arsacius of Constantinople; John of Constantinople; Theophilus of Alexandria; Amphilochius of Iconium; Cyprian of Carthage; Irenaeus of Lyons; Methodius of Olympus; Ephrem the Doctor; Isaac the Doctor, etc. We wish you to adhere to and embrace these men, and to love and embrace their pure and approved teachings, whatever they have accomplished in the holy Church of God from their birth to the end of their life, whether in canons, in writings, in decisions or in excommunications.

units.la: Et post aliqua iubet, ut subscribant Homologiam, & signum Crucis imprimant, iterumque subdit; [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~9 letters] [illegible, ~9 letters] [illegible, ~9 letters] [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters]
units.tr: And after some words he orders them to subscribe the Homology and to impress the sign of the Cross, and he adds again: [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] [illegible]

units.la: Quoniam ecce coram Deo protestor aduersus vos, Obseruate Canones Apostolicos, & Homologiam hanc, & intelligite, quod signum hoc adorandae Crucis testimonium futurum sit inter me, & vos in die Iudicij, si quippiam iftorum mutauritis, & dicent Amen, Amen.
units.tr: For behold, I protest before God against you: observe the Apostolic Canons and this Homology, and understand that this sign of the adorable Cross will be a witness between me and you on the day of judgment, if you change any of these things; and let them say: Amen, Amen.

units.la: Item Daniel in Breuiario Conftitutionum Ecclesiae Iacobitarum, capite 7. de Canone librorum, post sacras Paginas Patrum recenset libros. ومن الكتب[?] المقبولة أيضا كتب الآباء اعني[?] آبية الدين مثل اثاناسيوس وغريغوريوس[?] وغريغوريوس الثاولوغوس ويوحنا فم[?] الذهب ومن يرى بجراهم[?]
units.tr: Likewise Daniel, in the Breviary of the Constitutions of the Jacobite Church, chapter 7, on the canon of books, after the Sacred Scriptures, enumerates the books of the Fathers. Arabic [wa-min al-kutub al-maqbula aidan kutub al-aba', a'ni aibiyat al-din, mithl Athanasiyus wa-Ghrighuriyus wa-Ghrighuriyus al-Thawlughus wa-Yuhanna fam al-dhahab wa-man yura bi-jarahum]: Among the accepted books are also the books of the Fathers, that is, the pillars of religion, such as Athanasius, Gregory, Gregory the Theologian, John Chrysostom, and those who are of their rank.

units.la: Ex libris quoque receptis sunt libri Antistitum[?], nempe Praefulum Religionis, uti sunt Athanasij, Cyrilli, Gregorij Theologi, Ioannis Chrysostomi, & aliorum huius notae.
units.tr: Among the received books are also the books of the leaders, namely the prelates of religion, such as Athanasius, Cyril, Gregory the Theologian, John Chrysostom, and others of this note.

units.la: Ex Cophtitis. Abnal-haffal in Praefatione Collectionis Can. & Conftit. Ecclesiae Alexandrinae, postquam pluribus differuit de traditionibus Apostolicis, haec subdit: والاصل المعتمد عليه في جملة هذا المعنى هو قول ربنا له المجد لتلاميذه[?] امضوا وعلموا كل الامم وعمدوهم[?]
units.tr: From the Copts. Abnal-haffal, in the preface to his Collection of the Canons and Constitutions of the Church of Alexandria, after discussing the apostolic traditions at some length, adds this: "The principal foundation relied on for this whole matter is the saying of our Lord, to whom be glory, to his disciples: 'Go, teach all nations and baptize them'" [wa-l-aṣl al-muʿtamad ʿalayhi fī jumlat hādhā al-maʿnā huwa qawl rabbinā lahu al-majd li-talāmīdhihi: imḍū wa-ʿallimū kull al-umam wa-ʿammidūhum].

units.la: باسم الاب والابن والروح القدس وعلّموهم جميع ما وصيتكم به وهانذا انا معكم الى انقضا العالم . ومعلوم انهم لم يبقوا دايمـــا في العالم ظاهـــر انــــه اشار بهذا القول الى خلفايهـــم القايمين في التلميذ له مقامهم ويوكّـــد هـــذا قوله لهم الذى اقوله لكم للجميـــــع اقوله ولذلك قيلت قوانـــــن الجامـــع المقدسه والروسا القدسين العلما مثل يوليوس بطرديك رومـيــه وداسيليـــوس اسقف قيساريه ومـــن عـــري عجراهـــا [?]
units.tr: bi-ism al-ab wa-l-ibn wa-l-rūḥ al-qudus wa-ʿallimūhum jamīʿ mā waṣiytukum bihi wa-hāʾanadhā anā maʿakum ilā inqiḍāʾ al-ʿālam. Wa-maʿlūm annahum lam yabqawū dāʾiman fī al-ʿālam. Ẓāhir annahu ashāra bi-hādhā al-qawl ilā khalāʾifihim al-qāʾimīn fī al-talāmīdh lahu maqāmahum, wa-yuwakkid hādhā qawluhu lahum: alladhī aqūluhu lakum aqūluhu lil-jamīʿ. Wa-li-dhālika qīlat qawānīn al-jāmiʿ al-muqaddasa, wa-l-ruʾasāʾ al-qadisīn al-ʿulamāʾ mithl Yūliyūs Baṭrīdīk Rūmiyya wa-Dāsīliyūs usquf Qayṣariyya wa-man ʿarā ʿajrahā. [Here the Arabic text is corrupt and the last words cannot be restored.]

units.la: Principium autem, cui innitendum est in fum-ma huius sensus, est dictum Domini nostri, cui gloria, Discipulis suis: Ite, & docete omnes gentes, & baptizate eos in nomine Patris, & Filij, & Spiritus Sancti, & docete omnia quæ-cunque mandavi vobis: & ecce ego vobiscum sum usque ad Consummationem Seculi. Notum autem est, eos haud manifesse semper in Mundo. Manifestum igitur erit, eum hoc innuisse dicto illorum Successores, qui ei in docendo ipsorum supplent vicem. Quod & confirmat dictum illiillius ad eosdem : quod vobis dico, omnibus dico. Hinc recepti sunt Canones sanctorum Conciliorum, & Principum sanctorum Doctorum, uti sunt Iulij Patriarchæ Romæ, Basilij Episcopi Cæsareæ, & aliorum huius notæ. Idem cap. 4. De Patriarchis, inter ea, quæ obseruare Patriarcha tenetur, hanc primo recenset loco conditionem :
units.tr: The principle on which the whole substance of this meaning must rest is the saying of our Lord, to whom be glory, to his disciples: "Go, and teach all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and teach them all things whatsoever I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the world." It is known, however, that they did not remain in the world for ever. It will therefore be plain that by these words he pointed to their successors, who take their place in teaching them. This is also confirmed by his saying to the same men: "What I say to you, I say to all." Hence the canons of the holy councils have been received, and those of holy princes and doctors, such as Julius, Patriarch of Rome, Basil, Bishop of Caesarea, and others of that rank. The same chapter, on the Patriarchs, among the things which the Patriarch is bound to observe, first lists this condition:

units.la: ويلزمهم [?] ـــــــــ [illegible, ~3 letters] من امورهم خمسة أشيا احدها حفظ الدين على اصوله المقررة وما ذ[?]ـــ عند الاجماع من اقوال الرسول ثم الجامع المقبوله ثم الا[?] الحسن على قو[?]ـــــ اقوال [?]ـــ
units.tr: wa-yalzamuhum … min umūrihim khamsat ashyāʾ, aḥaduhā ḥifẓ al-dīn ʿalā uṣūlihi al-muqarrara wa-mā … ʿinda al-ijmāʿ min aqwāl al-rasūl, thumma al-jāmiʿ al-maqbūla, thumma al-… al-ḥasan ʿalā qawl … aqwāl … [The Arabic is partly illegible.]

units.la: Tenetur autem ad quinque; Unum est observare Religionem iuxta constantia principia, & quod confirmatum est communi consensu, seu traditionibus ex dictis Apostolorum: Deinde receptorum Conciliorum, demum Patrum, quorum unanimis consensus dicta acceptat.
units.tr: He is bound to five things. The first is to observe the religion according to its established principles, and what has been confirmed by common consent, or by tradition, from the sayings of the Apostles. Next come the received Councils; finally the Fathers, whose unanimous consensus they accept as the sayings [of the Apostles].

units.la: Ex Nestorianis. Iesuiab Patriarcha, & Scriptor perantiquus, secundum post sacra Eloquia Patrum Canonibus tribuit locum, sic in Præfatione ad tractatum de Iudiciis Ecclesiasticis, tam universalibus, quam particularibus scribens:
units.tr: Among the Nestorians. Jesuiab, the Patriarch and a very ancient writer, assigns the Canons second place after the holy oracles of the Fathers. In the preface to his treatise on ecclesiastical judgments, both universal and particular, he writes thus:

units.la: Hæc autem descripsi ex ipso contextu divinarum Scripturarum duplici de causa; una ut tanquam digito, & in speculo Principi, & Rectori Ecclesiarum conspiciantur, ut edificat, & a se dirigendos doceat divina præcepta, quæ per Prophetas, & Apostolos Spiritu prolata sunt. Altera, ut magis, quam Canones Patrum, hæc oporteat cordis tabulis obsignari, & custodiri. Subdit præterea, illa Scripturarum eloquia, & Patrum dicta, ut pupillam oculi custodiri oportere: [illegible, ~12 letters] diri oportere: [illegible, ~10 letters]
units.tr: I have drawn these things from the very text of the divine Scriptures for a twofold reason: first, that they may be looked upon, as it were by a finger and in a mirror, by the Prince and Ruler of the Churches, so that he may build up and learn to direct those under him by the divine precepts which were uttered by the Spirit through the Prophets and Apostles. Second, that these should be sealed on the tablets of the heart and kept more than the Canons of the Fathers. He further adds that those utterances of the Scriptures and the sayings of the Fathers ought to be kept as the pupil of the eye: [illegible] [illegible]

units.la: [illegible, ~60 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: Non enim ut reponantur divini libri in fenestris, scripti sunt; & neque ut sicut cantilena, & Parabola quedam mundana occinantur in Ecclesia: Sed ut ne unum quidem ex eis cadat super terram, & ut sicut pupilla oculi custodiantur.
units.tr: For the divine books were not written to be placed on windowsills, nor to be sung in the Church like some ditty or worldly parable. They were written so that not one of them should fall to the ground, and so that they should be kept like the apple of the eye.

units.la: Timotheus item Nestorianorum Patriarcha in sua Nationali Synodo Can. 1. hoc idem asserit:
units.tr: Timothy, likewise Patriarch of the Nestorians, asserts the same thing in his national Synod, Canon 1:

units.la: [illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: [illegible]

units.la: Canon primus. Quod Canones Apostolici, & priscorum Patrum in Synodis tam Occidentalibus, quam Orientalibus definiti, tanquam pupilla oculi custodiantur; nec ulli fas sit transgredi ullum eorum; & ut omnes pij Patres, & Rectores Ecclesiarum sedulo, & diligenter eos meditentur, ac in eorum se exerceant lectione, & custodiant illos. Ex his vide, doctissime Leo, quae sit Hottingeri in rebus Orientalibus eruditio, nisi id adscribatur malitiae, & fraudi, quae ipsi proprietas est inseparabilis. Sed ad reliqua.
units.tr: Canon 1. The Apostolic Canons and those defined by the ancient Fathers in Synods, both Western and Eastern, are to be kept as the apple of the eye; no one may lawfully transgress any of them; and all devout Fathers and rulers of the Churches are to meditate on them diligently, exercise themselves in reading them, and keep them. From these words, most learned Leo, see what Hottinger's learning about Eastern affairs is, unless it is to be ascribed to malice and deceit, which are inseparable from his character. But on to the rest.

units.la: Post haec plura aggerit Hottingerus tumultuarie, ac sine numerorum notis ad ostendendam varietatem Romanos inter, & Orientales, & primo: Sed & plures, inquit, ad euincendam varietatem, diversos dies festos, Ieiunia utrique habent, multum ipsis testibus, & Pontificiis, & Græcis distantia. Quasi vero dierum festorum, ac Ieiuniorum varietas ipsi officit Religioni, & variam efficit. Quod nemo profecto sanæ mentis dicet, nisi insanire, & Hottingerum agere velit. Etenim in ipsa Romana Ecclesia quidam alicubi celebrantur dies festi, qui alibi, vel minime, vel alio tempore, quemadmodum, & quædam Ieiunia.
units.tr: After this Hottinger heaps up more material in a disorderly way, without numbered notes, to show the variety between the Romans and the Orientals. First he says: But also, to prove the variety, the two have different feast days and fasts, very different, according to the testimony of the Papists themselves and of the Greeks. As if variety in feast days and fasts harmed religion or made it varied! No one of sound mind would say this, unless he were mad and wished to play the Hottinger. Indeed, even in the Roman Church certain feast days are kept in some places which are not kept elsewhere at all, or are kept at another time, and so with certain fasts.

units.la: Tamen nemo prudens existimat, hæc in Ecclesia Romana variam efficere Religionem. Hoc idem & Orientalibus solemnis-simum est; Nam quædam Jeiunia, aliter obseruantur a religiosis viris, aliter a Laicis; tam diuersitatem temporis, quod attinet, quam ciborum delectum. Imo & ipsi Religiosi eiusdem instituti, ac Laici eiusdem persuasionis aliter, atque aliter nonnulla obseruant Jeiunia in diuersis Prouincijs, quemadmodum, & ipsos dies festos. Et ut de cæteris nunc taceam, Cophtitarum aliqui Quadragesimale jejunium, ac Pascha, alio, quam reliqui, tempore celebrant, ut plene constat ex Epistola Michaëlis, & Basilij Episcoporum, hac de re differentium.
units.tr: Yet no sensible person thinks that these things make religion various within the Roman Church. The same is most certainly true among the Orientals. For certain fasts are observed differently by religious men and by laymen, both as regards the timing and as regards the choice of foods. Moreover, the religious of the same order and the laity of the same persuasion observe some fasts differently in different provinces, just as they do feast days. To say nothing of other examples, some of the Copts celebrate the Lenten fast and Easter at a different time from the rest, as is fully clear from the letter of the Bishops Michael and Basil, who discuss this matter.

units.la: Prosequitur Hottingerus: cetera de Scripptura sacra, eius authoritate, necessitate transferendi in linguas vernacula's &c.
units.tr: Hottinger goes on: the rest concerning Holy Scripture, its authority, the necessity of translating it into the vernacular tongues, etc.

units.la: Qui nunc extant in nostro Oriente, quidquæso, aliud censent de Scripturæ auctoritate, quam quod ipsi Romani a Nugiuendulo isto scire velim? contra id vero, quod dicit de necessitate transferendi Scripturam in vernaculas linguas, publicus vsus, & vbique per totum Orientem praxis reclamat, eumque consueti mendacii arguit, & temeritatis. Etenim Syri, Chaldæi, Cophtitæ, Armeni, Æthiopes, aliæque Christianæ gentes, licet nunc habeant Arabicam, vel Turcicam, vel Persicam, vel Indicam, & eiusmodi pro vernaculis, com. munibus, & vulgaribus, nihilominus tam ipsam Scripturam, quam diuinas Liturgias, Officia, aliasque Ecclesiasticas functiones nulla alia obeunt lingua, nisi ea, qua sacro-sanctum Evangelium ipsis primo prædicatum est, & Evangelica lex tradita.
units.tr: Those who now exist in our East, I beg to know, think differently about the authority of Scripture from what the Romans themselves think? But against what he says about the necessity of translating Scripture into the vernacular tongues, the public usage and the practice found everywhere throughout the East cry out, and convict him of his customary lie and rashness. For the Syrians, Chaldeans, Copts, Armenians, Ethiopians and other Christian peoples, although they now have Arabic, Turkish, Persian, Indian and similar tongues as their native, common and everyday languages, nevertheless perform Scripture itself, the divine Liturgies, the Offices and their other ecclesiastical functions in no language but that in which the most holy Gospel was first preached to them and the evangelical law delivered.

units.la: Arabicam linguam si obijciat Hottingerus, sciat, hanc esse primariam, & ea primo prædicatum fuisse Arabibus Evangelium, quemadmodum Latina Latinis, Græca Græcis, & Syriaca Syris. Nec id sane vetat modo Ecclesia Romana, quinimo plurimum favet, cum sacro-sanctum Evangelium Arabice hic Romæ ad usum illarum gentium jamdudum typis ediderit, & nunc una totum excudit ad eundem finem Ve-tus Testamentum. Et quidem si lingua Latina adhuc Latinis vulgaris esset, quemadmodum antiquitus erat, quando prædicatum est illis Evangelium, & sacræ Liturgiæ institutæ, nequaquam aliam sibi quæreret Ecclesia Latina reconditiorem linguam ad sua sacra obeunda. Garrit igitur Hottingerus cum Petro Molinæo in suo impio illo antibarbaro, & ca-lulumniandi quærit occasiones, & ansas.
units.tr: If Hottinger objects Arabic, let him know that this is their chief language, and that the Gospel was first preached to the Arabs in it, just as the Latin was to the Latins, the Greek to the Greeks and the Syriac to the Syrians. Nor does the Roman Church in fact forbid this now; rather it greatly favours it, since it has long since printed the most holy Gospel in Arabic here at Rome for the use of those peoples, and now is printing the whole Old Testament for the same purpose. And indeed, if Latin were still the vernacular of the Latins, as it was in ancient times when the Gospel was preached to them and the sacred Liturgies instituted, the Latin Church would by no means seek for itself some more obscure language in which to perform its sacred rites. So Hottinger chatters along with Peter Molinaeus in that impious Antibarbarus of his, and seeks occasions and handles for slander.

units.la: Pergit: De lapsu Adami, peccati primi enormitate amissa imagine Dei, & effectis lapsus.
units.tr: He continues: On the fall of Adam, the enormity of the first sin, the loss of the image of God, and the effects of the fall.

units.la: Ego sane quid his velit, ut ingenue fatear, non capio, nec quorsum collimat, scio; cum nihil aliud de his sentiant Orientales, quam quod Ecclesia Romana.
units.tr: What he means by these things, to be honest, I do not grasp, nor do I know what he is aiming at, since the Orientals think nothing else about these matters than the Roman Church does.

units.la: Prosequitur: Legem feruandi impossibi-litate.
units.tr: He goes on: The law cannot be kept because of impossibility.

units.la: Paradoxum hoc est Hottingeri in suorum Reformatorum gratiam, nimirum Caluini in cap. 15, Act. & 2. Institut. cap. 17. Bezæ 2. par. Respon. ad acta Colloq. Montisbel, Piscatoris in thes. lib. 2., & aliorum, nuper in Oriente a Hottingero excogitatum, cum in nostro nullum eiusmodi impium dogma habeatur, solumque dicant, ad id requiri fidem tanquam radicem, & gratiam tanquam adiutricem; proinde passim ita
units.tr: This is a paradox of Hottinger's, invented to please his own Reformers, namely Calvin in chapter 15 of the Acts and in the second book of the Institutes, chapter 17, Beza in the second part of his Response to the Acts of the Colloquy of Montbéliard, Piscator in the Theses, book 2, and others. It has lately been devised by Hottinger in the East, though no such impious doctrine is held in ours; they say only that faith is required for this as the root, and grace as the helper. Accordingly they everywhere pray to God thus:

units.la: Deum deprecantur: [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters]
units.tr: Deum deprecantur: [illegible] [illegible]

units.la: Da nobis Domine noster gratiam tuam, ut seruiemus omnia præcepta tua.
units.tr: Give us, O Lord our God, your grace, that we may keep all your commandments.

units.la: Pergit: De Iustificatione, qua absque verborum involucris ita proponitur, ut peccatori omnis gratiæ fons in Christi merito fi-
units.tr: He continues: On justification, which is set forth without verbal wrappings, so that for the sinner every fountain of grace flows from the merit of Christ...

units.la: Furumputum mendacium est, si intelligat, sola fide sine operibus nos iustificari. Contrarium quippe testatissimum est apud omnes Orientales, quibus, Catholica Epistola D. Iacobi authentica, & canonica est, ac proinde passim illum cum Paulo conciliare totis viribus satagunt, uti nos ex ipsis in nostris notis ad Commentaria D. Ioannis Maronis in Liturgiam D. Iacobi fuse demonstramus. De hoc etiam Doctissimorum Orientalium integra extant opuscula.
units.tr: It is a downright lie if he means that we are justified by faith alone without works. The contrary is most clearly attested among all the Orientals, for whom the Catholic Epistle of St James is authentic and canonical, and who therefore everywhere strive with all their might to reconcile him with Paul, as we have fully demonstrated from them in our notes to the Commentaries of St John Maron on the Liturgy of St James. There are also complete treatises on this by the most learned Orientals.

units.la: Pergit : De Ordinatione Ministrorum ad præconium Verbi divini, & Sacramentorum administrationem.
units.tr: He continues: On the ordination of ministers for the proclamation of the divine Word and the administration of the Sacraments.

units.la: Putidum quoque mendacium est, quia non solum ad hæc fit Ordinatio Ministrorum apud Orientales, verum etiam ad plura alia, & ea præcipua, uti expressissimis verbis habetur in ordine ordinationis Presbyterorum Ecclesiæ Syriacæ in Oratione invocationis Spiritus sancti. Et cumprimis quidem ad sacro-sanctum Missæ Sacrificium, ad peccata remittenda, soluendo, & ligando, & eiusmodi. Episcopi vero ordinantur insuper ad gregem sibi concreditum pascendum, ad alios ordinandos Ministros, ad Chrisma conficiendum, Ecclesias, Altaria, & multa alia id genus benenedicenda. Nunc ingenue dicat Hottingerus, velim, in quibus consentiunt Orientales cum Reformatis? forsan in numero Sacramentorum, ad quorum administrationem, ex ipsius sententia, ordinantur Ministri? An vero in ipsa Ministrorum Ordinatione? Sed quis nescit, septem numerari apud Orientales omnes Sacramenta, apud Reformatos vero adhuc fere non constare, duo sint, vel minus? de Ministrorum Orientalium Ordinationibus ipsa loquuntur Ritualia, & Pontificalia; quæ autem extent apud Reformatos, proferat Hottingerus ex Reformatorum Ritualibus, & Pontificalibus, si usquam reperiantur in rerum natura, & cum Orientalium tum conferat Ordinationibus, si tantus est, deinde confidentius prædicet illud suum, Plura tamen nobiscum sic. Conveniunt forsan in ritu celebrandi Missam, vel ipsius corporis Christi dogmate? Sed sane tantum absunt in utroque, quantum Oriens ab Occidente, imo quantum verum a falso.
units.tr: This too is a stinking lie, because ordination of ministers among the Orientals is performed not only for these things but for many other, and chief, functions, as is stated in the plainest words in the order of ordination of the elders of the Syriac Church, in the prayer of invocation of the Holy Spirit. Above all it is for the most holy sacrifice of the Mass, for remitting, loosing and binding sins, and the like. Bishops are moreover ordained to feed the flock entrusted to them, to ordain other ministers, to consecrate the chrism, and to bless churches, altars and many other things of that kind. Now let Hottinger frankly say, I would like to know, in what the Orientals agree with the Reformed? Perhaps in the number of the Sacraments, for whose administration, by his own opinion, ministers are ordained? Or indeed in the ordination of ministers itself? But who does not know that the Orientals count all seven Sacraments, while among the Reformed it is still almost undecided whether there are two or fewer? The rituals and pontificals speak of the ordinations of Oriental ministers; if Hottinger has any of the Reformed rituals and pontificals, let him produce them from the Reformed rituals and pontificals, if they are to be found anywhere in nature, and let him compare them with the ordinations of the Orientals, if he is so great, and then let him more confidently declare his Yet we agree with them in so many things. Perhaps they agree in the rite of celebrating the Mass, or in the doctrine of the body of Christ? But indeed they are as far apart in both as the East is from the West, or rather as truth is from falsehood.

units.la: Pergit ulterius: De regimine Ecclesiastico, Cleri coniugio, ea in promptu sunt Orientis testimonia, quibus ementitum Allatij, & Ecchellensis consensum facile pessundare alia occasione poterimus.
units.tr: He goes on further: On church government, the marriage of the clergy: the Oriental testimonies are ready to hand, by which we can easily overturn the feigned agreement of Allatius and Ecchellensis on another occasion.

units.la: Pessundare facile poterit, sed iure Hottingeriano, ex Cacabo de more depromptis consuetis paralogismis, fallacijs, mendacijs, & fraudibus, quæ semper ipsi in promptu sunt ex conficto[?] ab eo Oriente, non autem nostri, testimonijs, quæ ea sunt, ut facile tam impudentia mendacia in os illud impurum retundere possint. Quid Sodes, commune habent Orientales cum Hottingeri Reformatis, aut quod proxime accedit, regiminis Ecclesiastici? Illi omnes per ordinem Hierarchicum suas administrant Ecclesias. Suos enim habent Patriarchas, Metropolitas, Episcopos, Presbyteros, Diaconos, Hypodiaconos, reliquosque Ordines cum subordinatione inseriorum ad superiores. Primi tres ordines Chrisma conficiunt, Ordinationes obeunt, Ecclesias, Altaria, & instrumenta ad diuinum instituta cultum benedicunt, ac alia præstant eiusmodi, quæ aliis non licent. Ostendat modo Thrafo, hæc in sua Reformata Ecclesia, & magnus nobis erit Apollo. Quod vero de coniugio Cleri subdit, summæ impietatis, & petulantiæ nota non caret; cum Clerus constet primo, & principaliter ex Patriarchis, Metropolitis, & Episcopis. Hos vero non esse coniugatos apud Orientis gentes omnes, nec vel ipse Hottingerus ignorare potest, nisi semper Hottingerus esse velit. Præterea, cum nullus apud eosdem Orientales ad ordinem Patriarchalem, Metropolitanum, aut Episcopalem assumi potest, nisi ex ordine Monachali, ipsi quoque Monachi magnam Cleri constituunt partem, & Clero adscribuntur. Hos quoque non esse coniugatos Lippis, & Tonsoribus notissimum est. Planum igitur ex his relinquitur, Hottingerum temere hanc positionem protulisse simpliciter, & absolute. Si vero eam intelligit de simplicibus Presbyteris, id nemo ipsi negavit, aut negat. Porro isti non sunt Clerus, sed pars Cleri minus principalis.
units.tr: He will be able to overturn it easily, but in Hottinger's manner, with the usual paralogisms, fallacies, lies and frauds taken as always from his cauldron, from testimonies invented by him about that East, not ours, testimonies of such a kind that they can easily beat back those shameless lies into that impure mouth. Pray, what do the Orientals have in common with Hottinger's Reformed, or what comes closest to it, in church government? All of them administer their churches through a hierarchical order. For they have their Patriarchs, Metropolitans, Bishops, Presbyters, Deacons, Subdeacons, and the other orders, with the lower subordinated to the higher. The first three orders consecrate the chrism, perform ordinations, bless churches, altars and the instruments devoted to divine worship, and perform other such acts which are not permitted to others. Let Thrafo only show that these things exist in his Reformed Church, and he will be a great Apollo to us. As for what he adds about the marriage of the clergy, it is not free of the mark of the greatest impiety and insolence, since the clergy consists first and chiefly of Patriarchs, Metropolitans and Bishops. Yet that these are not married among all the peoples of the East, not even Hottinger himself can be ignorant, unless he always wishes to be Hottinger. Moreover, since no one among the same Orientals can be raised to the Patriarchal, Metropolitan or Episcopal order except from the monastic order, the monks too make up a large part of the clergy and are counted among the clergy. That these are not married is well known even to the blear-eyed and to barbers. It is plain, then, from these things that Hottinger has rashly put forward this proposition simply and absolutely. But if he understands it of simple presbyters, no one has denied it to him or denies it now. Yet these are not the clergy, but a less principal part of the clergy.

units.la: Verum neque Ecclesia Romana hoc damnat, cum libere permittat Presbyteris Orientalibus coniugatis, etiam hic Romæ Sacrum conficere, & reliqua obire Sacerdotalia munia; nimirum Græcis, Maronitis, Syris, Armenis, & Chaldæis. Pariter nec Orientales Coelibatum damnant Sacerdotum, imo de illius laudibus, & commendatione integri apud eos extant tractatus, uti Eliæ Nisibensis Nestoriani adversus Giahetum scriptorem Mohammedanum, qui id impugnat libro De Animalibus: Iahiæ Benadi Iacobitæ, Dissertatione adversus afferentes, Christianos divinis adversari legibus Coelibatum observantes:
units.tr: But neither does the Roman Church condemn this, since it freely permits married Eastern priests to celebrate Mass here at Rome and to perform the other priestly duties: namely Greeks, Maronites, Syrians, Armenians and Chaldeans. Likewise the Easterners do not condemn the celibacy of priests; indeed there are full treatises in its praise and recommendation, such as that of Elias of Nisibis, a Nestorian, against Giahetus, the Mohammedan writer, who attacks it in his book On Animals; and that of Iahia Benadi, a Jacobite, in a dissertation against those who assert that Christians who observe celibacy act contrary to the divine laws.

units.la: Seueri abnalmoksahi Cophtitæ Episcopi Asmonin in Ægypto lib. De Cœlibatu, & aliorum. In Commentarijs etiam ad hæc verba Apostoli Epist. 1. ad Timotheum cap. 3. juxta Syriacam editionem :
units.tr: Severus Abnalmoksahi, Coptic bishop of Asmoun in Egypt, in his book On Celibacy, and others. Also in his commentaries on these words of the Apostle in 1 Timothy, chapter 3, according to the Syriac edition:

units.la: Opertet, ut Presbyter fit ille, in quo macula non reperitur, & qui fuit vir unius uxoris. Multi volunt, Apostoli verba intelligenda hic esse de Bigamia, non autem de permissione unius uxoris viuentis, cum aperte tam hæc Syriaca editio, quam aliæ Orientales dicant: Qui fuit vir unius uxoris.
units.tr: It is required that the elder be one in whom no blemish is found, and who was the husband of one wife. Many want the words of the Apostle to be understood here of bigamy, and not of the permission of only one living wife, since this Syriac edition, as well as the other Oriental ones, plainly say: who was the husband of one wife.

units.la: De varijs opinionibus circa horum verborum intelligentiam agimus in notis ad cap. 7. lib. D. Joannis Maronis, De Sacerdotio, ubi de hoc disserit argumento, & varias affert Interpretum sententias in supra laudatam Pauli ad Timotheum Epistolam. Quapropter non desunt apud Orientales Presbyteri cœlibes, neque Cœlibatus apud eos ulla lege, Canone, aut decreto interdicitur, imo plurimum commendatur, ut apud supra laudatos Scriptores vividere est. Sed nunc ad ea duo palmaria Hottingeri capita, de Confessione nimirum peccatorum; & statu Animarum extra Purgatorium, quæ ad hunc locum reseruauimus.
units.tr: We discuss the various opinions about the understanding of these words in the notes on chapter 7 of the book of Lord John Maron, On the Priesthood, where he treats this subject and brings forward various interpreters' opinions on the aforementioned Epistle of Paul to Timothy. Therefore among the Easterners there are not lacking unmarried presbyters, nor is celibacy forbidden among them by any law, canon or decree; indeed it is very much commended, as can be seen among the writers cited above. But now to the two outstanding heads of Hottinger, namely on the confession of sins, and the state of souls outside Purgatory, which we have reserved for this place.

units.la: De Confessione sic habet Hottingerus: De Confessione peccatorum, cuius elegantiffimas formulas ad Deum conceptas Syriaca habet Ecclesia. Quasi hisce dicat, homines Ecclesiæ Syriacæ foli Deo sua confiteri peccata, non autem Sacerdotibus, & in hoc conuenire cum Reformatis. Vnde illud eius: Plura tamen nobiscum sic.
units.tr: On confession Hottinger says thus: On the confession of sins, whose most elegant formulas addressed to God the Syriac Church possesses. As if by these words he means that the people of the Syriac Church confess their sins to God alone and not to priests, and that in this they agree with the Reformed. Hence his remark: Yet more with us thus.

units.la: Mirum est, quantum mendacijs delectatur Hottingerus, & paralogismis, qui etiam confitendo ipsi Deo ab illis temperare nequit. An, quæso, quia Ecclesia Syriaca elegantissimas habet formulas ad Deum conceptas, negat propterea Confessionem, & formulas, quibus sua peccata pœnitentes confitentur Sacerdotibus? An vero formulæ illæ ex sua vi, & natura excludant alias, & auriculari Confessioni, tam Reformatis molestæ, aliquo opponantur modo? Sed an & Ecclesia Romana, quæ auricularem Confessionem inter Sacramenta enumerat, non habeat etiam elegantissimas formulas ad ipsum Deum conceptas? Audiat Hottin-gegerus Orationis præparatoriæ ad Confessionem verba: Tibi confiteor, Pater piissime, peccata mea: quæ si volo abscondere non possum tibi Domine; parce mihi, Christe, quem ego nuper multum offendi cogitando, loquendo, operando, & in omnibus modis in quibus ego fragilis homo, & peccator peccare potui, mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa. Ideo, Domine, precor tuam clementiam, qui de Cælo pro mea salute descendisti, qui David a peccati lapsu erexisti, parce mihi, Domine, parce mihi Christe, qui Petro te neganti pepercisti. &c. Eiusmodi infinitæ propemodum extant formulæ. Concordat itaq; Syriaca Ecclesia cum Romana in formulis ad Deum conceptis.
units.tr: It is remarkable how much Hottinger delights in lies and paralogisms, and he cannot even refrain from them when confessing to God himself. Pray, because the Syriac Church has most elegant formulas addressed to God, does it therefore deny confession, and the formulas by which penitents confess their sins to priests? Or do those formulas by their own force and nature exclude others, and are they opposed in some way to auricular confession, so troublesome to the Reformed? But does not the Roman Church as well, which counts auricular confession among the sacraments, have most elegant formulas addressed to God himself? Let Hottinger hear the words of the prayer preparatory to confession: I confess to you, most pious Father, my sins; which if I wish to hide, I cannot hide from you, Lord; spare me, Christ, whom I have lately offended greatly by thinking, speaking, doing, and in all the ways in which I, a frail man and sinner, could sin, through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore, Lord, I beseech your clemency, you who descended from heaven for my salvation, who raised David from the fall of sin, spare me, Lord, spare me, Christ, who spared Peter denying you, etc. Almost countless formulas of this kind exist. Thus the Syriac Church agrees with the Roman in formulas addressed to God.

units.la: Videndum itaq: nunc superest, utrum conveniat, & congruat etiam in auriculari, & sacramentali Confessione, quæ fit Sacerdotibus. Hoc enim est, quod male habet, & pungit Hottingerum, quasi aculeis, & stimulat.
units.tr: It remains now to see whether it agrees and accords also in auricular and sacramental confession, which is made to priests. For this is what troubles and pricks Hottinger, as if with goads and stings.

units.la: Quemadmodum Medicus, nisi praecognoscat corporea accidentia, quæ iuxta illius professionem notiones vocantur, nequit omnino curare aut mederi: ita & Sacerdos Medicus animarum nisi praecognoscat passiones animarum, nequit sanare.
units.tr: Just as a physician cannot cure or heal at all unless he first knows the bodily symptoms, which in his profession are called notions, so too a priest, the physician of souls, cannot heal unless he first knows the passions of the soul.

units.la: Infirmi vero, qui celant suos morbos, & procurant, seipsos sanare, aberrant a suo scopo, quoniam infirma est eorum virtus, & perturbatus humor, adeoque dulce videtur illis amarum. CONFIRMATIO. Iob: Si peccavi inuoluntarie, erubui a multitudine lasionis populi . Quem versiculum exponens S. Ioannes dicit: Vides animam Iob præclaram, quæ non erubuit coram toto populo dicere: peccata mea inuoluntaria . Si enim ille non erubuit, quanto magis id nos facere oportet. Dic itaque prius peccata tua, vt iustificeris . Proverbia Salomonis: Homo, qui abscondit iniquitatem suam, non prosperabitur: qui vero confitetur peccata sua, & ab illis recedit, liberabitur . Barafira ( Ecclesiasticus ): Ab iniquitatibus tuis recede, & ne erubescas confiteri peccata tua . Euangelium : Tunc exibat ad eum Ierosolyma, & omnis Iudæa, & omnis regio circa Iordanem, & baptizabantur ab eo in Iordane flumine, confitentes peccata sua . Iacobus: Confitemini ergo alterutrum peccata vestra, & orate pro inuicem, vt sanemini. Acta: Multi ex ijs, qui crediderunt, veniebant enarrantes peccata sua, & confitentes actus suos. Ioannes: Si confiteamur peccata nostra: fidelis est, & iustus, vt remittat nobis peccata nostra, & emundet nos ab omni iniquitate nostra . Theologus : Omne onus, quo iuste obtrectare videmur, ne nostros morbos nostris aperiamus medicis, eo tendit, vt id obtrectando, sanitatem euitemus. OBIECTIO. Confessio causa est, vt sine intermissione homines peccatis polluantur, nimirum contaminantur, vt sanctificentur confitendo, & rursus ad idem vomitum reuertendo, & sic omnibus diebus vitæ suæ suis concupiscentijs animas suas maculant ; Confessio igitur plus affert damni, quam vtilitatis . RESPONSIO.
units.tr: Sick people, however, who conceal their diseases and try to heal themselves, miss their aim, since their strength is weak and their humour disturbed, so that the bitter seems sweet to them. CONFIRMATION. Job: "If I have sinned unwittingly, I blushed before the multitude of the people." Expounding this verse, St John says: "You see the excellent soul of Job, who did not blush to say before the whole people: my sins were unwitting." For if he did not blush, how much more ought we to do so. "Tell your sins first, therefore, that you may be justified." Proverbs of Solomon: "The man who hides his iniquity will not prosper, but he who confesses his sins and turns from them will be delivered." Barafira (Ecclesiasticus): "Turn away from your iniquities, and do not be ashamed to confess your sins." Gospel: "Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region about the Jordan, and they were baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins." James: "Confess therefore your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed." Acts: "Many of those who had believed came, declaring and confessing their deeds." John: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all our iniquity." The Theologian: "Every burden by which we seem rightly to be hindered, namely not disclosing our sicknesses to our physicians, tends to this, that by hindering this we avoid health." OBJECTION. Confession is the cause by which men are without interruption polluted by sins, that is, contaminated, so that they are sanctified by confessing, and return again to the same vomit; and so all the days of their life they stain their souls with their lusts. Confession therefore brings more harm than benefit. ANSWER.

units.la: Ne ex aequiuocatione errorem inferatis ; quoniam non omnem Confessionem vtilem esse dicimus ; sed eam peculiarem tantum, quae fit post veram poenitentiam, quae est contritio animæ de peccato patrato tempore præterito, & discessus ab illo tempore præsenti, & promptus recessus tempore futuro . Post adimpletionem autem horum trium Canonum, si rursus succumbit natura, qua variabilis, & fluxa, non est mirum, nec desperemus, oportet, præsertim audientes illud : septuagies septies . Dilucidatione porro secunda septem recenset methodos, quibus animæ curantur morbi, analogia eleganter deducta ex curatione corporis morborum.
units.tr: Do not draw an error from an equivocation, for we do not say that every confession is useful, but only that particular confession which is made after true repentance, which is contrition of the soul for sin committed in past time, withdrawal from it in the present time, and a ready turning away from it in future time. After these three canons have been fulfilled, if nature, which is changeable and frail, gives way again, this is no wonder, and we should not despair, especially hearing that saying: "seventy times seven." Further, in the second elucidation he lists seven methods by which diseases of the soul are cured, an analogy elegantly drawn from the cure of bodily diseases.

units.la: Quoties accedit homo ad confitenda, & aperienda sua errata, adulterium scilicet, siue fornicationem, siue homicidium, siue furtum, siue fraudem, siue criminationem, siue quicquid eiusmodi est operum malorum peccati, oportet, vt Episcopus, siue Presbyter, siue quisquis mediator est, & confessioni praefectus magnopere caueat primo, ne vnquam manifestum faciat id, quod audiuit, sed vt Deus misericordia moueatur erga peccatores, nec temere omnino, aut aspernetur eum, qui peccauit. Secundo, ne diminuatur prorsus in oculis eius homo ille, eo quod percepit peccatum eius. Et quantumcumque durum, & amarum sit eius peccatum, ne deijciat eum spe, neque despiciat, sed quemadmodum aspiciebat illum ante Consessionem, sic aspiciat illum. Verum etiam nec accipiat faciem eius, siue propter amicitiam aliquam, siue propter gradum, & dignitatem, aut propter spem lucrorum immundorum, seu donorum, & munerum. Quippe qui medicus spiritualis est, adeoque oportet, vt juxta mensuram morbi dimetiatur ipsi medicamenta sanitatis, prout satis est peccatori ad ferendum. Fiat autem Confessio ita. Ad portam Ecclesiae sedeat ille, qui excipit, nempe sustinet Confessionem, siue ante januam Altaris ris ; poenitens vero aperto capite, & genu dextero super terra flexo, & inclinatus oculis in terram defixis , & complicatis ante pectus manibus , confiteatur tanquam coram Deo Consessionem perfectam, ac sine verecundia, nec aspiciat illum , cui confitetur, & aperit ; neque is in eum aspiciat, quoniam ipsi Deo, qui omnia videt ante esse , offertur Confessio . Tunc respondebit Sacerdos, & dicit poenitenti omni tranquillitate, & suavitate : vide mi dilectissime, & scito , quod si ex toto corde tuo confiteris, & caves , neiterum, & in æternum facies , quod modo revelasti, nec reverteris ad peccatum, ecce ex nunc Deus per me tibi dicit : remissa sunt peccata tua ; & opera ista peccatorum, quæ voluntarie revelasti, ac te fecisseconfessus es, nequaquam iterum revelabuntur, neque in die magni Judicij , neque ratio pro illis a te exigetur a Judice iusto. Tunc vero imponit illi Canonem , prout ipsi videtur , jejunium scilicet ad tempus determinatum, & genuflexiones temporibus orationum , & misericordiam , scilicet eleemosynas pauperibus elargiendas, secundum eius facultatem.
units.tr: Whenever a person comes forward to confess and disclose his sins, whether adultery, fornication, murder, theft, fraud, slander, or any other such wicked deed, the bishop, or presbyter, or whoever is the mediator and presides over the confession, must take great care. First, he must never make known what he has heard, but must act so that God is moved to mercy toward sinners, and he must not at all rashly reject the one who has sinned. Second, he must not let that man be diminished in his eyes because he has learned of his sin. However hard and bitter his sin may be, he must not cast him down with despair or despise him, but must look upon him just as he looked upon him before the confession. Nor must he show partiality, whether from some friendship, or on account of rank and dignity, or from hope of unclean gains, gifts, or bribes. For he is a spiritual physician, and so he must measure out the remedies of health according to the measure of the disease, as much as the sinner is able to bear. The confession is made in this way. The one who receives it, that is, who hears the confession, sits at the door of the Church, or before the door of the altar. The penitent, with his head uncovered, his right knee bent to the ground, his eyes inclined and fixed on the earth, and his hands folded before his breast, confesses a complete confession, as before God, and without shame; he does not look at the one to whom he confesses and discloses his sins, nor does that one look at him, since the confession is offered to God himself, who sees all things before they exist. Then the priest responds and speaks to the penitent with all calmness and gentleness: "See, my dearest, and know that if you confess with your whole heart, and take care never again, and for ever, to do what you have now revealed, and do not return to sin, behold, from now on God says to you through me: your sins are forgiven. And these works of sin which you have voluntarily revealed, and which you have confessed to have done, will by no means be revealed again, neither on the day of the great judgment, nor will an account be demanded of you for them by the just Judge." Then he imposes on him a canon of penance as seems fit to him, namely a fast for a set time, genuflections at the times of prayer, and acts of mercy, that is, alms to be given to the poor according to his means.

units.la: Hæc ex Jacobitis paulo fusius, & pauca ex multis, eo quod fuerunt nonnulli, qui mera quadam, futili, ac lepida assertione scriptum reliquerunt; Jacobitas Confessionem nullam admittere, sed soli Deo con-fifitendum censent . Hæc sententia sic sine vlla auctoritate , vel testimonio prolata plurimum arridet Aduersarijs, vt qui semper negatiuis, & falsis propositionibus gaudent . Sed quam falsa sit ex allatis mox ipsorum Iacobitarum Symbolicis scriptis , & Scriptoribus planissime constat . Qui autem eam amplectuntur, & laudant Hottingerus , & M. Elias Veielius Vlmensis , ostendant, demonstrent, & probent Iacobitarum Syrorum aliquam auctoritate , & testimonio , & herbam porrigemus vtrique. En Rhodus, en saltus . Nec satis est , vt Reformatis verbis , & inanibus appellet Veielius clarissimi viri Bartholdi Nihusijad id prouocationem , lepidam simul, &Thrasonicam inuitationem. Res ipsa in foris clamat, in patulo est. Accedat Veielius, accedat Hottingerus, accedant quicunque a partribus eorum sunt , videamusque , vtrum nos, an illi hæc thrasonice, & lepide iactent.
units.tr: I have set out these things from the Jacobites at some length, and only a few out of many, because there have been some who left behind in writing a bare, futile and witty assertion: that the Jacobites admit no confession, but hold that it is to be made to God alone. This opinion, put forward thus without any authority or testimony, greatly pleases the adversaries, who always delight in negative and false propositions. But how false it is, is quite plain from the symbolic writings of the Jacobites themselves, just cited, and from their writers. Let those who embrace and praise it, Hottinger and M. Elias Veielius of Ulm, show, demonstrate and prove some authority and testimony of the Syrian Jacobites, and we will hold out the white flag to both. Here is Rhodes, here is the leap. Nor is it enough that Veielius, in empty words, appeals to the challenge of the most distinguished man Bartholomew Nihusius, a witty and boastful invitation at the same time. The matter itself cries out in the open street; it is plain. Let Veielius come forward, let Hottinger come forward, let whoever are of their party come forward, and let us see whether it is we or they who boast of these things in a Thrasonic and witty way.

units.la: Quid porro hoc de argumento sentiant Nestoriani, & Cophtitæ, diximus alias in notis ad Catalogum librorum Hebediesu , eorumq; fuse retulimus testimonia , quo remittimus nunc Aduersarios, qui auctoritatibus, & testimonijs respondeant ad auctoritates & testimonia,cum hisce nunc certetur, non autem inanibus verbis, & nudis assertiotionibus. Hac enim ratione unico verbo, imo unica particula omnia Reformatorum effata & ego evertere possum, si dicam: Non.
units.tr: What the Nestorians and Copts think on this subject we have set out elsewhere, in the notes to the Catalogue of the books of Hebedjesu, and we reported their testimonies at length there. We now refer our opponents to that place. They should answer authorities and testimonies with authorities and testimonies, since that is what is now being contested, not with empty words and bare assertions. By this method I could overturn all the pronouncements of the Reformers with one word, or even one particle, by simply saying: No.

units.la: Ex Maronitis vero, praeter ea, quæ habentur in Catechismo, plures de hac etiam materia scripserunt, inter quos tamen Gabriel Klahi vir doctissimus, & in omni litterarum genere eruditissimus, integrum edidit Opusculum, quo petulantia ora retundi facile poterunt, si Epistolæ limites hoc nobis permitterent. Sed alias, & opportuniori occasione, Deo sospitante.
units.tr: Among the Maronites, many have also written on this subject besides those things found in the Catechism. Among them, Gabriel Klahi, a most learned man and most erudite in every kind of literature, published a complete little work by which the impudent mouths could easily be silenced, if the limits of a letter allowed it to us. But that will be for another occasion, and a more opportune one, God willing.

units.la: Melchitæ hoc de argumento fusè agunt in suo Catechismo, ubi inter cætera hæc subijcitur: هرذ ـــــه على الاعتراف
units.tr: The Melchites treat this subject at length in their Catechism, where, among other things, the following is added: (Hadha ... 'ala al-i'tiraf)

units.la: Adhortatio ad Confessionem, ligata oratione, ut facilius memoriae tradatur, & retineatur.
units.tr: An exhortation to Confession, in verse, so that it may be more easily committed to memory and retained.

units.la: بغير الاعتراف لا عحد لك توبة. ولاعو ذنب ولو قتلت شهيدا :ولو صمت كل الدهر بالمسك والعيا .واحفيت طي الركبتين مديدا :ولو سجدت يدك فى الارض بالعطا .
units.tr: (Bi-ghayr al-i'tiraf la yahsul laka tawba, wa-la yughfar lak dhanb, wa-law qutilta shahidan.) Without confession, you have no repentance, and no sin of yours is blotted out, even if you die a martyr.

units.la: على قاطبهها مزملا وشردا [?] :
units.tr: (ʿAla qatibiha muzammilan wa-sharadan.) Over all of them, wrapped up and ...

units.la: فما ذاك الا مثل خرقة حيضة [?] .
units.tr: (Fa-ma dhalika illa mithl khirqa ḥaydha.) This is nothing but like a menstruous rag,

units.la: اذا لم يكن اقرار منك لسيدا [?] :
units.tr: (Idha lam yakun iqrar minka li-sayyidi.) if there is no acknowledgment from you to your master,

units.la: فلا يطغوك الظالمين بقولهم [?] . الى الله
units.tr: Let not the wrongdoers mislead you by their saying [falā yaṭghawannaka al-ẓālimīna bi-qawlihim?] to God.

units.la: دفع الاعتراف حيدا [?] :
units.tr: The repelling of confession, turning aside [dafʿ al-iʿtirāf ḥaydan?].

units.la: فقد قال عزّ الله قولا [?] . ختم بـ [?]
units.tr: For God, mighty is He, has spoken a word [faqad qāla ʿazza Allāh qawlan?], sealed with [khatama bi-?].

units.la: فيكفا به من قايل وشهيدا [?] :
units.tr: (Fa-kafa bihi min qa'il wa-shahidan.) and with that as speaker and witness it is enough.

units.la: يا ين خلاص الناس بالناس كايف [?] . فلا
units.tr: (Ya'ni khalas al-nas bi-al-nas kayfa.) For the salvation of men is through men, how ...

units.la: تبقى بعدهسا لمزدا [?] :
units.tr: (Tabqa ba'dahha li-mazdan.) so that after it nothing remains for the one who ...

units.la: Sine Confessione nulla est tua pœnitentia, nec tuum deletur crimen, etiamsi Martyr obieris.
units.tr: Without confession your repentance is nothing, and your sin is not blotted out, even if you die as a martyr.

units.la: Et quamuis totum ieiunaueris seculum continentia, & laboribus, ac utrumque iugiter flexeris genu.
units.tr: Even if you fast your whole life long in continence and labours, and bend both knees continually,

units.la: Etiamsi elargita manus tua liberaliter fuerit in terra dando eius incolis obsequentibus, & inobedientibus.
units.tr: even if your hand has given generously to the earth, to its obedient and disobedient inhabitants,

units.la: Hoc nihil aliud erit, nisi instar panni menstruatæ, si præceptori confessus non fueris.
units.tr: this will be nothing other than a rag stained with menstruation, if you have not confessed to your teacher.

units.la: Nec te decipiant seductores dicendo: Deo Confessionem cfferre, est laudabile.
units.tr: Do not let the seducers deceive you by saying that offering confession to God is laudable.

units.la: Iam enim conclusit Deus gloriosus dicto, quod satis sit pro afferente, atque teste. Quod salus hominum per homines est, cui posthac nihil addendum esse contendas.
units.tr: For God the glorious has already settled it by his word that the one who brings it and the witness are enough, and that the salvation of men is through men; to this nothing further should be added, you may be sure.

units.la: Videatur etiam [illegible, ~12 letters] Ioannes Teiunator, [illegible, ~10 letters] Theodorus Abbas Monasterij [illegible, ~6 letters] Alastadiun, qui difertissime, & fusissime de hac scripserunt materia, vt nec ipsas minutissimas ad illam spectantes prætermiserint circumstantias. Nunc ad celeberrimam de Purgatorio quaestionem.
units.tr: Let there also be consulted John the Faster, [illegible] Theodore, Abbot of the Monastery [illegible] of Alastadiun, who wrote most fluently and fully on this matter, so that they did not omit even the smallest circumstances relating to it. Now to the much-debated question of Purgatory.

units.la: De Purgatorio fuse egimus in notis ad Catalogum librorum Hebediesu pagina 165. & seqq. vbi diximus primo loco, Orientales, Syros præsertim, nomine [illegible, ~5 letters] Sciul, seu Inferni intelligere tam locum, in quo cruciantur Damnati æternum, quam eum, in quo animæ leuioribus criminibus, & maculis coinquinatæ purgantur, atque (licet nomine differat) re tamen ipsa eundem esse, ac Romanum Purgatorium. Quinimo nunc addimus ibi dictis, nomine [illegible, ~5 letters] Scial apud Chaldæos de solo loco, in quo animæ ad tempus cruciantur, intelligi. Quod quidem con-stat stat ex ipsa definitione, seu descriptione ipsius [illegible, ~3 letters] Sciul, quam affert Hebed-iesu Chaldæus in suo libro inscripto: [illegible, ~6 letters] De Ordinatione, seu dispositione Iudiciorum, qui est collectio Canonum, & Constitutionum Ecclesiæ Nestorianorum, cap. de [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~24 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: We have treated Purgatory at length in the notes to the Catalogue of the books of Hebedjesu, page 165 and following, where we said first that the Orientals, the Syrians especially, understand by the name Sciul, or Hell, both the place where the damned are tormented eternally and the place where souls stained with lighter crimes and defilements are purified; and that, although the name differs, the thing itself is the same as the Roman Purgatory. Moreover, we now add to what was said there that among the Chaldeans the name Scial is understood to mean only the place in which souls are tormented for a time. This is evident from the very definition or description of the Sciul given by Hebedjesu the Chaldean in his book entitled On the Ordination, or Arrangement of Judgments, which is a collection of the canons and constitutions of the Church of the Nestorians, chapter on [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] [illegible].

units.la: Explicatione vocabulorum, quorum cognitio utilis, & necessaria est omnibus Christianis, præsertim ordini Sacerdotum; Ubi sic illud nomen definit: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters]
units.tr: Explanation of terms, whose knowledge is useful and necessary for all Christians, especially the order of priests; where he defines that name thus: [illegible] [illegible]

units.la: Sciul est domus Carceris tristis animarum imbecillium, seu coinquinatarum. A quo autem loco statim contradistinguit Gehennam, locum Damnatorum, ratione durationis, sic definiens: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] Gehenna est domus cruciatus, qui durat sine dissipatione[?], seu fine. Hinc quando oratur apud Orientales pro Defunctis, supplicatur Deus, vt animas eorum eruat a poenis Sciul siue Inferorum: At nunquam a poenis Gehennæ, a quibus nulla est redemptio; etsi oretur, ne mittantur in eam. In quo quidem sensu intelligendum venit illud Ecclesiæ Romanæ in Officio Defunctorum: A porta Inferi erue Domine animas eorum. Demonstrauimus præterea in ipsis notis, suffragia viuorum pro Defunctorum animabus, nihil prodesse Damnatis, & id ex capite 39. Constit. Ecclesiæ Maronitarum, & Melchitarum, cap. 22. Cophtitarum, & cap. 5. sect. 1. Iacobitarum; vbi verba referuntur traditionis Apostolicæ, ac inter cætera dicitur: Et sane credimus, id fieri pro illis, qui præditi sunt continentia, fide, & iustitia, nam pro maiorum (criminum) patratoribus, & Infidelibus, etsi in eleemosynam erogaretur quicquid in hoc mundo bonorum est, nihil illis proderit. Hanc eandem traditionem Apostolicam sub Iacobi nomine totidem, ac numeratis verbis refert Hebedie-su libro supra laudato, titulo
units.tr: Sciul is the sad prison-house of weak, or defiled, souls. But right after this place he distinguishes Gehenna, the place of the damned, by its duration, defining it thus: [illegible] [illegible] Gehenna is the house of torment which lasts without end or cessation. Hence, when prayer is made among the Orientals for the dead, God is entreated to deliver their souls from the punishments of Sciul, or Hell; never from the punishments of Gehenna, from which there is no redemption, even if prayer is made that they not be sent into it. In this sense must be understood that line of the Roman Church in the Office of the Dead: Deliver their souls, O Lord, from the gate of Hell. We have also shown in those same notes that the prayers of the living for the souls of the dead profit the damned nothing, and this from chapter 39 of the Constitutions of the Maronite Church, chapter 22 of the Melchites, chapter 22 of the Copts, and chapter 5, section 1, of the Jacobites, where the words of the Apostolic tradition are quoted, and among other things it is said: And surely we believe that this is done for those who are endowed with continence, faith and righteousness; for those who are perpetrators of greater crimes, and unbelievers, nothing will profit them, even if everything good in this world were given in alms. Hebedjesu, in the book cited above, under the title quoted, gives this same Apostolic tradition under the name of James, in just as many words and in the same order.

units.la: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~12 letters] De diebus obdormientium, siue Defunctorum & qui sunt absoluendi: Iacobi.
units.tr: [illegible] [illegible] On the days of those who have fallen asleep, or of the dead, and who are to be absolved: James.

units.la: Ostendimus etiam ibidem ex auctoritate, ac testimonio Ioannis Episcopi Darensis, Scriptoris celeberrimi 4. saeculi a Christo Domino apud Syros, animas Defunctorum leuioribus delictis, & sordibus coinquinatas igne Purgatorio purgari. Quam quidem tam vetusti Scriptoris auctoritatem, vt quae plurimum pungit, & vrget latera Hottingeri impudentissime afferentis, ac ferrea fronte pronunciantis, Nullam plane in Syrorum Symbolicis Scriptis Purgatorij mentionem esse, hic iterum repetere non pigebit, vt videant inde, qui ab eius stant partibus, qualem meretur in reliquis fidem. Verba ipsissima sunt ex lib. 4. De Resurrectione Mortuorum cap. 24. Si lenibus alis, inquit, predita est anima, in suo discessu ad illum, qui eam attraxit, in laetitia erit perfecta; si vero onus passionum gestat, afflictionem patitur, non quod odit, aut vlciscitur Creator, sed vt ad se attrahat PVRIFICATAM; Quemadmodum materiam, quae commixta est auro, in ignem immittunt, vt purificetur, quae confusa inimitur, & dissipatur, puritas vero auri remanet; ita quoque malitia, cum igne purificante omnia, absumitur, & dissipatur, necesse etiam est, vt anima, cui illa adhaesit, vna in igne fit, donec sordes, & malitia prauorum operum, quae in ea congregata sunt, illo igne purificentur. Et post pauca subdit: Ita etiam ab anima, quae passionibus materialibus est inquinata, vt tormentorum isthaec abraduntur. Haec autem afflictio non est ad damnationem, sed ad PVRGATIONEM peccatorum, & macularum. Et paucis interiectis: Scopus enim mentis divinae est, vt omnis perfectio fiat naturae nostrae. Sunt quippe, qui statim in mundo a malitia purgantur, & sunt etiam, qui post hanc vitam per ignem iuxta passiones suorum vulnerum curantur.
units.tr: We showed also in the same place, on the authority and testimony of John, Bishop of Dara, a most celebrated writer of the fourth century after Christ the Lord among the Syrians, that the souls of the dead, stained with lesser offences and defilements, are purged by Purgatorial fire. Since Hottinger, who attacks us most shamelessly and pronounces with brazen face that there is plainly no mention of Purgatory in the symbolic writings of the Syrians, pricks and presses our side so sharply, I will not hesitate to repeat that authority of so ancient a writer here, so that those on his side may see what trust his other statements deserve. The very words are from book 4, On the Resurrection of the Dead, chapter 24: "If the soul is endowed with gentle wings," he says, "then at its departure to him who drew it to himself, it will be in perfect joy; but if it bears the burden of passions and suffers affliction, this is not because the Creator hates or takes vengeance, but so that he may draw it to himself PURIFIED; just as they put material mixed with gold into the fire so that it may be purified, and what is mingled is consumed and dissipated while the purity of the gold remains; so too, when all wickedness is consumed and dissipated by the purifying fire, it is necessary that the soul to which it clung should be in the fire together with it, until the filth and malice of the evil deeds gathered in it are purified by that fire." And after a few words he adds: "So too the soul that has been defiled by material passions is scraped clean of these by torments. This affliction, however, is not for damnation but for the PURGING of sins and stains." And after a few words intervene: "For the aim of the divine mind is that every perfection should come to our nature. There are indeed some who are purged of malice at once in the world, and there are also some who, after this life, are healed by fire according to the sufferings of their wounds."

units.la: [illegible, ~25 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] [illegible, ~18 letters] Requiescere fac in regno tuo caelesti nos, & illos post egressum nostrum de hoc mundo; & ignosce, transfer, & remitte peccata nostra, ac Defunctorum fidelium, voluntaria, & inuoluntaria, vel deliquerimus scienter, vel ignoranter. Hinc quidem cognoscimus, peccata, & delicta dimitti non solum in hoc mundo, verum etiam in alio; Deumque exigere peccata in hoc, & illo mundo, vel commissa sint scienter, vel ignoranter. Et sane nisi ea exigeret, nequaquam pro illis Ecclesia deprecaretur; & nisi dimitteret, nequaquam Commemorationem faceret Defunctorum omni tempore, neque supplicaret pro illis in omnibus orationibus. Deum autem exigere peccata, & delicta quedam in eo mundo, manifestum est ex Euangelio: Non exies inde, donec reddas nouissimum quadrantem. Beatus vero Paulus Epistola prima ad Corinth. indicat, igne delicta eiusmodi deleri, & purgari: Uniuscuiusque opus manifestum erit; dies enim ille reuelabit illum, quoniam igne reuelabitur, & uniuscuiusque opus quale sit, ignis segregabit. Si cuius opus manserit, quod aedificauit, mercedem accipiet. Si cuius opus arserit, detrimentum patietur: ipse autem saluus erit: sic tamen quasi ex igne. Theologus quoque dicit: Accidit, ut ibi igne baptizentur nouissimo baptismo, qui longe laboriosior est, ac longior, quique comedit materiam tanquam stipulam, & consumit paruitatem totius malitiae. Gregorius quoque Nyssenus: quoniam itaque virtus purgatiua infit igni, & aquae, qui baptizati non sunt hac purgatione, scilicet aqua lacrymarum, & igne contritionis, necessario igne purgandi erunt. Abbas Euagrius: Cruciatus est dolor per ignem, qui iuste purgat passionem animae.
units.tr: [illegible] [illegible] "Cause us and them to rest in your heavenly kingdom after our departure from this world; and pardon, transfer and remit our sins, and those of the faithful departed, both voluntary and involuntary, whether we have offended knowingly or unknowingly." From this we recognise that sins and offences are forgiven not only in this world but also in the other; and that God requires satisfaction for sins committed in this world and in that, whether they were committed knowingly or unknowingly. Indeed, if he did not require it, the Church would never pray for them; and if he did not forgive, it would never make commemoration of the dead at every time, nor offer supplication for them in all its prayers. That God requires certain sins and offences in that world is evident from the Gospel: "You shall not get out thence until you have paid the last farthing" (Matt. 5). Moreover, the blessed Paul in his first Epistle to the Corinthians shows that offences of this kind are blotted out and purged by fire: "Every man's work shall be made manifest; for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work, of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss; but he himself shall be saved, yet so as by fire." The Theologian also says: "It happens that there they are baptised with fire, with the last baptism, which is far more laborious and longer, and which consumes the matter like stubble and consumes the smallness of all wickedness." Gregory of Nyssa also: "Since therefore the purgative power inheres in fire and in water, those who have not been baptised by this purification, namely the water of tears and the fire of contrition, must of necessity be purged by fire." Abbot Evagrius: "Torment is pain through fire, which justly purges the passion of the soul."

units.la: Hisce adstipulatur Gregorius Barhebraeus Iacobita tractatu De Fundamentis Ecclesiae, libro 7. capite 3. sectione 3.
units.tr: Gregory Barhebraeus, the Jacobite, agrees with these things in his treatise On the Foundations of the Church, book 7, chapter 3, section 3.

units.la: Animæ fidelium, si inquinatæ non fuerint, lætitia quadam spirituali exultant, ex perceptione precum pro se: si vero fuerint inquinatæ, perceptione precum pro se magis satagunt ad abstergendā sua Specula a maculis, quæ eis adhærent, ac tanquam submersi quidam a suis adiuti sociis sese mouent ad salutem. Ego vero maius agnosco emolumentum ex precibus, piorum porro hominum virtutibus præditorum, quia se conformando anima inquinata animabus eorum, diuinis informatis imaginibus, ipsa quoque deificatis illis sese insinuabit, & conformatione ad eas satis digna fiet. Infidelibus autem nulla prodest oratio, quia lumine carent, quemadmodum illa Samuelis minime Sauli profuit, & Hebrais illæ Prophetarum, qui pro eis grare satagebant. Hoc quippe redarguuntur: petitis, & non accipietis, eo quod male petatis.
units.tr: The souls of the faithful, if they are not defiled, rejoice with a certain spiritual gladness when they perceive that prayers are offered for them. If they are defiled, they strive all the more, on perceiving the prayers offered for them, to wipe the stains from their mirrors that cling to them, and, like men half-drowned who are helped by their companions, they move toward salvation. I, however, recognise a greater benefit from the prayers of pious men endowed with virtues: a defiled soul, by conforming itself to their souls, which are informed by divine images and themselves deified, insinuates itself into them and becomes sufficiently worthy of their likeness. But prayer profits unbelievers not at all, because they lack the light, just as Samuel's prayer did not profit Saul at all, and as the prayers of the Prophets, who laboured on behalf of the Hebrews, did not profit them. For this is the rebuke: "You ask, and do not receive, because you ask amiss."

units.la: De Sacrificijs, commemorationibus, & requiebus, quæ faciunt fideles pro Defunctis suis secundum Canones Apostolicos, dubitant indocti. Si enim nō prosunt Sacrificia, & commemorationes Defunctis, quomodo credimus, quod Dominus Iesus Christus (cuius Maiestati adoratio) semetipsum obtulerit Sacrificium Patri, & soluerit debitum patris nostri Adami, ac peccatum eius remiserit, quod fuit causa mortis? Qui enim de hoc dubitat, Christianus non est.
units.tr: Some uninstructed people doubt concerning the sacrifices, the commemorations and the requiems which the faithful perform for their dead according to the Apostolic Canons. For if sacrifices and commemorations do not profit the dead, how can we believe that the Lord Jesus Christ, to whose majesty adoration is due, offered himself as a sacrifice to the Father, paid the debt of our father Adam, and remitted the sin which was the cause of his death? For whoever doubts this is not a Christian.
