units.la: وادـــمـــا قـــال [?] باسيليوس اخبرني عن النصارى الذين خرجوا من هذه الدنيـــا وخطاياهـــم سجيـــه وقــــد حبستـــ نفوسهـــم في الذزاذين المظلمـــه ايتنفعهـــم القربـــانين الذين يقربونه في حياتهم وهل تخـــس النفس بذلك : أجابـــه غريغوريـــوس ان موسى الطوباني صنع قربانـــا وســـال الله ان يغفر لروبيل بن يعقـــوب ذنبـــه وكانت نفســـــه مع نفـــوس الخطـــاة فردها الله الى عنـــد أخوتـــه فكيـــف الكاهن الـذي أعطى السلطـــان ان يربط الخطايا ويحلّها . ومثلهـــم مثـــل اناس محبوسين ولهم اصدقا يهمون بهـــم فهم يظلمون الى القاضـي والوالى مـــن اجلهـــم كل حـــين والى القيـــام على راس رأس الملك وعلى بابه ولا يقرّون [?] حتى تخلص من اعاديهم [?]
units.tr: wa-qāla Bāsīlyūs: akhbirnī ʿan al-naṣārā alladhīna kharajū min hādhihi l-dunyā wa-khaṭāyāhum sajība, wa-qad ḥabasat nufūsuhum fī l-dhazādhīn al-muẓlima; a-yanfaʿuhum al-qurbānīn alladhī yuqarrabūnahu fī ḥayātihim, wa-hal taḥuss al-nafs bi-dhālika? Ajābahu Gharghūriyūs: inna Mūsā al-ṭūbānī ṣanaʿa qurbānan wa-sāʾal Allāh an yaghfira li-Rūbīl ibn Yaʿqūb dhanbahu, wa-kānat nafsuhu maʿa nufūs al-khuṭāt, fa-raddahā Allāh ilā ʿinda ikhwatihi; fa-kayfa al-kāhin alladhī aʿṭā l-sulṭān an yarbuṭa l-khaṭāyā wa-yaḥillahā? Wa-mithluhum mithl unās maḥbūsīn wa-lahum aṣdiqāʾ yahummūna bihim, fahum yaẓallūna ilā l-qāḍī wa-l-wālī min ajlihim kull ḥīn, wa-ilā l-qiyām ʿalā raʾs al-malik wa-ʿalā bābihi, wa-lā yaqirrūna ḥattā takhluṣ min aʿādīhim.

units.la: Dixit quoque Basilius: indica mihi de Christianis, qui demigrarunt ex hoc mundo peccatis coinquinati, quorumque animae inclusae sunt in locis tenebrosis, prodest ne illis Sacrificium, quod statis temporibus offertur? & utrum anima id percipiat? Respondit illi Gregorius: si B. Moyses Sacrificium operatus est, Deumque rogauit, ut condonaret Rubeno filio Iacobi peccatum illius, cuius anima cum animabus peccatorum erat, quam propterea restituit Deus ad fratres suos; quanto magis Sacerdos, cui data est potestas ligandi peccata, & soluendi? Horum autem comparatio est instar eorum hominum, qui in carcere detinentur, habentque amicos de ipsis sollicitos, qui omni tempore rogant pro eis iudicem, praesidem, & ad regis caput adstantes, & ad ianuam illius, nec desistunt, donec liberentur amici eorum. Et paulo inferius haec subdit:
units.tr: Basil also said: Tell me about the Christians who have departed from this world stained with sins, and whose souls are shut up in dark places: does the Sacrifice which is offered at the appointed times profit them? And does the soul perceive it? Gregory answered him: If the blessed Moses offered a Sacrifice and besought God to pardon Reuben the son of Jacob his sin, whose soul was among the souls of sinners, and God therefore restored him to his brethren, how much more should the priest, to whom power has been given to bind and to loose sins, do so? Their case is like that of men who are held in prison and have friends who are anxious about them, who at all times plead for them before the judge and the governor, and who stand at the head of the king and at his gate, and do not desist until their friends are freed. And a little further on he adds this:

units.la: وايضا فلو لم يسّوا براحة تنال اليهم من جهة القرابين والطلبات عنهم لما امرنا [?] به وخصّ فاعلوه بمجاهدة [?]
units.tr: wa-ayḍan fa-law lam yasūbbū rāḥa tanāl ilayhim min jihat al-qarābīn wa-l-ṭalabāt ʿanhum lamā amarnā bihi wa-khaṣṣa fāʿiluhu bi-mujāhada.

units.la: Praeterea, nisi perciperent aliquam requiem ex Sacrificijs, & precibus pro illis, nequaquam id nobis præceptum fuerit, neque nos id faceremus ex communi consensu.
units.tr: Moreover, unless they perceived some relief coming to them from the Sacrifices and the prayers offered for them, this would never have been commanded us, nor would we do it by common consent.

units.la: Ex hactenus allatis Orientalium testimonijs æquum ferant modo ludicium, vel ipsi Reformati de hoc Hottingeri pronunciato; De statu Defunctorum extra Purgatorium, cuius nulla plane in Syrorum, Arabum, Aethiopum scriptis Symbolicis mentio. Quo quid, quæso, magis temere, aut impudentius in mortalium theatrum, & lucem proferre poterat Hottingerus? Etenim vel hæc, & eiusmodi viderat ille, vel non. Si viderat; qua cauteriata conscientia negauit? si non viderat, insigni profecto temeritatis nota, & impudentiæ inurendus est. Etenim negauit, quasi vero omnia Orientalium euoluissent monumenta, quæ vix forte e limine salutauit, primisque degustauit labijs. Negando etiam, se rem, de qua loquitur, nescire apud omnes prædicat, quia ex Philosopho Metaph. 3. Ille scit rem, qui scit affirmatiue, non negatiue.
units.tr: Let the Reformed, from the testimonies of the Orientals brought forward so far, now pass a fair judgment on this pronouncement of Hottinger, On the state of the dead outside Purgatory, of which there is absolutely no mention in the Symbolic writings of the Syrians, Arabs and Ethiopians. What, I ask, could Hottinger have brought before the stage and light of mortals more rashly or more shamelessly? For either he had seen these and similar things, or he had not. If he had seen them, with what cauterised conscience did he deny them? If he had not seen them, he must certainly be branded with a distinct mark of rashness and shamelessness. For he denied them, as if he had unrolled all the monuments of the Orientals, when he had barely greeted them from the threshold and tasted them with the tips of his lips. By denying, he also proclaims to all that he does not know the matter about which he speaks, since, as the Philosopher says in the Metaphysics 3: "He knows a thing who knows it affirmatively, not negatively."

units.la: Huc etiam spectat, quod ibidem pag. 23. ad num. 25. ita scribit Hottingerus: Purgatorium incendere ignem irrita plane est opera, utrumque enim non violentis consequentiarum fidiculis: sed verbis expressis largiuntur cum reliquis Orientalibus Græci, & Purgatorium Romanum se ignorare, & tamen ritum orandi pro Defunctis, ut ex viatoribus fiant beati spectatores se retinere.
units.tr: To this also pertains what Hottinger writes in the same place, page 23, at number 25: "To say that fire burns in Purgatory is a plainly vain labour, for both are granted not by violent strings of consequences, but by express words, by the Greeks along with the other Orientals, who are ignorant of Roman Purgatory; and yet the rite of praying for the dead, so that from wayfarers they may become blessed spectators, is retained."

units.la: Hæc quam temere, ex allatis patet. Purgatorium ignem irrita opera incendimus violentis consequentiarum fidiculis, an Orientales ipsi expressissimis largiuntur verbis? Constat hoc ex eorum Symbolicis scriptis, nec ne? Nos ea attulimus Orientalium testimonia, quæ ignem hunc incendunt; proferat modo Hottingerus illa, quæ illum extinguunt, & in promptu habet, quibus ementitum, uti ait, Allatij, & Ecchellensis consensum facile pessundare poterit. Adiutrices porrigat manus M. Elias Veielius. Reforment Orientalium Purgatorium. De Græcis res Hottingero cum Magno Leone est. Reliquos Orientales Purgatorium Romanum ignorare, Hottingeri maxima ignorantia est, nisi consuetis commentis Romanorum nomine aliquod comminiscatur in agro Romano Purgatorium, quod ubi sit, facile ignorare potuerunt Orientales. Quod vero dicit de ritu orandi pro defunctis, ut ex viatoribus fiant beati spectatores, eodem excidit plane argumento. Quia hoc afferere, non est negare Purgatorium, neque cum dogmate de Purgatorio repugnat, etiamsi largiamur ei, animos separatos esse viatores, cum tamen proprie, & stricto modo non sint, nec id ab Orientalibus dicatur.
units.tr: How rashly this is said is clear from what has been brought forward. Do we kindle fire in Purgatory by violent strings of consequences, or do the Orientals themselves grant it in the most express words? Does this appear from their Symbolic writings or not? We have brought forward those Oriental testimonies which kindle this fire; let Hottinger now produce those which extinguish it, and if he has them at hand, with them he will easily be able to overthrow the agreement, as he says, invented by Allatius and Ecchellensis. Let Elias Veielius stretch out his helping hands. Let him reform Oriental Purgatory. As for the Greeks, the matter is between Hottinger and Leo the Great. That the remaining Orientals are ignorant of Roman Purgatory is the greatest ignorance on Hottinger's part, unless he invents, under the name of the Romans, some Purgatory in the Roman field, the location of which the Orientals could easily have been ignorant of. As for what he says about the rite of praying for the dead, so that from wayfarers they may become blessed spectators, it falls plainly under the same argument. For to assert this is not to deny Purgatory, nor does it conflict with the doctrine of Purgatory, even if we grant that the separated souls are wayfarers, although strictly and properly speaking they are not, and this is not said by the Orientals.

units.la: Concludit tandem Hottingerus: Quamquam in Syrorum libris leiturgicis obseruauerim, precibus, ideo potissimum Defunctos Deo commendari, vt tempore vltimi Iudicij clementem resuscitati experiantur Iudicem; gloriosaque adeo beentur resurrectione.
units.tr: Hottinger concludes at last: Although I have observed in the liturgical books of the Syrians that the dead are commended to God principally by prayers, so that at the time of the last Judgment, having been raised, they may experience a merciful Judge, and may be blessed with a glorious resurrection.

units.la: Concludit profecto, verbisque modo imponit finem Hottingerus; Sed si mutare potest Aethiops pellem suam, aut Pardus varietates suas, & Hottingerus poterit mutare malitiam, cum didicerit malum ab ipsa ineunte aetate. Imposuit finem verbis, sed vtinam fallacijs, vtinam paralogismis. Nam quis Hottingero id inficiatus est, aut inficiatur? An in Ecclesia quoque Romana hoc deprecandi genus pro Defunctis in vsu non sit? & an, qui id praestant, Purgatorium excludant, & negent? Nequaquam profecto, imo Syri vtrumque deprecandi genus impense pro Defunctis absoluunt, nimirum, vt Deus propitius sit eis tempore vltimi Iudicij, & vt eos liberet a poenis Purgatorijignis. Primum obseruauit probus, ac ingenuus suo more Hottingerus; adeoque probatione non eget; alterius, quod oculos illos Reformato linitos pharmaco fugerat, nobis incumbit probatio; quanquam satis superque ex jam allatis probatum fit . In Officio 5. Dominicæ Quadragesimæ, quod est de Paralytico sanitati a Christo Domino restituto, hæc apud Syros ad cantum:
units.tr: Hottinger indeed concludes, and now brings his words to an end: But if the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots, then Hottinger may also be able to change his malice, since he has learned evil from his earliest age. He has brought his words to an end, but would that he had ended his deceptions, would that he had ended his paralogisms! For who has denied, or who denies, this to Hottinger? Is not this kind of prayer for the dead in use in the Roman Church also? And do those who perform it exclude and deny Purgatory? By no means. Indeed the Syrians fervently perform both kinds of prayer for the dead, namely, that God may be propitious to them at the time of the last Judgment, and that he may free them from the punishments of the fire of Purgatory. Hottinger, honest and ingenuous in his manner, has observed the first point, and so it needs no proof; the proof of the other point, which he had overlooked with his eyes smeared by the Reformed ointment, falls to us, although it is already sufficiently and more than sufficiently proved from what has been brought forward. In the Office for the Fifth Sunday of Lent, which concerns the paralytic restored to health by Christ the Lord, the following is sung among the Syrians:

units.la: Infirmitatibus animæ, & corporis nostri, Domine Deus, elargire visitationem misericordiarum tuarum, ac tuæ pietatis, animas lauans nostras a malis, & peccatis: animas vevero Defunctorum nostrorum purga a sordibus & maculis iniquitatis, tu qui misericordiarum plenus es, & tuae misereris creaturae, Pater, & Fili, & Spiritus sancte.
units.tr: Lord God, grant the visitation of your mercies and your loving-kindness to the infirmities of our souls and bodies, washing our souls clean of evils and sins; but purge the souls of our departed from the filth and stains of iniquity, you who are full of mercy and have compassion on your creature, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit.

units.la: Teitaque, Medice bone, Deus vere, Creator sapiens, & instaurator magne, ac perite, deprecamur super suffitu hoc Aromatum, petentes a tuis misericordiis multiplicibus incolumitatem perfectam, & sanitatem integram omnibus infirmis, atque in angustia positis, qui magnam tuam miserationis pulsant januam, ut ignoscas, mundes, & purges peccata, & maculas nostras, & Defunctorum nostrorum.
units.tr: Therefore, good Physician, true God, wise Creator and great and skilful restorer, we beseech you over this fumigation of spices, asking from your manifold mercies perfect health and whole soundness for all the sick and for those in distress, who knock at the great gate of your compassion, that you would pardon, cleanse and purge our sins and stains, and those of our dead.

units.la: Haec pauca ex multis, unde planissime patet, Syros, quemadmodum & reliquas Orientis gentes non solum Defunctos Deo commendare, ut ipsum tempore ultimi Judicij clementem resuscitati experiantur Judicem; verum etiam, ut eorum animas purget, ac mundet a sordibus, & maculis iniquitatis, eisque peccata, & delicta ignoscat. Concluditur his itaque Hottingerus, & enormissimorum mendaciorum ex more agitur reus. Quamobrem concludamus & nos Epistolam hanc nostram, tibi clarissime, & doctissime Leo, Nestoreos deprecantes annos, ut diutissime incolumis, & sospes vivens Ecclesiam Catholicam tuis eruditissimis Scriptis exornare pergas, & Vulpeculis, quae fraudibus, & astutia vivunt, & scriptitant, terror, Leo semper sis, dolosque & fallacias in dies aperias; Titanos vero, & gigantes cum Deo, eiusque bellantes Ecclesia, veritatis gladio conficias, & prosternas. Felix diu Vale.
units.tr: These few things out of many make it quite plain that the Syrians, like the other peoples of the East, not only commend their dead to God, so that they may find him a merciful Judge at the last judgment, but also that he may purge and cleanse their souls from the filth and stains of iniquity, and forgive them their sins and offences. Hottinger is thereby refuted and, as is the custom, held guilty of the most monstrous lies. Wherefore we too conclude this our letter, most distinguished and learned Leo, praying for you Nestorian years, that you may long remain safe and sound and, living, go on adorning the Catholic Church with your most learned writings, and that you may always be a terror, Leo, to the little foxes who live by fraud and cunning and write their scribblings, opening up their deceits and fallacies day by day; and may you with God crush and overthrow the Titans and giants who wage war against God and his Church with the sword of truth. Farewell, and may you prosper for long.

units.la: Quid hic ais Hottingere? Vides? Eoæ Ecclesiæ, Coptitæ, Melchitæ, Maronitæ, Iacobitæ, Nestorianæ sanctos Angelos, Prophetas, Apostolos, Martyres, Doctores, Iustos invocant, eorum operam implorant, & apud Deum patrocinium. Provinciæ, Urbes singulæ, Artes, Professiones sibi privatum unum aliquem ex illis, quem sibi magis profuturum existimant, advocatum, & monitorem asciscunt, & in rebus adversis propitium, & generalibus, & privatis precibus intercedunt, ut sanent animas, ut ipsos seruent, ut custodiant, ut eripiant a grauissimis afflictionibus, ut auxilia præbeant egentibus, ut auxilientur, ut concilient tranquillitatem, & pacem omnibus diebus, ut sibi a Deo obtineant remissionem peccatorum, ut infirmi sanentur, curentur, claudi ut ambulent, & erigantur ab auxilijs officium eorum, & tandem ne mergantur in mari perturbato peccatorum. Et potissimum Deiparam Virginem, quam, & gratia plenam, fidelium refugium, fortissimum Christianorum, Mundique auxilium, matrem vitæ, fontem deliciarum, per quem omnia bona euenere hominibus, & quid non in laudem eius non [illegible, ~8 letters], sed ὄντως[?] accumulant? ut offerat pro salute, & liberatio-
units.tr: What do you say to this, Hottinger? Do you see? The Eastern Churches, the Copts, Melchites, Maronites, Jacobites and Nestorians, invoke the holy Angels, Prophets, Apostles, Martyrs, Teachers and Just, implore their help and their patronage before God. Provinces, individual cities, arts and professions each adopt for themselves as advocate and monitor some one of these whom they think will be most helpful to them, and in both general and private prayers they intercede with him as gracious in adversity: that he may heal souls, keep them safe, guard them, snatch them from the gravest afflictions, provide help to the needy, be helped himself, procure tranquillity and peace all their days, obtain for them from God the forgiveness of sins, that the sick may be healed and cured, the lame may walk and be raised up by their help, and finally that they may not be swallowed up in the troubled sea of sins. And above all they invoke the Virgin Mother of God, who is full of grace, the refuge of the faithful, the strongest defence of Christians and help of the world, mother of life, fountain of delights, through whom all good things have come to men; and what do they not heap upon her in praise, [illegible] truly [?], so that she may offer intercession for the salvation and deliverance

units.la: [illegible, ~8 letters]: the Greek word aster "non" in the line "non in laudem eius non", printed in Greek letters, could not be read with certainty. ne animarum, & corporum, vt misericordias faciat, vt sit semper alta moenia, munimentum, refugium, & vendicet, liberet, & custodiat animas fidelium a malo.
units.tr: [illegible text]: the Greek word for "not", printed in the line "non in laudem eius non", could not be read with certainty. of souls and bodies, that she may show mercies, that she may be a high wall, a bulwark and a refuge, and may claim, free and guard the souls of the faithful from evil.

units.la: Et cum inter Canones Ecclesiasticos Concilij Nicæni Canonem 44. numerent, eumque vt legitimum Nicæni agnoscant, Romanum quoque Pontificem agnoscunt super omnes Patriarchas, quemadmodum habebat Petrus super vniuersos Christianitatis Principes, & Concilia ipsorum, quorum Christi Vicarius est super redemptionem, Ecclesias, & cunctos populos eius. Et quicunque sanctioni huic contradixerit, Patres Synodi illum anathemate percellunt. Monachi earum instítutis illis, quibus & Pontificij, licet in nonnullis leuibus, & adiaphoris, vti & Pontificij inter se differunt, vitam agitant, corpus affligunt, vt animæ ab illecebris terrenis puriores euadentes, meliori mente cum immaterialibus consumant ætatem.
units.tr: And since they count among the ecclesiastical canons Canon 44 of the Council of Nicaea, and acknowledge it as a lawful canon of Nicaea, they also acknowledge the Roman Pontiff as above all the Patriarchs, just as Peter had authority over all the princes of Christendom; and their Councils, over which he is Christ's Vicar, over the redemption, the Churches and all his peoples. And whoever contradicts this decree, the Fathers of the Synod strike with anathema. The monks live by those rules by which the Papists also live, though the Papists differ among themselves in some slight and indifferent matters, and they mortify the body so that their souls, escaping purer from earthly allurements, may spend their life with a better mind on immaterial things.

units.la: Sanctorum Patrum, & Doctorum Ecclesiæ, nec non Conciliorum effata, vti Cynosuram, & Canonem sequuntur. Hinc eos vocant, Directores ad fidem Orthodoxam, Doctores illustres religionis, Duces ad sanctitatem, Decus principibus Sacerdotum, Lampadas, Solem, Architectos cerdotum, Lampadas, Solem, Architectos Fidei , Theologiæ lumina , Præcones Spiritus sancti , Erectores Ecclesiæ , veros Pastores , Euersores hæresum , Spiritus Sancti, uti Prophetæ fuere , Interpretes , & tandem Cynosuram , & Canonem .
units.tr: They follow the sayings of the holy Fathers and Teachers of the Church, and of the Councils as their Cynosure and Canon. Hence they call them directors to the orthodox faith, illustrious teachers of religion, leaders to holiness, the glory of princes and of priests, lamps, the sun, architects of the faith, lights of theology, heralds of the Holy Spirit, erectors of the Church, true ministers, overthrowers of heresies, as the prophets of the Holy Spirit were, interpreters, and finally their Cynosure and Canon.

units.la: Confer tu Hottingere reliqua Epistolæ, si tanti es ; postmodum insta classicum [?], clamaque , propius Reformatis Eoas Ecclesias accedere . Hinc collige a Romana dissidere ; tum eadem per eadem dicito. Ne te afflictes . aude aliquid pro more tuo , a thesi ad hypothesim arguta pedibus, quando sani capitis copia non est : caue tamen ne saltu illo pertinacius obluctando collum abrumpas. Vel saltem ad illa tua te conferas; Est tamen aliquid discrimen . Magnum tibi, qui caligantibus oculis veteris aliquid est. Eoæ Ecclesiæ concordant cum Pontificiis fere in omnibus, & discrepant ab illa aliquo discrimine . Ergo propius accedunt Reformatis. Quæ est hæc argumentandi ratio ? Si esset inter eas & Reformatos aliquid discrimen, in reliquis vero magna consensio, consensum cum Reformatis probantibus similia posses occinere . Sed apud te unum sunt omnia, & nox menti offusa non sinit statuere , quid interfit inter magnum, & paruum, virtutem , & vitium, pietatem & impietatem , veritatem & falsitatem , probitatem atque improbitatem. Hinc omnia confundis, & turbas , & pro albo nigrum venditas , & præposterè loqueris . Est tamen aliquid discrimen . Ergo propius accedunt Reformatis. Ergo consensus inter Ecclesias Eoas & Pontificiam nullus , sed dissensus in omnibus est . Pace tua dixero , quamuis sciam, quæcunque dixero , stultitia tua minora futura, non es apud te, ideoque alios ex tuo ingenio judicas, sed improbe, sed proterue, sed insulse,sed obtuse.
units.tr: Compare the rest of the letter yourself, Hottinger, if you are worth so much; then sound the trumpet and cry out that the Eastern Churches come closer to the Reformed. From this, conclude that they dissent from the Roman Church; then say the same things again and again. Do not trouble yourself. Dare something, as is your custom, leaping from one thesis to a hypothesis, nimble on your feet, since you lack the stock of a sound head; but take care lest, struggling too stubbornly in that leap, you break your neck. Or at least betake yourself to those things of yours: there is nonetheless some distinction. It is a great thing for you, who with dim eyes have something of the old. The Eastern Churches agree with the Papists almost in everything, and differ from them by some distinction. Therefore they come closer to the Reformed. What kind of reasoning is this? If there were some distinction between them and the Reformed, but great agreement in the rest, you could sing of agreement with the Reformed on the ground of similar points. But with you all things are one, and a night poured over your mind does not allow you to decide what difference there is between great and small, virtue and vice, piety and impiety, truth and falsehood, honesty and dishonesty. Hence you confuse everything, stir up confusion, sell black for white, and talk back to front. There is nonetheless some distinction. Therefore they come closer to the Reformed. Therefore there is no agreement between the Eastern Churches and the Papal Church, but dissent in everything. With your leave I shall say it, although I know that whatever I say will be less foolish than your own; you are not at home with yourself, and so you judge others by your own wit, but wickedly, insolently, foolishly and dully.

units.la: Conclusio Differtationis.
units.tr: Conclusion of the Dissertation.

units.la: ET tandem dic Hottingere. Fuit ne unquam ante Schisma Photij inter Ecclesiam Romanam, & Græcam unio, & consensio? si negas, ἐμβεβρυτῷ[?] ἅ[?], ἡ τὰ ἀληθεστέρα[?] ἐπαν[?], ἀντωτῶ[?]. Si fateris. Jam Jupiter mihi pluit mel. Sed tum cum nullum inter has Ecclesias dissidium erat, sed plenissima concordia, Græca Ecclesia trinam in Baptismo immersionem usurpabat, Chrismatis immediatam cum Baptismo unctionem, Panem enzymum in Eucharistia, multa alia tum in Missarum sacrificijs faciendis, & celebrandis, tum in Sacramentis conferendis, vel etiam suscipiendis observabat: cum tamen aliis ritibus, moribus, atque institutis Romana uteretur, a suffocatis abstinebat, Grana aquæ calidæ in consecrato calice admiscebat, Ieiunium præcipue quadragesimale, & alia rigidissime celebrabat, sa-cram Eucharistiam infantibus statim etiam a Baptismate porrigebat, sub utraque specie communicabat, Clerogamiam admittebat, Symbolum[?] absque additione recitabat[?], aliter divinum pensum exoluebat, aliter divinas preces recitabat, ante sacros ordines Lectores tantum Clericos, non item Ostiarios, non Exorcistas, non Acolythos, in peruigiliis Apostolorum ieiunium non suscipiebat, matrimonio adstrictos ad ordines promouebat, Sabbato non abstinebat a carnibus; cum Latina Ecclesia abstineret, matrimonio adstrictos non promoueret ad ordines, in peruigiliis Apostolorum ieiunaret, Clericos ordinaret ad quatuor ordines minores, aliter divinas preces recitaret, aliter divinum pensum exolueret, Symbolum cum additione recitaret, Clerogamiam prohiberet, sub unica tantum specie Azymo communicaret, infantibus communionem denegaret, ieiunia veluti Græca non celebraret, aquam calidam in consecrato calice non immiscerct, a suffocatis non abstineret, Chrifmatis vnctione adultos fignaret, vnicam immerfionem, vel infufionem obferuaret; & tamen vnio & confenfus perftabat, eratque cum Græca Romanæ arctiffima confuetudo. Ergo prænarrata omnia, quæ tu vel alij inter diffidij capita commemorant, nulla funt. Nanque fi nunc diffidij capita funt, tum quoque fuiffent: Neque enim in Ecclefia quod femel iudicatum eft innoxium, noxium fubfecutis temporibus fuerit; nifi noua emergente hæresi illud ad eam fuftinendam, vel comprobandam affumatur: tum enim non ipfius, fed hæreseos caufa improbatur, vt vidimus in voce Chriftipara, quam prohibuiffe Ecclefiam, cum Neftoriana hæresis graffaretur, ea poftmodum extincta in Ecclefiam redijffe, certum eft. Ergo infulfiffimi funt, qui ob hæc, vel fimilia capita diffidium inter vtrafque Ecclefias vrgent, & inter eos Hottingerus fruftra operam infumit, cum in difcrimine difcrimen aliquod expifcatur, vt diffidium probet. Quodfi id ftabilire animus fuiffet, non vndique dicta Auctorum emendaffet, qui diffidia inter Græcos, & Pontificios narrant; fed dicta Ecclefiæ Græcæ, & illius Doctorum ab Allatio producta confiderate examinaffet, poftmodum refpondiffet ferio, quod cum non feceric, neneque scriptis ab Allatio rescripserit, sed in rabiem versus, aliorum verbis insulsissime, & extra rem obganniens chartas oppleuerit, plane deprehensus est, ἀλαζονείας πολύξοπον τῇ πνιγῇ[?], καὶ τῇ Σοφίστῃ τῆς κακίας[?]. Habes iam Hottingere, & quicunque alius, qui similia consensui nostro opponit, rationes aliquando etiam repetitas inculcatasque, pro vt opponentium calumniae deposcebant. plurimae praeferri possent, si tam imperitorum ardelionum lucubrationes dignae essent, quae semel, atque iterum lectae ad amussim examinarentur. Quibus lectis cui non persuasum fuerit, tantam esse Hottingeri inscitiam, quanta illorum esse potest, qui nec ingenij, aut iudicij acumine, nec multa, accurataque lectione sunt commendandi; ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν καὶ πέρα τῆς μάχης[?].
units.tr: And finally, tell me, Hottinger: was there ever, before the schism of Photius, any union and agreement between the Roman Church and the Greek? If you deny it, then [garbled Greek, apparently a taunt] [ἐμβεβρυτῷ[?] ἅ[?], ἡ τὰ ἀληθεστέρα[?] ἐπαν[?], ἀντωτῶ[?]]. If you admit it, then now Jupiter is raining honey on me! [Jam Jupiter mihi pluit mel]. But at a time when there was no discord between these Churches, and complete harmony, the Greek Church used a threefold immersion in Baptism, an anointing with chrism immediately after Baptism, and unleavened bread in the Eucharist, and it observed many other practices, both in performing and celebrating the sacrifices of the Mass and in administering or receiving the sacraments. Yet although it used the Roman rites, customs and institutions in other respects, it abstained from things strangled, mixed a few drops of hot water into the consecrated chalice, observed the Lenten fast and others very strictly, gave the sacred Eucharist to infants immediately after Baptism, communicated under both kinds, admitted clerical marriage, recited the creed without addition, performed the divine office differently, recited the divine prayers differently, and before the sacred orders admitted only readers as clergy, not doorkeepers, exorcists or acolytes. It did not fast on the vigils of the Apostles, promoted married men to orders, did not abstain from meat on Saturdays. The Latin Church, on the other hand, abstained from these things: it did not promote married men to orders, fasted on the vigils of the Apostles, ordained clergy to the four minor orders, recited the divine prayers and performed the divine office in its own way, recited the creed with the addition, forbade clerical marriage, communicated with unleavened bread under the one kind only, denied communion to infants, did not celebrate fasts in the Greek manner, did not mix hot water into the consecrated chalice, did not abstain from things strangled, anointed adults with chrism, and observed only a single immersion or infusion. And yet union and agreement persisted, and there was the closest custom between the Greek and the Roman Church. Therefore all the things mentioned above, which you and others cite as heads of discord, are nothing. For if they are heads of discord now, they would also have been so then. Indeed, in the Church what was once judged harmless does not become harmful in later times, unless, when a new heresy arises, it is adopted to sustain or confirm that heresy. For then it is condemned not on its own account but on account of the heresy, as we have seen in the word Christipara, which the Church forbade when the Nestorian heresy was raging, and which, after that heresy was extinguished, is certainly known to have returned into the Church. Therefore those are utterly foolish who urge these or similar heads as proof of discord between the two Churches, and Hottinger wastes his effort among them, since in a difference he seeks out some difference in order to prove discord. But if he had really wished to establish this, he would not have merely corrected the sayings of authors who describe the disagreements between the Greeks and the Papists; he would have examined carefully the statements of the Greek Church and its teachers brought forward by Allatius, and afterwards would have answered seriously. Since he has not done this, and since he has not replied to Allatius in writing, but has gone into a rage and, with the words of others, has filled his pages with the most silly and irrelevant barking, he is plainly exposed as full of [garbled Greek, apparently "of boasting much-sharpened by strangling, and of the sophistry of wickedness"] [ἀλαζονείας πολύξοπον τῇ πνιγῇ[?], καὶ τῇ Σοφίστῃ τῆς κακίας[?]]. You have it now, Hottinger, and whoever else opposes our agreement with similar arguments: arguments, some even repeated and pressed again and again, as the calumnies of our opponents demanded. Many more could be brought forward, if the lucubrations of such unskilled busybodies were worth reading once or twice and examining exactly. Having read them, who would not be persuaded that Hottinger's ignorance is as great as that of those who deserve praise neither for the keenness of their talent or judgement nor for wide and careful reading? [garbled Greek, apparently "but these things are even beyond the battle"] [ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν καὶ πέρα τῆς μάχης[?]].

units.la: DE IOANNA PAPISSA FABVLA AB ALLATIO PROFLIGATA Nonnullorum Clarorum Virorum ELOGIA.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE FABLE OF POPE JOAN, UTTERLY REFUTED BY ALLATIUS; ENCOMIA OF SOME ILLUSTRIOUS MEN.

units.la: ANTONIVS CARACCIOLVS Cler. Regul. & in Dioecesi Neapolitana Librorum Censor.
units.tr: ANTONIUS CARACCIOLUS, regular cleric and censor of books in the Diocese of Naples.

units.la: OPusculum hoc eruditissimi Viri, & Graecis literis excultissimi Leonis Allatij adversus Ioannam Papissam τῷ μυθώδῃ[?], si paginas Lector numeres, paruum profecto est; si pondera expendas argumentorum, re vera magnum, adeoque validum, ut sicut de Tertulliano Lirinensis ait, quot in eo sensus, tot sint victoriae. Complures quidem ad idem monstrum interimendum suas quisque ingenij, stylique vires certatim contulerunt, sed pace illorum dixerim, Allatius a Gracis quibusdam Scriptoribus, quos hactenus nemo hominum tam diligenter excussit, ea profert iacula rationum, ut, nisi velint se ipsos excaecare haeretici, cogendi sint, cum legent, fabellam abijcere quam in Romana Ecclesia probrum, vaframento plane ridiculo, adornauerant. Quocirca Lucubratiuncula hæc aureola, & laude dignissima est, & in Bibliothecis omnibus merito locum habebit, Quod attestor.
units.tr: This little work of the most learned man, and most accomplished in Greek letters, Leo Allatius, against the mythical Pope Joan [τῷ μυθώδῃ], is indeed small if the reader counts the pages; but if you weigh the force of its arguments, it is truly great and so strong that, as Lirinensis says of Tertullian, there are as many victories as there are senses in it. Many, it is true, have each striven with all the powers of their wit and style to destroy this monster; but with due respect to them, Allatius brings forward from certain Greek writers, whom no one until now has examined so diligently, such missiles of argument that, unless the heretics wish to blind themselves, they will be compelled, when they read them, to cast away the fable which they had devised as a reproach against the Roman Church, with a plainly ridiculous trick. Wherefore this little work of ours is both golden and most worthy of praise, and it will rightly take its place in all libraries, as I attest.

units.la: BARTHOLOMÆVS VECCHIVS I. C. Senensis.
units.tr: BARTHOLOMÆUS VECCHIUS, doctor of both laws, of Siena.

units.la: BARTHOLOMÆO SANGVINACCIO, Archidiacono Patauino, & Vicario Capitulari.
units.tr: To BARTHOLOMEW SANGUINACCIO, Archdeacon of Padua and Capitular Vicar.

units.la: Quod olim Herodianus de Marco Antonino Philosopho, & Imperatore dixit, Πολύ τι πλῆθος σοφῶν[?] ἀνδρῶν ἤνεγκεν ἡ τῆς ἐκείνου κεφαλῆς φορά[?]. Φιλὰ γάρ πως ἀεὶ τὸ ὑπήκοον ζήλῳ τῆς τοῦ ἀρ-χοντος[?] γνώμης βιοῦν, hodie etiam, Præsul Reuerendissime, experimur. Quando enim maior fuit in omni studiorum genere litteratorum hominum proventus, quam hoc, alioqui ferreo, atque infelici ævo, quo Vrbanus VIII. Pont. Max. magno Christiana Reipublica bono gloriose, feliciterque dominatur? qui non solum auctoritate, ac benignitate, sed etiam, quod semper rarum fuit in Viris Principibus, exemplo bonarum artium omnium studia promouet. Leonis Allatij de Ioanna Papissa fabula Commentationem nuper editam, doctam Iupiter, & laboriosam, magna mea cum voluptate relegi, Auctoris eruditionem ac diligentiam admiratus. Certe fuit operae pretium Romanae Ecclesiae calumniatores, etiam ab ipsis hostibus, quod egregie praestitit Allatius, sumptis argumentis convincere. Quare docta huic Commentationi Davidicum illud meo iudicio ὑποσχοι ἂν ης δικαίως[?] יִסְפַּר פִּי דִּבְרֵי עֵקֶר[?] Gratias igitur tibi maximas ago, Praesul Reuerendiffime, quod mihi eam legendi copiam feceris. Vale.
units.tr: What Herodian once said of Marcus Antoninus the philosopher and emperor, that the head of that man bore forth a great multitude of wise men, we too experience today. For the subject, as it is always inclined to live by the zeal of the ruler's mind, is so inclined. Most Reverend Prelate, when has there been a greater abundance of learned men in every kind of study than in this age, otherwise iron and unhappy, in which Urban VIII, Supreme Pontiff, gloriously and happily reigns to the great good of the Christian commonwealth? He promotes the study of all the liberal arts not only by his authority and kindness but also by example, which has always been rare in princes. I have read through with great pleasure the commentary on the fable of Pope Joan recently published by Leo Allatius, learned and laborious, by Jupiter, admiring the erudition and diligence of the author. Certainly it was worth the effort to refute the calumnies of the Roman Church by arguments, even from its enemies themselves, which Allatius has accomplished splendidly. Therefore, in my judgment, the verse of David applies to this learned commentary: "My tongue shall speak of thy word" [ψαλμ. 119 — the Hebrew reads: "my tongue shall sing of thy word", as in Psalm 119.172]. I therefore give you the greatest thanks, Most Reverend Prelate, for granting me the opportunity to read it. Farewell.

units.la: FORTVNIVS LICETVS Eidem.
units.tr: FORTUNIUS LICETUS to the same.

units.la: Leo Allatius, Reuerendissime Domine, secundo Maximi Pontificis Vrbani VIII. Spiritu nixus, & mira sua eruditione, summaque iudicii solertia, seu geminis intellectus alis, adeo sublime scandere potuit, vt celsissimum antiquitatis Olympum superauerit; ibique lectas in Ara Historicae veritati dicata, densis ignorantiae nubibus, ventosisque malitiae turbinibus inaccessa, priscorum scriptiones non altero tantum anno, sed multis retro seculis exaratas ad nos tandem retulit incorruptas, quibus vt de Ioanna Papissa vulgatam aliquando famam vere fabulam esse conuincit, ita Leo mysticus interemit Hæreseos vrsam, quae fidelem cacanem contubernalem Valeriano dilacerare tentaverat. Vale ex Musaeo nostro IV. Nonas Novembris MDCXXX.
units.tr: Leo Allatius, Most Reverend Lord, relying on the Spirit of our most Supreme Pontiff Urban VIII, and on his wonderful erudition and great sharpness of judgment, or on the two wings of his intellect, has been able to climb so high that he has surpassed the lofty Olympus of antiquity; and there, having gathered the ancient writings, written not merely a year ago but many centuries back, consecrated on the altar dedicated to historical truth, inaccessible through the dense clouds of ignorance and the windy whirlwinds of malice, he has at last brought them back to us uncorrupted. By these he proves that the rumour once spread about Pope Joan is truly a fable, just as the mystical Leo has slain the she-bear of heresy, which had tried to tear apart the faithful... Farewell, from our Museum, on the fourth of the Nones of November, 1630.

units.la: FRANCISCVS MOLINVS Canonicus Patauinus. Eidem.
units.tr: FRANCISCUS MOLINUS, Canon of Padua. To the same.

units.la: Ioannis Papissae fabulam, prauorum figmentum, Hæreticorum commentum semper recta indicavit lance; tum quia illius temporis Scriptores, tam Catholici, quam Hæretici, de ea ne verbum quidem, sed fideli historicasuccessione, Leoni IV. Benedicto III. Benedicto Nicolaum, Nicolao Adrianum &c. sufficiunt. Cum etiam mihi nunquam in animum inducere potuerim, Spiritum sanctum, qui de fide universali aflat Ecclesia contra Iesu Christi, & Dei institutum, hoc monstrum, & portentum in Ecclesia dedecus permisisse. Hinc Reverendissime Domine, summa animi voluptate, spiritalique gustu diligenter perlegi, quae abs te mihi missa sunt hac de re Leonis Allatii scripta. Vere Leo animalium princeps Leonis ad instar inter omnes aurea corona, regalique sceptro donandus; vere Allatus, cum se ad sublime super omnes evexerit. Dignum quaeso mecum adiudica, vt de eo Ecclesia Romana, quam ex Hæreticorum sordibus, & squalloribus exemet, met vindicauit, non vulgariter bene mereatur. Bene vale. ex Laribus nostris iii. Nonas Nouembris MDCXXX.
units.tr: He has always weighed the fable of Pope Joan, the figment of wicked men and the invention of heretics, on the true scales; for the writers of that time, both Catholic and heretical, say not a word about her, but the faithful historical succession (Leo IV, Benedict III, Benedict, Nicholas, Nicholas, Adrian, etc.) is enough for them. Nor could I ever persuade myself that the Holy Spirit, who breathes on the universal faith of the Church against the institution of Jesus Christ and of God, would have permitted this monster and portent to be a disgrace in the Church. Hence, most Reverend Sir, I have read through with the greatest pleasure and spiritual delight the writings of Leo Allatius on this matter which you sent me. Truly Leo deserves to be crowned with gold among all animals, as the prince of animals, and to be given a royal sceptre, like a lion; truly Allatius, since he has raised himself above all others. Please judge with me that the Roman Church, which he has freed from the filth and squalor of heretics and has vindicated, owes him no small debt of gratitude. Farewell. From our household gods, 3 Nones of November 1630.

units.la: IOANNES THVILIVS Humaniorum literarum in Gymnasio Patauino Professor . Eidem.
units.tr: IOANNES THUILIUS, Professor of the Humanities in the Padua Gymnasium. To the same.

units.la: Singulari voluptate legi Commentarium Leonis Allatij de Ioanna Papissa, doctum sane & elegantem, si quidquam aliud. Gratulor seculo nostro, quo Hæreticorum temeritas maxime sibi plaudit, eandem nouis telis configi, & profligari. Nam præter quam absurditas istius fabulæ ex pluribus patescit, nimirum, quod nemo Scriptorum eius temporis id memoriæ prodidit, a recentioribus autem dubio vestigio tactum sit; quod Moguntinus simul, & Anglus iste Ioannes fuisse fertur, cum Moguntia toto Orbe, ut sic dicam, ab Anglia diuisa sit: præter quam quod grauidam fingunt, iam senio effœtam, & si quæ sunt alia omnibus nænijs anilibus leuiora, quæ iam pridem sublimium ingeniorum calamo fuerunt explosa: solidum nobis iste Commentarius suggerit argumentum ab ipsis aduersarijs desumptum, qui si hoc delirum figmentum veritatis aliquid habuisse comperissent, bone Deus, quam illi albis equis triumphassent, & Pontificiam auctoritatem temerario ausu conculcassent, præsertim Photius ille Graecorum Schismatum antesignanus.
units.tr: I read with singular pleasure the commentary of Leo Allatius on Pope Joan, learned and certainly elegant, if anything is. I congratulate our age, in which the rashness of the heretics prides itself most, that this fable is again assailed with new weapons and overthrown. For, besides the absurdity of that story, which is evident from many points, namely that none of the writers of that time committed it to memory, and that it has been touched only with a doubtful trace by more recent authors; that John is said to have been both a native of Mainz and an Englishman, though Mainz is, so to speak, divided from England by the whole world; besides the fact that they imagine her pregnant, already worn out with age, and whatever other old-wives' tales are lighter than all nursery nonsense, which have long since been driven out by the pens of the more eminent minds: this commentary of his supplies us with solid argument drawn from the adversaries themselves, who, if they had discovered that this mad fiction had any ground in truth, good God, how they would have triumphed on white horses and trampled rashly on papal authority, especially that Photius, the standard-bearer of the Greek schisms.

units.la: Verum hac de re latius tecum differere non patitur tua doctrina, nec præsumit mea modestia, ne videar aquam in mare. Interim habeo gratias, quod me tam iucunda lectione non indignum iudicaueris. Vale Vir eruditissime & Reuerendissime. Patauij ex Musaeo meo.
units.tr: But your learning does not allow me to discuss this matter with you at greater length, nor does my modesty presume to do so, lest I seem to be pouring water into the sea. Meanwhile I thank you that you have judged me not unworthy of so pleasant a reading. Farewell, most learned and Reverend Sir. From my household at Padua.

units.la: MARTINVS SANDELLIVS Patauinus Philosophiae Professor, Eidem.
units.tr: MARTINUS SANDELLIUS, Professor of Philosophy at Padua, to the same.

units.la: Commentationem Leonis Allatij de Ioanna Papissa fabula ab humanitate tua mihi commodatam, Reuerendissime Domine, legi, ac relegi pari animi voluptate, & Autoris admiratione; qui in eo argumento adeo feliciter est versatus, vt vel ab hostibus ipsius veritatis extorserit veritatem, & tam veterum, quam recentiorum Hæreticorum calumnias meridiana luce effecerit clariores. Agit enim, vt dicitur, signatis tabulis, & ita annorum, ac Pontificum ducit rationem, vt plane stupidus sit, qui ex ipsamet supputatione, fucum factum bonis Autoribus, non agnoscat. Multi sane in ea fabula refutanda cum laude versati sunt, quos Autor ipse in calce disputationis recenset: verum eruditissimus Allatius mihi videtur huic operi coronidem imposuisse, atque omne, vt aiunt, tulisse punctum. Quod ipsum tibi optimo rerum æstimatori, & aliis viris doctissimis audio summopere probari. D.O.M. Reuerendissimam Dominationem tuam ad Ecclesia Patauina bonum, & nobilissimam familiam tuam ornamentum diutissime tueatur incolumem. Patauij ex meis ædibus VIII. Idus Nouembris, anno Christi MDCXXX.
units.tr: I have read and re-read, Most Reverend Sir, the commentary of Leo Allatius on the fable of Pope Joan, which your kindness lent me, with equal pleasure of mind and admiration for its author, who has handled this subject so happily that he has wrung the truth even from the enemies of truth, and has made the calumnies of the old and recent heretics clearer than the noonday light. For he proceeds, as they say, with marked tables, and reckons the years and the popes so exactly that anyone who fails to recognise from that very reckoning the deception practised on good authors must be quite dull. Indeed many have distinguished themselves in refuting that fable, and the author himself lists them at the end of his disputation; but the most learned Allatius seems to me to have put the crown on this work and, as they say, to have carried every point. I hear that you, a most excellent judge of affairs, and other very learned men greatly approve this. May God, the Best and Greatest, keep your Reverend Lordship long safe for the good of the Church of Padua and as an ornament to your most noble family. From my own house at Padua, 8 Ides of November, in the year of Christ 1630.

units.la: LAVRENTIVS PIGNORIVS Eidem.
units.tr: LAURENTIUS PIGNORIUS, to the same.

units.la: Percurri, vt tu imperasti, Commentarium Leonis Allatij, conscriptum aduersus imposturam male feriatorum quorundam, qui Ioannam, nescio quam, Papissam nobis obtrudere sunt conati. Is mihi adeo sapidus est visus, vt bis, terque regustare libuerit. Multos equidem vidi, qui idem argumentum tractauerunt, non sine laude: at vero qui adeo perite collimauerit, adhuc neminem. Ego sane gratulor Auctori, quem rogatum velim, vt ad huiusmodi conscriptiones conferat stylum, quo multis misere deceptis lux aliqua tandem veritatis affulgeat. Vale. Vir Reuerendissime, non sine insigni a me gratiarum actione. Domi.
units.tr: As you ordered, I have gone through the commentary of Leo Allatius, written against the imposture of certain idle good-for-nothings who have tried to foist upon us a certain Joan as Pope. It seemed to me so savoury that I was pleased to taste it again two or three times. Indeed I have seen many who have treated the same subject, not without praise; but as yet I have seen no one who has aimed so skilfully. I certainly congratulate the author, and I would ask him to turn his pen to writings of this kind, so that some light of truth may at last shine upon the many who have been wretchedly deceived. Farewell, Most Reverend Sir, with no small thanks from me. At home.

units.la: IDEM PIGNORIVS LEONI ALLATIO. Romam .
units.tr: The same Pignorius, a letter brought to Leo. Rome.

units.la: Eruditissimus fœtus tuus literarius, Vir Reverendissime, quem Antonius meus ad me transmisit, præter voluptatem, qua me ubertim affecit, illud etiam perfecit, ut eruditissimos viros, non huius nostri Italici cœli alumnos, compulerit, quod factum gaudeo in tui venerationem, cum amussitata veritatis indagatione. Argumentum pertractatum aliys, tu causa, & industria ista fecisti adeo tuum, ut nemo in posterum audeat sibi ne tantillum quidem arrogare. Reponat tibi Deus præmium, quod & homines non fero accurabunt. Quæso te, ut pergas strenue nostrum hoc seculum ditare aureis conscriptionibus, quas calamus parit iam olim consecratas immortalitati. Obsequium, studiumque Pignorij tui deferet tibi Antonius meus, tui admirator acerrimus, cui ego dedi in mandatis, ut te conveniat frequenter, pollicitus illi futuram consuetudinem tuam fructui, & laudi. bene vale Vir Reverendissime, quem Deus bene fortunet. Patavij die XXVI. Novembris MDCXXX.
units.tr: Your most learned literary work, Most Reverend Sir, which my Antonius sent to me, besides the pleasure it gave me in abundance, has also brought it about that learned men, not nurslings of this our Italian sky, have been moved to write, which I am glad of, to your honour, since the truth has been sought with a precise rule. You have made a subject already treated by others so much your own, through your cause and diligence, that no one in future will dare to claim even the smallest share of it for himself. May God repay you with a reward, which men too will not fail to bestow. I beg you to continue vigorously to enrich our age with golden writings, which the pen already brings forth, consecrated to immortality. The respect and zeal of your Pignorius will be conveyed to you by my Antonius, your most ardent admirer, to whom I gave instructions that he should visit you frequently, promising him that your acquaintance would be to his profit and credit. Farewell, Most Reverend Sir, whom God prosper. Padua, 26 November 1630.

units.la: FLAVIUS DE FLISCO, Jano de Amico.
units.tr: FLAVIUS DE FLISCO, to Janus of Amico.

units.la: De Joanna Papissa fabula disertam Commentationem ad te mitto, Amice, vere amicum, scio enim te diu Romanorum Pontificum historias perscrutatum esse, & quandoque Joannis Baptistæ Platinæ incuriam, ut ita dicam, pace tua, ægre tulisse, qui inter sua monumenta aliquid de hac fabella delineauit. Habes nunc veritatem ex selectis auctoribus ab eruditissimo viro Leone Allatio accurate excerptam. Videbis malignam Hæreticorum impietatem non solum auctoritatibus, sed huius ingenio, & argumentis euersam, profligatam. Fateor me pluries hoc opusculum legisse, itaque a te facturum arbitror, cum elocutionem, dispositionem, confutationem, & concinnitatem gustaueris. Vale.
units.tr: I am sending you, my friend, a learned treatise on the fable of Pope Joan, since I know you have long examined the histories of the Roman Pontiffs, and have at times, if I may say so with your pardon, taken it hard that Giovanni Battista Platina was careless, who in his records sketched something about this little tale. You now have the truth, carefully extracted from select authors by the most learned man Leone Allacci. You will see that the malicious impiety of the heretics has been overthrown and routed not only by authorities but also by his talent and arguments. I confess I have read this little work many times, and so I think you will do the same once you have tasted its style, arrangement, refutation and elegance. Farewell.

units.la: FRANCISCUS MARINUS Clericus Regularis Civitatis Vincentiæ Præpositus.
units.tr: FRANCESCO MARINO, Regular Clerk, Provost of the City of Vicenza.

units.la: Fabulam esse leuissimam, nullo roboratam argumento, de Joanna Papissa Hæreticorum figmentum, Chimæram ostendit Leo Allatius. Vere Leo, Marianum Scotum, Sigibertum, Martinum Polonum ab Hæreticis pessime ha-bibitos, turpiter fœdatos, erudite, acute tuetur. Ipsos Hæreticos impostores fraude detecta adeo valide probat, vt monstri huius assertores[?] confodiat, nec hiscere audeant.
units.tr: Leone Allacci shows that the fable of Pope Joan is most frivolous, supported by no argument, a figment of the heretics, a chimera. Truly, Leone defends with learning and sharpness Marianus Scotus, Sigebert and Martin of Poland, who were shamefully treated and disfigured by the heretics. He proves so forcefully that the heretics themselves are impostors, their fraud exposed, that he runs through the upholders of this monster, and they dare not open their mouths.

units.la: IOANNES ARGOLVS ANDREÆ F. Antonio Bruno.
units.tr: JOHN OF ARGOS, SON OF ANDREAS, to Antonio Bruno.

units.la: Gratulare mihi Brune, sodalis doctissime, Leo Allatius noster librum edidit paruum, profecto, sed qui vel parulus immortalitatem Auctori suo venari satis valeat. De antiqua illa Ioannæ Papissæ fabula, scias, a [illegible, ~3 letters] est; Spectrum, quod Ecclesia obuolutare tamdiu visum, auditumque fuit; piaculo tandem veritatis cessit, oppressumque a se locum, quem imagine teterrima, terroreque Romanæ Sedis formidoloso pro Hæreticis suis tenebat, leuauit Leo Allatius, Græcorum nostri aui iuxta cognomen suum vere sal, cum larua luctatus, ecce vltra vulgi paroemiam non vile opus molitus est, vt qui assuetudine didicerat inanes imagines, & sine corpore vitas effringere, quique paullo antea Engastrimythum, seu ventriloquæ historiam Samuelis ad Saulem referentis imaginem contra Originem valide propugnaculo calami tutatus sit, nupera vero opella nihil Hæreticis formidolosius, aut Catholicis felicius obuenire poterat, quam vt Idolon nempe, mulier scilicet sexu impotens, natura incapax supremus in templis Sacerdos, ac Pontifex creata monstrum immane, ingens, Pythia femella in tripode sedente monstruosius euanesceret. Mulier hac Atalante instar plures cursores in stadio literarum defatigauerat. Hippomeni vero Allatio victam se praebuit. Miraberis cum legas, quae tela contorqueat, quae remittat in hostes suo telo iugulaturus annorum seriem laceratam mirum est, quomodo acu Chronica recomponat, effugiaque, ac latibula claudat aduersantibus suo Leonino, ut ait Plautus, cauo tutus eaarte, doctrinaque, ut & opinio apte haereat; quodque velit absque controuersia, ac, ut fertur, diuina virgula consequatur. Fateor, ut colophonem laudi adhibeam, posse aliud aliquando facundius, copiosius, aut doctius a Leone isto tractari, nunquam gratius, nunquam utilius.
units.tr: Congratulate me, Bruno, most learned comrade. Our Leo Allatius has published a little book, small indeed, but one which even in its smallness is able to win immortality for its author. Know that concerning that ancient fable of Pope Joan it is [illegible]. The specter which the Church has so long been seen and heard to wrap in obscurity has at last yielded to the expiation of truth. Leo Allatius has lifted the place which it held, crushed by him, the place which through a most hideous image and the dreadful terror of the Roman See it kept for its heretics. Truly salt, as his Greek surname indicates, our grandfather's kinsman, he has wrestled with a mask, and behold, beyond the common proverb, he has undertaken no slight work. Having learned by habit to break open empty images and lives without bodies, and having a little earlier defended with the rampart of his pen the story of the ventriloquist's image of Samuel speaking to Saul against Origen, yet this recent little work could bring nothing more terrifying to the heretics or more fortunate to the Catholics than this: that the Idol, namely a woman impotent by sex and incapable by nature, created as supreme priest and pontiff in the temples, a huge monstrous creature, should vanish more monstrously than a little Pythian woman seated on the tripod. This woman, like Atalanta, had worn out many runners in the stadium of letters, but she showed herself defeated by Allatius, as by Hippomenes. You will be amazed when you read what weapons he hurls, what he sends back against his enemies, intending to slay them with their own weapon. It is wonderful how he restores the torn series of years with a needle, and closes off the escapes and hiding places of his opponents, safe, as Plautus says, in his Leonine hollow, by his art and learning, so that opinion also clings aptly. What he wishes he attains without controversy and, as they say, by a divine wand. I confess, to add a finishing touch to his praise, that the subject could at some time be treated by another more eloquently, more copiously, or more learnedly, but never more pleasingly, never more usefully, than by this Leo.

units.la: De eodem libello quid sentias expecto, licet nihil aliud, quam laudem, & commendationem Vale. meq; Gaspari de Simeonibus omnium horarum homini commenda. Habeo Gratijs tuis gratias, quod tu earum numero quartam e Suada medulla tui carminis progenitam adiunxeris. Vale iterum.
units.tr: Tell me what you think of the same little book; I expect nothing but praise and commendation. Farewell, and commend me to Gaspar de Simeonibus, a man for all hours. I return thanks for your thanks, since you have added to their number a fourth, born from the marrow of your poem, the goddess of persuasion Suada. Farewell again.

units.la: IOANNES BAPTISTA PASSERVS Genua Patauinus.
units.tr: Giovanni Battista Passeri of Genoa, of Padua.

units.la: Causam tueri nesciunt, nolunt, aut nequeunt Hæretici, nisi aculeatis probris inuehantur in Orthodoxos, & proscindant genio, & ingenio indulgentes: imbecillitatis indicium. Nam sat est proftraffe Leoni. Monstrum de Ioanna Papissa, vel fabulam discerpit Leo Allatius, vt conuicijs abstineat, & Leonem agat. Feram interficere, ac triumphare tentarunt multi, sed frustra. Vni Leoni Allatio amarantina gloria, gloriosus triumphus.
units.tr: Heretics cannot, will not, or are unable to defend their cause, unless they rail with stinging insults against the Orthodox and tear them to pieces, giving free rein to wit and talent. This is a sign of weakness. For it is enough to have thrown down the monster or the fable of Pope Joan, as Leo Allatius tears it apart, so as to abstain from abuse and to act the lion. Many have tried to kill the beast and win the triumph, but in vain. To Leo Allatius alone belongs the amaranthine glory, the glorious triumph.

units.la: Torserat in monstrum validus lethalia miles Tela, sed irrisit vulnera magna ferox. Sæpe resurgit ouans: fortem timet ecce Leonem, Aggreditur, lacerat: ficta Ioanna perit. Namque Leo superat fortissimus omnia monstra: Parcit & inuictus: præstat utrumque Leo.
units.tr: The mighty soldier hurled deadly weapons at the monster, but the fierce beast laughed at his great wounds. Often it rises again exulting; behold, it fears the brave Leo, it attacks and is mangled, and the feigned Joan perishes. For Leo, most brave, overcomes all monsters, and the unconquered Leo spares and offers both.

units.la: AVBERTVS MIRÆVS In Chronico Belgico edito Antuerpiæ in sol. Anno 1636. pag. 184.
units.tr: AUBERTUS MIRAEUS, In Chronico Belgico, edited at Antwerp in folio, 1636, p. 184.

units.la: De Ioanna Papissa. Quin etiam Photius ipse, qui illa ætate vixit nullo interiecto Leoni Benedictum, huic Nicolaum, tum Ioannem substituit, vt Leo Allatius accurate docet in sua Commentatione 1630. Roma edita.
units.tr: On Pope Joan. Indeed, Photius himself, who lived in that age, placed Benedict directly after Leo, then Nicholas after him, and then John, as Leo Allatius shows accurately in his Commentary published at Rome in 1630.

units.la: SILVESTER PETRASANCTA In Caluiniano Verberone contra Andream Riuetum cap. 30. pag. 415. De Ioanna Papissa.
units.tr: SILVESTER PETRASANCTA Against Andreas Rivetus's Calvinist Club, ch. 30, p. 415. On Pope Joan.

units.la: Prolixius confutare fabulam hanc, vt dixi, esset actum agere, cum Onuphrius Panuinus, Genebrardus, Baronius, Bernardinus, Serrarius, Alanus Copus, Sanderus, Miraeus, Gretserus, Floremundus Remundus, Leo Allatius, Vittorellus, & Scriptores alij complures eruditis suis Commentarijs detexerint eius impostu-ram, & vanitatem.
units.tr: To refute this fable at greater length, as I have said, would be to do work already done, since Onuphrius Panvinius, Genebrardus, Baronius, Bernardinus, Serarius, Alanus Copus, Sanderus, Miraeus, Gretserus, Florimond de Raemond, Leo Allatius, Vittorelli and several other writers have exposed its imposture and emptiness in their learned commentaries.

units.la: TOLDO CONSTANTINO Protonotario Apostolico, e Presidente nel Collegio de Nobili di Padoua. Nel Poema intitolato, Iudicio estremo nel Canto 10.
units.tr: TOLDO CONSTANTINO, Apostolic Protonotary and President of the College of Nobles in Padua. In the poem entitled The Last Judgement, Canto 10.

units.la: Che certo finta l'ha spirto mendaceNon nel suo original Martino inserta. Suffrido che quel hebbe ancor viuaceNelle proprie sue man, del ver n'accerta. E'l dotto Allatio, che un non men veraceManuscritto letto ha fa fede aperta. Come il testo è incorrotto, e'l margin nettoD'un cotal mostro fauolofo inetto.
units.tr: Surely a lying spirit invented it, not inserted by Martin in his original. Suffrido, who read it in his own hand, which was still lively, confirms the truth of this. And the learned Allatius, who has read a manuscript no less trustworthy, bears open witness. As the text is uncorrupted and the margin clean of such a foolish, fabulous monster.

units.la: FERDINANDVS VGHELLVS In Italia Sacra De Pontificibus Romanis in Leone IV.
units.tr: FERDINANDUS UGHELLI, In Italia Sacra, On the Roman Pontiffs, under Leo IV.

units.la: Sed fabulam Ioanna egregie detexere Baronius in suis Annalibus, Leoque Allatius homo hoc doctissimo seculo eruditissimus in sua deIoanna Papissa Fabula, Commentatione, ita vt hic haud pluribus verbis opus sit ad iugulandum turpissimum commentum.
units.tr: But Baronius has excellently exposed the fable of Joan in his Annals, and Leo Allatius, the most learned man of this very learned age, in his commentary on the fable of Pope Joan, so that there is no need here for many words to slay this most shameful invention.

units.la: IOANNES RHO Mediolanensis S.I.P. In Interrogationibus Apologeticis ad Ioannem Baptistam Castaldum Interrogat. 4. pag. 69.
units.tr: JOHANNES RHO, Milanese, S.I., priest. In Apologetic Interrogations to Giovanni Battista Castaldo, Interrogation 4, p. 69.

units.la: Hic enimuero mihi venit in mentem nobilis illius fabella, quam superiorum seculorum indiligentia progenitam, atque impio plausu a Sectarijs nouatoribusque exceptam Baronius, Bellarminus, virique alij oppido magni, & nuperrime Leo Allatius, eruditissimo edito libello profligarunt, de Ioanna Papissa.
units.tr: For indeed there comes to my mind that famous little tale of Pope Joan, begotten by the carelessness of earlier centuries and greeted with impious applause by the sectaries and innovators, which Baronius, Bellarmine, and other very great men, and most recently Leo Allatius in a most learned little book, have routed.

units.la: FLORAVANTES MARTINELLVS In Imagine B. Mariae Virginis vindicata .
units.tr: FLORAVANTES MARTINELLUS, In The Image of the Blessed Virgin Mary Vindicated.

units.la: Et si vniuersa Chronica, quae sub Martini nomine, vel typis, vel scripto circumfertur, ab integritatis suæ gradu deturbata aliorum imperitia, vel negligentia, & forte maleuolentia fiunt, ut notauit Allatius in difertissima Ioanna Papissæ fabula.
units.tr: And even if the whole chronicle that circulates under Martin's name, whether in print or in manuscript, has been knocked from the level of its integrity by the ignorance or carelessness, and perhaps the malice, of others, as Allatius has noted in his most eloquent treatment of the fable of Pope Joan.

units.la: MELCHIOR INCOFER S. I. In Annalibus Ecclesiasticis Regni Vngariæ Anno 879. p. 96.
units.tr: MELCHIOR INCHOFER, S.I., In the Ecclesiastical Annals of the Kingdom of Hungary, Year 879, p. 96.

units.la: Atque hinc erupit fabula de Ioanna Papissa, quam Marianus Scotus, Platina, aliíque ex istis impudenter veri insulso figmento obtruserunt. Sed plurimi doctissimi viri egregie consutarunt, quos inter recentissimus palmam extulit Leo Allatius multis eruditis lucubrationibus clarus, & plane ludos fecit, qui hinc Ecclesiæ Romanæ puerliter officere se existimant.
units.tr: From this burst forth the fable of Pope Joan, which Marianus Scotus, Platina and others of that sort have shamelessly foisted upon us as truth in a silly fiction. But very learned men have excellently refuted it, and among the most recent of these Leo Allatius, distinguished by many learned works, has carried off the palm, and he has made fools of those who think the Roman Church is childishly harmed by it.

units.la: BARTOLDUS NIHUSIUS In Hypodigmate in Præfatione. p. 11.
units.tr: BARTHOLD NIHUSIUS, In the Hypodigma, Preface, p. 11.

units.la: Sed hanc istorum hominum vitilitigationem pluribus excutimus, tum alibi, tum in editis ad Allatium de Papissa, nostrumque Prosphonematicum, tum in Hypodigmate.
units.tr: But we have examined this idle wrangling of those men at length, both elsewhere and in our published works on Allatius's book on Pope Joan, and in our Prosphonematicum, and in the Hypodigma.

units.la: Idem
units.tr: The same.

units.la: Cuius tamen generis malignitas tua plu-ribus quoque detecta per nos non sciscitabulo solum, ac prologo belli Allatiani de Papissa alibique, verum & pastillo quo te locupletatum a me nosti, ut odorem tuis adspiret naribus.
units.tr: Yet your malignity of this kind has also been exposed at length by us, not only in the little book and preface of the war with Allatius on Pope Joan, and elsewhere, but also in the lozenge with which you know I have furnished you, so that it may breathe its odour into your nostrils.

units.la: JOANNES HENRICUS BOECLERUS In Commentario de rebus seculi a Christo nato IX. & X. per seriem Germanorum Caesarum.
units.tr: JOHANN HEINRICH BOECLER, In the commentary on the events of the ninth and tenth centuries after the birth of Christ, through the succession of German emperors.

units.la: Eos qui negaverunt Joannam Papissam foeminam recenset, numeroque accedit Baronius: Adduntur Leo Allatius, & Davit Blondellus.
units.tr: He lists those who have denied that Joan the Pope was a woman, and Baronius joins their number. Leo Allatius and David Blondel are added.

units.la: CLAUDIUS SARAVIUS Senator Parisiensis Epistola ad Vincentium Fabrum scripta Anno 1640. pag.41.
units.tr: CLAUDE SARAVIUS, Senator of Paris, in a letter written to Vincent Faber in 1640, p. 41.

units.la: De Salmasio. De primatu Papa, prolixum opus mouet, centum puta, & amplius Quaternionum cum duabus Appendicibus de Antichristo, & de Joanna Papissa, in priore Pontificios κἀ ἰσως τὸν πάνυ Γρώπον[?]: in posteriore Leonem Allatium, & Davidem Blon-
units.tr: On Salmasius. He has set in motion a lengthy work on the primacy of the Pope, a hundred quires and more, with two appendices, one on the Antichrist and one on Pope Joan: in the former the Papists [κἀ ἰσως τὸν πάνυ Γρώπον], and in the latter Leo Allatius and David Blondel.

units.la: PHILIPPVS LABBÆVS S. I. Presbyter.
units.tr: PHILIPPUS LABBÆUS S. I. Presbyter.

units.la: In Cenotaphio Ioannæ Papissæ. p. 838.
units.tr: Against the Cenotaph of Joan the Papess. p. 838.

units.la: Leonem Allatium Chium, qui ex monu-mentis Græcis confutationem fabulæ illius edidit Romæ Anno 1630. quam recudendam curauit Coloniæ anno 1645. Bartoldus Nihusius, adiunctis Prologo, Epilogo, & Telescopio.
units.tr: Leo Allatius of Chios, who from Greek monuments published at Rome in 1630 a refutation of that fable, which Bartholdus Nihusius had it reprinted at Cologne in 1645, with a Prologue, an Epilogue and a Telescopium added.

units.la: Pag. 913. Quorum annis si adjicias Ioannæ Papissæ duos annos, menses quinque & dies quatuor non anni 45. sed 47. numerandi fuerant, ut ait Leo Allatius, qui etiam aduertit a primo Leonis anno, &c.
units.tr: Page 913. If to the years of these you add the two years of Joan the Papess, then not 45 but 47 years, five months and four days were to be counted, as Leo Allatius says, who also observes that from the first year of Leo, etc.

units.la: LEONIS ALLATII Libri editi in Typographia S. Con- gregationis Fidei propagandæ.
units.tr: Books by Leo Allatius, published in the press of the Sacred Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith.

units.la: I.[?] DE ætate, & interstitijs in Collatione Ordinum etiam apud Græcos seruandis, ad Cardinalem FRANCISCVM BRANCACCIVM. addita sunt eiusdem ALLATII Ode Pindarica, & Epigrammata vii. Græca in Assumptam DEIPARAM. 1638. in 8.
units.tr: I.[?] On the age and the intervals to be observed in the conferring of orders, also among the Greeks, addressed to Cardinal Francesco Brancaccio. To it are added a Pindaric ode by the same Allatius and seven Greek epigrams on the Assumption of the Mother of God. 1638, in octavo.

units.la: II. ORTHODOXAE GRAECIAE Scriptores NICEPHORVS BLEMMIDA, IOANNES VECCVS Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, PETRVS Episcopus Mediolanensis GREGORIVS PACHYMERES, ESAIAS CYPRIVS, IOANNES ARGYROPYLVS, GREGORIVS Protosyncellus Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, GEORGIVS TRAPEZVNTINVS, IOANNES PLVSIADENVS, HILARIO Monachus, De Processione Spiritus sancti a Patre, & Filio. NICETAE BYZANTII Philosophi, & Magistri Refutatio Epistolæ scriptæ ab Armenorum Principe, qua fidem Catholicam, & Chalcedonensem Synodum criminabatur, & alijs. Tomus primus. LEO ALLATIVS nunc primum e tenebris eruit, & Latine vertit, ad Cardinalem ALOYSIVM CAPPONIVM. Addita est, de GREGORIO PALAMA Archiepiscopo Thessalonicensi in numerum Sanctorum a nonnullis Græcis adscito Græcorum[?] sententiæ, nec non GREGORII ACINDYNI, de Haeresibus Palamæ Carmen. 1652. in 4.
units.tr: II. Greek Orthodox writers: Nicephorus Blemmida, John Veccus, Patriarch of Constantinople, Peter, Bishop of Milan, Gregory Pachymeres, Isaiah Cyprius, John Argyropulus, Gregory Protosyncellus, Patriarch of Constantinople, George Trapezuntius, John Plusiadenus, and Hilarion the monk, on the Procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son. The Refutation by Nicetas of Byzantium, philosopher and teacher, of a letter written by the Prince of the Armenians, in which he accused the Catholic faith and the Council of Chalcedon, and other works. Volume one. Leo Allatius, now first brought out of darkness and translated into Latin, addressed to Cardinal Aloysius Cappononius. Added is a work on Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessalonica, admitted by some Greeks into the number of the saints, together with the opinions of the Greeks, and also a Poem by Gregory Akindynos on the heresies of Palamas. 1652, in quarto.

units.la: III. ORTHODOXAE GRAECIAE Scriptores, IOANNES VECCVS Patriarcha Constantinopolitanus, CONSTANTINVS MELITENIOTA Chartophylax, GREGORIVS METOCHITA Diaconus magnæ Ecclesiæ, MAXIMVS CHRYSOBERGA De Processione Spiritus sancti, & alijs. ad Eminentissimum Cardinalem FLAVIVM GHISIVM S.R.F. Bibliothecarium, Tomus Secundus, LEO ALLATIVS nunc primum e tenebris eruit, & Latine vertit. 1659. in 4.
units.tr: III. Greek Orthodox writers: John Veccus, Patriarch of Constantinople, Constantine Meliteniotes, chartophylax, Gregory Metochites, deacon of the Great Church, Maximus Chrysoberges, on the Procession of the Holy Spirit, and others. Addressed to the most eminent Cardinal Flavio Ghisi, librarian of the Holy Roman Church. Volume two. Leo Allatius, now first brought out of darkness and translated into Latin. 1659, in quarto.

units.la: IV. De triumphe Ecclesiæ ORIENTALIS atque OCCIDENTALIS perpetua in dogmate de Purgatorio consensione, ad ALEXANDRUM VII. Pont. Opt. Max. Addita sunt. Eiusdem Epistola ad JOANNEM CHRISTIANUM de BOINEBURG, De perpetua Ecclesiæ ORIENTALIS atque OCCIDENTALIS tum in dogmate, tam in Ritibus consensione. Ad BARTOLDUM NIHUSIUM Epistola secunda De communione Græcorum sub unica specie; & De textu Machabæorum De Sacrificio pro mortuis, & textum Græcum dicere, quod exprimit textus Latinus. EUSTRATII Constantinopolitani De Animabus separatis, IOANNIS VECCI Patriarchæ Constantinopolitani ad Sugdæa THEODORUM liber tertius, de causa schismatis, Græce, & Latine eodem ALLATIO Interprete, 1655. in 8.
units.tr: IV. On the perpetual agreement of the Eastern and Western Church in the doctrine of Purgatory, to Pope Alexander VII, Best and Greatest. Also added: a letter by the same author to John Christian von Boineburg, On the perpetual agreement of the Eastern and Western Church both in doctrine and in rites; to Bartold Nihusius, a second letter on the communion of the Greeks under one kind, and on the text of the Maccabees concerning sacrifice for the dead, where the Greek text says what the Latin text expresses; the work On Separated Souls by Eustratius of Constantinople; and the third book by John Veccus, Patriarch of Constantinople, to Theodore of Sugdaea, on the cause of the schism, in Greek and Latin, with Allatius as translator. 1655, in octavo.

units.la: V. Carmina Græca, in CHRISTINAM Suecorum Reginam. Ibidem in 4. 1656
units.tr: V. Greek poems addressed to Christina, Queen of the Swedes. In the same place, in quarto. 1656.

units.la: VI. S. METHODII Episcopi, & Martyris CONVIVIVM decem Virginum, siue, De Castitate, ad ALEXANDRUM VII. Pont. Opt. Max. LEO ALLATIUS hactenus non editum primus Græce vulgavit, Latine vertit, NOTAS, & DIATRIBAM De Methodiorum scriptis. 1656. in 8.
units.tr: VI. The Banquet of the Ten Virgins, or On Chastity, by Methodius, Bishop and Martyr, to Pope Alexander VII, Best and Greatest. Leo Allatius, the first to publish it in Greek, a work hitherto unpublished, translated it into Latin and added notes and a dissertation on the writings of Methodius. 1656, in octavo.

units.la: VII. Vindiciæ Synodi EPHESINÆ, & S. CYRILLI De Processione ex Patre & Filio Spiritus sancti. 1659. in 8.
units.tr: VII. Defences of the Council of Ephesus, and of Cyril, on the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son. 1659, in octavo.

units.la: VIII. Enchiridion De processione Spiritus sancti, Lingua Græcorum vernacula. 1658. in 12.
units.tr: VIII. Handbook on the Procession of the Holy Spirit, in the vernacular Greek language. 1658, in duodecimo.

units.la: IX. De Symbolo S. ATHANASII lingua Græcorum vernacula. Ibidem. in 12.
units.tr: IX. On the Creed of St Athanasius, in the vernacular Greek language. In the same place, in duodecimo.

units.la: X. IOANNES HENRICUS HOTTINGERUS Fraudis, & impostura manifestæ convictus a LEONE ALLATIO. 1661. in 8.
units.tr: X. John Henry Hottinger, convicted of fraud and manifest imposture by Leo Allatius. 1661, in octavo.

units.la: XI. LEONIS ALLATII De Octava Synodo PHOTIANA. Adnexa est eiusdem IOANNIS HENRICI HOTTINGERI Disputationis Apologeticæ De Ecclesia Orientalis, atque Occidentalis tam in Dogmatibus quam in Ritibus diffensus, & JUVENIS ULMENSIS Exercitationis Historico-Theologicæ de Ecclesia Græcanica Indiernx, REFUTATIO. 1662. in 8.
units.tr: XI. Leo Allatius, On the Eighth Council of Photius. Appended is the apologetic disputation of John Henry Hottinger himself, On the differences between the Eastern and Western Churches both in doctrines and in rites, and a refutation of the historical-theological exercise of a young man of Ulm on the present-day Greek Church. 1662, in octavo.
